paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: absorption-theorem
title: Absorption Theorem
statement_text: If R ≤ _ sd A × B is a subdirect binary relation and A , B are finite idempotent Taylor algebras, and if R is linked , then either R = A × B , A has a proper binary absorbing or centrally absorbing subalgebra, or B has a proper subalgebra which is both binary absorbing and centrally absorbing.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If R ≤ _ sd A × B is a subdirect binary relation and A , B are finite idempotent Taylor algebras, and if R ∘ R ^- = A × A , then either there is some b ∈ B such that A × {b} ⊆ R , A has a proper binary absorbing subalgebra, or every element of A is contained in a proper centrally absorbing subalgebra.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If R ≤ _ sd A × B is a subdirect binary relation and A , B are finite idempotent Taylor algebras, and if there is some b ∈ B such that A × {b} ⊆ R , then either R = A × B , A has a proper binary absorbing or centrally absorbing subalgebra, or the right center of R is a proper binary absorbing subalgebra of B .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: absorption-free-binary
statement_text: Let A , B be finite idempotent Taylor algebras with no proper binary or centrally absorbing subalgebras. If B is simple, then every subdirect binary relation R ≤ _ sd A × B is either the full relation or the graph of a surjective homomorphism A twoheadrightarrow B .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A digraph D = (V,E) is called smooth if every vertex of D has indegree at least one and outdegree at least one. Note that this is equivalent to the relation E ⊆ V × V being subdirect.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If D = (V,E) is a digraph, then the largest smooth digraph D _ sm which is contained in D is exactly the set of vertices v of D such that there exists a bi-infinite directed walk through v . If D is finite, with n vertices, then the vertex set of D _ sm may be defined by the pp-formula v ∈ D _ sm ⟺ ∃ v_ -n , ..., v_n\ (v_0 = v) ∧ wedge_ -n ≤ i < n (v_i,v_ i+1 ) ∈ E. The set D _ sm will be nonempty iff D contains a directed cycle (or a bi-infinite directed path, in the infinite case).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If D is a digraph and D _ sm is defined as in the previous proposition, then we call D _ sm the smooth part of the digraph D .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If D is a digraph and a,b are in the smooth part of D , then every vertex of D which can be found along any directed path from a to b is also contained in the smooth part of D .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If S lhd R and R , S ≤ A × A correspond to digraphs R , S with vertex set A , and if R is smooth, then the smooth part S _ sm of the digraph S has vertex set equal to an absorbing subalgebra of A , which will be nonempty as long as S contains some directed cycle.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If R ≤ A × A , and if B ≤ A is finite and satisfies either B ⊆ B + R or B ⊆ B - R , then the restriction R ∩ ( B × B ) of R to B has nonempty smooth part.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: loop-linked
title: Loop Lemma, linked case
statement_text: Suppose that A is a finite Taylor algebra and that R ≤ _ sd A × A is a linked subdirect relation. Then R contains a loop, that is, R ∩ Δ_ A ≠ ∅ .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: The algebraic length of a weakly connected digraph D is the least common multiple of all integers k such that there is a digraph homomorphism from D to a directed cycle of length k .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: The algebraic length of a weakly connected digraph D = (V,E) is the greatest common divisor of all integers k such that there exist v ∈ V and k_1, k_2, ..., k_m ∈ N such that v ∈ {v} + k_1E - k_2E + ... ± k_mE and k = k_1 - k_2 + ... ± k_m . Furthermore, there exists a digraph homomorphism from D to a directed cycle C iff the algebraic length of D is a multiple of the length of the cycle C .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If D = (V,E) is a smooth, weakly connected digraph of algebraic length k , then the digraph D ^ ∘ m = (V,E^ ∘ m ) has gcd (k,m) weakly connected components, and each weakly connected component of D ^ ∘ m has algebraic length (k)/(gcd (k,m)) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-alg-length-linked
statement_text: If D = (V,E) is smooth and weakly connected, then D has algebraic length 1 if and only if there is some m ≥ 0 such that the relation E^ ∘ m is linked.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If D = (V,E) is smooth and has a weakly connected component C ⊆ V of algebraic length 1 , and if v ∈ C , then the set C can be defined by a primitive positive formula using the singleton unary relation {v} and the binary relation E .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: loop-lemma
title: Loop Lemma
statement_text: If A is a finite Taylor algebra and R ≤ _ sd A × A corresponds to a smooth digraph R = ( A , R ) which has a weakly connected component of algebraic length 1 , then R has a loop, i.e. R ∩ Δ_ A ≠ ∅ .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: siggers-term
title: Siggers term ,
statement_text: If A is a finite Taylor algebra, then A has a 4 -ary idempotent term t which satisfies the identity t(x,x,y,z) ≈ t(y,z,z,x).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: An algebraic structure A is called abelian if there is a congruence Θ on A × A such that the diagonal Δ_ A = {(a,a) | a ∈ A } is one of the congruence classes of Θ .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: ternary-abelian
statement_text: Suppose that R ≤ _ sd A × A × A has the property that for each a ∈ A , and for each permutation (i,j,k) of (1,2,3) , the binary relation π_ ij (x ∈ R ∧ x_k = a) is the graph of an automorphism of A . Then A is abelian.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: We say that an algebra A is hereditarily absorption free if every subalgebra of A is absorption free, that is, if C lhd B ≤ A implies that C = B or C = ∅ .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose A , B are idempotent and hereditarily absorption free. Then A × B is also hereditarily absorption free.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: haf-malcev
title: HAF implies Mal'cev
statement_text: If A is finite, idempotent, Taylor, and hereditarily absorption free, then A is Mal'cev.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If an algebra A is abelian and has at least two elements, then A does not have a near-unanimity term.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: abelian-haf
title: Abelian implies HAF
statement_text: If a finite algebra A is abelian, then it is absorption free.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: taylor-abelian
title: Fundamental Theorem of Abelian Algebras, finite Taylor case , , ,
statement_text: If A is a finite abelian Taylor algebra, then A is affine.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: absorption-free
title: Zhuk
statement_text: Suppose that A is finite, simple, idempotent, Taylor, has no binary or centrally absorbing subalgebras, and is not affine. Then every subdirect relation R ≤ _ sd A ^n is the intersection of its binary projections, each of which is either a full relation or the graph of an automorphism of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: defn-subdirectly-complete
statement_text: We say that an algebra A is subdirectly simple if every subdirect relation R ≤ _ sd A ^n is the intersection of its binary projections, each of which is either a full relation or the graph of an automorphism of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Every subdirectly simple finite algebra is polynomially complete.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: zhuk-four-cases
title: Zhuk's four cases
statement_text: If A is a nontrivial finite idempotent Taylor algebra, then at least one of the following is true. A has a proper binary absorbing subalgebra, A has a proper centrally absorbing subalgebra, A has a nontrivial affine quotient, or A has a nontrivial subdirectly simple quotient.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: We say that a finite idempotent algebra A is affine-free if no quotient of any subalgebra of A is affine.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: absorption-free-ternary
statement_text: Suppose R ≤ _ sd A × B × C is subdirect, A has no proper binary or centrally absorbing subalgebra and no affine quotient, π_ 23 ( R ) has no proper binary absorbing subalgebra, π_ 12 ( R ) = A × B , π_ 13 ( R ) = A × C , and A , B , C are finite idempotent Taylor algebras. Then R = A × π_ 23 ( R ) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A , B are finite Taylor algebras, R , S ≤ _ sd A × B , and the linked components of R on A sqcup B contain the corresponding linked components of S , then R ∩ S ≠ ∅ .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: cor-abs-free-arc
statement_text: If A _1, ..., A _n are finite idempotent Taylor algebras with no proper binary or centrally absorbing subalgebras such that all but at most two of the A _i s have no affine quotients, and if R ≤ _ sd A _1 × ... × A _n is a subdirect relation such that each π_ ij ( R ) is full, then R = A _1 × ... × A _n .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: cor-abs-free-pq
statement_text: If A _1, ..., A _n are finite idempotent Taylor algebras with no proper binary or centrally absorbing subalgebras and no affine quotients, and if R ≤ _ sd A _1 × ... × A _n × A _1 is a subdirect relation such that Δ_ A _1 ⊆ π_ 1,n+1 ( R ) and π_ ij ( R ) is full for all pairs (i,j) other than (1,n+1) , then R contains every tuple whose first and last coordinates are the same.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that the instance X is pq -consistent, and that x, θ_x are chosen as above. Suppose that y is a proper variable, and that p,q are two paths from y to x such that P _p/θ_x, P _q/θ_x are the graphs of homomorphisms iota _p, iota _q: A _y twoheadrightarrow A _x/θ_x . Then iota _p = iota _q .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: proper-path
statement_text: Suppose that the instance X is pq -consistent, and that each domain has no proper binary or centrally absorbing subalgebra. Suppose p is a path from y to a proper variable z . Then one of the following is true: P _p/θ_z = A _y × A _z/θ_z , or y is also proper, and P _p/(θ_y × θ_z) is the graph of an isomorphism iota _p : A _y/θ_y xrightarrow A _z/θ_z such that iota _y = iota _z ∘ iota _p .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: affine-free-pq
title: Kozik
statement_text: If X is a pq -consistent instance of a CSP such that every domain is finite, idempotent, Taylor, and affine-free, then X has a solution.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that X is a pq -consistent instance of a CSP such that every domain is finite, idempotent, Taylor, and affine-free. If x is a variable with domain A _x , then for any element a ∈ A _x such that there is a sequence of subalgebras A _x = A _0 ⊇ ... ⊇ A _n = {a} such that for each i either A _ i+1 is a minimal absorbing subalgebra of A _i or A _ i+1 is a congruence class of a congruence θ ∈ Con ( A _i) such that A _i/θ is polynomially complete and A _i is absorption free, there is a solution to the instance X in which x is assigned the value a .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: affine-free-variety
title: A special case of Lemma
statement_text: If A _1, ..., A _n are finite, idempotent, Taylor, and affine-free, then the variety V ( A _1, ..., A _n) which they generate does not contain any nontrivial abelian algebras.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a finite idempotent algebra, then A is Taylor and affine-free if and only if the variety V ( A ) is congruence meet-semidistributive.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A relational structure A with a finite domain has CSP ( A ) solved by pq -consistency if and only if A does not pp-construct any of the relational structures ( Z /p,{1},x+y=z) , p prime.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: defn-weak-prague
statement_text: An instance X of a CSP with variable domains A _x is called a weak Prague instance if it satisfies the following three conditions. The instance X is arc-consistent, that is, each constraint relation R ≤ Π _ x_i A _ x_i is subdirect. For every variable x , every set A ⊆ A _x , and every cycle p from x to x , we have the implication A + p = A ⇒ A - p = A. For every variable x , every set A ⊆ A _x , and every pair of cycles p,q from x to x , we have the implication A + p + q = A ⇒ A + p = A.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-p2
statement_text: A subdirect binary relation P ≤ _ sd A × A on a finite algebra A satisfies the implication A + P = A ⇒ A - P = A for all A ⊆ A if and only if the digraph P = ( A , P ) satisfies one of the following equivalent conditions: every weakly connected component of P is strongly connected, every edge of P is contained in a directed cycle of P , there is some k ≥ 0 such that P ^- ⊆ P ^ ∘ k .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-p2*
title: Barto, Kozik
statement_text: If an instance satisfies condition (P1), then (P2) is equivalent to the following condition. For all variables x , sets A ⊆ A _x , and cycles p from x to x such that A + p = A , if p_1 is the first step of the cycle p , then we have A + p_1 - p_1 = A . Note that A + p_1 - p_1 = A if and only if A is a union of linked components of p_1 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: lp-p1-p2
statement_text: If X is an instance of a CSP such that the basic linear relaxation of X has a solution assigning probability vectors p_C to each constraint C of X and probability vectors p_x to each variable x , then the instance X ' obtained by restricting each constraint relation of X to the support of the corresponding probability distribution p_C (and similarly for the variable domains) satisfies conditions (P1) and (P2).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: lp-p1-p2-converse
statement_text: If X is an instance of a CSP such that the associated hypergraph of variables and relations consists of a single cycle, then X has properties (P1) and (P2) if and only if the basic linear relaxation of X has a solution such that for each constraint C of X , the support of the corresponding probability distribution p_C is exactly equal to the relation corresponding to C .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: When there is more than one cycle, properties (P1) and (P2) do not necessarily imply that the basic linear relaxation has a solution, even if all relations are binary. Consider the following instance, with two variables x,y taking values in the domain A_x = A_y = {a,b,c} : x x & ∈ { a b , b a , c c } ∧ x x & ∈ { a c , b c , c a , c b } ∧ x y & ∈ { a a , b b , b c , c b , c c } ∧ y y & ∈ { a b , b c , c a }. First we check that the basic linear relaxation to this instance has no solutions. Suppose for a contradiction that the basic linear relaxation had a solution p . The first constraint implies that p_ x,a = p_ x,b , and the second constraint implies that p_ x,a + p_ x,b = p_ x,c , so we must have p_ x,a = p_ x,b = 1/4 and p_ x,c = 1/2 . Similarly, the last constraint implies that p_ y,a = p_ y,b = p_ y,c = 1/3 . But the constraint connecting x to y implies that p_ x,a = p_ y,a , which is a contradiction as 1/4 ≠ 1/3 . Now we check that this instance satisfies (P2), using Proposition . We only need to check condition (P2) for singletons, since the domains have size 3 and for A ⊆ A_x and for any cycle p from x to x , A + p = A is equivalent to (A_x \ A) - p = (A_x \ A) as long as the instance is arc-consistent. In order to check (P2) for singletons, first we check that there is no path through the instance which takes {a,c}, {b,c} ⊆ A_x or {a,b}, {a,c}, {b,c} ⊆ A_y to any singleton, and we check that there is no path from x to x which takes {c} ⊆ A_x to either of {a}, {b} ⊆ A_x . Then we check that for any path p_1 of length 1 such that A + p_1 doesn't contain one of the bad sets which can never reach a singleton, either A is a union of linked components of p_1 or else A is one of {a}, {b} ⊆ A_x , p_1 corresponds to the second constraint, and A + p_1 = {c} ⊆ A_x .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: An instance X with finite variable domains A _x satisfies condition (P3) if and only if it satisfies the following condition. For all variables x , for all pairs of cycles p,q from x to x , and for all a ∈ A _x , there is some j ≥ 0 such that {a} + j(p+q) = {a} + j(p+q) + p = {a} + j(p+q) + p + q.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-prec-p3
statement_text: An instance X satisfies condition (P3) at a variable x if and only if there is a partial order preceq on the power set P ( A _x) , such that for every cycle p from x to x and every A ⊆ A _x , we have A preceq A+p. The instance X satisfies (P3) everywhere if and only if there is a quasiorder preceq on the set of ordered pairs (x,A) with A ⊆ A _x , such that for each binary projection R _ ij ≤ A _x × A _y of any constraint relation of X and for each A ⊆ A _x , we have (x,A) preceq (y,A+ R _ ij ), and such that for each x , the restriction of preceq to {x} × P ( A _x) defines a partial order on P ( A _x) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: weak-prague-pq
statement_text: Every weak Prague instance is pq -consistent.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Here we give an example of a pq -consistent instance (in fact, even a singleton arc-consistent instance!) which is not a weak Prague instance. Consider the instance of 2-SAT with just one variable x , domain A _x = ({0,1}, maj ) , and a binary constraint relation R ≤ _ sd A _x × A _x imposed on (x,x) given by R = {(0,0),(0,1),(1,1)} (that is, R is the binary relation ≤ ). Since Δ_ {0,1} ⊆ R , we see that this instance is pq -consistent. However, this instance does not satisfy property (P2) of a weak Prague instance: we have {1} + R = {1}, but {1} - R = {0,1} ≠ {1}. Alternatively, we can check that (P2) is not satisfied by noting that the digraph ({0,1}, ≤ ) is weakly connected but not strongly conected.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: pq-p1-p3
title: Kozik
statement_text: Every pq -consistent instance satisfies conditions (P1) and (P3).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: There is an example of an instance which satisfies (P1) and (P3), but which is not pq -consistent. As in the previous example, this instance will have just a single variable x and a single binary constraint R ≤ _ sd A _x × A _x . We take the algebra A _x to be the three-element dual discriminator algebra ({0,1,2},d(x,y,z)) from Example . The binary relation R is the 0/1/all constraint displayed below. To see that this is not pq -consistent, note that there is no j such that (0,0) ∈ R ^ ∘ j . To see that this instance satisfies condition (P3), we use the following total ordering on P ({0,1,2}) : ∅ preceq {0} preceq {0,1} preceq {1} preceq {0,2} preceq {2} preceq {1,2} preceq {0,1,2}.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: We say that a probability distribution μ on a finite set A is in general position if we have μ(S) ≠ μ(T) for every pair of disjoint subsets S,T ⊆ A with μ(S), μ(T) ≠ 0 . We say that a solution to the linear relaxation of an instance X is in general position if the probability distribution which it assigns to each variable domain is in general position.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If there is a solution to the linear programming relaxation of X which is in general position, then the instance we get by restricting each variable domain and relation to the support of this solution is a weak Prague instance (and is therefore pq -consistent as well).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prob-p1-p3
statement_text: Is it true that every instance of an affine-free CSP which satisfies conditions (P1) and (P3) has a solution?

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: bounded-width-terms
title: Height 1 identities for bounded width , ,
statement_text: Suppose A is a relational structure on a finite domain. Then CSP ( A ) has bounded relational width iff there are ternary polymorphisms f,g ∈ Pol _3( A ) satisfying the height 1 identities g(x,x,y) ≈ g(x,y,x) ≈ g(y,x,x) ≈ f(x,x,y) ≈ f(x,y,x) ≈ f(x,y,y). In this case, every pq -consistent instance of CSP ( A ) has a solution.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that X is an instance of a CSP such that every variable domain is contained in A , but possibly the variable domains and the relations of X are not closed under the operations of A . Define Sg _ A ( X ) to be the instance of CSP ( A ) where every variable domain and every relation of X is replaced by the subalgebra it generates.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: pq-algebraic-closure
statement_text: If X is a pq -consistent instance as above, then Sg _ A ( X ) is also pq -consistent.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If X is a weak Prague instance as above, then Sg _ A ( X ) is also a weak Prague instance.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose X is an instance of a CSP over the two-element domain {x,y} with no unary relations, such that every binary projection π_ i,j (R) of every relation R is subdirect in {x,y}^2 and has (x,x) ∈ π_ i,j (R) . Then X is pq -consistent.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose CSP ( A ) has bounded relational width and A is finite. Then there is a binary polymorphism c(x,y) , and an infinite family of polymorphisms h_n^ F ∈ Pol _n( A ) indexed by the collection of maximal intersecting families F of subsets of [n] , such that for each set S ∈ F with S ≠ [n] , if we define v_i^S by v_i^S = x & i ∈ S, y & i ∉ S, we have the identity h_n^ F (v_1^S, ..., v_n^S) ≈ c(x,y).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose we are given a finite relational structure A = (A, R_1, ..., R_n) , where each relation R_i has arity m_i and is described by explicitly listing out its tuples, and suppose that we are promised that A is core. Then we can determine whether CSP ( A ) has bounded width in polynomial time, and in the case where CSP ( A ) has bounded width, we can explicitly find ternary functions f,g ∈ Pol _3( A ) as in Theorem .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: bounded-width-term
statement_text: A finite relational structure A has bounded relational width if and only if it has a ternary polymorphism g ∈ Pol _3( A ) such that, if f is the binary term f(x,y) coloneqq g(x,x,y) , we have g(x,x,y) ≈ g(x,y,x) ≈ g(y,x,x) ≈ f(x,y) ≈ f(f(x,y),f(y,x)) ≈ f(f(x,y), f(x,y)).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that g is a ternary term as in Theorem , and that f is the associated binary term. Then for any a,b , either f(a,b) = f(b,a) , or the set {f(a,b), f(b,a)} is closed under g , and ({f(a,b),f(b,a)},g) is isomorphic to a two-element majority algebra.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A finite idempotent algebra A has bounded relational width if and only if it has a ternary term m and an associated binary term s(x,y) coloneqq m(x,x,y) , which satisfy the identities m(x,x,y) ≈ m(x,y,x) ≈ m(y,x,x) ≈ s(x,y) and s(x,s(x,y)) ≈ s(s(x,y),x) ≈ s(x,y).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: defn-stability
statement_text: Suppose that V is a pseudovariety of finite algebras. We say that a binary relation Yleft on V is a stability concept (or just a stability ) on V if Yleft satisfies the following axioms. If B Yleft A , then B ≤ A . If C Yleft B Yleft A , then C Yleft A . If B , C Yleft A and B ∩ C ≠ ∅ , then B ∩ C Yleft B . If f : A twoheadrightarrow B is a surjective homomorphism, then if C Yleft A , then f( C ) Yleft B , and if D Yleft B , then f^ -1 ( D ) Yleft A . If B , C , D Yleft A are such that B ∩ C ≠ ∅ , C ∩ D ≠ ∅ , and B ∩ D ≠ ∅ , then B ∩ C ∩ D ≠ ∅ . If A ∈ V has | A | > 1 , then either there is some B Yleft A such that B ≠ A , ∅ , or there is some proper congruence θ ∈ Con ( A ) such that A /θ is an affine algebra. Given a stability concept Yleft on V , we say that B is a stable subalgebra of A if B Yleft A . We say that an element a ∈ A is a stable element if {a} Yleft A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If Yleft is a binary relation on V which satisfies the propagation axiom from Definition , then for any subdirect relation R ≤ _ sd A × B in V , we have C Yleft A ⇒ C + R Yleft B .

statement_text: If Yleft satisfies the Helly axiom and the intersection axiom from Definition , then for any n and any B _1, ... B _n Yleft A such that B _i ∩ B _j ≠ ∅ for all i, j ∈ [n] , we have cap_ i ∈ [n] B _i ≠ ∅ .

label: prop-stable-element

statement_text: If V is an affine-free pseudovariety of finite idempotent Taylor algebras, then there is at least one stability concept Yleft on V .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: An arc-consistent instance X of a CSP, with variable domains A _x , is called weakly consistent if it satisfies for all nonempty subsets A ⊆ A _x and cycles p,q from x to x , we have A + p + q = A ⇒ A ∩ (A + p) ≠ ∅ .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-weakly-consistent-cycle
statement_text: An arc-consistent instance X with finite variable domains A _x is weakly consistent if and only if it satisfies for all a ∈ A _x and cycles p,q from x to x , there exist j,k ≥ 0 such that a ∈ {a} + j(p+q) + p - k(p+q). In fact, if X is weakly consistent then for each x and each pair of cycles p,q we can find some j ≥ 0 such that Δ_ A _x ⊆ P _ j(p+q) + p - j(p+q) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: An arc-consistent instance X of a CSP, with variable domains A _x contained in a variety V with a stability concept Yleft , is called stably consistent if it satisfies for all nonempty stable subalgebras B Yleft A _x and cycles p,q from x to x , we have B + p + q = B ⇒ B ∩ ( B + p) ≠ ∅ .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If X is stably consistent and the variable domains A _x are affine free and are not all singletons, then there is some arc-consistent reduction X ' of X such that every variable domain of X ' is a stable subalgebra of the corresponding variable domain in X , and such that at least one variable domain shrinks.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If X is stably consistent and X ' is an arc-consistent stable reduction of X , then X ' is also stably consistent.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: thm-weakly-consistent
statement_text: If X is a weakly consistent instance of CSP ( A _1, ..., A _n) , where the A _i are finite bounded width algebras, then X has a solution. In fact, in this case X has a stable solution (i.e. a solution in which each variable x is assigned to a stable element of its variable domain A _x ).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that V is a pseudovariety of finite idempotent algebras, and that V ' is an affine-free reduct of V . If Yleft is a stability concept on V ' , then the restriction of Yleft to V is also a stability concept.

statement_text: A pseudovariety V of finite algebras has a stability concept iff every finitely generated subvariety of V has a stability concept.

statement_text: If V is a pseudovariety of finite idempotent strongly prepared Taylor algebras, then we say that B Yleft A if there is a sequence of subalgebras A = A _0 ≥ A _1 ≥ ... ≥ A _n = B such that for each i , one of the following is true: A _ i+1 contains a strongly absorbing subalgebra of A _i , A _ i+1 centrally absorbs A _i , or there is a congruence θ on A _i such that A _i/θ is polynomially complete, binary absorption-free and central absorption-free, and such that A _ i+1 is a congruence class of θ . We say that B is stable in one step if we can take n = 1 in the above. Following , if the third bullet point above holds for B , then we say that B is a PC subalgebra of A with PC congruence θ .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If V is a pseudovariety of finite idempotent strongly prepared Taylor algebras, then the binary relation Yleft on V from Definition is a stability concept.

statement_text: Let P _ ∅ (A) be the set of non-empty subsets of a set A . A vague element of A is defined to be a total quasiorder preceq on P _ ∅ (A) such that there is no pair of disjoint subsets S, T ⊂ A with S T , where S T means that S preceq T and T preceq S . If R ⊆ _ sd A_1 × ... × A_n is subdirect, then we say that a collection of vague elements preceq _i of the A_i s vaguely satisfies the relation R if there exists a total quasiorder preceq _R on the disjoint union P _ ∅ (A_1) sqcup ... sqcup P _ ∅ (A_n) such that the restriction of preceq _R to P _ ∅ (A_i) is preceq _i for each i , and such that for each i,j ∈ [n] and each nonempty S ⊆ A_i , we have S preceq _R S+π_ ij (R). statement_text: Every weakly consistent instance has a vague solution. In fact, there is always a vague solution where each vague element preceq _x extends the inclusion order ⊆ on P _ ∅ (A_x) (possibly identifying some subsets with each other as well).

statement_text: Consider the Siggers instance, which has one variable u with domain A_u = {x,y,z} , and one binary relation R ⊆ _ sd A_u × A_u given by R = { x y , x z , y z , z x }. Nevertheless, the Siggers instance does have a vague solution: take preceq _u to be the total order {y} prec _u {x} prec _u {z} prec _u {x,y} prec _u {y,z} prec _u {x,z} prec _u {x,y,z}. To see that (preceq _u,preceq _u) vaguely satisfies R , use the following total quasiorder preceq _R on [2] × P _ ∅ (A_u) : (1,{y}) &prec _R (2,{y}) prec _R (1,{x}) prec _R (2,{x}) _R (1,{z}) prec _R (2,{z}) &prec _R (2,{x,y}) prec _R (1,{x,y}) _R (2,{y,z}) prec _R (1,{y,z}) prec _R (2,{x,z}) prec _R (1,{x,z}) &prec _R (1,{x,y,z}) _R (2,{x,y,z}).

statement_text: There is an arc-consistent instance X such that X ^ bin has a vague solution but X does not: take the 5 -ary relation R ⊆ _ sd {a,b,c,d}^5 given by R = { a a b c d , a b c d a , b c d a a , c d a a b , d a a b c }, and let X be the instance with a single variable x which is supposed to satisfy the constraint (x,x,x,x,x) ∈ R . To see that X has no vague solution, it's enough to consider the relative order of the singleton sets {b} and {c} . On the other hand, X ^ bin has a vague solution where all five vague elements are given by {d} prec {c} prec {b} prec {c,d} prec {b,d} prec {a} prec {b,c} prec {a,d} ... {a,b,c,d}. The fact that examples like this exist seems to be a hint that vague solutions are nowhere near to being the last word on bounded width CSPs.

statement_text: If R ⊆ _ sd A_x × A_y and preceq _x, preceq _y are vague elements of A_x, A_y , respectively, then the pair (preceq _x,preceq _y) vaguely satisfies R iff the following implication holds for all S ⊆ A_x, T ⊆ A_y : S + R preceq _y T ∧ T - R preceq _x S ⇒ S + R _y T ∧ T - R _x S.

statement_text: A finite algebra A has bounded relational width if and only if it has a 4 -ary term t which satisfies the identities t(x,x,y,z) ≈ t(y,z,z,x) ≈ t(z,x,y,x) and t(x,y,x,z) ≈ t(x,z,y,x) ≈ t(y,z,x,x) simultaneously.

statement_text: If R ⊆ A_x × A_x is a smooth, weakly connected digraph of algebraic length 1 , then the instance X which consists of only the variable x and the constraint (x,x) ∈ R has a vague solution. As a consequence, the instance Sg ( X ) has a stable solution in any finite bounded width algebra.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: defn-robust
statement_text: We say that CSP ( A ) is robustly solvable if there is a function f : [0,1] → [0,1] such that lim _ ε → 0 f(ε) = 0, and a polynomial time algorithm that takes as input an instance X of CSP ( A ) , and outputs an assignment to the variables of X such that if it is possible to satisfy a 1-ε fraction of the constraints of X , then the assignment found by the algorithm satisfies at least a 1-f(ε) fraction of the constraints of X .

Then for every fixed ε > 0 , it is NP-hard to solve the following problem: given an instance X of CSP ( A ) such that there exists an assignment satisfying at least a 1-ε fraction of the constraints, find an assignment which satisfies at least a frac 1 | A | + ε fraction of the constraints.

statement_text: Consider the following instance of 2-SAT: we have three variables x,y,z , and each pair of variables has a ≠ constraint imposed between them. This instance has no perfect solution, but the standard linear programming relaxation is incapable of noticing this. Let's see how the semidefinite relaxation does. The matrix M_p has six rows and six columns, corresponding to the pairs (x,0),(x,1),(y,0) , (y,1),(z,0),(z,1) , in that order. If M_p comes from a probability distribution over perfect solutions to this instance of 2-SAT, then it must have the following shape: M_p = * & 0 0 & * & vline & 0 & * * & 0 & vline & 0 & * * & 0 hline 0 & * * & 0 & vline & * & 0 0 & * & vline & 0 & * * & 0 hline 0 & * * & 0 & vline & 0 & * * & 0 & vline & * & 0 0 & * . Additionally, the entries in each block of M_p must sum to 1 (and be ≥ 0 ), and for each fixed row or column of M_p , the sum of the entries in the intersection of the row/column with any block must only depend on the row/column. Putting these linear constraints together, we quickly see that every nonzero entry of M_p must actually be equal to (1)/(2) . So far, this is exactly what the linear programming relaxation will guess. The matrix M_p found above, with all nonzero entries equal to (1)/(2) , is not positive semidefinite. To see this, note that we have 1 & -1 & vline & 1 & -1 & vline & 1 & -1 tfrac 1 2 & 0 0 & tfrac 1 2 & vline & 0 & tfrac 1 2 tfrac 1 2 & 0 & vline & 0 & tfrac 1 2 tfrac 1 2 & 0 hline 0 & tfrac 1 2 tfrac 1 2 & 0 & vline & tfrac 1 2 & 0 0 & tfrac 1 2 & vline & 0 & tfrac 1 2 tfrac 1 2 & 0 hline 0 & tfrac 1 2 tfrac 1 2 & 0 & vline & 0 & tfrac 1 2 tfrac 1 2 & 0 & vline & tfrac 1 2 & 0 0 & tfrac 1 2 1 -1 hline 1 -1 hline 1 -1 = -3 < 0. So the semidefinite relaxation of the problem can detect that we can't perfectly solve this instance of 2-SAT. Now suppose that we give up on finding a perfect solution, and instead look for an approximate solution. This means that some of the entries of M_p which were required to be 0 before are instead required to be small . One choice of M_p that works is M_p = (1)/(8) 4 & 0 0 & 4 & vline & 1 & 3 3 & 1 & vline & 1 & 3 3 & 1 hline 1 & 3 3 & 1 & vline & 4 & 0 0 & 4 & vline & 1 & 3 3 & 1 hline 1 & 3 3 & 1 & vline & 1 & 3 3 & 1 & vline & 4 & 0 0 & 4 , which the reader may verify is positive semidefinite. This seems to satisfy each particular constraint with a probability of (3)/(4) . So the semidefinite relaxation thinks it might be possible to satisfy a (3)/(4) fraction of the constraints. An easy brute force search reveals that the best we can do in reality is to satisfy a (2)/(3) fraction of the constraints.

statement_text: Given an instance X of a CSP, with variable domains A _v and constraints C imposing relations R _C ≤ Π _ i ≤ m_C A _ v_ C,i on the variables v_ C,1 , ..., v_ C,m , the basic semidefinite relaxation of X is the following optimization problem. We wish to find a system of ``probabilities'' p_ C,r for r ∈ Π _ i ≤ m_C A _ v_ C,i , such that Σ _ r p_ C,r = 1 for each constraint C and p_ C,r ≥ 0 for each C,r , and to find vectors x_a ∈ R ^N for each variable x and value a ∈ A _x , where N = Σ _x | A _x| is the number of pairs (x,a) , such that for each C and each pair of variables x = v_ C,i , y = v_ C,j involved in the constraint C , we satisfy the compatibility condition x_a · y_b = Σ _ r_i = a, r_j = b p_ C,r . For each pair of variables x,y of X which occur together in some constraint C , any solution to the basic semidefinite relaxation will automatically have the following properties: For all a ≠ b ∈ A _x , we have x_a · x_b = 0 . We have Σ _ a ∈ A _x |x_a|^2 = | Σ _ a ∈ A _x x_a|^2 = 1 . For all a ∈ A _x, b ∈ A _y , we have x_a · y_b ≥ 0 . We have Σ _ a ∈ A _x, b ∈ A _y x_a · y_b = 1 . Our goal is to find such a system of probabilities p_ C,r and vectors x_a such that the quantity tfrac 1 \#C Σ _C Σ _ r ∈ R _C p_ C,r is maximized. The maximum possible value of that sum is called the value of the semidefinite relaxation. If the value of the semidefinite relaxation is equal to 1 , then we say that the system of probabilities p_ C,r and vectors x_a perfectly solves the semidefinite relaxation.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: cor-diagram-reversible
statement_text: If an instance X is diagrammatic and reversible, then for each variable domain A _x we can find a total quasiorder preceq _x on P ( A _x) with the following properties: for any B ⊂ C ⊆ A _x , we have the strict inequality B prec _x C , and for any constraint of X corresponding to a homomorphism π : A _x twoheadrightarrow A _y , and for any B, C ⊆ A _y we have B preceq _y C ⟺ π^ -1 (B) preceq _x π^ -1 (C).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A strictly monotone preference on a set A is defined to be a total quasiorder preceq on P (A) such that B ⊂ C ⊆ A ⇒ B prec C. Note the strict inequalities!

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If F is a functor from finite sets to sets, and if V is a variety, then a rounding rule for F on V is defined to be a family of maps r_S : F(S) → F _ V (S) such that for every map π : S → T and every x ∈ F(S) we have F _ V (π)(r_S(x)) = r_T(F(π)(x)), where F _ V (π) : F _ V (S) → F _ V (T) is the corresponding map of free algebras. In other words, r is a natural transformation (also known as a minion homomorphism ) from F to F _ V .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: The vague minion is defined to be the functor W which takes a finite set A to W (A) = {(S, preceq ) | S ∈ P _ ∅ (A) and preceq is a vague element of S which extends the inclusion order ⊆ }, and which takes a map π : A → B to W (π) : (S, preceq ) mapsto (π(S), preceq ^π), where preceq ^π is the vague element of π(S) defined by U preceq ^π V ⟺ π^ -1 (U) preceq π^ -1 (V) for U, V ⊆ π(S) . (See Definition for the definition of vague elements.)

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: thm-vague-minion
statement_text: If V is a locally finite bounded width variety, then there is a rounding rule for the vague minion W on V , that is, there is a minion homomorphism r^ W : W → F _ V .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: The reversible minion is defined to be the functor M which takes a finite set A to M (A) = {(S, preceq ) | S ∈ P _ ∅ (A) and preceq is a strictly monotone preference on S}, and which takes a map π : A → B to M (π) : (S, preceq ) mapsto (π(S), preceq ^π), where preceq ^π is the strictly monotone preference on π(S) defined by U preceq ^π V ⟺ π^ -1 (U) preceq π^ -1 (V) for U, V ⊆ π(S) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: thm-reversible-minion
statement_text: If V is a locally finite variety which has symmetric term operations of every arity, then there is a rounding rule for the reversible minion M on V , that is, there is a minion homomorphism r^ M : M → F _ V .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If V is a locally finite variety such that CSP ( V ) is solved by the basic linear programming relaxation, then every reversible instance of CSP ( V ) has a solution.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that Γ is a finite constraint language such that CSP (Γ) is solved by the basic linear programming relaxation. If we are given an instance X of CSP (Γ) such that the basic linear programing relaxation of X is 1 - ε satisfiable, then we can efficiently find a solution which satisfies a 1 - O ((1)/( log (1/ε)) ) fraction of the constraints of X .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: cor-lp-decidable
statement_text: If A is a finite relational structure, then CSP ( A ) is solved by the basic linear programming relaxation iff there is a homomorphism M ( A ) → A . In particular, if A has a finite relational signature, then we can decide whether CSP ( A ) is solved by the basic linear programming relaxation in a finite amount of time.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prob-lp-algebraic
statement_text: Given a finite algebraic structure A as input, can we decide whether or not A has symmetric term operations of all arities?

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Call an operation k -symmetric if it is symmetric on all tuples where at most k distinct values show up.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If a locally finite variety V has bounded width and has a binary symmetric term operation s_2(x,y) , then V has 2 -symmetric term operations of every arity.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: lem-three-orders
statement_text: For any set S , we can find three total orderings preceq _0, preceq _1, preceq _2 on P (S) , such that for every partition of S into three disjoint nonempty sets U, V, W with W prec _0 V prec _0 U, the restrictions of preceq _1, preceq _2 to {U,V,W} are given by U &prec _1 W prec _1 V, V &prec _2 U prec _2 W. In particular, the three restrictions preceq _i|_ {U,V,W} together with their three reversals succeq _i|_ {U,V,W} make up all six total orderings of the set {U,V,W} , each occuring once.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: thm-3-symmetric
statement_text: If a locally finite variety V has bounded width and has a binary symmetric term operation s_2(x,y) and a ternary cyclic term operation c_3(x,y,z) , then V has 3 -symmetric term operations of every arity.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Lemma 4 of
statement_text: If s_2(x,y) is a binary symmetric operation and c_3(x,y,z) is a ternary cyclic operation, then s_3(x,y,z) coloneqq s_2(c_3(x,y,z),c_3(z,y,x)) is a ternary symmetric operation, and if we define 4 -ary operations t, s_4 by t(x,y,z,w) &coloneqq s_2(s_2(x,y), s_2(z,w)), s_4(x,y,z,w) &coloneqq s_3(t(x,y,z,w), t(x,z,w,y), t(x,w,y,z)), then s_4 is a 4 -ary symmetric operation.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If a locally finite variety V has bounded width and has a binary symmetric term operation s_2(x,y) and a ternary cyclic term operation c_3(x,y,z) , then V has a 4 -symmetric term operation of arity 5 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: An m -ary operation c is called cyclic if it satisfies the identity c(x_1, x_2, ..., x_m) ≈ c(x_2, ..., x_m, x_1).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Multiplicative property of cyclic terms
statement_text: A variety V has a cyclic term c_ mn of arity mn if and only if V has cyclic terms c_m, c_n of arity m and n , respectively.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A variety V has a cyclic term operation of arity m if and only if V has a cyclic term operation of arity p for every prime p which divides m .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Semantic meaning of cyclic terms
statement_text: Suppose that V is a variety. Then for any m ∈ N , the following are equivalent. V has no cyclic term operation of arity m . There is some A ∈ V and an automorphism σ ∈ Aut ( A ) such that σ^m = 1 and σ has no fixed point.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: cyclic-local-crit
title: Local criterion for cyclic terms
statement_text: If A is a finite algebra, then A has an m -ary cyclic term if and only if it is the case that for all a_1, ..., a_m ∈ A , there exists some m -ary term t such that t(a_1, a_2, ..., a_m) = t(a_2, ..., a_m, a_1) = ... = t(a_m, a_1, ..., a_ m-1 ).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A relation R ≤ A ^m is called cyclic if R is invariant under cyclically permuting its coordinates, that is, (a_1, a_2, ..., a_m) ∈ R ⟺ (a_2, ..., a_m, a_1) ∈ R .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Relational criterion for cyclic terms
statement_text: If A is a finite algebra, then A has a cyclic term operation of arity m if and only if every m -ary cyclic relation R ≤ A ^m contains a constant tuple.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: cyclic-terms
title: Finite Taylor algebras have cyclic terms , refined by Zhuk
statement_text: Suppose A is a finite idempotent Taylor algebra and that p is prime. Then one of the following is true: either A has a cyclic term operation of arity p , or there is some B ∈ HS( A ) and some automorphism σ ∈ Aut ( B ) such that σ^p = 1 and σ has no fixed points. In particular, if p > | A | then A has a cyclic term operation of arity p .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a finite Taylor algebra and m has no prime factors p which are less than or equal to | A | , then A has an idempotent m -ary cyclic term.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Let A _n be the dual discriminator algebra from Example on a domain of size n . Then every subset of A _n is a subalgebra with full automorphism group, so A _n does not have cyclic terms of any arity between 2 and n . By the previous results, we see that A _n has a cyclic term operation of arity m if and only if m has no prime factors which are less than or equal to n .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Siggers term from cyclic term
statement_text: If A is a finite Taylor algebra, then A has an idempotent 4 -ary Siggers term t , satisfying the identity t(x,x,y,z) ≈ t(y,z,z,x) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: daisy-chain-terms
title: Daisy chain terms
statement_text: If A is a finite Taylor algebra, then there are idempotent terms w_i(x,y,z) for i ∈ Z such that for all i we have w_i(x,x,y) ≈ w_i(y,x,x) ≈ w_ i-1 (x,y,x), and the sequence of terms w_i is periodic with some finite period.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: consecutive-daisy
statement_text: A finite algebra A is Taylor if and only if it has a pair of idempotent ternary terms p,q satisfying the identities p(x,x,y) & ≈ p(y,x,x), q(x,x,y) & ≈ q(y,x,x) ≈ p(x,y,x).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A clone O on a finite domain is called a minimal Taylor clone if O is Taylor and every proper subclone of O is not Taylor. A finite algebra A is called a minimal Taylor algebra if Clo ( A ) is a minimal Taylor clone.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Every Taylor clone on a finite domain contains a minimal Taylor clone.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: The number of minimal Taylor clones on a domain of size n is at most n^ 2n^3 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: minimal-taylor-subalg
statement_text: If A is a minimal Taylor algebra and B ∈ HSP_ fin ( A ) , then B is also a minimal Taylor algebra. In fact, if S ⊆ B is a subset of B (not assumed to be a subalgebra), t ∈ Clo ( A ) is any term operation of A , and θ is an equivalence relation on S such that the set S is closed under t , every equivalence class of θ is a subalgebra of B , the equivalence relation θ is a congruence of the algebraic structure (S,t) , and the quotient (S,t)/θ is a Taylor algebra, then in fact the following must all be true: the set S is actually the underlying set of a subalgebra S of B (i.e. S is a subuniverse of B ), the equivalence relation θ is actually a congruence on the subalgebra S , and the restriction of every term operation of A to the quotient S /θ is in the clone generated by the restriction of t to (S,t)/θ . Note that taking θ to be the trivial equivalence relation 0_S is always allowed, since every minimal Taylor algebra is automatically idempotent.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-minimal-prepared
statement_text: If A is a minimal Taylor algebra, then a, b ∈ A have b b ∈ Sg _ A ^2 { a b , b a } if and only if {a,b} is a semilattice subalgebra of A with absorbing element b .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-recognition-with-automorphism
statement_text: If A is a minimal Taylor algebra and a, b ∈ A are such that Sg _ A ^2 { a b , b a } is the graph of an automorphism of order two, then we have a a a ∈ Sg _ A ^3 { a a b , a b a , b a a } iff {a,b} is a majority subalgebra of A , and we have b b b ∈ Sg _ A ^3 { a a b , a b a , b a a } iff {a,b} is a Z /2^ aff subalgebra of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: not-sd-complete
statement_text: If a minimal Taylor algebra A is generated by two elements a,b , then A is not subdirectly simple. As a consequence, either A has an affine quotient or A has a proper ternary absorbing subalgebra.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that a minimal Taylor algebra A is generated by two elements. Is it possible for A to be polynomially complete?

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a minimal Taylor algebra, then a, b ∈ A have a & b a & b a & b ∈ Sg _ A ^ 3 × 2 { a & b a & b b & a , a & b b & a a & b , b & a a & b a & b } if and only if {a,b} is a majority subalgebra of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a minimal Taylor algebra and a,b,c ∈ A satisfy a → c , b → c (i.e. {a,c} and {b,c} are semilattice subalgebras of A with absorbing element c ), then we have c c ∈ Sg _ A ^2 { a b , b a } if and only if {a,b,c} is isomorphic to the free semilattice on two generators.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-minimal-binary-strong
statement_text: Suppose that A is a minimal Taylor algebra, and that B lhd _ bin A is a binary absorbing subalgebra of A . Then the following must hold. B is a strongly absorbing subalgebra of A , that is, any term f ∈ Clo ( A ) which depends on its first input satisfies f( B , A , ..., A ) ⊆ B . There is an equivalence relation θ_ B ∈ Con ( A ) such that B is a congruence class of θ_ B , and all other congruence classes of θ_ B are singletons. For every a ∉ B , B ∪ {a} is a subalgebra of A , and ( B ∪ {a})/θ_ B is a two-element semilattice with absorbing element B /θ_ B . For every a ∉ B , there is some b ∈ B such that {a,b} is a two-element semilattice with absorbing element b . For every a,b ∉ B such that Sg _ A {a,b} ∩ B ≠ ∅ , Sg _ A {a,b}/θ_ B is isomorphic to the free semilattice on two generators. For every a_1, ..., a_k ∉ B such that Sg _ A {a_i,a_j} ∩ B ≠ ∅ for all i ≠ j , Sg _ A {a_1, ..., a_k}/θ_ B is isomorphic to a semilattice of size k+1 . In particular, if A is generated by two elements and B is a proper binary absorbing subalgebra, then A /θ_ B is either a two-element semilattice, or is isomorphic to the free semilattice on two generators.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: We say that a sequence of idempotent ternary terms w_i , defined for all i ∈ Z , is a sequence of daisy chain terms if it satisfies the following properties: the sequence w_i is purely periodic in i with some finite period, and for all i ∈ Z , we have w_i(x,x,y) ≈ w_i(y,x,x) ≈ w_ i-1 (x,y,x) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A = (A, ∨ ) is a semilattice, then any sequence of daisy chain terms of A must have w_i(x,y,z) ≈ x ∨ y ∨ z for all i ∈ Z .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A = (A,m) is a majority algebra, then in any sequence of daisy chain terms of A , each w_i must be a majority term, that is, we have w_i(x,x,y) ≈ w_i(x,y,x) ≈ w_i(y,x,x) ≈ x for all i ∈ Z .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is minimal Taylor and affine, then there is an abelian group structure on the underlying set A such that A is term equivalent to (A,x-y+z) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: affine-daisy
statement_text: If A = (A,x-y+z) is an affine algebra such that the abelian group A has exponent n , then for any sequence of daisy chain terms w_i of A , there is a sequence of elements a_i ∈ Z /n such that w_i(x,y,z) ≈ a_ix + (1-2a_i)y + a_iz and a_ i+1 ≡ 1-2a_i pmod n for all i ∈ Z .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A = (A,x-y+z) is an affine algebra such that |A| is a power of 2 , then any sequence of daisy chain terms of A must have w_i(x,y,z) ≈ (x+y+z)/(3) for all i ∈ Z . In particular, if the abelian group A has exponent 2 , then each w_i is the Mal'cev operation x-y+z ≈ x+y+z .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A = (A,x-y+z) is an affine algebra such that the abelian group A has exponent 3^k , then any sequence of daisy chain terms of A must have period equal to 3^k , and there must be some i ∈ Z such that w_ i-1 (x,y,z) & ≈ (x+z)/(2), w_i(x,y,z) & ≈ y, w_ i+1 (x,y,z) & ≈ x-y+z.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a minimal Taylor algebra, then it is possible to choose a sequence of daisy chain terms w_i of A such that for every affine B ∈ HSP_ fin ( A ) of odd order, the restriction of w_1 to B is the Mal'cev operation x-y+z .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a minimal Taylor algebra and B ∈ HSP( A ) is affine, then the exponent n of B is finite, with n ≤ | A |^ | A |^2 , and every prime p which divides n is bounded by | A | .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A , B are minimal Taylor algebras, then there are minimal Taylor algebras A ', B ' such that A is term equivalent to A ' and B is term equivalent to B ' , A ' and B ' have the same signature, and A ' × B ' is minimal Taylor.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: thm-minimal-central
statement_text: Suppose that A is minimal Taylor, and that there is a majority algebra M on the domain {0,1} (with the same signature as A ) such that A × M is minimal Taylor. For any C ≤ A , the following are equivalent: C is a ternary absorbing subalgebra of A , for every prime p > | A | there is a p -ary cyclic term c of A × M such that whenever \#{i | x_i ∈ C } > (p)/(2) , we have c(x_1, ..., x_p) ∈ C , and furthermore the restriction of c to M is the p -ary majority operation, the binary relation R ⊆ A × M given by R = ( A × {0}) ∪ ( C × {0,1}) is a subalgebra of A × M , C centrally absorbs A , every daisy chain term w_i(x,y,z) witnesses the fact that C ternary absorbs A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: cor-minimal-central-majority
statement_text: Suppose that A is minimal Taylor and that C , D lhd _Z A are two ternary absorbing subalgebras of A . Then C ∪ D is a subalgebra of A . If C ∩ D = ∅ , then the equivalence relation θ on C ∪ D with parts C and D is a congruence on C ∪ D , and ( C ∪ D )/θ is isomorphic to the two element majority algebra.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a minimal Taylor algebra which is generated by two elements a,b ∈ A , then at least one of the following is true: there is a congruence θ ∈ Con ( A ) such that A /θ is an affine algebra of prime order, there is a congruence θ ∈ Con ( A ) such that A /θ is a two element semilattice, there is a congruence θ ∈ Con ( A ) such that A /θ is a two element majority algebra, or there are proper ternary absorbing subalgebras C , D lhd _Z A such that a ∈ C , b ∈ D , C ∪ D = A , and C ∩ D ≠ ∅ .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Is there any minimal Taylor algebra which is simple, is generated by two elements, has size at least 3 , and is not affine?

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose A is a finite idempotent algebra, and a, b are any pair of distinct elements of A . We say that (a,b) is a semilattice edge if there is a binary term t such that t(a,b) = t(b,a) = b . We say that {a,b} is a weak majority edge if there is a congruence θ on Sg {a,b} and a ternary term m such that {a/θ,b/θ} is closed under m and ({a/θ,b/θ},m) is a two-element majority algebra. We say that {a,b} is a weak affine edge if there is a congruence θ on Sg {a,b} and a term p such that ( Sg {a,b}/θ, p) is an affine algebra. We drop the modifier ``weak'' on an edge if θ is a maximal congruence on Sg {a,b} , and for any a', b' ∈ Sg {a,b} such that a' ≡ _θ a and b' ≡ _θ b , we have Sg {a,b} = Sg {a',b'} . Note that semilattice edges are directed, while majority and affine edges are undirected.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-weak-semilattice-edge
statement_text: If there is a congruence θ on Sg {a,b} and an idempotent binary term t such that t(a,b) ≡ _θ t(b,a) ≡ _θ b , then there is some b' ∈ Sg {a,b} such that b' ≡ _θ b and a partial semilattice term s ∈ Clo (t) such that s(a,b') = s(b',a) = b' .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: We say that a finite idempotent algebra A has a hereditarily connected colored graph if for all B ≤ A , the colored graph of B is connected (ignoring the directions on the semilattice edges).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Let A be a finite idempotent algebra. If the colored graph of weak edges of A is hereditarily connected, then the colored graph of edges of A is also hereditarily connected.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: hereditarily-connected-product
statement_text: If A , B are finite idempotent algebras (of the same signature) with hereditarily connected colored graphs, then so is A × B . More generally, if A is a finite idempotent algebra and θ ∈ Con ( A ) is such that A /θ is hereditarily connected and every congruence class of θ is also hereditarily connected, then A is hereditarily connected.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a finite idempotent algebra with a hereditarily connected colored graph and θ ∈ Con ( A ) , then A /θ also has a hereditarily connected colored graph.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a finite idempotent algebra with a hereditarily connected colored graph, then A is Taylor.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: colored-graph
title: Bulatov ,
statement_text: A finite idempotent algebra A is Taylor if and only if it has a hereditarily connected colored graph.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is any algebra, we define the hypergraph of proper subalgebras of A to be the hypergraph with vertex set equal to the underlying set of A , and with a hyperedge B for every proper subalgebra B ≤ A . We say that A is disconnected if the hypergraph of proper subalgebras of A is not connected. We define the connected component equivalence relation _ A (or just if A is clear from context) on A by a _ A b if a is connected to b by a sequence of proper subalgebras of A (note that in general, _ A will not be a congruence).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a disconnected algebra, then for any a not _ A b we have Sg {a,b} = A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: colored-claim-0
statement_text: Suppose that A is finite, idempotent, simple, and disconnected. For any binary relation R ≤ A × A with π_2( R ) = A , either R is the graph of an automorphism of A or there is some a ∈ A such that {a} × A ⊆ R .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: colored-claim-1
statement_text: Suppose that A is finite, idempotent, simple, and disconnected, and that a not _ A b are such that neither (a,b) nor (b,a) are semilattice edges. Then the binary relation S _ ab coloneqq Sg _ A ^2 { a b , b a } is the graph of an automorphism of order two which interchanges a and b .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Define the equivalence relation ^s_ A by a ^s_ A b if a can be connected to b by a chain of proper subalgebras and semilattice edges.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: colored-claim-1-cor
statement_text: If A is finite, idempotent, and simple, and if ^s_ A is not the full equivalence relation A × A , then Aut ( A ) acts transitively on A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: colored-claim-2
statement_text: Suppose that A is finite, idempotent, and simple. For any a not ^s_ A b , if the ternary relation R _ ab coloneqq Sg _ A ^3 { b a a , a b a , a a b } contains (a,a,a) or (b,a,b) , then {a,b} is a majority edge.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a finite idempotent algebra and C lhd _Z A is a centrally absorbing subalgebra with ternary absorbing operation t , then for any a ∈ A \ C , there exists some c ∈ C such that either (a,c) is a semilattice edge, or such that Sg {a,c} has an automorphism of order two which interchanges a and c .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A k -ary operation f : A^k → A is conservative if for all a_1, ..., a_k ∈ A we have f(a_1, ..., a_k) ∈ {a_1, ..., a_k}. An algebraic structure A is called conservative if every basic operation of A is conservative.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: An algebraic structure A is conservative if and only if every subset S ⊆ A is actually a subalgebra of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A relational clone Γ on a domain A is called conservative if every unary relation U ⊆ A is an element of Γ , i.e. P (A) ⊆ Γ . A relational structure A is called conservative if every unary relation U can be primitively positively defined using the basic relations of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If a relational structure A and an algebraic structure A are related by the Inv - Pol Galois correspondence, then A is conservative if and only if A is conservative.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A relational structure A with finite underlying set A is conservative if and only if, for every a ∈ A , the unary relation A \ {a} is primitively positively definable from the basic relations of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A natural example of a conservative CSP template (on an infinite domain) is the list-coloring problem for graphs: the domain A is an infinite set, and the relations consist of the binary ≠ relation and the collection of all possible subsets U ⊆ A as unary relations.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A conservative 2 -semilattice is called a tournament . The rock-paper-scissors algebra is probably the most famous example of a tournament which is not totally ordered.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If an affine CSP is conservative, then the domain must have size two: the only conservative affine algebra is Z /2^ aff , up to term equivalence.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: We say that a relational clone Γ is k - conservative if every unary relation U ⊆ A with size |U| ≤ k is an element of Γ , and we define k -conservative clones, algebras, and relational structures similarly.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: An algebra is idempotent iff it is 1 -conservative.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: The k - list-coloring problem for graphs corresponds to the relational structure with infinite domain A , and relations consisting of the binary ≠ relation and the collection of all possible subsets U ⊆ A with |U| ≤ k . This problem is equivalent to 2-SAT for k = 2 , and is NP-hard for k ≥ 3 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: The only 2 -conservative affine algebras are ( Z /2^ aff )^k , up to term equivalence and isomorphism.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Every reduct of a conservative algebra is also conservative. In particular, every conservative Taylor clone contains a minimal Taylor clone which is also conservative.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: 3-conservative
statement_text: A minimal Taylor algebra is conservative if and only if it is 3 -conservative.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: conservative-ternary
statement_text: If A is a 2 -conservative minimal Taylor algebra and w_i is any daisy chain term for A , then we have w_i(x,x,y) ≈ w_i(x,y,x) ≈ w_i(y,x,x), so in fact every w_i is a ternary weak near-unanimity operation. The binary function f(x,y) coloneqq w_i(x,x,y) is independent of i , and completely determines the colored graph of A . In addition, the binary function s(x,y) coloneqq f(x,f(y,x)) is a partial semilattice term operation of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-conservative-free
statement_text: The free algebra F _ V (x,y) on two generators in the variety V generated by conservative minimal Taylor algebras has size 6 : its elements are x, y, f(x,y), f(y,x), s(x,y), s(y,x) (defined as in the previous proposition). The colored graph of the algebra F _ V (x,y) is as follows. Here the semilattice edges are directed, the majority edges are straight and undirected, and the Z /2^ aff edges are drawn as zigzags. This algebra has {f(x,y), f(y,x), s(x,y), s(y,x)} as a binary absorbing subalgebra, corresponding to a semilattice quotient, and has {x,f(x,y),s(x,y)} and {y,f(y,x),s(y,x)} as ternary absorbing subalgebras, corresponding to a majority quotient.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: ternary-iteration
statement_text: If w is a ternary weak near-unanimity term operation of a finite algebra A , then there is a ternary weak near-unanimity term g ∈ Clo (w) which also satisfies the identity g(g(x,y,z),g(y,z,x),g(z,x,y)) ≈ g(x,y,z). If | A | = 3 and A has no ternary cyclic term, then any such g satisfies g(x,y,z) = x whenever x,y,z are all different.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: thm-minimal-no-cyclic
statement_text: If a minimal Taylor algebra has size 3 and has no ternary cyclic term, then (after renaming elements) it is term equivalent to one of the following four algebras: the affine algebra Z /3^ aff , the rock-paper-scissors algebra A _ rps from Section , the three element dual discriminator algebra from Example , or the three element simple nonabelian Mal'cev algebra from Example . All but the first are conservative, all but the second have a full automorphism group, and the first two have binary cyclic terms.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that a minimal Taylor algebra A has the following properties: A is 2 -conservative, that is, for all a,b ∈ A the subset {a,b} is a subalgebra of A , the colored graph of A does not contain any majority triangles, and the colored graph of A does not contain any affine triangles. Then A is conservative, and Clo ( A ) is determined by the colored graph of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a three element minimal Taylor algebra with underlying set {a,b,c} , then we will say that an element x of A is circled if (x,x) ∈ Sg {(a,b),(b,c),(c,a)} . Note that the set of circled elements of A does not depend on the ordering of a,b,c .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that A is a conservative three element minimal Taylor algebra with a ternary cyclic term g , such that either all three of the edges of A are majority or all three are affine. Then (after renaming elements) A is term equivalent to one of the following three algebras: the three element solvable nonabelian Mal'cev algebra from Example , with * as the unique circled element, the three element median algebra {0,1,2} , with the median element 1 as the unique circled element, or the three element minimal majority algebra ({a,b,c}, m) , with m a cyclic majority operation such that m(a,b,c) = b and m(a,c,b) = c , with {b,c} as the set of circled elements. In particular, every conservative three element minimal Taylor algebra is determined up to term equivalence by its colored graph and set of circled elements. Furthermore, in any conservative minimal Taylor algebra, we can choose a ternary operation g as in Theorem such that if we take g as the basic operation, then every three element majority subalgebra with two circled elements is isomorphic to the third algebra listed above (not just term-equivalent).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: The number of conservative minimal Taylor clones on a set of size n is exactly Σ _ 3 -edge-colorings of K_n 2^ \#( color red semilattice ) 4^ Δ( color blue affine ) 7^ Δ( color orange majority ) = (1+o(1)) · 7^ binom n 3 , where Δ(c) is the number of monochromatic triangles of color c . In particular, for large n almost all conservative minimal Taylor clones are clones of majority algebras.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a minimal Taylor algebra of size 3 other than Z /3^ aff , then the graph on A with edges given by the two-element subalgebras of A is connected - in other words, A has at least two subalgebras of size two.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a minimal Taylor algebra with underlying set {a,b,c} such that A is generated by a and b , then A does not have a semilattice subalgebra of the form c → a .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a minimal Taylor algebra with underlying set {a,b,c} such that A is generated by a and b , and if A has a semilattice subalgebra of the form a → c , then A is isomorphic to a subdirect product of its two-element subalgebras {a,c} and {b,c} .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that A is a minimal Taylor algebra with underlying set {a,b,c} which is generated by a and b , such that some automorphism iota of A swaps a and b . Then A is either Z /3^ aff or the free semilattice on two generators.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a minimal Taylor algebra with underlying set {a,b,c} which is generated by a and b , then at least one of {a,c}, {b,c} is not a Z /2^ aff -subalgebra of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a minimal Taylor algebra with underlying set {a,b,c} which is generated by a and b , then at least one of {a,c}, {b,c} is not a majority subalgebra of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that A is a minimal Taylor algebra with underlying set {a,b,c} which is generated by a and b , that {a,c} is a Z /2^ aff -subalgebra, and that {b,c} is a majority subalgebra of A . Then A is the same as the algebra described in Example , up to isomorphism and term equivalence. In particular, {a,c} is a centrally absorbing subalgebra of A , and A has a congruence θ corresponding to the partition {a},{b,c} such that A /θ cong {a,c} is Z /2^ aff .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a minimal Taylor algebra on a set of size 3 , then up to term equivalence and isomorphism A is one of the following 24 algebras: one of the 19 conservative minimal Taylor algebras classified in the previous section, the affine algebra Z /3^ aff = ( Z /3, x-y+z) , the free semilattice on two generators, the three-element subdirect product of ({0,1},x ∨ y ∨ z) with ({0,1}, maj (x,y,z)) , the three-element subdirect product of ({0,1},x ∨ y ∨ x) with Z /2^ aff = ( Z /2, x+y+z) , the three-element algebra from Example , which has a 3 -edge term, a two-element centrally absorbing subalgebra, and a Z /2^ aff quotient.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: For each one of the 24 minimal Taylor algebras on a set of size 3 , find a generating set of relations for the corresponding relational clone. Are they all finitely related?

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Let X be an instance of a CSP, with variable domains A _x for each variable x . We say that X is unlinked at a variable x of X if there are some a,b ∈ A _x such that there are no cycles p of X from x to x with b ∈ {a} + p . We say that X is unlinked if it is unlinked at every variable. If an instance X is unlinked at a variable x , then we define the linking relation θ_ X of X at x as the equivalence relation on A _x defined by (a,b) ∈ θ_ X iff there is some cycle p from x to x such that b ∈ {a} + p .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If X is cycle-consistent and unlinked at x , then the linking relation θ_ X is a congruence of A _x .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that we have a multisorted CSP template CSP ( A _1, ..., A _n) such that the CSP template CSP ( B _1, ..., B _m) can be solved in polynomial time, where B _1, ..., B _m is the collection of all algebras B which are isomorphic to a proper subalgebra of some A _i (note that max | B _i| < max | A _j| ). Then we can solve any unlinked instance X of CSP ( A _1, ..., A _n) in polynomial time.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If X is an instance of a multisorted CSP with variable domains A _x , then we define the implication digraph to be the directed graph on X where the vertices are pairs (x, B ) such that x is a variable and B ≤ A _x , and where we have a directed edge from (x, B ) to (y, C ) if there is a path p of length 1 from x to y in X such that B + p = C . We write (x, B ) preceq (y, C ) if there is a path p of any length from x to y such that B + p = C . The resulting quasiorder is the implication qoset . Let E be a subdigraph of the implication digraph, and consider E as a subqoset of the implication qoset by taking its transitive closure. A strand of E is just an equivalence class of E . Often we might take E to be the subdigraph of pairs (x, B ) such that B is a proper subalgebra of A _x (or a proper absorbing subalgebra, etc.). We say that S is a maximal strand of E if it is a maximal equivalence class of the qoset E . If E is not specified, then a strand can be any strongly connected subset of the implication digraph. A strand is called absorbing if for all (x, B ) ∈ S we have B lhd A _x . Note that as long as X is arc-consistent, if this occurs for some (x, B ) ∈ S then it occurs for all (x, B ) ∈ S . We define the partial restriction of X to the strand S by reducing the domain of each variable x to cap_ (x, B ) ∈ S B if some (x, B ) ∈ S , and leaving the domain of x unchanged otherwise.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-cycle-strand-finding
statement_text: If X is cycle-consistent, E is a subdigraph of the implication digraph, and we are given some (x, B ) ∈ E , then we can find a maximal strand of E in polynomial time.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If X is an arc-consistent instance, then each strand S of X includes at most one pair (x, B ) for each variable x as long as X satisfies property (P3) from Definiion : B + p + q = B ⇒ B + p = B for all pairs of cycles p,q from x to x and all B ≤ A _x . In particular, this always occurs if X is pq -consistent.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: defn-full-restriction
statement_text: Suppose that X is an instance, and let S be any strand of X such that for each variable x , there is at most one B _x such that (x, B _x) ∈ S . We define the full restriction of X to S to be the instance X ' whose variable set is the set of variables x such that some (x, B _x) ∈ S , with each variable domain reduced to B _x , where for each relation of X we project it onto the set of variables in X ' and restrict each of its coordinates to B _x .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If X is an arc-consistent instance, then for each strand S , each (x, B ) , and each a ∉ B , there is a strand S ' , involving the same set of variables as S , such that (x, B ') ∈ S ' for some B ' ≤ A _x with a ∈ B ' and B ∩ B ' = ∅ , as long as X also satisfies property (P2) from Definition : B + p = B ⇒ B - p = B for all cycles p from x to x and all B ≤ A _x . In this case, a more precise statement is true: for each (x, B ) ∈ S there is a congruence θ_ S on A _x such that B is a union of congruence classes of θ_ S , and each congruence class B ' of θ_ S is contained in a parallel strand S ' .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: An arc-consistent instance X is called a Prague instance if for every (x, B ), (y, C ) in the same equivalence class of the implication qoset, and for every path p of length 1 from x to y , we have B + p = C .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If X is a Prague instance, then X satisfies conditions (P2) and (P3) of Definition , so X is a weak Prague instance.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-prague
title: Barto and Kozik ,
statement_text: If X is arc-consistent, then the following are equivalent: for every (x, B ), (y, C ) in the same equivalence class of the implication qoset, and for every path p of length 1 from x to y , we have B + p ⊆ C . X is a Prague instance, for every variable x and every pair of paths p,q from x to x such that the variables involved in p are a subset of the variables involved in q , if b ∈ {a} + p then there is some j ≥ 0 such that b ∈ {a} + jq , for every variable x and every pair of paths p,q from x to x such that the variables involved in p are a subset of the variables involved in q , then for every sufficiently large j we have {a} + p ⊆ {a} + jq .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-prague-reduction
statement_text: If X is a Prague instance, and if S is a strand of X , then the full restriction of X to S (which restricts both the set of variables and the domains) will be arc-consistent - in fact, it will also be a Prague instance. If S is also a maximal strand in the qoset of pairs (x, B ) such that B < A _x , then the partial restriction of X to S (which restricts the domains but not the set of variables) is also arc-consistent. If S is additionally absorbing, then the partial restriction of X to S will even be a Prague instance.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: An instance X is (l,k) - minimal , for k ≥ l , if every set of at most k variables of X is in the scope of some constraint, and for any set S of at most l variables and any pair of constraints C_1, C_2 of X whose scopes contain S , the existential projections of C_1 and C_2 to the variables in S are the same.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If X is (2,3) -minimal, then X is a Prague instance, and X is cycle-consistent.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: defn-relation-strand
statement_text: If R ≤ _ sd A _1 × ... × A _n , and if B _i ≤ A _i for all i , then an ( R , B ) - strand is an equivalence class of the quasiorder preceq on [n] which is the transitive closure of B _i + π_ ij ( R ) = B _j ⇒ i preceq j.
