The equivalence classes of this quasiorder are the same as the equivalence classes of the more permissive quasiorder i preceq ' j ⟺ B _i + π_ ij ( R ) ⊆ B _j, and these quasiorders are the same in the special case where B _i is a minimal absorbing subalgebra of A _i for each i .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-relation-strand
statement_text: If R ≤ _ sd A _1 × ... × A _n , and if B _i ≤ A _i for all i , then for each ( R , B ) -strand S ⊆ [n] there is a congruence θ_i ∈ Con ( A _i) for each i ∈ S such that each B _i is a union of congruence classes of θ_i , and for any i,j ∈ S , the binary relation π_ ij ( R )/(θ_i × θ_j) ≤ _ sd A _i/θ_i × A _j/θ_j is the graph of an isomorphism.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: thm-rectangularity-conservative-absorbing
title: Rectangularity Theorem for conservative Taylor algebras, absorbing version
statement_text: If R ≤ _ sd A _1 × ... × A _n is a subdirect product of conservative Taylor algebras A _i , and if a system of minimal absorbing subalgebras B _i mathrlap < lhd A _i for each i satisfies R ∩ ( B _1 × ... × B _n) ≠ ∅ , then R ∩ ( B _1 × ... × B _n) = Π _ S an ( R , B ) -strand (π_S( R ) ∩ Π _ i ∈ S B _i ).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a subdirect product of conservative minimal Taylor algebras, then we define a quasiorder on the elements of A by a preceq _ as b if there is a sequence a = a_0, a_1, ..., a_n = b such that for each i either {a_i,a_ i+1 } is a Z /2^ aff -subalgebra or a_i → a_ i+1 . We say that a subset B ⊆ A is an as-component of A if B is a maximal equivalence class of the quasiorder preceq _ as . We say that A is strongly as-connected if A consists of a single equivalence class of the quasiorder preceq _ as .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: thm-rectangularity-conservative-as
title: Rectangularity Theorem for conservative Taylor algebras, as-component version
statement_text: If R ≤ _ sd A _1 × ... × A _n is a subdirect product of conservative minimal Taylor algebras A _i , and if a system of as-components B _i ⊆ A _i for each i satisfies R ∩ ( B _1 × ... × B _n) ≠ ∅ , then R ∩ ( B _1 × ... × B _n) = Π _ S an ( R , B ) -strand (π_S( R ) ∩ Π _ i ∈ S B _i ).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-absorption-free-linking
statement_text: Let R ≤ _ sd A _1 × A _2 be a subdirect product of absorption-free idempotent algebras, and let θ_1 be a maximal congruence on A _1 . Then either θ_1 contains the linking congruence of R on A _1 , in which case there is a maximal congruence θ_2 on A _2 such that R /(θ_1 × θ_2) ≤ A _1/θ_1 × A _2/θ_2 is the graph of an isomorphism from A _1/θ_1 xrightarrow A _2/θ_2 , or else we have (a/θ_1) + R = A _2 for each congruence class a/θ_1 of θ_1 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: lem-conservative-subalgebra-absorption-free
title: Barto
statement_text: If A is an absorption-free conservative algebra, θ is a proper congruence on A , and B ≤ A is any subalgebra such that B has at least one element from each congruence class of θ , then B is also absorption-free.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: thm-conservative-subdirect-absorption-free
title: Barto
statement_text: If R ≤ _ sd A _1 × ... × A _n is a subdirect product of absorption-free conservative algebras, then R is also absorption-free.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Barto
statement_text: Suppose R ≤ _ sd A _1 × A _2 , where A _1 is conservative, A _2 is idempotent, and both are finite Taylor algebras. Suppose further that B _i mathrlap < lhd _X A _i for i=1,2 , that R ∩ ( B _1 × B _2) ≠ ∅ , and that there is some (a,b) ∈ R with a ∈ A _1 \ B _1 and b ∈ B _2 . Then B _1 × B _2 ⊆ R .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Barto
statement_text: Suppose R ≤ _ sd A _1 × ... × A _n × A _ n+1 , where A _1, ..., A _n are conservative, A _ n+1 is idempotent, and each A _i is a finite Taylor algebra. Suppose that we have B _i mathrlap < lhd _X A _i for all i ∈ [n+1] , that R ∩ ( B _1 × ... × B _n × B _ n+1 ) ≠ ∅ , that [n] is an ( R , B ) -strand, and that there is some (a_1, ..., a_n, b_ n+1 ) ∈ R such that a_i ∈ A _i \ B _i for i ∈ [n] while b_ n+1 ∈ B _ n+1 . Then we have R ∩ ( B _1 × ... × B _n × B _ n+1 ) = (π_ [n] ( R ) ∩ ( B _1 × ... × B _n)) × B _ n+1 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: thm-rectangularity-application
title: Barto
statement_text: Suppose that X is a Prague instance such that each variable domain A _x is a conservative Taylor algebra. Let E be the subdigraph of the implication digraph which consists of pairs (x, B ) such that B ≤ A _x and B has a proper absorbing subalgebra, and let S be any maximal strand of E . Suppose that for each (x, B _x) ∈ S we choose a minimal absorbing subalgebra C _x mathrlap < lhd B _x , such that the system of variable domains C _x defines an arc-consistent reduction of the full restriction of X to the strand S . Then one of the following is true: the instance X has no solutions with any variable x assigned to any value in B _x , for any (x, B _x) ∈ S , the instance X ' which we get by restricting to the variables in S and by restricting each variable domain to the corresponding C _x has a solution, and every solution of X ' extends to a solution of X , or for some strand T of the subdigraph C of the implication digraph consisting of the pairs (x, C _x) for x occuring in S , the full restriction of X to T has no solutions.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Algorithm correctly solves every instance X of any multisorted CSP where each variable domain is a conservative Taylor algebra. If each variable domain has size at most k , then Algorithm runs in time | X |^ O(k) , where | X | is (up to a logarithmic factor) the number of bits needed to describe the instance X .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: The CSP dichotomy conjecture is true for all CSP templates on a domain of size at most 3 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: conservative-uniform
statement_text: Given as input an instance X of any CSP together with a conservative ternary weak near-unanimity polymorphism which preserves the relations of X , can we solve the instance X in time polynomial in | X | ?

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A restriction oracle O _R for a relation R ⊆ A_1 × ... × A_n is defined as a black box function which takes as input a tuple of subsets B_i ⊆ A_i , and returns ``true'' if and only if we have R ∩ (B_1 × ... × B_n) ≠ ∅ .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A concrete example of a high-arity relation which has an efficient restriction oracle is the all-different relation wedge_ i ≠ j x_i ≠ x_j . This relation occurs naturally in Sudoku and its generalizations. For any sets B_1, ..., B_n , we can determine whether or not {x | ∀ i ≠ j, x_i ≠ x_j} ∩ (B_1 × ... × B_n) ≠ ∅ as follows. We start by drawing a bipartite graph with parts A = {1, ..., n} and B = cup_i B_i , with an edge from i ∈ A to b ∈ B exactly when b ∈ B_i . Then we use the standard augmenting path algorithm to find a maximum matching in this graph - if there is a matching of size n , then the edges of this matching can be viewed as an assignment from variables x_i to values in B_i which are all different.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Consider the problem where we are given an instance X of a CSP together with a conservative ternary weak near-unanimity polymorphism which is promised to preserve the relations of X , but instead of having explicit descriptions of the constraint relations, the constraint relations are given to us implicitly in terms of restriction oracles. Is there an algorithm which determines whether X has a solution and makes only polynomially many calls to the restriction oracles which describe the constraint relations?

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: We can efficiently describe high-arity relations R on Z /3^ aff by writing down systems of linear equations. If we could convert a description of R as the solution set of a system of linear equations into an efficient restriction oracle O _R , however, then we would be able to solve 1-IN-3 SAT. To see this, note that for x,y,z ∈ Z /3^ aff we have (x,y,z) ∈ {(0,0,1),(0,1,0),(1,0,0)} ⟺ x,y,z ∈ {0,1} ∧ x+y+z ≡ 1 pmod 3 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that A = (A,Γ) is a 3 -conservative CSP template. We define the associated multisorted template A _3 to have a sort for each subset of A of size at most 3 , with two types of relations: for each relation R ∈ Γ of arity m , and for every triple of elements u,v,w ∈ R (not necessarily distinct), we have a multisorted relation R ∩ ({u_1,v_1,w_1} × ... × {u_n,v_n,w_n}) ⊆ {u_1,v_1,w_1} × ... × {u_n,v_n,w_n}, for every a,b,c ∈ A (not necessarily distinct), we have the binary inclusion relation {(a,a), (b,b)} ⊆ {a,b} × {a,b,c}.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-conservative-multi-ternary
statement_text: There is a bijection between conservative ternary polymorphisms of A and ternary polymorphisms of the associated multisorted structure A _3 which preserves height 1 identities.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that A = (A,Γ) is a 3 -conservative CSP template, and let U ⊆ P (A) be a collection nonempty subsets of A each of size at most 3 which is closed under taking nonempty subsets. We define the multisorted template A _ U to be the template whose sorts are exactly the elements of U , such that for each m -ary relation R of A _3 with at least one coordinate of a sort in U , if S ⊆ [m] is the set of coordinates of R which have a sort in U , then the relation π_S(R) is a relation of A _ U .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that A = (A,Γ) is a 3 -conservative CSP template. Let U ⊆ V ⊆ P (A) be collections of nonempty subsets of A each of size at most 3 which are closed under taking nonempty subsets. Suppose that f is a ternary polymorphism of the multisorted structure A _ U , and that R is an m -ary relation of A _ V . Let S ⊆ [m] be the set of coordinates of the relation R with sorts from U . Then for any y ∈ π_ [m] \ S (R) , the relation R_y coloneqq {x | ∃ r ∈ R s.t. π_S(r) = x, π_ [m] \ S (r) = y} ⊆ π_S(R) is preserved by the polymorphism f .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-conservative-indicator
statement_text: If B = ( U , Γ) is a multisorted relational structure with sorts U , then B has a ternary weak near-unanimity polymorphism f iff the following instance of CSP ( B ) has a solution: ∃ f={f_U ∈ U^ U^3 }_ U ∈ U s.t. & wedge_ U ∈ U ( wedge_ a ∈ U f_U(a,a,a) ∈ {a} ∧ wedge_ a,b ∈ U f_U(a,a,b) = f_U(a,b,a) = f_U(b,a,a) ) & ∧ wedge_ R ∈ Γ wedge_ u,v,w ∈ R f(u,v,w) ∈ R.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a 3 -conservative relational structure, then Algorithm runs in time polynomial in | A | , and either correctly determines that CSP ( A ) is NP-complete or produces a ternary weak near-unanimity polymorphism of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Mar\'oti
statement_text: If X is the set of all variables, and if each variable domain A _x has a congruence θ_x with the Mal'cev-on-top property, then an M-constraint on I ⊆ X is a subalgebra R ≤ Π _ x ∈ I A _x × Π _ y ∈ X \ I A _y/θ_y. We will say that the M-arity of an M-constraint on I is |I| . By a compact representation of R , we mean a collection of compact representations of the relations a_I + R = {b ∈ Π _ y ∈ X \ I A _y/θ_y | (a_I,b) ∈ R }, for all a_I ∈ Π _ x ∈ I A _x .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A subalgebra restriction oracle O _ R for a relation R ≤ A _1 × ... × A _n is defined as a black box function which takes as input a tuple of subalgebras B _i ≤ A _i , and returns ``true'' if and only if we have R ∩ ( B _1 × ... × B _n) ≠ ∅ .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Let R ≤ Π _x A _x , and for I ⊆ X consider the M-relation on I given by R /θ_ X \ I ≤ A _I × A _ X \ I /θ_ X \ I , where we have made the abbreviations A _I = Π _ x ∈ I A _x , and similarly for A _ X \ I and θ_ X \ I . If A _ X \ I /θ_ X \ I has a k -edge term, and if we are given a subalgebra restriction oracle O _ R for R , then we can compute a compact representation for R /θ_ X \ I using at most Π _ x ∈ I | A _x| × ( Σ _ y ∈ X \ I | A _y/θ_y| )^k calls to the oracle O _ R .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that A _i, θ_i have the Mal'cev-on-top property. An M-restriction oracle O ^ M _ R for a relation R ≤ A _1 × ... × A _n is defined as a black box function which takes as input a tuple of compact representations of M-unary M-constraints B _i ≤ A _i × Π _ j ≠ i A _j/θ_j, and returns a compact representation of ( R ∩ B _1 ∩ ... ∩ B _n )/ Π _i θ_i.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that θ_i ∈ Con ( A _i) for all i , and that for each i we have a relation B _i ≤ A _i × Π _ j ≠ i A _j/θ_j. Then we have ( B _1 ∩ ... ∩ B _n )/ Π _i θ_i = ( B _1/θ_1) ∩ ... ∩ ( B _n/θ_n).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that we are given a k -edge term e for the algebras A _x/θ_x , along with a compact representation of an M-constraint R ≤ A _I × A _ X \ I /θ_ X \ I and a tuple of compact representations of M-unary M-constraints B _x ≤ A _x × A _ X \ {x} /θ_ X \ {x} . Then we can compute a compact representation of ( R ∩ cap_ x ∈ X B _x )/θ_X in time polynomial in the sum of the sizes of the compact representations of R and the B _x s.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Given black box access to the subalgebra restriction oracle O _ R for an unknown relation R ≤ A _1 × ... × A _n of high arity, not necessarily an M-constraint, together with a k -edge term e for the algebras A _i/θ_i , can we implement the M-restriction oracle O ^ M _ R using only polynomially many calls to O _ R ?

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that A _i, θ_i have the Mal'cev-on-top property. We say that an instance of CSP ({ A _i}) is M-arc-consistent if for each constraint relation R _i ≤ A _X = Π _x A _x and each tuple of congruences a/θ_X ∈ R _i/θ_X, the instance we get by restricting each variable domain A _x to the congruence class a_x/θ_x is arc-consistent.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that A _i, θ_i have the Mal'cev-on-top property, and that X is an instance of CSP ({ A _i}) . Then Algorithm runs in polynomial time, and at the end of Algorithm , if we define a new instance X ' by restricting each variable domain to A _x' coloneqq π_x( B _x) and restricting each constraint relation R _i ≤ A _X of X to R _i' coloneqq R _i ∩ B _X ≤ A _X', then the instance X ' is M-arc-consistent. Furthermore, for any tuple of congruence classes a/θ_X ∈ A _X/θ_X we have a/θ_X ∈ B _X/θ_X ⟺ running arc-consistency on X _ a/θ_X doesn't prove that no solution exists , where X _ a/θ_X is the instance we get by restricting each variable domain A _x to the congruence class a_x/θ_x .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that A _i, θ_i have the Mal'cev-on-top property. We say that an instance of CSP ({ A _i}) is singleton M-arc-consistent if for each variable x ∈ X , each value a_x ∈ A _x , each constraint relation R _i ≤ A _X , and each tuple of congruences a_ X \ {x} /θ_ X \ {x} ∈ (a_x + R _i)/θ_ X \ {x} , running arc-consistency on the restricted instance we get by replacing A _x by {a_x} and replacing each A _y with a_y/θ_y for y ≠ x doesn't prove that the restricted instance has no solution.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that A _i, θ_i have the Mal'cev-on-top property, and that X is an instance of CSP ({ A _i}) . Then Algorithm runs in polynomial time, and if it doesn't prove that there is no solution to X , then it will find a solution to X .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If X , A are (possibly multisorted) relational structures of the same signature, then we define a new multisorted relational structure coprod _ X A with a new signature (depending on X ) as follows: for each sort X_i of X , and for each element x ∈ X_i , there is a sort A_x of coprod _ X A , which is a copy of the corresponding sort A_i of A , and for each relation C_j ⊆ X_ i_1 × ... × X_ i_m of X , and for each tuple c = (x_1, ..., x_m) ∈ C_j , there is a relation R_c ⊆ A_ x_1 × ... × A_ x_m of coprod _ X A which is a copy of the corresponding relation R_j ⊆ A_ i_1 × ... × A_ i_m of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: For a given (possibly multisorted) relational signature, we define the terminal structure * to have one element of each sort, and to have a single tuple in each relation.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If X , A are two relational structures of the same signature, then a homomorphism X → A is the same thing as a homomorphism coprod _ X * → coprod _ X A , which is the same thing as a constant (i.e., 0 -ary) polymorphism of coprod _ X A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Following Mar\'oti
statement_text: If A = (A, {f_i}) is an algebraic structure and e : A → A is any unary operation satisfying e(e(a)) = e(a) for all a ∈ A , we define the retract e( A ) of A with respect to e by e( A ) coloneqq (e(A), {e ∘ f_i}), considered as an algebraic structure with the same signature as A via f_i^ e( A ) = e ∘ f_i|_ e( A ) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If the basic operations f_i, f_j of A satisfy an identity of height at most one, i.e. f_i(x_1, ..., x_k) ≈ f_j(y_1, ..., y_l) for some sets of (possibly repeated) variables x_1, ..., x_k, y_1, ..., y_l or f_i(x_1, ..., x_k) ≈ x, for some set of (possibly repeated) variables x_1, ..., x_k, x , then the basic operations e ∘ f_i, e ∘ f_j of e( A ) satisfy the same identity (as long as e(e(x)) ≈ e(x) , for the second type of identity).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: For any multisorted relational structures X , A sharing a common signature, there are natural bijections between the set of unary polymorphisms coprod _ X A → coprod _ X A , the set of homomorphisms A × X → A , and the set of constant polymorphisms coprod _ A × X * → coprod _ A × X A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Mar\'oti , slightly simplified
statement_text: Let X be an instance of CSP ({ A _i}) , and let t be a binary term operation of { A _i} satisfying the identity t(x,t(x,y)) ≈ t(x,y) . The decomposition t( X ) is defined to be the instance of CSP ({t^a( A _i) | a ∈ A _i}), where t^a(x) coloneqq t(a,x) , whose variables and relations are defined as follows: for each variable x of X with variable domain A _x , and for each a ∈ A _x , we have a variable (a,x) of t( X ) with variable domain t^a( A _x) , where t^a( A _x) is the retract of A _x with respect to t^a , for each constraint tuple c = (x_1, ..., x_m) with constraint relation R ≤ A _ x_1 × ... × A _ x_m of X , and for each tuple r = (a_1, ..., a_m) ∈ R , we have a constraint tuple (r,c) = ((a_1, x_1), ..., (a_m, x_m)) with corresponding constraint relation given by t^r( R ) ≤ t^ a_1 ( A _ x_1 ) × ... × t^ a_m ( A _ x_m ), where t^r( R ) is the retract of R with respect to t^r . The reader should take a moment to check that the constraint relation t^r( R ) really is a subalgebra of t^ a_1 ( A _ x_1 ) × ... × t^ a_m ( A _ x_m ) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-tree-on-top-unary-poly
title: Mar\'oti
statement_text: If the instance X of CSP ({ A _i}) has a solution given by x mapsto c_x ∈ A _x , then for any binary term operation t of { A _i} the decomposition t( X ) has a solution given by the mapping (a,x) mapsto t(a,c_x).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-tree-on-top-partial-solution
title: Mar\'oti
statement_text: Suppose that A = { A _2, ...} is a finite collection of similar finite idempotent algebras such that CSP ( A ) can be solved in polynomial time, and suppose that A _1 is a finite idempotent algebra of the same signature with a binary term operation t satisfying the identity t(x,t(x,y)) ≈ t(x,y) such that a ∈ A ∈ { A _1} ∪ A ⇒ t^a( A ) ∈ A . Then for any instance X of CSP ({ A _1} ∪ A ) , we can check whether any given partial assignment to the variables of t( X ) extends to a solution to the decomposition t( X ) in polynomial time.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Mar\'oti
statement_text: Let X be an instance of CSP ( A ) , and let t be any binary polymorphism of A . If the decomposition t( X ) has a solution given by (a,x) mapsto φ^ A_x (a), then φ defines a homomorphism of multisorted relational structures φ : coprod _ X A → coprod _ X A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: defn-tree-on-top-eliminated
title: Mar\'oti
statement_text: If A is a finite idempotent algebra, then we say that A can be eliminated if A has a binary term operation t satisfying the identity t(x,t(x,y)) ≈ t(x,y), such that for each a ∈ A there is some x ∈ A such that t(a, x) ≠ x , and A is not generated by {c ∈ A | t_c : x mapsto t(x,c) is a permutation } .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Mar\'oti
statement_text: Suppose that A = { A _2, ...} is a finite collection of similar finite idempotent algebras such that CSP ( A ) can be solved in polynomial time, and suppose that A _1 is a finite idempotent algebra of the same signature such that A ∈ { A _1} ∪ A , φ( A ) ≠ A , φ ∘ φ = φ ⇒ φ( A ) ∈ A , or in other words, such that { A _1} ∪ A is closed under taking retracts. Suppose additionally that A _1 can be eliminated, in the sense of Definition . Then CSP ({ A _1} ∪ A ) can be solved in polynomial time.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: We say that an element a is a neutral element of a partial semilattice operation s on A if we have s(a,x) = x for all x ∈ A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Mar\'oti , slight variation
statement_text: If A is a finite idempotent algebra with a partial semilattice term operation s and a quotient A /θ such that (A/θ, s) is a semilattice with at least two elements, and if s has no neutral element on A , then A can be eliminated.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: The simplest algebra which the results we have proved so far still can't handle is the 4-element algebra A = ({0,1,2,*}, · ) , where · is the commutative binary operation given by c|cccc · & 0 & 1 & 2 & * hline 0 & 0 & 2 & 1 & 0 1 & 2 & 1 & 0 & 1 2 & 1 & 0 & 2 & 2 * & 0 & 1 & 2 & * , which has * as a neutral element. It's a good exercise to find an algorithm which solves CSP ( A ) in polynomial time.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is an algebra and a unary operation e : A → A with e ∘ e = e has e(A) closed under the basic operations of A , then e( A ) is the subalgebra of A with underlying set e(A) . In particular, if A is a conservative algebra, then every retract of A is a subalgebra of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Bulatov
statement_text: If A is a finite conservative algebra with a partial semilattice term operation s such that s has no neutral element on A and such that there is at least one pair of elements a ≠ b ∈ A with s(a,b) = b , then A can be eliminated.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Here is a 4-element example which can't be handled by the results proved so far, but which doesn't have a neutral element. Of course, it will neither be conservative nor have a semilattice quotient. We take A = ({a,b,c,*}, g) , where g is the ternary operation which is determined by the following properties: g is a symmetric function of its variables, * is a strongly absorbing element for g , i.e. g(*, A , A ) = {*} , each of the sets {a,b}, {a,c}, {b,c} forms a two-element Z /2^ aff subalgebra of A , with g acting as the minority operation on each of these pairs, and g(a,b,c) = * . Note that A is 2 -conservative (i.e., every two-element subset of A is closed under g ), and it is not too hard to check that A is also minimal Taylor. The reader should be able to find a polynomial time algorithm which solves CSP ( A ) without much difficulty.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: The length of a finite chain is the number of elements in the chain minus 1 . The length of a poset is the supremum of the lengths of all of its chains.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A poset satisfies the Jordan-Dedekind chain condition if for any a ≤ b , any two maximal chains from a to b have equal length.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A poset is called upper semimodular if whenever an element a has two distinct covers b,c , there is some element d which covers both b and c .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If a is any element of an upper semimodular poset which has no infinite chains, then any two maximal chains starting at a (going upwards) have the same length.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Birkhoff
statement_text: An upper semimodular poset which has no infinite chains satisfies the Jordan-Dedekind chain condition.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Birkhoff
statement_text: A ranked lattice of finite length is upper semimodular if and only if its height function satisfies the inequality h(x) + h(y) ≥ h(x ∨ y) + h(x ∧ y).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Birkhoff
statement_text: A lattice of finite length is modular iff it satisfies the Jordan-Dedekind chain condition and its height function satisfies h(x) + h(y) = h(x ∨ y) + h(x ∧ y).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: diamond-isom-lattice
title: Diamond Isomorphism Theorem
statement_text: If a,b are elements of a modular lattice, then the maps φ : llbracket a, a ∨ brrbracket → llbracket a ∧ b, brrbracket and φ: llbracket a ∧ b, brrbracket → llbracket a, a ∨ brrbracket given by φ : x mapsto x ∧ b and φ : y mapsto y ∨ a are lattice isomorphisms.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If a, b are elements of a lattice, then we say that the intervals llbracket a, a ∨ b rrbracket and llbracket a ∧ b, brrbracket are perspective to each other, and we abbreviate this with either the notation llbracket a, a ∨ b rrbracket searrow llbracket a ∧ b, b rrbracket or the notation llbracket a ∧ b, b rrbracket nearrow llbracket a, a ∨ brrbracket . If two intervals in a lattice can be connected by a chain of perspectivities, then we say that they are projective to each other.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: thm-jordan-holder
title: Jordan-H\"older for semimodular lattices
statement_text: Suppose we have two maximal chains 0 &= a_0 < a_1 < ... < a_n = 1, 0 &= b_0 < b_1 < ... < b_n = 1 in an upper semimodular lattice of finite length. Then there is a permutation σ ∈ S_n such that each llbracket a_ i-1 , a_irrbracket is projective in two steps (going nearrow , searrow ) to llbracket b_ σ(i)-1 , b_ σ(i) rrbracket .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A subgroup M ≤ G is subnormal iff the sequence of groups G = G _0 rhd G _1 rhd ... defined by taking G _ i+1 to be the normal closure of M inside G _i eventually reaches M . As a consequence, the intersection of two subnormal subgroups is also subnormal.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If G is a group of finite composition length, then the collection of subnormal subgroups of G forms a lower semimodular lattice. If llbracket N _1, M _1 rrbracket , llbracket N _2, M _2 rrbracket are searrow , nearrow projective covers in this lattice, then M _1/ N _1 cong M _2/ N _2 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Dedekind
statement_text: The free modular lattice on 3 generators is finite, with exactly 28 elements and length 8 . It is isomorphic to a subdirect product of six copies of the two-element lattice and a single copy of the diamond lattice M _3 . In particular, one can test whether a given 3 -variable lattice identity is a consequence of modularity in finite time, by testing whether it holds on M _3 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Shifting Lemma
statement_text: If A is congruence modular, x,y,z,w ∈ A and α,β,γ ∈ Con ( A ) with α ∧ β ≤ γ and x ≡ _α y, z ≡ _α w, x ≡ _β z, y ≡ _β w , then z ≡ _γ w ⇒ x ≡ _γ y .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: day-terms
title: Day terms
statement_text: In any congruence modular variety V , if F _ V (x,y,z,w) is the free algebra on four generators, and if we let θ_ a,b be the congruence generated by identifying a,b , then there are quaternary terms m_0, ..., m_n ∈ F _ V (x,y,z,w) such that m_0 &= x, m_i\ &(θ_ x,y ∨ θ_ z,w ) ∧ (θ_ x,z ∨ θ_ y,w )\ m_ i+1 for i even, m_i\ &θ_ z,w \ m_ i+1 for i odd, m_n &= y. In other words, the m_i satisfy the following system of identities: m_0(x,y,z,w) & ≈ x, m_i(x,x,z,z) & ≈ x for all i , m_i(x,y,x,y) & ≈ m_ i+1 (x,y,x,y) for i even, m_i(x,y,z,z) & ≈ m_ i+1 (x,y,z,z) for i odd, m_n(x,y,z,w) & ≈ y.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: day-congruence
statement_text: Let A be an algebra with Day terms m_0, ..., m_n , θ ∈ Con ( A ) , and a,b,c,d ∈ A with (c,d) ∈ θ . Then (a,b) ∈ θ iff for all i ≤ n we have m_i(a,b,a,b) ≡ _θ m_i(a,b,c,d) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: The Shifting Principle
statement_text: If A has Day terms m_0, ..., m_n , then A satisfies the Shifting Principle: if x,y,z,w ∈ A and α,γ ∈ Con ( A ) and Λ ≤ A ^2 is a reflexive relation preserved by the m_i with α ∩ Λ ⊆ γ and x ≡ _α y, z ≡ _α w, (x,z) ∈ Λ, (y,w) ∈ Λ , then z ≡ _γ w ⇒ x ≡ _γ y .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If the Shifting Principle holds for an algebra A in the special case where α ≥ γ , then A is congruence modular.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A variety is congruence modular iff it has Day terms.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A variety V is not congruence modular if and only if there are congruences α, β, γ on the free algebra F _ V (x,y,z,w) such that γ &< α, α ∘ β &= β ∘ γ ∘ β, α ∧ β & ≤ γ. If V is also idempotent, then we can strengthen the above as follows: V fails to be congruence modular iff the congruence θ of F _ V (x,y)^2 generated by identifying (y,x) with (y,y) satisfies θ < ker π_1, ker π_2 ∘ θ ∘ ker π_2 = 1.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If p(x,y,z) is a Mal'cev term, then we can take m_0(x,y,z,w) &= x, m_1(x,y,z,w) &= p(z,w,y), m_2(x,y,z,w) &= y as a sequence of Day terms. Rather than laboriously checking the Day identities, it is easier to verify that this sequence of terms can be used in the Shifting Lemma setup to show that x ≡ _γ y . We have x\ (α ∧ β)\ p(z,w,y)\ γ\ y , so from α ∧ β ≤ γ we get x\ γ\ y .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If g(x,y,z) is a majority term, then we can take m_0(x,y,z,w) &= x, m_1(x,y,z,w) &= g(x,y,z), m_2(x,y,z,w) &= g(x,y,w), m_3(x,y,z,w) &= y as a sequence of Day terms. Again, in the Shifting Lemma setup, we have x\ (α ∧ β)\ g(x,y,z)\ γ\ g(x,y,w)\ (α ∧ β)\ y , so x\ γ\ y .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: An algebra is congruence regular if every congruence on A is uniquely determined by any of its congruence classes.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Gumm
statement_text: If every subalgebra of A ^2 is congruence regular, then A is congruence modular.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: mod-cube-lemma
title: The Cube Lemma
statement_text: Suppose every subalgebra of A ^2 satisfies the Shifting Lemma. If α, β, γ ∈ Con ( A ) with γ ≥ α ∧ β , and if a,b,c,d,a',b',c',d' ∈ A with (a,b),(c,d),(a',b'),(c',d') ∈ α , (a,d),(b,c),(a',d'),(b',c') ∈ β , and (a,a'),(b,b'),(c,c') ∈ γ , then (d,d') ∈ γ .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose A has Day terms m_0, ..., m_n . For α, β ∈ Con ( A ) , we define X(α,β) to be the set of pairs (m_i(a,b,a,b),m_i(a,b,c,d)) for a & c b & d ∈ M (α,β) and i ≤ n .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If we have a Mal'cev term p(x,y,z) and take m_0 = x, m_1 = p(z,w,y), m_2 = y as our sequence of Day terms, then X(α,β) is the set of pairs (a,p(c,d,b)) for a & c b & d ∈ M (α,β) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If we have a majority term g(x,y,z) and take m_0 = x, m_1 = g(x,y,z), m_2 = g(x,y,w), m_3 = y as our sequence of Day terms, then X(α,β) is the set of pairs (a,g(a,b,c)) for a & c b & d ∈ M (α,β) . For (a,b) ∈ α ∧ β , we have g ( a & a b & b , a & b a & b , b & b b & b ) = a & b b & b ∈ M (α,β), so (a,g(a,b,b)) = (a,b) ∈ X(α,β) . Thus X(α,β) = α ∧ β for majority algebras.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: day-commutator
title: Commutator via Day terms
statement_text: If A has Day terms m_0, ..., m_n and α,β,δ ∈ Con ( A ) , then the following are equivalent. X(α,β) ⊆ δ , X(β,α) ⊆ δ , C(α,β;δ) holds, C(β,α;δ) holds, [α,β] ≤ δ .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: mod-commutator
statement_text: If A is contained in a congruence modular variety, then for congruences on A we have [α,β] = [β,α] , [α ∧ γ, β] ≤ [α,β] ∧ γ , [ vee_i α_i, β] = vee_i[α_i,β] , if f : A twoheadrightarrow B is surjective, then f([α,β] ∨ ker f) = [f(α ∨ ker f), f(β ∨ ker f)] , if B ≤ A , then [α|_ B ,β|_ B ] ≤ [α,β]|_ B , if A = Π _ i ∈ I A _i , then [ oplus_i α_i, oplus_i β_i] = oplus_i[α_i,β_i] , where oplus_i α_i is the set of pairs (a,b) in Π _i α_i such that for all but finitely many i we have a_i = b_i , if A = Π _ i ∈ I A _i , then [ Π _i α_i, Π _i β_i] ≤ Π _i [α_i, β_i] .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If α,β ≥ π are congruences in a congruence modular variety, then their relative commutator is given by the formula [α,β]_π = [α,β] ∨ π .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: diamond-isom
title: Diamond Isomorphism Theorem for relative commutators
statement_text: If A is in a congruence modular variety and α, β ∈ Con ( A ) , then the maps φ : llbracket α,α ∨ βrrbracket → llbracket α ∧ β, βrrbracket and φ: llbracket α ∧ β, βrrbracket → llbracket α,α ∨ βrrbracket given by φ : x mapsto x ∧ β\ and \ φ : y mapsto y ∨ α are lattice isomorphisms which respect the relative commutators [ · , · ]_α, [ · , · ]_ α ∧ β . Furthermore, in this case we have the equality of relative centralizers (α:α ∨ β) = (α ∧ β:β) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: For α,β ∈ Con ( A ) , if we consider α ≤ A ^2 as an algebra of column vectors then we can treat M (α,β) (from Definition ) as a binary relation on α , so ( a b , c d ) ∈ M (α,β) means that a & c b & d ∈ M (α,β) . We define Δ_α^β to be the transitive closure of this binary relation on α .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A has a Mal'cev polynomial p and α,β ∈ Con ( A ) , then Δ_α^β = M (α,β) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: shifting-commutator
statement_text: Suppose that the Shifting Lemma holds for every subalgebra of A ^2 . Then for x,y ∈ A and α,β ∈ Con ( A ) , the following are equivalent: (x,y) ∈ [β,α] , x & y y & y ∈ Δ_α^β , there exists a ∈ A such that x & a y & a ∈ Δ_α^β , there exists b ∈ A such that x & y b & b ∈ Δ_α^β .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If every subalgebra of A ^2 satisfies the Shifting Lemma, then for α, β_i ∈ Con ( A ) we have [ vee_i β_i, α] = vee_i[β_i,α] .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If every subalgebra of A ^2 satisfies the Shifting Lemma, then for f : A twoheadrightarrow B surjective and α, β ≥ ker f , we have f([β,α] ∨ ker f) = [f(β),f(α)] .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: commutator-transpose
statement_text: Suppose that the Shifting Lemma holds for every subalgebra of A ^4 . If Δ _α^β denotes the set of transposes of matrices from Δ_α^β , then Δ _α^β is transitively closed as a binary relation on β and we have Δ _α^β = Δ_β^α . In particular, we have [α,β] = [β,α] .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: In a congruence modular variety, any alternative commutator [ · , · ]' which satisfies [α,β]' ≤ α ∧ β and f([α,β]' ∨ ker f) = [f(α),f(β)]' for f surjective and α,β ≥ ker f has [α,β]' ≤ [α,β] for all α, β .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: gumm-difference
title: Gumm difference term
statement_text: For any variety with Day terms m_0, ..., m_n , there is a ternary term p satisfying the following two properties: p satisfies the identity p(y,y,x) ≈ x , and for any (x,y) ∈ θ , θ any congruence, we have p(x,y,y)\ [θ,θ]\ x . Furthermore, in a congruence modular variety, a ternary term p satisfies (i) and (ii) iff it satisfies the following property: for any congruences α,β,γ with α ∧ β ≤ γ , the implication in the following picture holds. Finally, if a variety has a term p which satisfies (iii), then it is congruence modular.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Factor Permutability
statement_text: If A = A _1 × A _2 is contained in a congruence modular variety, then the factor congruences ker π_1,ker π_2 permute with every congruence γ ∈ Con ( A ) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Any abelian algebra which is contained in a congruence modular variety is affine.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A nontrivial algebra A in a congruence modular variety is abelian iff there is some B ≤ _ sd A × A such that M _3 is a 0,1 -sublattice of Con ( B ) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: For any congruence α , define [α]^n inductively by [α]^0 = α, [α]^ n+1 = [[α]^n,[α]^n] .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If p is a Gumm difference term, and if we define terms p_n inductively by p_0 = p and p_ n+1 (x,y,z) = p_n(x,p_n(x,y,y),p_n(x,y,z)), then each p_n is also a Gumm difference term, and for any (x,y) ∈ θ we have p_n(x,y,y)\ [θ]^ 2^n \ x .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: cor-modular-solvable-malcev
statement_text: Any solvable algebra in a congruence modular variety is Mal'cev.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: difference-commutator
statement_text: Suppose p is a Gumm difference term for a congruence modular variety and α ≥ β . Then Δ_β^α is given by x & w y & z ∈ Δ_β^α ⟺ (p(x,y,z)\ [α,β]\ w) ∧ (x\ β\ y\ α\ z).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: difference-graph
statement_text: If α ≥ β and [α,β] = 0 , then the restriction of the graph of p(x,y,z) to triples with x\ β\ y\ α\ z is preserved by all polynomial operations of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A variety V is congruence distributive if for every A ∈ V , Con ( A ) is a distributive lattice, that is, if the inequality α ∧ (β ∨ γ) ≤ (α ∧ β) ∨ (α ∧ γ) holds for all α, β, γ ∈ Con ( A ) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: distributive-m3
title: Birkhoff
statement_text: In any modular lattice, if a,b,c do not satisfy the distributive law, and if we define elements d,e,f by d = (b ∧ c) ∨ (a ∧ (b ∨ c)) = ((b ∧ c) ∨ a) ∧ (b ∨ c), with e,f defined by cyclic permutations of the variables a,b,c in the above formula, then d,e,f generate a sublattice isomorphic to the diamond lattice M _3 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A variety is congruence distributive iff it is congruence modular and none of its algebras has a nontrivial abelian congruence. In particular, the commutator is given by [α,β] = α ∧ β and p(x,y,z) = z is a Gumm difference term in any congruence distributive variety.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: The variety of unital rings is not congruence distributive, even though it is congruence modular (in fact, congruence permutable, since it has a Mal'cev term x-y+z ) and contains no nontrivial abelian algebras (any such algebra would have x · y = 0 for all x,y , and plugging in y = 1 would give x = 0 for all x ). The reason for this is that the congruence on the ring Z /p^2 corresponding to the ideal (p) is abelian, but no congruence class of this ideal forms a unital subring of Z /p^2 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: jonsson-terms
title: J\'onsson terms
statement_text: A variety is congruence distributive iff it has ternary terms q_0, ..., q_n satisfying the system of identities q_0(x,y,z) & ≈ x, q_i(x,y,x) & ≈ x for all i, q_i(x,y,y) & ≈ q_ i+1 (x,y,y) for i odd, q_i(x,x,y) & ≈ q_ i+1 (x,x,y) for i even, q_n(x,y,z) & ≈ z.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: The variety of lattices is congruence distributive. For the J\'onsson terms, we may take n = 2 and q_1(x,y,z) to be the majority term (x ∧ y) ∨ (y ∧ z) ∨ (z ∧ x) . More generally, any variety with a near-unanimity term is congruence distributive.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: commutator-permute
statement_text: If α, β are any two congruences in a congruence modular variety, then α ∘ β ⊆ [α,α] ∘ β ∘ α.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If α, β, γ are congruences in a congruence modular variety, then (α ∘ β) ∩ γ ⊆ ((α ∧ β) ∨ (α ∧ γ)) ∘ β ∘ α.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: gumm-terms
title: Gumm terms
statement_text: A variety is congruence modular iff it has ternary terms q_0, ..., q_n, p satisfying the system of identities q_0(x,y,z) & ≈ x, q_i(x,y,x) & ≈ x for all i, q_i(x,y,y) & ≈ q_ i+1 (x,y,y) for i odd, q_i(x,x,y) & ≈ q_ i+1 (x,x,y) for i even, q_n(x,y,y) & ≈ p(x,y,y), p(x,x,y) & ≈ y. Furthermore, a ternary term p is a Gumm difference term iff there exist terms q_0, ..., q_n satisfying the above system of identities.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: directed-gumm-terms
title: Directed Gumm terms
statement_text: A variety is congruence modular iff it has ternary terms f_1, ..., f_m, p with f_1(x,x,y) & ≈ x, f_i(x,y,x) & ≈ x for all i, f_i(x,y,y) & ≈ f_ i+1 (x,x,y) for all i, f_m(x,y,y) & ≈ p(x,y,y), p(x,x,y) & ≈ y, and if the variety is congruence distributive then we can take f_m(x,y,y) ≈ y (directed J\'onsson terms).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A ≤ _ sd Π _ i ∈ I A _i is a subdirect product, then wedge_ i ∈ I ker π_i = 0_ A . In particular, if no π_i is an isomorphism then the congruence 0_ A can be written as a meet of some family of nontrivial congruences. Conversely, if 0_ A can be written as a meet of congruences α_i ∈ Con ( A ) for i ∈ I , then A ≤ _ sd Π _ i ∈ I A /α_i .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: An algebraic structure A is subdirectly irreducible if every way of writing A as a subdirect product A ≤ _ sd Π _ i ∈ I A _i has at least one coordinate i such that the projection map π_i : A → A _i is an isomorphism. The least nontrivial congruence on a subdirectly irreducible algebra is called its monolith .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: An element α of a complete lattice L is meet-irreducible if for any set of elements α_i ∈ L with wedge_ i ∈ I α_i = α , some α_i is equal to α . In this case, we define the cover of α , written α^* , to be the least element of L with α < α^* .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Birkhoff's Subdirect Representation Theorem
statement_text: Any algebraic structure A can be represented as a subdirect product of subdirectly irreducible algebras.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: defn-algebraic-lattice
statement_text: An element α of a complete lattice is called compact if for any family α_i such that α ≤ vee_ i ∈ I α_i , there is some finite subset {i_1, ..., i_k} ⊆ I such that α ≤ α_ i_1 ∨ ... ∨ α_ i_k . A complete lattice is called algebraic if every element can be written as a join of compact elements.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: meet-irreducible-rep
statement_text: Let L be an algebraic lattice. Then every element α of L can be written as a meet of some family of meet-irreducible elements of L .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: meet-irreducible
statement_text: If α < β in an algebraic lattice, then there is a meet-irreducible γ such that γ ≥ α but γ not ≥ β .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If I is a set, then a collection of subsets U ⊆ P (I) is a filter if U does not contain ∅ , U,V ∈ U ⇒ U ∩ V ∈ U , and U ⊆ V, U ∈ U ⇒ V ∈ U . We say that U is an ultrafilter if additionally for every U ⊆ I , one of U, I \ U is in U .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Any filter is contained in an ultrafilter.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A _i is a collection of structures which share a common signature σ and are indexed by i ∈ I , and if U is an ultrafilter on I , then we define the ultraproduct Π _i A _i/ U to be the quotient of Π _i A _i by the congruence defined by a ≡ _ U b ⟺ {i | a_i = b_i} ∈ U . That ≡ _ U is compatible with functions f ∈ σ follows from the fact that U is a filter. If R ∈ σ is an m -ary relation, then R is interpreted on Π _i A _i/ U by R(a^1/ U , ..., a^m/ U ) ⟺ {i | R(a^1_i, ..., a^m_i)} ∈ U . If all the A _i are isomorphic to A , then we call A ^I/ U an ultrapower of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If U is an ultrafilter on I and U_1, ..., U_k partition I into k disjoint parts, then exactly one of U_1, ..., U_k is in U .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: ultraproduct-finite
statement_text: If | A _i| ≤ n for all i ∈ I , then | Π _i A _i/ U | ≤ n as well. If each A _i is finite and only finitely many isomorphism classes occur among the A _i , then Π _i A _i/ U is isomorphic to some A _i .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: L o\'s's Theorem
statement_text: Let φ(x_1, ..., x_n) be any first order formula in the signature σ with parameters x_1, ..., x_n , then for any a^1, ..., a^n ∈ Π _ i ∈ I A _i and any ultrafilter U on I , we have Π _i A _i/ U models φ(a^1/ U , ..., a^n/ U ) ⟺ {i | A _i models φ(a^1_i, ..., a^n_i)} ∈ U .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: jonsson-modular
statement_text: Let { A _i} be a family of algebras, and let V = V ({ A _i}) be the variety they generate. If V is congruence modular, B ∈ V is subdirectly irreducible, and α = (0_ B : 0_ B ^*) is the centralizer of the monolith 0_ B ^* of B , then B /α is a homomorphic image of a subalgebra of an ultraproduct of the A _i s, that is, B /α ∈ HSP_u({ A _i}) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: J\'onsson's Lemma
statement_text: Let { A _i} be a family of algebras, and let V = V ({ A _i}) be the variety they generate. If V is congruence distributive and B ∈ V is subdirectly irreducible, then B ∈ HSP_u({ A _i}) . In particular, if { A _i} is a finite set of finite algebras, then B ∈ HS({ A _i}) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: For any two finite subdirectly irreducible algebras A , B with the same signature which generate congruence distributive varieties, we have A cong B iff the set of identities that hold in A is the same as the set of identities that hold in B .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Consider the variety of distributive lattices, and the two-element lattice ({0,1},max ,min ) . It is easy to see that every identity that holds in the two-element lattice is implied by the lattice axioms together with distributivity (since these allow us to put every term into conjunctive normal form), so the variety of distributive lattices is generated by the two-element lattice. By J\'onsson's Lemma, the only subdirectly irreducible distributive lattice is the two-element lattice itself, so we see that in fact every distributive lattice is a sublattice of {0,1}^I for some index set I , that is, every distributive lattice is a sublattice of the lattice of subsets of some set I .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Let G , M be abelian groups and let R be a finite subgroup of Hom ( G , M ) , such that there is a nonzero element a ∈ M so that for all x ∈ G there is an r ∈ R with rx = a . Then | G | is a prime power dividing | R | .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Let R be a finite ring, and let M be a subdirectly irreducible module over R . Then | M | is a prime power dividing | R | .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: subdirect-ab-prime-power
statement_text: Suppose that B ∈ V is subdirectly irreducible, and V is locally finite and congruence modular. If α ∈ Con ( B ) is abelian and | B /α| = k , then every congruence class of α has size a prime power bounded by | F _ V (k+1)| .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: subdirect-bound-ab
statement_text: If | A | = m is finite and V ( A ) is congruence modular, and if B ∈ V ( A ) is subdirectly irreducible with (0_ B :0_ B ^*) abelian, then | B | ≤ m · m^ m^ m+1 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A variety V is called residually small if there is a cardinal κ such that every subdirectly irreducible algebra B ∈ V has | B | < κ , and residually finite if every subdirectly irreducible algebra in V is finite. An algebra A is called residually small if the variety V ( A ) generated by A is residually small.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: ultraproduct-fin-gen
statement_text: If B is subdirectly irreducible, then B is a subalgebra of an ultraproduct of a family of finitely generated subdirectly irreducible algebras in HS( B ) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: residually-infinite
statement_text: If a locally finite variety contains an infinite subdirectly irreducible algebra, then it contains arbitrarily large finite subdirectly irreducible algebras.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: The commutator identity [α ∧ β, β] = α ∧ [β,β] is equivalent to the implication α ≤ [β,β] ⇒ [α,β] = α .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is in a congruence modular variety and satisfies the commutator identity [α ∧ β,β] = α ∧ [β,β] hereditarily, then so does every quotient B of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A _1, A _2 are in a congruence modular variety and satisfy the commutator identity [α ∧ β, β] = α ∧ [β,β] hereditarily, then so does their product A _1 × A _2 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If | A | = m is finite and V ( A ) is congruence modular, and if A satisfies the commutator identity [α ∧ β,β] = α ∧ [β,β] hereditarily, then every subdirectly irreducible algebra B ∈ V ( A ) has | B | ≤ m · m^ m^ m+1 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: The symmetric group S_3 on three letters is residually small, since it satisfies the commutator identity [α ∧ β, β] = α ∧ [β,β] hereditarily: the only interesting case to check is that [A_3,S_3] = A_3 , where A_3 is the alternating group on three letters. We have HS(S_3) = {1, Z /2, Z /3, S_3} , and all three nontrivial elements are subdirectly irreducible. The general theory shows that every subdirectly irreducible G ∈ V (S_3) has an abelian normal subgroup N with G / N ∈ HS(S_3) , with | N | a prime power bounded by | F _ V (S_3) (| G / N |+1)| ≤ 6^ 6^7 . Since N ∈ V (S_3) and every element of S_3 has order dividing 6 , N has exponent 2 or 3 . From here it is not too hard to check that the only nontrivial subdirectly irreducible algebras in V (S_3) are Z /2, Z /3, S_3 , and all three of these are subgroups of S_3 . Thus every group in V (S_3) is a subgroup of a power of S_3 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is contained in a congruence modular variety but does not satisfy the commutator identity [α ∧ β,β] = α ∧ [β,β] hereditarily, then there is some subdirectly irreducible B ∈ HS( A ) such that the centralizer of the monolith of B is not abelian.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is contained in a congruence modular variety but does not satisfy the commutator identity [α ∧ β,β] = α ∧ [β,β] , then V ( A ) is not residually small. In fact, for every cardinal κ , V ( A ) contains a subdirectly irreducible algebra whose congruence lattice has size at least κ .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: residual-crit
statement_text: Let V be a finitely generated congruence modular variety. Then the following are equivalent: V is residually small, every algebra in V satisfies the commutator identity [α ∧ β, β] = α ∧ [β,β] , V is generated by a finite algebra A such that for every subdirectly irreducible B ∈ HS( A ) , the centralizer of the monolith of B is abelian, V is generated by a finite algebra which satisfies the commutator identity [α ∧ β, β] = α ∧ [β,β] hereditarily, V has a finite bound on the size of its subdirectly irreducible elements.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is in a congruence modular variety and has size | A | ≤ 3 , then V ( A ) is residually small.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: residual-nilpotent
statement_text: If A satisfies the commutator identity [α ∧ β,β] = α ∧ [β,β] , then every nilpotent congruence on A is abelian.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: sylow-abelian
title: Ol' v s anski u i
statement_text: If all the Sylow subgroups of a finite group G are abelian, then the center Z( G ) and the commutator subgroup [ G , G ] intersect trivially, that is, Z( G ) ∧ [ G , G ] = 0_ G .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
title: Ol' v s anski u i
statement_text: A finite group is residually small iff all of its Sylow subgroups are abelian.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: We say that subdirectly irreducible algebras A , B in a congruence modular variety V are similar if there exists an algebra C ∈ V with congruences α, β, γ, δ ∈ C such that C /α cong A , C /β cong B , and llbracket α, α^* rrbracket searrow llbracket γ, δ rrbracket nearrow llbracket β, β^* rrbracket . If furthermore C ≤ _ sd A × B and α, β are the kernels of the projections to A , B , then we say that C is the graph of a similarity from A to B .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: similarity-graph
statement_text: If A , B are similar, then there is a witnessing algebra C ≤ _ sd A × B which is the graph of a similarity from A to B . If α,β are the kernels of the projections to A , B , then (α:α^*) = (β:β^*) and C /(α:α^*) is the graph of an isomorphism A /(0_ A :0_ A ^*) xrightarrow B /(0_ B :0_ B ^*). If A , B are similar but not isomorphic, then they must both have abelian monoliths.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A , B are similar such that σ is the corresponding isomorphism σ: A /(0_ A :0_ A ^*) xrightarrow B /(0_ B :0_ B ^*), then they are similar via the algebra R = {(x,y) ∈ A × B | σ(x/(0_ A :0_ A ^*)) = y/(0_ B :0_ B ^*)} .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: similar-detail
statement_text: A similarity from A to B can be described by the following data: an isomorphism σ: A /(0_ A :0_ A ^*) xrightarrow B /(0_ B :0_ B ^*) together with a congruence δ ∈ Con ( R ) , where R = {(x,y) ∈ A × B | σ(x/(0_ A :0_ A ^*)) = y/(0_ B :0_ B ^*)} , such that for every (a,b) ∈ R and every a' ∈ a/0_ A ^* , there exists a unique b' ∈ b/0_ B ^* such that a & a' b & b' ∈ δ. In particular, if A , B are idempotent, then for any (a,b) ∈ R the congruence classes a/0_ A ^* and b/0_ B ^* are isomorphic to each other.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Similarity is an equivalence relation on subdirectly irreducible algebras.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: monolith-bound
statement_text: If B ∈ V ( A ) is subdirectly irreducible, A is finite, and V ( A ) is congruence modular, then every congruence class of 0_ B ^* has size at most | A | .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose A is a subdirectly irreducible algebra in a congruence modular variety. If 0_ A ^* is nonabelian, define D( A ) to be A . Otherwise, consider 0_ A ^* as a subalgebra of A ^2 and Δ_ 0_ A ^* ^ (0:0^*) as a congruence on 0_ A ^* , and define D( A ) = 0_ A ^*/Δ_ 0_ A ^* ^ (0:0^*) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a subdirectly irreducible algebra in a congruence modular variety with an abelian monolith, then D( A ) is subdirectly irreducible with monolith (0_ A :0_ A ^*)_ D( A ) , and A , D( A ) are similar via the algebra 0_ A ^* and the congruences ker π_1, Δ_ 0_ A ^* ^ (0:0^*) ∈ Con (0_ A ^*) . Furthermore, the monolith (0_ A :0_ A ^*)_ D( A ) of D( A ) is its own centralizer.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A , B are subdirectly irreducible algebras in a congruence modular variety, then A is similar to B iff D( A ) cong D( B ) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If B ∈ V ( A ) is subdirectly irreducible, A is finite, and V ( A ) is congruence modular, then B is similar to a subdirectly irreducible algebra in HS( A ) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Let's work out what D( G ) is when G is a subdirectly irreducible group. Let M lhd G be the normal subgroup corresponding to the monolith 0_ G ^* , and let N = C_ G ( M ) lhd G be the normal subgroup corresponding to the centralizer (0_ G : 0_ G ^*) . First off, what is the group structure on the congruence 0_ G ^* ? By definition, we have 0_ G ^* = {(x,y) ∈ G ^2 | x^ -1 y ∈ M }. We have a natural exact sequence of groups 0 → M hookrightarrow 0_ G ^* twoheadrightarrow G → 0, where the inclusion is the map m mapsto (1,m) and the quotient map is the first projection π_1 . The quotient 0_ G ^* twoheadrightarrow G has a section Δ : G hookrightarrow 0_ G ^* given by g mapsto (g,g) . Thus we can write 0_ G ^* as a semidirect product 0_ G ^* cong M rtimes G , where the action of G on M is the standard conjugation action. How about the congruence Δ_ 0_ G ^* ^ (0:0^*) ∈ Con (0_ G ^*) ? By Theorem , we have x & w y & z ∈ Δ_ 0_ G ^* ^ (0:0^*) ⟺ (xy^ -1 z = w) ∧ (x\ ≡ _ M \ y\ ≡ _ N \ z). Since this is a congruence on a group, we just need to understand the congruence class of the identity, so we plug in x = y = 1 and ask what values (w,z) can take. We find that Δ_ 0_ G ^* ^ (0:0^*) corresponds to the normal subgroup {(n,n) | n ∈ N }, so under the isomorphism 0_ G ^* cong M rtimes G it corresponds to N , considered as a subgroup of G . Thus we have D( G ) = 0_ G ^*/Δ_ 0_ G ^* ^ (0:0^*) cong ( M rtimes G )/ N cong M rtimes ( G / N ). That any of this makes sense follows from N = C_ G ( M ) . We see that M is the normal subgroup corresponding to the monolith of D( G ) , that M is equal to its own centralizer in D( G ) , and that the natural map G / N hookrightarrow D( G ) has image transverse to the monolith, and induces an isomorphism σ : G / N xrightarrow D( G )/ M . To complete the description of the similarity from G to D( G ) , we let R be the fiber product of G and D( G ) over G / N , and define the congruence δ ∈ Con ( R ) as the 4 -ary relation a & a' b & b' ∈ δ\ ⟺ \ a b , a' b' ∈ R \ ∧ \ a^ -1 a' = b^ -1 b' ∈ M . That δ is closed under multiplication must be checked - it follows from the fact that N centralizes M , and the fact that for any a,b,a',b' satisfying the above conditions all of a,b,a',b' must necessarily map to the same element of G / N . What are the possible values for D( G ) , assuming the monolith is abelian? Note that if we consider M as a module via the G / N action, then it must be a simple module, since if it has any nontrivial submodule M ' , then M ' will be a smaller normal subgroup of G . Thus the general situation is that M is some simple module over the ring Z [ G / N ] (where G / N acts faithfully on M ), and D( G ) cong M rtimes ( G / N ) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If we take G = S_3 in the above, we find that D(S_3) cong Z /3 rtimes Z /2 cong S_3 . The 4 -ary relation δ ≤ S_3^ 2 × 2 corresponding to the trivial similarity from S_3 to itself is given by a & a' b & b' ∈ δ\ ⟺ \ s(a) = s(b) = s(a') = s(b')\ ∧ \ a^ -1 a' = b^ -1 b', where s : S_3 → { ± 1} is the sign homomorphism. We can think of the relation δ as having two ``strands'' corresponding to the two possible signs of permutations, and if we restrict to either strand then δ becomes an affine relation over Z /3 . The fact that we can multiply elements of δ which come from different strands and still get an element of δ is worth thinking about. Now suppose that G is some other subdirectly irreducible group such that D( G ) cong S_3 , with monolith corresponding to M lhd G and N = C_G( M ) . Then since G is similar to S_3 , we must have M cong Z /3 and G / N cong Z /2 by Corollary , with G / N acting on M by negation since D( G ) cong M rtimes ( G / N ) cong S_3 . If the action of G / N on N is given by an involution τ , then for any n ∈ N \ {1} we must have M contained in the normal subgroup of N generated by n, n^τ . In particular, if N is abelian then we see that n + n^τ, n - n^τ ∈ M for all n ∈ N , and additionally in this case N must have prime power order by Theorem . Thus if N is abelian then we must actually have N = M , and G cong S_3 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If we take G = Q_8 = { ± 1, ± i, ± j, ± k} the quaternion group with i^2 = j^2 = k^2 = ijk = -1 , then the monolith is equal to the center, corresponding to the normal subgroup { ± 1} , and the centralizer of the monolith is the full congruence 1_ Q_8 . Thus D(Q_8) cong { ± 1} cong Z /2. The relation δ ≤ (Q_8 × Z /2)^2 is then given by a & a' b & b' ∈ δ\ ⟺ \ a' = (-1)^ b + b' a. This relation closely resembles an affine relation over Z /2 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-quasiorder-poly
statement_text: An equivalence relation θ on an algebra A is a congruence of A iff θ is preserved by every unary polynomial operation of A . More generally, a quasiorder preceq on A is a subalgebra of A ^2 if and only if preceq is preserved by every unary polynomial of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: cor-quasiorder-poly
statement_text: Suppose A is an algebra and let Pol _1( A ) be the set of unary polynomials of A . If R is any quasiorder of A , then among all quasiorders on A which are also subalgebras of A ^2 , the minimal compatible quasiorder containing R is the transitive closure of the set {(f(a), f(b)) | (a,b) ∈ R and f ∈ Pol _1( A )}, and the maximal compatible quasiorder contained in R is given by {(a,b) | ∀ f ∈ Pol _1( A ), (f(a), f(b)) ∈ R}.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: For any algebra A , we define E( A ) to be the set of unary polynomials e ∈ Pol _1( A ) such that e ∘ e = e . Elements of E( A ) might be called the idempotents or projections of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is an algebra and U ⊆ A , then we define the restriction Pol ( A )|_U to be the set of restrictions f|_U of polynomial operations f ∈ Pol ( A ) which preserve the subset U , and we define the induced algebra A |_U to be (U, Pol ( A )|_U) (up to term equivalence).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: lem-idempotent-surjective-lattice
title: P\'alfy and Pudl\'ak ,
statement_text: For any idempotent e ∈ E( A ) , if we set U = e( A ) , then the map taking the congruence θ ∈ Con ( A ) to e(θ) = θ|_U defines a surjective lattice homomorphism: θ mapsto θ|_U : Con ( A ) twoheadrightarrow Con ( A |_U). More generally, if N ⊆ U , then: A |_N = ( A |_U)|_N , if N is a union of θ|_U congruence classes, then the map α mapsto α|_N defines a lattice homomorphism from the interval llbracket 0_ A , θ rrbracket of Con ( A ) to the interval llbracket 0_N, θ|_N rrbracket of Con ( A |_N) , and if N is equal to a congruence class of θ|_U , then the map α mapsto α|_N is a surjective lattice homomorphism llbracket 0_ A , θ rrbracket twoheadrightarrow Con ( A |_N) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: defn-restrict-order
statement_text: Write B preceq _| A if there is some idempotent e ∈ E( A ) , congruence θ ∈ Con ( A ) , and a ∈ e( A ) , such that if we define U = e( A ) and N = U ∩ (a/θ), then B is polynomially equivalent to A |_N . (Note that in general B will have a different signature than A .)

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-restrict-transitive
statement_text: The relation preceq _| is transitively closed on finite algebras: if C preceq _| B preceq _| A and A is finite, then C preceq _| A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-restrict-variety
statement_text: If A is finite and B preceq _| A is such that every constant of B is a term operation of B , and if D ∈ HSP_ fin ( B ) , then there is some C ∈ HSP_ fin ( A ) such that D preceq _| C .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If α < β ∈ Con ( A ) , then we define U_ A (α, β) to be the collection of sets given by U_ A (α, β) = {f( A ) | f ∈ Pol _1( A ) and f(β) ⊄ α}. We define M_ A (α, β) to be the collection of minimal sets in U_ A (α, β) , and we call the sets in M_ A (α, β) the (α, β) - minimal sets of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-prime-tame
statement_text: If β is a cover of α in Con ( A ) and A is finite, then for each (α,β) -minimal set U ∈ M_ A (α,β) , there is some e ∈ E( A ) such that U = e( A ) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A 0,1 - lattice is defined to be a lattice with constants 0 and 1 which satisfy 0 ≤ x ≤ 1 for all x . Note that every interval llbracket α, β rrbracket in a lattice can be regarded as a 0,1 -lattice, with 0 interpreted as α and 1 interpreted as β . A 0,1 - separating homomorphism is a lattice homomorphism such that f^ -1 (f(0)) = {0} and f^ -1 (f(1)) = {1} .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: defn-tame
statement_text: A congruence quotient is defined to be an ordered pair of congruences (α,β) such that α < β . A congruence quotient (α,β) is called prime if β covers α . A congruence quotient (α,β) is called tame if there is some U ∈ M_ A (α,β) and some e ∈ E( A ) such that e( A ) = U , and such that the restriction homomorphism llbracket α, β rrbracket twoheadrightarrow llbracket α|_U, β|_U rrbracket is a 0,1 -separating homomorphism, that is, for α ≤ γ ≤ β we have γ|_U = α|_U ⇒ γ = α and γ|_U = β|_U ⇒ γ = β . An algebra A is called tame if (0_ A ,1_ A ) is tame.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If U,V ⊆ A , then we say that U,V are polynomially isomorphic in A if there are unary polynomials f,g ∈ Pol _1( A ) such that f(U) = V, g(V) = U, g ∘ f|_U = id _U, f ∘ g|_V = id _V. In this case we write f : U simeq V .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If f : U simeq V in A , then f|_U defines an isomorphism from A |_U to A |_V (up to term equivalence). Furthermore, for any θ ∈ Con ( A ) we have f|_U(θ|_U) = θ|_V .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If U,V ⊆ A and A is finite, then U simeq V iff there are f, g ∈ Pol _1( A ) such that f(U) = V and g(V) = U . If additionally we have f( A ) = V , then there is some idempotent e ∈ E( A ) such that e( A ) = U .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: thm-minimal-sets
title: Minimal sets for tame quotients
statement_text: If (α,β) is a tame congruence quotient on a finite algebra A , then all of the following are true. For all U,V ∈ M_ A (α,β) , we have U simeq V in A . For all U ∈ M_ A (α,β) , there is some e ∈ E( A ) such that e( A ) = U , and the restriction homomorphism llbracket α, β rrbracket twoheadrightarrow llbracket α|_U, β|_U rrbracket is a 0,1 -separating homomorphism. For all U ∈ M_ A (α, β) and (x,y) ∈ β \ α , there is some f ∈ Pol _1( A ) such that f( A ) = U and (f(x),f(y)) ∉ α . For all U ∈ M_ A (α, β) , β is the transitive closure of α ∪ cup_ g ∈ Pol _1( A ) g(β|_U) . For all U ∈ M_ A (α, β) and f ∈ Pol _1( A ) such that f(β|_U) ⊄ α , we have f(U) ∈ M_ A (α, β) and f : U simeq f(U) . For any f ∈ Pol _1( A ) such that f(β) ⊄ α , there is some U ∈ M_ A (α,β) such that f : U simeq f(U) . For any (x,y) ∈ β \ α , there is some U ∈ M_ A (α, β) and e ∈ E( A ) such that e( A ) = U and (e(x), e(y)) ∉ α .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If (α,β) is a tame congruence quotient on a finite algebra A and U ∈ M_ A (α,β) , then every unary polynomial f of A |_U is either a permutation of U or has f(β|_U) ⊆ α|_U .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If (α,β) is a tame congruence quotient on A and U ∈ M_ A (α,β) , then a set N ⊆ U is called an (α,β) - trace in U if N is a congruence class of β|_U which is not also a congruence class of α|_U . We define the body of the (α,β) -minimal set U to be the union of the (α,β) -traces, and we define the tail of U to be the set of congruence classes of β|_U which are also congruence classes of α|_U .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: cor-trace-permutational
statement_text: If (α,β) is a tame congruence quotient on a finite algebra A and N is an (α,β) -trace, then every unary polynomial f of A |_N is either a permutation, or has f(N) contained in some congruence class of α|_N . In particular, every unary polynomial of A |_N/α|_N is either a permutation or is constant.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: We say that an algebra is permutational or minimal if every unary polynomial is either a permutation or is constant. More generally, if (α,β) is a congruence quotient on A , we say that A is (α,β) - minimal if every unary polynomial f of A is either a permutation or has f(β) ⊆ α . Note that in this case, (α,β) is necessarily tame, with M_ A (α,β) = {A} .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: cor-trace-iso
statement_text: If (α,β) is a tame congruence quotient on a finite algebra A and N is an (α,β) -trace, then for every unary polynomial f of A either f(N) is contained in some congruence class of α , or f(N) is another (α,β) -trace and f : N simeq f(N) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: cor-trace-closure
statement_text: If (α,β) is a tame congruence quotient on a finite algebra A , then β is the transitive closure of α ∪ {N^2 | N is an (α,β) -trace }.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-prime-poly-iso
statement_text: If (α,β) is a prime congruence quotient of a finite algebra A (i.e., if β is a cover of α ), then all of the (α,β) -traces are polynomially isomorphic in A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If α < β ∈ Con ( A ) and there is some finite (α,β) -minimal set U which satisfies Theorem (c) and (d), then (α,β) is tame.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-tame-quotient
statement_text: If δ ≤ α < β are congruences on a finite algebra A , then (α,β) is tame on A iff (α/δ, β/δ) is tame on A /δ . If (α,β) is tame, then we have M_ A /δ (α/δ,β/δ) = {U/δ | U ∈ M_ A (α,β)}. In particular, the (α/δ,β/δ) -traces are exactly the quotients of the (α,β) -traces by δ .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If (α,β) is a tame congruence quotient on a finite algebra A , and if C is a congruence class of β which is not also a congruence class of α , then A |_C/α|_C is a tame algebra.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If α ≤ γ < β and (α,β), (γ,β) are both tame quotients on a finite algebra A , then M_ A (α,β) = M_ A (γ,β) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-minimal-sets-perspective
statement_text: If llbracket α, β rrbracket searrow llbracket γ, δ rrbracket in Con ( A ) , then M_ A (α,β) = M_ A (γ,δ) and M_ A (γ,β) ⊆ M_ A (γ,α) ∪ M_ A (γ, δ) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If α,β are congruences on a finite algebra and the interval llbracket α, β rrbracket is isomorphic to the diamond lattice M _n for some n ≥ 3 , then (α, β) is tame and every congruence quotient contained in llbracket α, β rrbracket has the same collection of minimal sets.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If (α,β) is a tame congruence quotient on a finite algebra A and U is an (α,β) -minimal set, then for any γ' < δ' ∈ llbracket α|_U ,β|_U rrbracket , there are lifts γ < δ ∈ llbracket α, β rrbracket such that γ|_U = γ', δ|_U = δ' , with (γ,δ) a tame quotient. For any such γ, δ we have M_ A (γ,δ) = M_ A (α,β) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a finite lattice and α < β ∈ Con ( A ) , then the (α,β) -minimal sets all have the form {a,b} with a < b and (a,b) ∈ β \ α , and any pair {a,b} which satisfies those conditions and additionally has b covering a is an (α,β) -minimal set. Each such set with b covering a is the image of the idempotent unary polynomial x mapsto (x ∧ b) ∨ a, however, in order for the restriction homomorphism to be 0,1 -separating, β must be a cover of α . Thus the tame congruence quotients of A are exactly the same as the prime quotients. Additionally, every (α,β) -minimal set consists of just a single (α,β) -trace (i.e., the minimal sets have no tails), and every trace is the image of some pair {a,b} with b covering a under some unary polynomial of A , and is polynomially equivalent to a two element lattice.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a finite module over a ring R (which we may assume acts faithfully on A without loss of generality) and α < β ∈ Con ( A ) , then we can represent the congruences α,β by the submodules M _α = 0/α , M _β = 0/β of A . Every unary polynomial f of A has the form f : x mapsto rx + c , and we have f(β) ⊆ α ⟺ r M _β ⊆ M _α. The set of r ∈ R such that r M _β ⊆ M _α is called the annihilator of M _β/ M _α , and forms a (two-sided) ideal I of R . Then M _β/ M _α is a module over R / I , and R / I acts faithfully on M _β/ M _α . We will show that (α,β) is a tame congruence quotient if and only if I is maximal among two-sided ideals of R , that is, iff R / I is a simple ring. By the classification of finite simple rings, this is equivalent to proving that R / I is isomorphic to a matrix ring M_n( F _ p^k ) over a finite field F _ p^k for some n and some prime power p^k . Additionally, we will show that M _β/ M _α is one of the modules F _ p^k ^ n × m for some m , with the action of R / I on M _β/ M _α given by matrix multiplication. To prove this, it is simpler to think only about the module M _β/ M _α - note that M _β/ M _α is a tame algebra, with (e A ∩ M _β)/ M _α = e M _β/ M _α as a (0,1) -minimal set, for any e ∈ R such that e^2 = e and e A is an (α,β) -minimal set.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that M is a finite module over a finite ring R which acts faithfully on M , and suppose that M is a tame algebra. Then R is isomorphic to a matrix ring M_n( F _ p^k ) over a finite field F _ p^k for some n and some prime power p^k , and M is F _ p^k ^ n × m for some m .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: thm-wedderburn-little
title: Wedderburn's little theorem
statement_text: If R is a finite division ring, then R is a field.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose L is a lattice with a 0 and a 1 . A lattice homomorphism f : L → L ' is 0,1 -separating if we have f^ -1 (f(0)) = {0}, f^ -1 (f(1)) = {1}. A lattice L is 0,1 -simple if it has a 0 and a 1 which are not equal to each other, and if every nonconstant lattice homomorphism L → L ' is 0,1 -separating. A meet endomorphism of a lattice L is a function μ : L → L which preserves ∧ , i.e. such that μ(x ∧ y) = μ(x) ∧ μ(y). A function μ : L → L is called increasing if μ(x) ≥ x for all x ∈ L , and is called strictly increasing if μ(x) > x for all x ∈ L \ {1} . A lattice L is called tight if L is 0,1 -simple and every strictly increasing meet endomorphism of L is constant.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: thm-tight-tame
statement_text: If A is a finite algebra and if the interval llbracket α, β rrbracket of Con ( A ) is tight, then the congruence quotient (α, β) is tame: for every U ∈ M_ A (α, β) , there is an idempotent unary polynomial e ∈ E( A ) such that e( A ) = U .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A lattice L is 0,1 -simple iff there is a unique dual atom θ prec 1_ L ∈ Con ( L ) and the associated map L twoheadrightarrow L /θ is 0,1 -separating.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If a complete lattice L is 0,1 -simple and θ is a proper congruence on L , then L is tight iff L /θ is tight.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A simple lattice L of finite length is tight iff it has no nontrivial tolerances. Equivalently, a 0,1 -simple lattice of finite length is tight iff it has no proper connected tolerances.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If L is a finite lattice, then the following are equivalent: L is simple and tight, for any a < b ∈ L , there is a unary polynomial f of L such that f(a) = 0 and f(b) = 1 , the only compatible binary relations on L which contain the diagonal are the diagonal Δ_ L , the partial orders ≤ _ L and ≥ _ L , and the full relation L ^2 , L is order polynomially complete.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If L is a lattice of finite length, then the smallest connected tolerance on L is generated by the diagonal and the pairs (x,y) such that either y covers x or x covers y .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If the join of the atoms of a 0,1 -simple lattice L of finite length is equal to 1 , or if the meet of the co-atoms is equal to 0 , then L is tight.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: The lattice L _ M of subspaces of a finite-dimensional vector space M over a field F is always tight.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a finite set, then the lattice L _A of equivalence relations on A is tight.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If a lattice L of finite length is complemented, then the join of the atoms of L is 1 and the meet of the co-atoms is 0 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If L twoheadrightarrow L ' is 0,1 -separating, then L is complemented iff L ' is complemented, and the atoms of L join to 1 iff the atoms of L ' join to 1 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If L is a modular lattice of finite length, then the map μ given by μ : x mapsto x ∨ vee{y | x prec y}, which takes x to the join of the collection of covers of x , is a strictly increasing meet endomorphism.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If L is a modular lattice of finite length, then L is tight iff L is simple and complemented.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
