statement_text: An operation f of arity n depends on its i th input if there is some tuple a_1, ..., a_n and some b_i such that f(a_1, ..., a_n) ≠ f(a_1, ..., a_ i-1 , b_i, a_ i+1 , ..., a_n). An operation f is essentially unary if it only depends on one of its inputs - equivalently, f is essentially unary if it can be written as the composition of a projection π_i and a unary operation.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-depend-inputs
title: Salomaa
statement_text: If a polynomial f of arity n depends on all of its inputs, then it is possible to substitute a constant for one of its inputs to get a polynomial of arity n-1 which also depends on all of its inputs. In fact, if n ≥ 2 , then it is possible to find at least two different inputs to f where constants can be substituted to get polynomials depending on all n-1 of their inputs.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: lem-permutational-quasigroup
statement_text: Suppose that f ∈ Pol _2( A ) is a binary polynomial of a finite permutational algebra A which depends on both of its inputs, and suppose that | A | ≥ 3 . Then f is a quasigroup operation, that is, every unary polynomial of the form f(a, · ) or f( · , b) is a permutation.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: cor-permutational-malcev
statement_text: Suppose A is a finite permutational algebra with | A | ≥ 3 , and suppose that some operation of A is not essentially unary. Then A has a Mal'cev polynomial p(x,y,z) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: cor-permutational-depend
statement_text: Suppose A is a finite permutational algebra with | A | ≥ 3 , and suppose f ∈ Pol _n( A ) has f(a_1, ..., a_n) = f(a_1, ..., a_ i-1 , b_i, a_ i+1 , ..., a_n) for some a_1, ..., a_n and some b_i ≠ a_i . Then f does not depend on its i th coordinate.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: lem-permutational-zero
statement_text: Suppose A is a finite permutational algebra with | A | ≥ 3 , f,g ∈ Pol _n( A ) , and suppose that for some 0 ∈ A we have f(x_1, ..., x_n) = g(x_1, ..., x_n) for all x_1, ..., x_n ∈ A such that all but one x_i is 0 . Then f = g .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: thm-permutational-big
title: P\'alfy
statement_text: Suppose A is a finite permutational algebra with | A | ≥ 3 , and suppose that some operation of A is not essentially unary. Then A is affine, and in fact A is polynomially equivalent to a vector space over a finite field.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A has underlying set {0,1} , then A is polynomially complete iff ¬ , ∧ ∈ Pol ( A ) . Additionally, we have ⊕ ∈ Pol ( A ) ⇒ ¬ ∈ Pol ( A ) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: lem-permutational-monotone
statement_text: If A has underlying set {0,1} and if there is some f ∈ Pol ( A ) which is not monotone, then the unary negation ¬ is a polynomial of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: lem-permutational-xor
statement_text: If A has underlying set {0,1} and ⊕ ∈ Pol ( A ) , and if there is any f ∈ Pol ( A ) which is not affine-linear over Z /2 , then ∧ ∈ Pol ( A ) , so A is polynomially complete.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: The polynomial clone of ({0,1}, ∧ , ∨ ) is exactly the clone of all monotone functions.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: lem-permutational-or
statement_text: If A has underlying set {0,1} and ∨ ∈ Pol ( A ) , and if f ∈ Pol ( A ) is monotone but is not contained in the clone generated by ∨ , then ∧ ∈ Pol ( A ) , so Pol ( A ) contains the clone of all monotone functions.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: palfy-five-types
statement_text: If A is a finite permutational algebra, then up to isomorphism and polynomial equivalence, A is one of the following: a unary algebra, with the set of unary operations equal to a finite permutation group, a vector space over a finite field, the boolean algebra ({0,1}, ∨ , ∧ , ¬ ) , the lattice ({0,1}, ∨ , ∧ ) , or the semilattice ({0,1}, ∨ ) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a finite permutational algebra, then Pol ( A ) is generated by the binary polynomials of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If (α,β) is a tame congruence quotient of a finite algebra A , and if N is an (α,β) -trace, then we say that N has unary type , or type 1 , if A |_N/α|_N is polynomially equivalent to a unary algebra, affine type , or type 2 , if A |_N/α|_N is polynomially equivalent to a vector space over a finite field, boolean type , or type 3 , if A |_N/α|_N is polynomially equivalent to a boolean algebra, lattice type , or type 4 , if A |_N/α|_N is polynomially equivalent to a lattice, semilattice type , or type 5 , if A |_N/α|_N is polynomially equivalent to a semilattice. We say that the tame congruence quotient (α,β) has type i if there is any (α,β) -trace with type i . As we will see in the next section, all of the traces of a tame congruence quotient (α,β) have the same type as each other.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A finite algebra A is called (α,β) - minimal , for α < β ∈ Con ( A ) , if for every unary polynomial f ∈ Pol _1( A ) , either f is a permutation or f(β) ⊆ α .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: We say that an idempotent binary operation s is a partial semilattice if it satisfies the identity s(x,s(x,y)) ≈ s(s(x,y),x) ≈ s(x,y). Equivalently, s is a partial semilattice if for all x,y , the set {x,s(x,y)} is closed under s , and acts like a semilattice subalgebra with absorbing element s(x,y) under s . We write a → _s b if s is a partial semilattice and s(a,b) = b .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-tame-partial-semi
statement_text: If A is (α,β) -minimal and has a trace N of type 3 , 4 , or 5 (that is, of either boolean, lattice, or semilattice type), then A has a partial semilattice polynomial s ∈ Pol _2( A ) such that N is closed under s , and such that (N/α, s) is a two-element semilattice. Furthermore, if N has type 3 or 4 (i.e. boolean or lattice type), then there is another partial semilattice s' ∈ Pol _2( A ) such that (N, s, s') is a two-element lattice. If s is a partial semilattice term and a,b ∈ N have s(a,b) not ≡ _α a , then a → _s x for all x ∈ A and a/α = {a} .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-single-trace
statement_text: If A is (α,β) -minimal and has at least two different (α,β) -traces, then all of the (α,β) -traces have type 1 or 2 (that is, they all have either unary or affine type).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-abelian-minimal-set
statement_text: If A is (α,β) -minimal, then β is abelian over α if and only if all of the (α,β) -traces have type 1 or 2 (i.e., unary or affine type).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: lem-pseudo-malcev
statement_text: If A is (α,β) -minimal and has an (α,β) -trace N of type 2 , then there is a ternary polynomial p ∈ Pol _3( A ) such that, if B is the union of all (α,β) -traces (the ``body''), we have N is closed under p , and the restriction of p(x,y,z) to A |_N/α is the Mal'cev operation x - y + z , p is idempotent, that is p(a,a,a) = a for all a ∈ A , for all a ∈ A , b ∈ B we have p(a,b,b) = a , and for all a ∈ A , b ∈ B we have p(b,b,a) = a .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is (α,β) -minimal and has a trace of type 2 (i.e. affine type), and if B is the union of the (α,β) -traces, then we call any idempotent ternary polynomial p ∈ Pol _3( A ) such that p(a,b,b) = p(b,b,a) = a for all a ∈ A and all b ∈ B a pseudo-Mal'cev polynomial for A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: thm-pseudo-malcev
statement_text: Suppose that A is (α,β) -minimal and has a trace of type 2 (i.e. affine type), let B be the union of the (α,β) -traces, and let p be any pseudo-Mal'cev polynomial for A . Then for all a,b ∈ B , the unary polynomials x mapsto p(x,a,b), p(a,x,b), p(a,b,x) are all permutations, B is closed under p and the restriction of p to B is Mal'cev, and all of the (α,β) -traces are polynomially isomorphic. In particular, if one of the (α,β) -traces has type 2 then they all do.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: thm-same-type
statement_text: If (α,β) is a tame congruence of a finite algebra A , then all of the (α,β) -traces have the same type. If this type is not 1 , or if (α,β) is a prime quotient, then all of the (α,β) -traces are polynomially isomorphic to each other. If the type is not 1 or 2 , then each (α,β) -minimal set has just one trace, and if the type is 3 or 4 then every (α,β) -trace has size two.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If α ≤ β ∈ Con ( A ) , then β is strongly abelian over α if for all f ∈ Pol ( A ) , all (u,v) ∈ β and all tuples x, y, z with x_i ≡ y_i ≡ z_i pmod β , we have f(u,x_1, ..., x_n) ≡ _α f(v, y_1, ..., y_n) ⇒ f(u, z_1, ..., z_n) ≡ _α f(v, z_1, ..., z_n). An algebra A is strongly abelian if 1_ A is strongly abelian over 0_ A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-strong-abelian-minimal-set
statement_text: If A is (α,β) -minimal, then β is strongly abelian over α iff all of the (α,β) -traces have type 1 (i.e. unary type).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose that A has a Taylor polynomial and that α < β ∈ Con ( A ) . Then β is not strongly abelian over α . As a consequence, if A is a finite Taylor algebra then no tame congruence quotient of A has type 1 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: An algebra A is strongly abelian iff, for each n -ary polynomial t of A , there are equivalence relations R_i on A such that t(a_1, ..., a_n) = t(b_1, ..., b_n) ⟺ ∀ i ≤ n, (a_i, b_i) ∈ R_i. In particular, if A is finite and strongly abelian then every polynomial of A depends on at most log _2| A | of its inputs.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Every finite, idempotent, strongly abelian algebra can be written as a product of algebras where every operation is a projection.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A rectangular band is an idempotent semigroup which satisfies the identity xyx ≈ x. This identity implies the apparently stronger identity xyz ≈ xz, as follows: xyz ≈ xy(zxz) ≈ (xyzx)z ≈ xz. Every rectangular band A is strongly abelian, and is therefore isomorphic to a product of two semigroups A _1, A _2 such that · ^ A _1 = π_1 and · ^ A _2 = π_2 . The multiplication on the rectangular band A _1 × A _2 is explicitly given by the rule (a,b) · (c,d) = (a,d).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: ex-strongly-abelian-not-quasiaffine
title: From
statement_text: There is a 5 -element strongly abelian algebra A = ({a,b,c,d,e}, · _1, · _2) which is not quasiaffine (of course, this algebra is not idempotent). The basic binary operations of A are given below. cc c | c c c c c · _1 & a & b & c & d & e hline a & a & b & a & b & b b & a & b & a & b & b c & c & d & c & d & d d & c & d & c & d & d e & c & d & c & d & d & c | c c c c c · _2 & a & b & c & d & e hline a & a & b & a & b & b b & a & b & a & b & b c & c & e & c & e & e d & c & e & c & e & e e & c & e & c & e & e This algebra fails to be quasiaffine because it fails to satisfy the two term condition: a · _1 a = a · _2 a, a · _1 b = a · _2 b, c · _1 a = c · _2 a, but c · _1 b ≠ c · _2 b. To see that it is strongly abelian, note that for each i,j we have the identities x · _i (y · _j z) ≈ x · _i z, (x · _i y) · _j z ≈ x · _j z, so every term operation of A is one of x, x · _i x, x · _i y for some i ∈ {1,2} , up to permuting its inputs.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A p -cyclic groupoid is an idempotent binary operation · which satisfies the following identities: x(yz) & ≈ xy, (xy)z & ≈ (xz)y, (...((xunderbrace y)y) ... ) y _ p y s & ≈ x. See for the theory of p -cyclic groupoids for arbitrary primes p . The free 2 -cyclic groupoid on two generators a,b is isomorphic to the idempotent algebra A = ({a,b,c,d}, · ) with basic operation · given below. c | c c c c · & a & b & c & d hline a & a & c & a & c b & d & b & d & b c & c & a & c & a d & b & d & b & d This algebra has a congruence θ corresponding to the partition {a,c}, {b,d} , such that · on A /θ is first projection - in particular, 1_ A is strongly abelian over θ . Additionally, θ is strongly abelian over 0_ A , so A is strongly solvable. The algebra A is (0_ A ,θ) -minimal, and the (0_ A ,θ) -traces are {a,c} and {b,d} . The reader may check that the (0_ A ,θ) -traces {a,c} and {b,d} are not polynomially isomorphic in A . The algebra A |_ {a,c} is polynomially equivalent to the unary algebra with the unary operation which swaps a and c , corresponding to the polynomial x mapsto x · b . The reader may check that A is abelian (and even quasiaffine) as well. If we let η be the congruence corresponding to the partition {a}, {c}, {b,d} , however, then we see that A /η is not abelian - so quotients of idempotent abelian algebras are not necessarily abelian. This is one of the senses in which type 1 can be pathological. More generally, the free p -cyclic groupoid on n generators is (up to isomorphism) the subalgebra of (( Z /p^2)^n, (x,y) mapsto x + p(y-x) ) generated by the basis vectors (1,0,...,0), (0,1,...,0), ..., (0,...,0,1) - this algebra has np^ n-1 elements. The free p -cyclic groupoid on n generators is always quasiaffine and strongly solvable in 2 steps via the congruence corresponding to reduction modulo p , and for p,n ≥ 2 it always has a quotient which is not abelian.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: type-strong-abelian
statement_text: If A is a finite algebra and (α, β) is a tame congruence quotient, then β is strongly abelian over α if and only if the type of (α, β) is 1 (i.e., unary).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: type-abelian
statement_text: If A is a finite algebra and (α, β) is a tame congruence quotient, then β is abelian over α if and only if the type of (α, β) is 1 or 2 (i.e., unary or affine type).

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a finite algebra and if the interval llbracket α, β rrbracket is a tight sublattice of Con ( A ) of size at least 3 , then β is abelian over α . If additionally llbracket α, β rrbracket does not have a 0,1 -separating homomorphism onto the congruence lattice of a vector space, then β is strongly abelian over α .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If α is a congruence on A and R is a binary relation on A , then we say that R is α -closed if whenever (a,b) ∈ R and a ≡ c pmod α , b ≡ d pmod α , we also have (c,d) ∈ R . We define the α -closure of R to be the binary relation α ∘ R ∘ α.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: For α ∈ Con ( A ) and R ≤ A ^2 , the α -closure of R is the smallest α -closed relation on A which contains R . There is a bijection between α -closed binary relations on A and binary relations on A /α .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: thm-basic-tolerance
statement_text: If (α,β) is a prime congruence quotient of a finite algebra A with type different from 1 , then there is a unique minimal α -closed tolerance τ with α ⊊ τ ⊆ β. This tolerance τ is the α -closure of the relation Sg _ A ^2 (Δ_ A ∪ {N^2 | N is an (α,β) -trace } ). Furthermore, if the type is 2 or 3 , then τ is also minimal among reflexive α -closed relations which properly contain α and are contained in β .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If the type is equal to 1 , then there might not be a unique minimal α -closed tolerance containing α . Consider the unary algebra A = ( Z /5, x mapsto x+1 pmod 5 ) , which is simple and permutational. The minimal tolerances of A are τ_1 = {(x,y) | x-y ∈ {-1,0,1} pmod 5 } and τ_2 = {(x,y) | x-y ∈ {-2,0,2} pmod 5 }.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If (α,β) is a prime congruence quotient with type different from 1 , then we define the basic tolerance of (α,β) to be the minimal α -closed tolerance τ with α ⊊ τ ⊆ β .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If (α,β) is a prime congruence quotient of a finite algebra A with type 2 or 3 , then the basic tolerance of (α,β) is just the α -closure of Δ_ A ∪ {N^2 | N is an (α,β) -trace }, without needing to apply Sg _ A ^2 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: thm-basic-reflexive
statement_text: If (α,β) is a prime congruence quotient of a finite algebra A with type 4 or 5 , then there are exactly two minimal α -closed reflexive relations ρ_0, ρ_1 which strictly contain α and are contained in β . These relations have the following properties: ρ_1 = ρ_0^- , that is, ρ_1 = {(y,x) | (x,y) ∈ ρ_0} , ρ_0 ∩ ρ_1 = α , ρ_0 ∪ ρ_1 is the α -closure of Δ_ A ∪ {N^2 | N is an (α,β) -trace } , the basic tolerance of (α,β) is the α -closure of Sg _ A ^2 (ρ_0 ∪ ρ_1) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: We say that a compatible binary relation ζ ≤ A ^2 is an (α,β) -preorder if ζ is a quasiorder on A , ζ ∩ ζ^- = α , and the transitive closure of ζ ∪ ζ^- is β . Note that every compatible quasiorder ζ on A is an (α,β) -preorder for some pair of congruences (α,β) , since the transitive closure of ζ ∪ ζ^- is exactly the linking congruence of ζ . We say that a congruence quotient (α,β) is orderable if an (α,β) -preorder exists.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If (α,β) is a tame congruence quotient with type different from 1 , then (α, β) is orderable if and only if the type of (α,β) is 4 or 5 . In fact, if the type of (α,β) is 4 or 5 , then there are exactly two minimal (α,β) -preorders ζ_0, ζ_1 and two maximal (α,β) -preorders ξ_0, ξ_1 such that every (α,β) -preorder η satisfies ζ_i ⊆ η ⊆ ξ_i for either i = 0 or i = 1 .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If the type of (α,β) is 1 , then (α,β) can sometimes be orderable and sometimes not. To see this, consider the unary algebra A _1 = ({0,1}) with no operations, and the unary algebra A _2 = ({0,1}, 1-x) with just a single operation which swaps the two elements. Then (0_ A _1 ,1_ A _1 ) is orderable but (0_ A _2 , 1_ A _2 ) is not.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is an algebra, then an ordered pair of elements (a,b) ∈ A ^2 is a 2-snag if there is a binary polynomial s ∈ Pol _2( A ) such that s(a,a) = s(a,b) = s(b,a) = a, s(b,b) = b. In other words, we require ({a,b},s) to be a semilattice with b → _s a . We write Sn _2( A ) ⊆ A ^2 for the set of 2-snags of A .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is an algebra, then an ordered pair of elements (a,b) ∈ A ^2 is a 1-snag if there is a binary polynomial s ∈ Pol _2( A ) such that s(a,b) = s(b,a) = a, s(b,b) = b. We write Sn _1( A ) for the set of 1-snags of A , and note that Sn _2( A ) ⊆ Sn _1( A ) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If (α,β) is a tame congruence quotient of a finite algebra A , then β is abelian over α iff β ∩ Sn _2( A ) = α ∩ Sn _2( A ) , and β is strongly abelian over α iff β ∩ Sn _1( A ) = α ∩ Sn _1( A ) . As a consequence, for any α ≤ β ∈ Con ( A ) , we have β is solvable over α iff β ∩ Sn _2( A ) = α ∩ Sn _2( A ) , and β is strongly solvable over α iff β ∩ Sn _1( A ) = α ∩ Sn _1( A ) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is an algebra and α, β ∈ Con ( A ) , then we write α stackrel s β when β ∩ Sn _2( A ) = α ∩ Sn _2( A ) , and α stackrel ss β when β ∩ Sn _1( A ) = α ∩ Sn _1( A ) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: thm-locally-solvable-congruence
statement_text: If A is a finite algebra, then each of the equivalence relations stackrel s , stackrel ss defines a congruence on the lattice Con ( A ) . In particular, we have α stackrel s β iff α ∨ β is solvable over α ∧ β , and similarly α stackrel ss β iff α ∨ β is strongly solvable over α ∧ β .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is a locally finite algebra, then each of the equivalence relations stackrel s , stackrel ss defines a congruence on the lattice Con ( A ) . In particular, we have α stackrel s β iff α ∨ β|_ B is solvable over α ∧ β|_ B for every finite subalgebra B of A , and similarly for stackrel ss .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-solvable-quotient-algebraic
statement_text: If A is locally finite, then the congruences stackrel s , stackrel ss are compatible with arbitrary meets and joins, and the lattices Con ( A )/ stackrel s , Con ( A )/ stackrel ss are algebraic.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is locally finite and α, β, γ ∈ Con ( A ) form a copy of the pentagon lattice N _5 with α ∧ γ ≤ β ≤ γ ≤ α ∨ β, then α stackrel s α ∧ γ ⇒ β stackrel ss γ.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is locally finite, then every equivalence class of stackrel s / stackrel ss is a modular sublattice of Con ( A )/ stackrel ss .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If V is a locally finite variety, then we say that V omits type i if for every finite A ∈ V and every tame congruence quotient (α,β) of A , the type of (α,β) is not i . We write typ ( V ) for the set of types which V does not omit.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If V is a locally finite variety, then the locally solvable algebras in V form a subvariety V _s , and similarly the locally strongly solvable algebras in V form a subvariety V _ ss .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If V is a locally finite variety which omits type 1 , then the subvariety V _s of locally solvable algebras in V has a Mal'cev term.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If A is finite and B preceq _| A is such that every constant of B is a term operation of B , then typ ( V ( B )) ⊆ typ ( V ( A )) .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: thm-loc-solvable-malcev
statement_text: If V is a locally finite variety which omits type 1 , then V has an idempotent ternary term p such that for any A ∈ V and any a,b ∈ A , Cg _ A {(a,b)} stackrel s 0_ A ⇒ p(a,b,b) = p(b,b,a) = a.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: An idempotent ternary term p is called a weak difference term for V if for any A ∈ V , any a,b ∈ A , and any θ ∈ Con ( A ) with (a,b) ∈ θ , we have p(a,b,b) ≡ _ [θ,θ] p(b,b,a) ≡ _ [θ,θ] a.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A locally finite variety omits type 1 iff it has a weak difference term. In particular, every locally finite Taylor variety has a weak difference term.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If V is a locally finite variety which omits type 1 , A ∈ V , and α, β ∈ Con ( A ) , then α stackrel s β ⇒ α ∨ β = α ∘ β = β ∘ α.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If V is a locally finite variety which omits type 1 , A ∈ V , and α, β ∈ Con ( A ) , then β stackrel s α ∧ β ⇒ α ∨ β = α ∘ β ∘ α.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If L is a lattice and α ≤ β ∈ L , then we say that δ is the weak pseudocomplement of β over α if δ is the greatest element of L such that β ∧ δ = α , that is, if β ∧ γ = α ⟺ γ ∈ llbracket α, δ rrbracket . A closely related concept is the relative pseudocomplement: for any α, β ∈ L , δ is called the relative pseudocomplement of β with respect to α if β ∧ γ ≤ α ⟺ γ ≤ δ, and this is written in symbols as δ = β → α or δ = β thinsupset α . If α = 0 , then a weak or relative pseudocomplement δ of β over 0 is just called a pseudocomplement of β , and written in symbols as δ = ¬ β or δ = β^* . Similarly, for α ≤ β ∈ L we say that δ is the dual weak pseudocomplement of α under β if α ∨ γ = β ⟺ γ ∈ llbracket δ, β rrbracket . Additionally, for any α, β ∈ L , δ is called the dual relative pseudocomplement of α with respect to β if α ∨ γ ≥ β ⟺ γ ≥ δ, and some authors write this in symbols as δ = β - α or δ = β backslash α .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: If α ≤ β ∈ L and the relative pseudocomplement of β with respect to α exists and is equal to δ , then δ is also the weak pseudocomplement of β over α .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A Heyting algebra is an algebraic structure H = (H, ∧ , ∨ , thinsupset , 0, 1) such that (H, ∧ , ∨ , 0, 1) is a 0,1 -lattice and for every pair of elements α, β ∈ H , β thinsupset α is the relative pseudocomplement of β with respect to α .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: heyting-distributive
statement_text: A complete lattice is the lattice reduct of a Heyting algebra iff it satisfies the infinite distributive law α ∧ ( vee_ β ∈ S β ) = vee_ β ∈ S (α ∧ β). tag D _ ∞ ( ∧ )

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: A lattice L is meet-semidistributive , written SD( ∧ ), if for all α, β, γ ∈ L we have α ∧ β = α ∧ γ ⇒ α ∧ (β ∨ γ) = α ∧ β. Similarly, a lattice L is join-semidistributive , written SD( ∨ ), if for all α, β, γ ∈ L we have α ∨ β = α ∨ γ ⇒ α ∨ (β ∧ γ) = α ∨ β. A lattice is called semidistributive if it is both meet-semidistributive and join-semidistributive.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-infinite-semidistributive-algebraic
statement_text: An algebraic lattice L is meet-semidistributive iff for all α ≤ β ∈ L , there is a weak pseudocomplement of β over α . In this case, L also satisfies the following infinite form of meet-semidistributivity: ∀ i,j\ α ∧ β_i = α ∧ β_j \ ⇒ \ ∀ i\ α ∧ ( vee_j β_j ) = α ∧ β_i. tag SD _ ∞ ( ∧ )

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-semidistributive-prime-pseudocomplement
statement_text: If α ∧ β = α ∧ γ = δ but α ∧ (β ∨ γ) ≠ δ , then for any ε such that δ prec ε ≤ α ∧ (β ∨ γ), there is no weak pseudocomplement of ε over δ .

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
label: prop-centralizer-pseudocomplement
statement_text: If (α, β) is a nonabelian prime congruence quotient on A , then the relative centralizer (α : β) is the weak pseudocomplement of β over α in Con ( A ) . In particular, in this case the weak pseudocomplement of β over α exists. More generally, if α ≤ β then (α : β) is the weak pseudocomplement of β over α if and only if β ∧ (α : β) = α, and this occurs if the lattice llbracket α, β rrbracket is atomic and every prime congruence quotient (α,δ) with α prec δ ≤ β is nonabelian.

paper_title: Notes on CSPs and Polymorphisms
statement_text: Suppose (α,β) is a nonabelian prime congruence quotient on a finite algebra A . Let U ∈ M_ A (α,β) be any (α,β) -minimal set, and as in Proposition let a ∈ U be an element of the unique (α,β) -trace N , such that there is a partial semilattice polynomial s ∈ Pol ( A |_U) with s(a,x) = x for all x ∈ U . paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: def.sv
title: SV generator
statement_text: The Shpilka--Volkovich (SV) Generator for @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n] is paramet\-rized by the following data: A positive integer l . For each i ∈ [n] , a distinct abscissa a_i ∈ @ifstar F . The generator @ifstar G * SV ^ l takes as seed l pairs of fresh variables (y_1,z_1), ... ,(y_l,z_l) and substitutes x_igets Σ _ t=1 ^l z_t · L_i(y_t), where the Lagrange interpolant L_i is the unique univariate polynomial of degree at most n-1 satisfying L_i(a_i)=1 and L_i(a_j) = 0 for j ∈ [n] \ {i} .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: def.rfegen
title: RFE generator
statement_text: The Rational Function Evaluation Generator (RFE) for @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n] is parametrized by the following data: A non-negative integer k , the numerator degree . A non-negative integer l , the denominator degree . For each i ∈ [n] , a distinct abscissa a_i ∈ @ifstar F . The generator @ifstar G * RFE ^ k _ l takes as seed a rational function f ∈ @ifstar F (α) such that f can be written as g/h for some g,h ∈ @ifstar F [α] with deg (g) ≤ k , deg (h) ≤ l , and h(a_i) ≠ 0 for all i ∈ [n] . From f , it generates the substitution x_i gets f(a_i) for each i ∈ [n] .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: thm.ideal.generators
title: generating set
statement_text: Let k, l, n ∈ N and let a_i for i ∈ [n] be distinct elements of @ifstar F . The vanishing ideal of @ifstar G * RFE ^ k _ l in @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n] for the given choice of abscissas (a_i)_ i ∈ [n] is generated by the following polynomials over all choices of k+l+2 indices i_1, i_2, ... , i_ k+l+2 ∈ [n] : EVC ^ k _ l [i_1,i_2, ... , i_ k+l+2 ] doteq det a_ i_j ^ k & a_ i_j ^ k-1 & ... & 1 & a_ i_j ^l x_ i_j & a_ i_j ^ l-1 x_ i_j & ... & x_ i_j _ j=1 ^ k+l+2 . Moreover, for any fixed set C ⊆ [n] of size k+1 , the polynomials EVC ^ k _ l [C sqcup L] form a generating set of minimum size when L ranges over all (l+1) -subsets of [n] that are disjoint from C , where EVC ^ k _ l [S] doteq EVC ^ k _ l [i_1,i_2, ... ,i_ |S| ] for S = {i_1, ... , i_ |S| } ⊆ [n] with i_1 < i_2 < ... < i_ |S| .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: ex.rfe01
statement_text: Consider the special case where k=0 and l=1 . The generator for Van [@ifstar G * RFE ^ 0 _ 1 ] when i_1=1 , i_2=2 , and i_3=3 is given by EVC ^ 0 _ 1 [1,2,3] doteq 1 & a_1 x_1 & x_1 1 & a_2 x_2 & x_2 1 & a_3 x_3 & x_3 = (a_1-a_2)x_1x_2 + (a_2-a_3)x_2x_3 + (a_3-a_1)x_3x_1. For any fixed i^* ∈ [n] , the polynomials EVC ^ 0 _ 1 [S] form a generating set of minimum size when S ranges over all subsets of [n] of size 3 that contain C = {i^*} . As an aside, they also constitute minimal polynomials not computable by read-once formulas, which is consistent with the fact that @ifstar G * SV ^ 1 hits all read-once formulas (see Theorem ).

label: thm.ideal.membership

statement_text: Let k, l, n ∈ N and let a_i for i ∈ [n] be distinct elements of @ifstar F . A multilinear polynomial p ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n] belongs to Van [@ifstar Gen@star G * RFE ^ k _ l ] if and only if both of the following conditions hold: There are no monomials of degree l or less, nor of degree n-k or more, in p . For all disjoint subsets K,L ⊆ [n] with |K|=k and |L|=l , .partial _ L p |_ K gets 0 is zero upon the following substitution for each i ∈ [n] \ (K ∪ L) , where z denotes a fresh variable: x_i gets z · frac Π _ j ∈ K (a_i - a_ j ) Π _ j ∈ L (a_i - a_ j ) .

label: prop.vangen.basic
statement_text: For every k,l ∈ N , EVC ^ k _ l is skew-symmetric in that, for any i_1, ... ,i_ k+l+2 ∈ [n] and permutation π of [k+l+2] , EVC ^ k _ l [i_1, ... , i_ k+l+2 ] = sign (π) · EVC ^ k _ l [i_ π(1) , ... ,i_ π(k+l+2) )]. For any S ⊆ [n] with |S|=k+l+2 , EVC ^ k _ l [S] is a nonzero, multilinear, and homogeneous polynomial of total degree l+1 , and every multilinear monomial of degree l+1 in x_ i_1 , ... ,x_ i_ k+l+2 appears with a nonzero coefficient. More specifically, for S = {i_1, ... , i_ k+l+2 } ⊆ [n] with i_1 < i_2 < ... , i_ k+l+2 , EVC ^ k _ l [S] = Σ _ substack Ksqcup L= S |L|=l+1 γ_ K,L · Π _ i ∈ L x_i, where γ_ K,L doteq (-1)^ XInv (K,L) · det (A_ K ) · det (A_ L ).

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: def.sunform
title: monomial support and cored polynomial
statement_text: The support of a monomial m ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n] , denoted supp (m) , is the set of indices i ∈ [n] such that m depends on x_i . For c,t ∈ N , a polynomial p ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n] is said to be (c,t) -cored if there exists C ⊆ [n] , called the core , such that |C| ≤ c and for every monomial m of p , | supp (m) \ C| ≤ t . For any subset C ⊆ [n] and monomial m = Π _ i ∈ [n] x_i^ d_i , we call Π _ i ∈ C x_i^ d_i the C -part of m , and Π _ i ∈ [n] \ C x_i^ d_i the non- C -part of m .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: prop.lem.vangen-coredform
statement_text: Let k,l,n ∈ N , let C be a (k+1) -subset of [n] , and let I denote the ideal generated by the polynomials EVC ^ k _ l [C sqcup L] where L ranges over all (l+1) -subsets of [n] \ C . Consider a monomial m ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n] such that | supp (m) \ C| > l . Modulo I , m is equal to a linear combination of monomials whose non- C -parts have lower degree than the non- C -part of m .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: lem.vangen-coredform
statement_text: Let k,l,n ∈ N , let C be a (k+1) -subset of [n] , and let I be the ideal generated by the polynomials EVC ^ k _ l [C sqcup L] where L ranges over all (l+1) -subsets of [n] \ C . Modulo I , every polynomial is equal to a (k+1,l) -cored polynomial with core C .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: cor-gen-sv
statement_text: Let l, n ∈ N and let a_i for i ∈ [n] be distinct elements of @ifstar F . For any fixed set C ⊆ [n] of size l , the polynomials EVCSV ^ l [C sqcup L] form a generating set of minimum size for Van [ @ifstar Gen@star G * SV ^ l ] when L ranges over all (l+1) -subsets of [n] that are disjoint from C . paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: def.degree-pattern
title: degree pattern
statement_text: Let J ⊆ [n] . A degree pattern with domain J is a J -indexed tuple d ∈ N ^J of nonnegative integers. A degree pattern d matches a monomial m ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n] if, for every j ∈ J , m has degree exactly d_j in x_j . We say that d is in p if d matches some monomial in p . For any fixed J , every polynomial p ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n] can be written uniquely in the form p = Σ _ d ∈ N ^J p_d · x^d where x^ smash d doteq Π _ j ∈ J x_j^ smash d_j and p_d depends only on variables not indexed by J . We refer to p_d as the coefficient of x^d in p .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: def.extremal

statement_text: Let K, L ⊆ [n] . A degree pattern d^* ∈ N ^ K ∪ L is (K,L) -extremal in a polynomial p ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n] if d^* is the unique degree pattern d ∈ N ^ K ∪ L in p that satisfies both d_j ≤ d^*_j for all j ∈ K , and d_j ≥ d^*_j for all j ∈ L .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: eq.multi-zsub-deriv.sub

statement_text: Let K,L ⊆ [n] , let p ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n] , and let d^* ∈ N ^ K ∪ L be a degree pattern that is (K,L) -extremal in p . If the coefficient p_ d^* is nonzero upon the substitution x_i gets z · frac Π _ j ∈ K \ L ( a_i - a_j ) Π _ j ∈ L \ K ( a_i - a_j ) ∀ i ∈ [n] \ (K ∪ L) where z is a fresh variable, then @ifstar G * RFE ^ k _ l hits p for any k ≥ |K| and l ≥ |L| .

label: prop.multi-zsub-deriv.helper
statement_text: Let @ifstar F = @ifstar F (ζ_1, ... ,ζ_r) be the field of rational functions in indeterminates ζ_1, ... , ζ_r , let V ⊆ @ifstar F consist of the rational functions whose denominator has nonzero constant term, and let Φ : V → @ifstar F be the function that maps each rational function in V to its value after substituting ζ_j gets 0 for all j ∈ [r] . label: lem.membership-coredform

label: def.smvan1

paper_title: On the amortized complexity of approximate counting
title: (k,ε,δ) -approximate counter
statement_text: Let N_1, ... , N_k be k counters all initially set to 0 . We say a randomized algorithm A is a (k,ε,δ) -approximate counter if it supports two operations: increment ( i ) increments N_i by 1 , and query ( i ) returns a value N_i such that P (| N _i - N_i| ≥ ε N_i ) ≤ δ. When k =1 , we will simply call this an (ε, δ) -approximate counter.

paper_title: On the amortized complexity of approximate counting
statement_text: For any δ < c_1 and ε < c_2/ log log (1/δ) , if k < c_3 n then after a sequence of at most n updates any (k,ε,δ) -counter must use Ω(kmin { log (n/k), log log (n/k) + log (1/ε) + log log (1/δ)}) bits of memory in expectation. Else if k > c_3 n , then a lower bound of Ω(n log (2 k/(c_3 n))) holds; c_1, c_2, c_3 ≥ 0 are universal constants. Furthermore, for both ranges of k , these lower bounds are tight up to constant factors.

paper_title: On the amortized complexity of approximate counting
label: prop:chain_rule
title: Chain rule
statement_text: For random variables X_1, X_2, Y, Z we have I(X_1,X_2 ; Y | Z) = I(X_1 ; Y | Z, X_2) + I(X_2 ; Y | Z).

There is a distribution D over inputs such that the information cost of A on (X_1, ... , X_n) D satisfies IC ( A ; D ) = Ω(n log log (1/δ) ), where P [ Σ _ i=1 ^n X_i ≤ n] = 1 and n ≥ c_3 log ^ c_4 (1/δ) . This implies the space lower bound (1)/(n) Σ _ i=1 ^ n E |M_i| = Ω( log log (1/δ)) = Ω(min { log n, log log (1/δ)}).

statement_text: For any ε ∈ (0,c_1) , δ ∈ (0, c_2) and 1<k ≤ n , any (k,ε, δ) -approximate counter A that maintains k counters with total sum at most n must use |M| = Ω (min {k log (n/k), k log (1/ε) + k log log (n/k)} ) bits of memory.

paper_title: On the amortized complexity of approximate counting
statement_text: An error correcting code C of length k over a finite alphabet Σ is a subset of Σ^k . The elements of C are called code words . The distance of the code C , denoted Δ(C) , is defined as the minimum hamming distance between any two code words c_1, c_2 ∈ C , i.e. Δ(C) := min _ substack c, c' ∈ C c ≠ c' Δ(c, c'), where Δ(c, c') := |{i : c_i ≠ c_i' }| is the hamming distance between two vectors.

statement_text: For any alphabet size q > 1 , code length k and distance d ≤ k , there exists an error correcting code C with size, |C| ≥ frac q^k Σ _ i=0 ^ d-1 binom k i (q-1)^i . Consequently, for d = 0.9 k and any q larger than a universal constant, there is a code C with size |C| ≥ q^ 0.05k .

paper_title: On the amortized complexity of approximate counting
label: thm:ny22
statement_text: For any ε,δ ∈ (0,1/2) , there is an (ε,δ) -approximate counter with expected space usage O( log log N + log log (1/δ) + log (1/ε)) bits.

paper_title: On the amortized complexity of approximate counting
label: cor:ub
statement_text: For any ε,δ ∈ (0,1/2) and 1 ≤ k ≤ N , there is a (k,ε,δ) -approximate counter that uses O(k( log log (2N/k) + log log (1/δ) + log (1/ε))) bits in expectation.

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
title: ranking, inversion, Inv _ · ( · )
statement_text: A ranking ρ of a set X of n items is a bijection from X to [n] . Given two rankings σ and ρ , an inversion of σ with respect to ρ is a pair of items x_1,x_2 ∈ X such that ρ(x_1) < ρ(x_2) but σ(x_1) > σ(x_2) . The number of inversions is denoted by Inv _ρ(σ) . An inversion in an array A of values is an inversion of σ with respect to ρ where σ denotes the ranking by array index and ρ the ranking by value; in this setting we write Inv (A) for Inv _ρ(σ) .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
title: cross inversions, XInv _ · ( · , · )
statement_text: Let ρ be a ranking of X , and A, B ⊆ X . A cross inversion from A to B with respect to ρ is a pair (x_1,x_2) ∈ A × B that is out of order with respect to ρ , i.e., such that ρ(x_1) > ρ(x_2) . The number of cross inversions is denoted by XInv _ρ(A,B) . For two arrays A and B of values, a cross inversion from A to B is a cross inversion from the set of entries in A to the set of entries in B where ρ denotes the ranking by value; in this setting we write XInv (A,B) for XInv _ρ(A,B) .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
title: inversion minimization on trees, MinInv ( · , · ) , Π_ ·
statement_text: Inversion minimization on trees is the computational problem with the following specification: A rooted tree T with leaf set X of size n , and a ranking ρ of X . MinInv (T,ρ) , the minimum of Inv _ρ(σ) over all possible orderings of T , where σ denotes the left-to-right ranking of X induced by the ordering of T . For any fixed tree T with leaf set X , we use the short-hand Π_T to denote the computational problem that takes as input a ranking ρ of X and outputs MinInv (T,ρ) .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
title: leaf set, L ( · ) , and subtree
statement_text: For a tree T , the leaf set of T , denoted L (T) , is the set of leaves of T . For a node v to T , T_v denotes the subtree of T rooted at v .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: thm:main:general
title: lower bound for general trees
statement_text: Let T be a tree with n leaves, and v a node with | L (T_v) | = ℓ . The query complexity of inversion minimization on T is at least log _2(Γ( ( ℓ (n- ℓ ))/(n)+1 )) . In particular, the complexity is at least log _2(Γ((k)/((k+1)^2) · n+1)) where k denotes the degree of T .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: thm:main:binary
title: lower bound for binary trees
statement_text: For binary trees T with n leaves, the query complexity of inversion minimization on T is at least log _2(n!) - O( log n) .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: def:leaf-child-set
title: leaf child set, LC ( · )
statement_text: The leaf child set LC (v) of a vertex v in a tree T is the set LC (v) of all the children of v that are leaves in T .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: thm:main:special
title: lower bound for restricted classes
statement_text: Let T be a tree without nodes of degree 1 such that the leaf child sets have size at most k , at most one of them is odd, and if there exists an odd one, say LC (v^*) , then all ancestors of v^* have empty leaf child sets. The query complexity of inversion minimization on T is at least log _2(n!) - O(k log k) . In particular, the lower bound applies to: perfect trees of even degree k , and full binary ( k=2 ) trees with at most one leaf without a sibling leaf.

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: thm:Mann-Whitney
title: lower bound for counting cross inversions
statement_text: Counting cross inversions from a set A of size a to a set B of size b ≥ a with respect to a ranking ρ of X doteq A sqcup B requires Ω((a+b) log (a)) queries in the comparison-query model, as does inversion minimization on the tree of Figure .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: def:computational-problem
title: computational problem and algorithm in the comparison-query model
statement_text: A computational problem in the comparison-query model is a total function on the rankings of a set X . An algorithm in the comparison-query model can access an input ranking ρ: X → [n] using comparison queries: For given x_1,x_2 ∈ X , test if ρ(x_1)< ρ(x_2) .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: def:execution-and-deterministic
title: execution trace, complexity measures D ( · ) and Q ( · )
statement_text: Consider an algorithm A for a problem Π in the comparison-query model. An execution trace of A is the sequence of comparisons that A makes on some input ρ , as well as the outcomes of the comparisons. The complexity D (Π) is the minimum over all possible algorithms for Π of the number of distinct traces the algorithm has over the set of all inputs ρ . The complexity Q (Π) is the minimum, over all possible algorithms for Π of the maximum number of comparisons that the algorithm makes over the set of all inputs ρ .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
title: adjacent-rank transposition, affected items
statement_text: An adjacent-rank transposition is a permutation τ of [n] of the form τ = (r,r+1) , where r ∈ [n-1] and n denotes the number of items. Given τ and a ranking ρ: X → [n] , the affected items are the two elements x ∈ X for which τ(ρ(x)) ≠ ρ(x) , i.e., the items with ranks r and r+1 under ρ .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: def:sensitivity
title: sensitivity, average sensitivity, s( · )
statement_text: Let Π be a computational problem in the comparison-query model on a set X of items. For a fixed ranking ρ and adjacent-rank transposition τ , we say that Π is sensitive to τ at ρ if Π(ρ) ≠ Π(τ ρ) . The sensitivity of Π at ρ is the number of adjacent-rank transpositions τ such that Π is sensitive to τ at ρ . The average sensitivity of Π , denoted s(Π) , is the average sensitivity of Π at ρ when ρ is drawn uniformly at random from all rankings of X .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: lemma:sensitivity
title: Sensitivity Lemma
statement_text: For any problem Π in the comparison-query model with n items, D (Π) ≥ Γ(s(Π)+2)/n .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
title: permutahedron graph, G( · ) , G ( · )
statement_text: Let Π be a computational problem in the comparison-query model on a set X of items. The permutahedron graph of Π , denoted G(Π) , has the rankings of X as vertices, and an edge between two rankings ρ_1 and ρ_2 if Π(ρ_1) = Π(ρ_2) and there exists an adjacent-rank transposition such that ρ_2 = τ ρ_1 . The complementary permutahedron graph of Π , denoted G (Π) , is defined similarly by replacing the condition Π(ρ_1) = Π(ρ_2) by its complement, Π(ρ_1) ≠ Π(ρ_2) .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: lemma:connectivity
title: Connectivity Lemma
statement_text: For any problem Π in the comparison-query model, D (Π) is at least the number of connected components of G(Π) .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: lemma:sensitivity:strong
title: Strong Sensitivity Lemma
statement_text: Consider an algorithm A in the comparison-based model with n items, color each vertex of the permutahedron with its execution trace under A , and let H denote the subgraph with the same vertex set but only containing the bichromatic edges. The number of distinct execution traces of A is at least g(deg _ avg ( H )+1)/n , where g: [1, ∞ ) → R is any convex function with g(x) = x! for x ∈ [n] .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: fact:Boolean
statement_text: Let A be a query algorithm on binary strings of length n . Color each vertex of the n -dimensional hypercube by its execution trace under A , and let H denote the subgraph with the same vertex set but only containing the bichromatic edges. Then the number of distinct execution traces is at least 2^ deg _ avg (H) .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: claim:encoding
statement_text: Let R denote the set of all rankings ρ that follow a particular execution trace on A , and let d ∈ {0, ... ,n-1} . The number of rankings ρ ∈ R with deg _ H (ρ) = d is at most (n!)/((d+1)!) .

label: lemma:k-ary:subtree-sensitivity

statement_text: Consider a tree T with n doteq | L (T) | leaves, and some node v in T with ℓ doteq | L (T_v) | leaves. We have s(Π_T) ≥ ( ℓ (n- ℓ ))/(n)-1.

label: claim:k-ary:decreasing-transposition

label: claim:k-ary:transposition-to-gap
statement_text: For any ordering σ , the number of r such that σ(ρ^ -1 (r))>σ(ρ^ -1 (r+1)) is at least one less than the number of s such that ρ^ -1 (s) ∈ L (T_v) and ρ^ -1 (s+1) ∉ L (T_v) .

label: claim:k-ary:gap-count

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: fact:k-ary:balance
statement_text: If T is a tree of degree k with n leaves, there exists a node v in T such that ℓ doteq | L (T_v) | = α · n , where (1)/(k+1) ≤ α ≤ (k)/(k+1) .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: eq:MRInv
title: root inversions, RInv ( · , · , · ) , MinRInv ( · , · )
statement_text: Given a tree T , a ranking ρ of the leaves of T , and an ordering σ of T , a root inversion of σ with respect to ρ is an inversion ( ℓ _1, ℓ _2) of σ with respect to ρ for which the lowest common ancestor LCA ( ℓ _1, ℓ _2) is the root of T . The number of root inversions of σ with respect to ρ in T is denoted by RInv (T,ρ,σ) . The minimum number of root inversions in T with respect to ρ is denoted MinRInv (T,ρ) doteq min _σ RInv (T,ρ,σ), where σ ranges over all possible orderings of T .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: prop:change
statement_text: Let ρ be a ranking of the leaf set X of a tree T , τ an adjacent-rank transposition, and ℓ _1 and ℓ _2 be the affected leaves. Then MinRInv (T_v,ρ) = MinRInv (T_v,τ ρ) for all nodes v in T except possibly v = LCA ( ℓ _1, ℓ _2) . Moreover, the difference is at most 1 in absolute value.

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: lemma:sensitivity:lipschitz
statement_text: Given a tree T , if a subtree T_ v^* with ℓ leaves is replaced with a tree T'_ v^* with the same number of leaves, resulting in the tree T' , then |s(Π_T)-s(Π_ T' )| ≤ ( ℓ ( ℓ -1))/(n).

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: claim:root:insensitive
statement_text: MinRInv (T_v,ρ) = MinRInv (T'_v,ρ) holds for every node v outside of T_ v^* (or equivalently, outside of T'_ v^* ).

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
title: cross inversion difference, DInv _ · ( · , · )
statement_text: For a ranking ρ of a set X , and two subsets A, B ⊆ X , DInv _ρ(A,B) doteq XInv _ρ(A,B) - XInv _ρ(B,A).

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: prop:sensitivity:criterion
statement_text: Let T be a binary tree, ρ a ranking of the leaves of T , τ an adjacent-rank transposition, ℓ _ lo and ℓ _ hi the two leaves affected by τ under ρ such that ρ ranks ℓ _ lo before ℓ _ hi . Referring to the notation in Figure , we have that MinInv (T,ρ) = MinInv (T, τ ρ) & ⟺ DInv _ρ(L_ lo ,L_ hi ) = DInv _ρ({ ℓ _ lo },{ ℓ _ hi }) & ⟺ DInv _ρ(A,B) = |A_<| - |A_>| + |B_>| - |B_<|.

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: def:root-sensitivity
title: root sensitivity
statement_text: Let T be a tree. The root sensitivity of T is the probability that MinRInv (T_v,ρ) ≠ MinRInv (T_v,τ ρ) when ρ is a uniform random ranking of L (T) , and τ a uniform random adjacent transposition with the condition that the affected leaves are in subtrees of different children of the root of T .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
title: cross inversion distribution, X_ · , ·
statement_text: For nonnegative integers a and b , X_ a,b denotes the random variable XInv (A,B) that counts the number of cross inversions from A to B , where A is an array of length a , B an array of length b , and the concatenation AB is a uniformly random permutation of [a+b] .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: thm:gaussian:main

label: lemma:sensitivity:root
statement_text: There exists a constant c such that for every binary tree T with at leaves 3 leaves and a root of degree 2, the root sensitivity of T is at least 1 - frac c sqrt n_1 n_2 (n_1+n_2) , where n_1 and n_2 denote the number of leaves in the subtrees rooted by the two children of the root.

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: lemma:sensitivity:binary
statement_text: The average sensitivity of Π_T for binary trees T with n ≥ 2 leaves is n-O(1) .

label: claim:sensitivity:sum

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
title: randomized query complexity, RQ _ · ( · ) , and distributional query complexity, DistQ _ · ( · , · )
statement_text: Let Π be a problem in the comparison-query model and ε ∈ [0,1] . A randomized algorithm R for Π is said to have error ε if on every input ρ , the algorithm outputs Π(ρ) with probability at least 1-ε . The query complexity of R is the maximum, over all inputs ρ , of the expected number of queries that R makes on input ρ . The ε -error randomized query complexity of Π , denoted RQ _ ε (Π) , is the minimum query complexity of R over all ε -error randomized algorithms R for Π . Let 0.06cm be a probability distribution on the inputs ρ . A deterministic algorithm A for Π has error ε with respect to 0.06cm if the probability that A(ρ)=Π(ρ) is at least 1-ε where the input ρ is chosen according to 0.06cm . The query complexity of A with respect to 0.06cm is the expected number of queries that A makes on input ρ when ρ is chosen according to 0.06cm . The ε -error distributional query complexity of Π with respect to 0.06cm , denoted DistQ _ ε (Π,0.06cm) , is the minimum query complexity of A with respect to 0.06cm over all deterministic algorithms A for Π that have error ε with respect to 0.06cm .

label: lemma:yaos-principle

statement_text: Let Π be a problem in the comparison-query model, ε ∈ [0,1/2] , and 0.06cm a distribution on the inputs ρ . RQ _ ε (Π) ≥ (1)/(2) DistQ _ 2ε (Π, 0.06cm).

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: claim:sensitivity:average

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: def:partition-property
title: partition property
statement_text: A computational problem Π in the comparison-query model on a set X of n items has the partition property if the set X can be partitioned into sets X_i such that for any ranking ρ of X and adjacent-rank transposition τ = (r, r+1) with r ∈ [n-1] , Π(ρ) = Π(τ ρ) if and only if ρ^ -1 (r) and ρ^ -1 (r+1) belong to the same partition class X_i . If every partition class X_i has size at most k , we say that Π has the partition property with class size at most k .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
title: successor graph, S( · , · )
statement_text: Let Π be a computational problem in the comparison-query model on a set X of n items, and ρ a ranking of X . The successor graph of Π on ρ , denoted S(Π,ρ) , has vertex set [n] and contains all edges of the form (r,r+1) with r ∈ [n-1] such that Π(ρ) = Π(τ ρ) , where τ denotes the adjacent-rank transposition (r,r+1) .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: prop:successor:components

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: lemma:connectivity:sensitive

statement_text: Let Π be a computational problem in the comparison-query model on a set of size n . If Π satisfies the partition property with class size at most k , then then D (Π) ≥ n!/(2(k!)^2) .

statement_text: There is a quantum algorithm A that, given black-box access to an unknown d -dimensional unitary channel Z ∈ U ( d ) and any ε > 0 , outputs a classical description of a unitary. (Gate complexity) If the d -dimensional qudit is embedded in n = lceil log _2 d rceil qubits, then A uses poly ( d ,1/ε) one- and two-qubit quantum gates in total beyond the queries to the black box, and the classical time complexity is poly ( d ,1/ε) . (Closeness of output unitary) The unitary output by A is ε -close to the unknown Z in diamond norm with high probability. Specifically, E [ diamnorm U ( Z )- U (Z) ^2 ] ≤ ε^2 , which implies Pr [ diamnorm U ( Z ) - U (Z) ≤ 3ε ] ≥ tfrac 2 3 . (Closeness of output channel) We can also view the output of A as a channel. statement_text: The estimation task for unitary channels is the following: One is given black-box access to a unitary channel by Z ∈ U ( d ) . After applying the unitary channel some Q times, the algorithm should output a classical description Throughout this paper, for ease of exposition we will be treating these descriptions as if they have infinite precision. To formalize our results when numbers can only be specified up to a machine precision ε_ mach , we consider the sets of unit vectors and unitary matrices that can be generated from O( log ^3(1/ε)) -depth quantum circuits. This discretizes these spaces into O(ε_ mach ) -nets by the Solovay--Kitaev theorem. Then, a classical description of a unitary matrix or a unit vector is a list of numbers defining a matrix or vector that need not exactly satisfy the desired constraints, but is ε_ mach -close to an element of the net. When we need to implement a unitary from its classical description, we implement this element. We only care about vectors and matrices up to poly (ε/ d ) error, since this is the magnitude of sampling error from state tomography, which is where these classical descriptions come from. So, if we set ε_ mach to be smaller than this, then the errors from working in finite precision are negligible, and we incur a polylog (1/ε_ mach ) overhead (which is only polylog ( d /ε) ) in time complexity. This issue only affects constant factors in our proofs in a very minor way, and we trust the diligent reader to take note of the required changes. of a unitary Z ∈ U ( d ) . The algorithm may be probabilistic and hence Z should be thought of as a random variable. The goal is to achieve E [ error ( U (Z), U ( Z ))] < ε. Here, error ( · , · ) is some accuracy measure between unitary channels.

statement_text: The SAR task for unitary channels (Storage-And-Retrieval) involves developing two quantum algorithms . The ``storage'' algorithm S is given black-box access to a unitary Z ∈ U ( d ) ; after applying the unitary some Q times, S should output a possibly mixed quantum state ψ . The ``retrieval'' algorithm R takes as input ψ and implements a possibly nonunitary qudit channel C , which may be random with some distribution. This retrieval may destroy ψ . The goal is to achieve the following: Pr _ C [ error ( U (Z), C ) > ε ] ≤ η. Note that here error ( · , · ) is measuring the error between a unitary channel and a possibly nonunitary channel. The storage complexity of the algorithm is the number of qubits used for ψ .

She represents this forest by a kl binary kl relation variable P , where InRel P FOVar [1], FOVar [2] is intended to mean “the parent of FOVar [1] is FOVar [2] ”. If she succeeds, one should thus always reach an unselected kl node by following parent pointers. Then, kl Adam tries to disprove kl Eve 's claim that P represents a forest by showing that the relation contains a directed cycle. To do so, he chooses a subset X of kl nodes , and then asks kl Eve to assign a charge (positive or negative) to each kl node such that roots are positive, children outside X have the same charge as their parent, and children in X have the opposite charge of their parent. label: ex:one-selected
statement_text: To kl define ONESELECTED on GRAPH , we intuitively let kl Eve and kl Adam play a similar 3 -move game as in Example , but now we tighten the rules for kl Eve so that her spanning forest P must be a spanning tree rooted at the unique selected kl node . Again, kl Adam tries to refute her choice, and this time he has two possible lines of attack: either find a directed cycle in P (as before), or show that there are at least two selected kl nodes . He launches both attacks simultaneously by choosing a single subset X of kl nodes , and then presenting kl Eve with two challenges: to charge each kl node positively or negatively according to X (as described in Example ), and to tell each kl node whether the selected kl node belongs to X . As before, if P contains a directed cycle, he can make kl Eve fail the first challenge. But now, if there are at least two selected kl nodes , he can make her fail the second challenge by choosing a set X that contains only one selected kl node . In this way, no matter what kl Eve tells each kl node about the supposedly unique selected kl node 's membership in X , there will necessarily be an inconsistency between two adjacent kl nodes that receive conflicting information. Formally, we represent kl Eve 's responses to kl Adam 's challenges by two kl unary kl relation variables Y and Z , the former corresponding to the set of positive kl nodes (as before), and the latter intended as a Boolean predicate indicating whether the selected kl node belongs to X . label: ex:non-hamiltonian
statement_text: We kl define NONHAMILTONIAN based on the following characterization: a kl graph is kl Hamiltonian if and only if it contains a kl spanning subgraph (i.e., a kl subgraph containing all kl nodes ) that is 2 -kl regular (i.e., all kl nodes have kl degree 2 ) and kl connected (i.e., any two kl nodes are linked by a kl path ). Intuitively, the kl complement of this kl (graph) property can be tested through the following game, where kl Adam starts by proposing a supposed kl Hamiltonian cycle , and then kl Eve tries to prove that his proposition is incorrect: First, kl Adam chooses a 2 -kl regular kl spanning subgraph , which he represents by a kl binary relation H . The intended meaning of InRel H FOVar [1], FOVar [2] is “the kl edge Set FOVar [1], FOVar [2] belongs to the kl subgraph ”. He claims that the chosen kl subgraph is a kl Hamiltonian cycle . Next, kl Eve tries to disprove this claim. If she is right, there are two possible cases: either kl Adam did not really propose a 2 -kl regular kl spanning subgraph , or his kl subgraph is not kl connected i.e., it consists of multiple disjoint kl cycles . To tell the kl nodes which of the two cases applies (say, giving priority to the first if both apply), kl Eve assigns each kl node a bit, which she represents by a kl unary relation C . In the first case, represented by NOT InRel C FOVar [1] , she constructs a spanning forest P whose roots are kl nodes at which the 2 -kl regularity condition is violated. In the second case, represented by InRel C FOVar [1] , she chooses a subset S of kl nodes containing some but not all kl components of kl Adam 's kl subgraph , without cutting any kl components , and then constructs a spanning forest P whose roots witness that S does indeed partition the kl subgraph into two nonempty parts. (There must be at least one witness, since we require by definition that the input kl graph is kl connected .) In both cases, the spanning forest is validated using the technique from Example . This adds two more steps to the game, where kl Adam challenges her with a set X and she responds with a set Y . statement_text: An [n,k,d]_q code C is a k -dimensional subspace of F _q^n , and d coloneqq min { wt (v) : v ∈ C \ {0}} is called the minimum distance of C . The elements of C are called codewords . Moreover, a generator matrix for C is a matrix G ∈ F _q^ k × n such that C ={uG : u ∈ F _q^k}; that is, the rows of G span C .

paper_title: Strong blocking sets and minimal codes from expander graphs
statement_text: Let {n_i }_ i ≥ 1 be an increasing sequence of lengths and suppose that there exist sequences {k_i}_ i ≥ 1 and {d_i}_ i ≥ 1 such that for all i ≥ 1 there is an [n_i, k_i, d_i]_q code C _i . Then the sequence { C _i}_ i ≥ 1 is called an (R,δ)_q -family of codes , where the rate of this family is defined as R coloneqq liminf _ i → ∞ (k_i)/(n_i), and the relative distance is defined as δ coloneqq liminf _ i → ∞ (d_i)/(n_i).

statement_text: Let C be an [n,k,d]_q code. A nonzero codeword v ∈ C is said to be minimal (in C ) if σ(v) is minimal with respect to the inclusion in the set σ( C ) coloneqq { σ(c) : u ∈ C \ {0}}. The code C is a minimal linear code if all its nonzero codewords are minimal.

statement_text: A set M ⊆ PG (k-1,q) is said to be a strong blocking set if ⟨ H ∩ M ⟩ =H, for every hyperplane H of PG (k-1,q) .

statement_text: Over any field, there are instances of n × n × n Tensor Isomorphism that require PC degree Ω(n) to refute. Over R , they also require Sum-of-Squares degree Ω(n) to refute.

label: thm:upper
statement_text: Over any field, the Nullstellensatz degree of refuting isomorphism of two n × n × n tensors of tensor rank ≤ r is at most 2^ O(r^2) . If working over a finite field F _q and including the equations x^q - x , the PC degree is at most O(qr^2) . In particular, isomorphism of constant-rank tensors can be decided in polynomial time.

statement_text: The unsatisfiable system of equations XY= Id _n where X is n × r and Y is r × n with 1 ≤ r < n , requires degree ≥ r/2+1 to refute in PC, over any field.

paper_title: A Topological Version of Schaefer's Dichotomy Theorem
label: thm:schaefer
statement_text: (Schaefer's dichotomy theorem ) For every finite set S of logical relations, the boolean constraint satisfaction problem SAT(S) is polynomial-time solvable if there exists one condition in the following list that holds for all logical relations R ∈ S : R is 0 -valid: (0, ... ,0) ∈ R . R is 1 -valid: (1, ... ,1) ∈ R . Horn SAT: R is equivalent to a CNF formula in which every clause has at most one non-negated variable. Dual-Horn SAT: R is equivalent to a CNF formula in which every clause has at most one negated variable. 2-SAT: R is equivalent to a CNF formula in which every clause has at most two literals. R is affine: R can be expressed as the set of solutions to a system of affine equations over GF(2) . If there is no such condition, SAT(S) is NP -complete. For SAT_C(S) , the boolean CSP with constants , the same classification holds, except that only the conditions 3.--6. are used.

We call d ≥ 1 the dimension of Φ , and n ≥ 1 its number of constraints .

statement_text: A multi-tape probabilistic Turing machine (PTM) M consists of two components ( M ,φ) , where M is a regular multi-tape deterministic Turing machine and φ is a random-bit generator. In addition to the input, output, and work tapes, the machine M has a special random-bit tape. The computation of the machine M on an input x can be informally described as follows: At each move, the generator φ first writes a random bit b=0 or 1 on the square currently scanned by the tape head of the random-bit tape. Then the DTM M makes the next move according to the current state and the current symbols scanned by the tape heads of all (but output) tapes, including the random-bit tape. The tape head of the random-bit tape always moves to the right after each move.

paper_title: Symmetric Exponential Time Requires Near-Maximum Circuit Size
title: The GGM tree construction
statement_text: Let C : {0, 1}^n → {0, 1}^ 2n be a circuit. Let n,T ∈ N be such that T ≥ 4n and let k be the smallest integer such that 2^k n ≥ T . The function GGM _T[C] : {0, 1}^n → {0, 1}^T is defined as follows. Consider a perfect binary tree with 2^k leaves, where the root is on level 0 and the leaves are on level k . Each node is assigned a binary string of length n , and for 0 ≤ j < 2^i , denote v_ i, j ∈ {0, 1}^n the value assigned to the j -th node on level i . Let x ∈ {0, 1}^n . We perform the following computation to obtain GGM _T[C](x) : we set v_ 0, 0 := x , and for each 0 ≤ i < k , 0 ≤ j < 2^i , we set v_ i+1, 2j := C(v_ i, j )_ [0, n) (i.e., the first half of C(v_ i, j ) ) and v_ i+1, 2j+1 := C(v_ i, j )_ [n, 2n) (i.e., the second half of C(v_ i, j ) ). (We say the nodes (i+1, 2j) and (i+1, 2j+1) are ``children'' of (i, j) .) Finally, we concatenate all values of the leaves and take the first T bits as the output: GGM _T[C](x) := (v_ k, 0 ∘ v_ k, 1 ∘ ... ∘ v_ k, 2^k-1 )_ [0, T) .
