statement_text: MinCore with arbitrary uniform thresholds and edge sizes is NP -complete.

paper_title: Quantum k-SAT Related Hypergraph Problems
label: def:neighbor
statement_text: In a hypergraph H = (V,E) a vertex w ∈ V is a neighbor from v ∈ V if there is an edge e ∈ E with lbrace w,v rbrace ⊆ e .

paper_title: Quantum k-SAT Related Hypergraph Problems
statement_text: Given a hypergraph H with a core C , the radius of all cores with size |C| is greater than log _ j (n/|C|)-1 , where j is the number of neighbors.

paper_title: Quantum k-SAT Related Hypergraph Problems
title: Hyperpath
statement_text: A hyperpath in H = (V,E) between two distinct vertices v_1, v_k ( k is a positive integer > 2) is a sequence (v_1, e_1,..., v_ k-1 , e_ k-1 , v_k) with distinct vertices v_1,...,v_k ∈ V and not necessarily distinct edges e_1,...,e_ k-1 ∈ E , where lbrace v_i , v_ i+1 rbrace ∈ e_i for i ∈ [k-1] . The positive integer k-1 is the length of a hyperpath.

paper_title: Quantum k-SAT Related Hypergraph Problems
title: Diameter
statement_text: The diameter, diam(H) of a hypergraph H is the maximum distance between any pair of vertices in H . The distance d(i,j) , between two vertices i,j in a hypergraph H is the minimum length of a hyperpath from i to j .

paper_title: Quantum k-SAT Related Hypergraph Problems
label: theorem:diameter_radius
statement_text: Given a hypergraph H and a core C for H . Then r(C) > lfloor (diam(H))/(2|C|) rfloor .

paper_title: Quantum k-SAT Related Hypergraph Problems
label: lemma:diameter
statement_text: Given a hypergraph and a core C . Every vertex, where the shortest path to a vertex in C is d , is at least in layer d .

paper_title: Collapses in quantum-classical probabilistically checkable proofs and the quantum polynomial hierarchy
label: def:unique-qcpcp
title: Unique quantum-classical probabilistically checkable proof, UniqueQCPCP
statement_text: Let c, s be completeness and soundness parameters, and let p, q : N → N , and c, s : R _ ≥ 0 → R _ ≥ 0 . A promise problem A = (A_ YES , A_ NO ) is in (p(n), q(n), c, s) - UniqueQCPCP if there exists a uniformly generated family of quantum circuits {V_n : n ∈ N } of polynomial size such that each V_n receives an input x ∈ {0,1}^n and a proof string y ∈ {0,1}^ p(n) , from which at most q(n) bits can be queried. The verifier accepts by measuring a designated output qubit and observing outcome 1 , and satisfies the following: (Completeness and Uniqueness) If x ∈ A_ YES , then there exists a unique y ∈ {0,1}^ p(n) such that Pr [V_n(x, y) accepts ] ≥ c , and for all y' ≠ y , Pr [V_n(x, y') accepts ] ≤ s . (Soundness) If x ∈ A_ NO , then for all y ∈ {0,1}^ p(n) , Pr [V_n(x, y) accepts ] ≤ s . We write UniqueQCPCP [q] if p(n) = poly (n) , c = 2/3 , and s = 1/3 .

paper_title: Collapses in quantum-classical probabilistically checkable proofs and the quantum polynomial hierarchy
label: def:unique-mtp
title: Unique multilinear threshold problem, UniqueMTP
statement_text: Let P : {0,1}^N → R be a degree- d multilinear polynomial with real coefficients {β_S}_ S ⊆ [N], |S| ≤ d . Suppose the image of P lies in a finite set D ⊂ [0,1] of evenly spaced values, such that log _2 |D| ≤ poly (N) . Denote by δ_D the maximum element of D . Given a polynomial-size classical description of P (i.e., the coefficients {β_S} ), the set D , and a threshold a ∈ D , decide between the following two cases: There exists a unique y ∈ {0,1}^N such that P(y) ≥ a and P(y') < a for all y' ≠ y . For all y ∈ {0,1}^N , it holds that P(y) < a .

paper_title: Collapses in quantum-classical probabilistically checkable proofs and the quantum polynomial hierarchy
label: def:unique-sat
title: Unique propositional satisfiability problem, UniqueSAT
statement_text: Let φ be a Boolean formula over n variables. Define the set of satisfying assignments as SAT (φ) = {x ∈ {0,1}^n : φ(x) = 1} . Then the language UniqueSAT = {φ : | SAT (φ)| = 1} consists of Boolean formulas that admit exactly one satisfying assignment.

paper_title: Collapses in quantum-classical probabilistically checkable proofs and the quantum polynomial hierarchy
label: def:rp-reduction
title: Randomized polynomial-time reduction
statement_text: Let A and B be languages. A randomized polynomial-time reduction from A to B is a randomized algorithm R such that, for every input x : If x ∈ A , then Pr [ R (x) ∈ B] ≥ 1/2 . If x ∉ A , then Pr [ R (x) ∈ B] = 0 . The algorithm R must run in time polynomial in |x| .

paper_title: Collapses in quantum-classical probabilistically checkable proofs and the quantum polynomial hierarchy
label: lem:valiant-vazirani
title: Valiant-Vazirani
statement_text: There exists a randomized polynomial-time algorithm R : { CNF formulas over n variables } → { CNF formulas } such that, for every Boolean formula φ over n variables, the following holds: (Completeness) If φ is satisfiable, then Pr [| SAT ( R (φ))| = 1 ] ≥ 1 / (2n) . (Soundness) If φ is unsatisfiable, then R (φ) is unsatisfiable with probability 1 . Moreover, R runs in time polynomial in |φ| .

paper_title: Collapses in quantum-classical probabilistically checkable proofs and the quantum polynomial hierarchy
label: def:bq-1
title: BQ -operator
statement_text: Let C be a class of promise problems. Define BQ · C as the class of all promise problems A for which there exists a promise problem B ∈ C such that A reduces to B via a polynomial-time quantum reduction with success probability at least 2/3 : BQ · C := { A : A ≤ _q B for some B ∈ C } .

paper_title: Collapses in quantum-classical probabilistically checkable proofs and the quantum polynomial hierarchy
label: def:bq-2
title: Alternative formulation of BQ -operator
statement_text: Let C be a class of promise problems. Then BQ · C consists of all promise problems A = (A_ YES , A_ NO ) such that there exists a promise problem B = (B_ YES , B_ NO ) ∈ C and a polynomial-time quantum algorithm Q with the following properties: for all x with |x| = n , (Completeness) If x ∈ A_ YES , then Pr _ z Q (x) [(x, z) ∈ B_ YES ] ≥ 2/3 . (Soundness) If x ∈ A_ NO , then Pr _ z Q (x) [(x, z) ∈ B_ NO ] ≥ 2/3 .

paper_title: Collapses in quantum-classical probabilistically checkable proofs and the quantum polynomial hierarchy
label: lem:mtp-sat
title: Deterministic polynomial-time reduction from MTP to SAT
statement_text: The MTP can be reduced to SAT deterministically and in polynomial time.

paper_title: Collapses in quantum-classical probabilistically checkable proofs and the quantum polynomial hierarchy
label: lem:usat-to-umtp
title: Deterministic polynomial-time reduction from UniqueSAT to UniqueMTP
statement_text: There exists a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from UniqueSAT to UniqueMTP .

paper_title: Collapses in quantum-classical probabilistically checkable proofs and the quantum polynomial hierarchy
label: lem:umtptouqcpcp
title: BQ reduction from UniqueMTP to UniqueQCPCP
statement_text: Let Ψ = (P(y), a, δ_D) be an instance of the UniqueMTP over Boolean variables y ∈ {0,1}^m , where P(y) = Σ _ substack S ⊆ [m], |S| ≤ d β_S Π _ i ∈ S y_i, and suppose that Ψ satisfies the following promise: ∃ ! y^* ∈ {0,1}^m such that P(y^*) ≥ a & (YES instance) , ∀ y ∈ {0,1}^m, P(y) < a & (NO instance) , with a gap parameter δ_D > 0 . Then there exists a polynomial-time deterministic quantum algorithm that outputs the description of a verifier V_Ψ ∈ UniqueQCPCP [p(m) = m, q = d, c, s] , where c = frac a + δ_D Σ _ j=1 ^ N |β_ S_j | and s = frac a - δ_D Σ _ j=1 ^ N |β_ S_j | , such that: If Ψ is a YES instance with unique witness y^* , then V_Ψ accepts exactly on the proof y^* and rejects all other y . If Ψ is a NO instance, then V_Ψ rejects every proof y .

paper_title: Collapses in quantum-classical probabilistically checkable proofs and the quantum polynomial hierarchy
label: thm:qcpcp-to-uqcpcp
title: Reduction from QCPCP to UniqueQCPCP
statement_text: Let V be a QCPCP verifier for a promise problem A = (A_ YES , A_ NO ) , with completeness c , soundness s , proof length l_n , and running time T_n . Then there exists a randomized polynomial-time algorithm which, given V , outputs a verifier V' for a UniqueQCPCP system with the following properties: V' runs in time O (T_n) and expects proofs of length l_n + O ( log (l_n)) . (Completeness): If x ∈ A_ YES , then with probability at least Ω(1/ poly (l_n)) over the randomness of the reduction, there exists a unique proof y^* ∈ {0,1}^ l_n + O ( log (l_n)) such that Pr [V'(x, y^*) = 1] ≥ c - γ , and ∀ y' ≠ y^*, Pr [V'(x, y') = 1] ≤ γ , where γ = negl (n) is negligible in n . (Soundness) If x ∈ A_ NO , then with probability 1 over the randomness of the reduction, it holds that for all y ∈ {0,1}^ l_n + O ( log (l_n)) , Pr [V'(x, y) = 1] ≤ s + γ .

paper_title: Collapses in quantum-classical probabilistically checkable proofs and the quantum polynomial hierarchy
label: def:qsigma-i
title: QΣ _i(c,s)
statement_text: Let A = (A_ YES , A_ NO ) be a promise problem, and let c, s : N → [0,1] be polynomial-time computable functions. Then A ∈ QΣ _i(c, s) if there exists: a polynomially bounded function p : N → N , and a polynomial-time uniform family of quantum circuits {V_n}_ n ∈ N , such that for every input x ∈ {0,1}^n , the verifier V_n takes p(n) -qubit quantum states ρ_1, ... , ρ_i as input proofs and outputs a single qubit. The verifier measures the output qubit in the computational basis, and the acceptance probability is defined on input ρ_1 ⊗ ... ⊗ ρ_i . (Completeness) If x ∈ L_ YES , then ∃ ρ_1 ∀ ρ_2 ... Q_i ρ_i such that Pr [V_n accepts ] ≥ c(n) . (Soundness) If x ∈ L_ NO , then ∀ ρ_1 ∃ ρ_2 ... Q _i ρ_i such that Pr [V_n accepts ] ≤ s(n) . Here, Q_i = ∀ if i is even and Q_i = ∃ if i is odd; Q _i denotes the complementary quantifier. When the completeness and soundness parameters are not specified, we define the class QΣ _i := cup_ c-s ∈ Ω(1/ poly (n)) QΣ _i(c,s).

paper_title: Collapses in quantum-classical probabilistically checkable proofs and the quantum polynomial hierarchy
label: def:qph
title: Quantum polynomial hierarchy, QPH
statement_text: The quantum polynomial hierarchy QPH is defined as QPH := cup_ i ∈ N QΣ _i = cup_ i ∈ N QΠ _i, where QΠ _i := co - QΣ _i .

paper_title: Collapses in quantum-classical probabilistically checkable proofs and the quantum polynomial hierarchy
label: def:bqp-qpoly
title: BQP / qpoly
statement_text: A promise problem A = (A_ YES , A_ NO ) is in BQP / qpoly if there exist: a polynomial-size family of quantum circuits {C_n}_ n ∈ N , and a sequence of polynomial-size quantum advice states {|ψ_n ⟩ }_ n ∈ N , such that for all x ∈ {0,1}^n , the circuit C_n takes input |x ⟩ ⊗ |ψ_n ⟩ and satisfies: (Completeness) If x ∈ A_ YES , then Pr [C_n(|x ⟩ ⊗ |ψ_n ⟩ ) = 1] ≥ 2/3 . (Soundness) If x ∈ A_ NO , then Pr [C_n(|x ⟩ ⊗ |ψ_n ⟩ ) = 1] ≤ 1/3 . Note that BQP / qpoly is the quantum analogue of BPP / poly , where quantum advice states replace classical advice strings.

paper_title: Collapses in quantum-classical probabilistically checkable proofs and the quantum polynomial hierarchy
label: def:qsigma2-qpoly

label: def:factors
title: Factors
statement_text: For rooted forest T we define the following three kinds of factors: A tree factor is a set V(T_x) for some x ∈ V(T) . We call x the root of the factor. A forest factor is a nonempty union of tree factors whose roots are siblings. In particular, a tree factor is also a forest factor but the empty set is not. The set of roots of the tree factors included in the union are called the roots of the factor. If they are not roots of components of T , we define their joint parent as the parent of the factor. Note that We consider two nodes of T siblings when they have a joint parent or if they both roots of components of T . This convention is chosen to remain consistent with the notation of . A context factor is a set U=X \ Y where X is a tree factor and Y is a forest factor whose roots are strict descendants of the root of X . The root of U , denoted by rt(U) , is the root of X and the roots of Y are called the appendices of U . Note that a tree factor is not a context factor. We will sometimes refer to X as the base tree factor of U and to Y as the removed forest of U . For clarity we sometimes denote X and Y as X(U) and Y(U) . We also denote the parent of the appendices by pr(U) and let the spine of U , denoted by spine(U) , be the path from rt(U) to pr(U)

statement_text: Consider the quantity (|V(G)|-1)^ 2 = (n-1)^ 2 ≥ 0 for n -vertex graphs G . Moreover, the quadratic term \# K_ 1 ^2 can be linearized This holds because \# K_ 1 ^2 counts the pairs (u,v) ∈ V(G)^2 , and so does the linear combination 2 \# K_ 2 + 2 \# I_2 + \# K_ 1 , whose summands correspond to the isomorphism type of G[{u,v}] , which is either K_2 , I_2 , or K_1 . As we will elaborate later, graph motif parameters enjoy a general linearization property: Any polynomial combination of induced subgraph counts can be expressed as a unique linear combination. statement_text: For a fixed graph H , we consider the problem of finding an induced H -copy in a large graph G . The graph G is given as (x, O) where O: Σ^ * → {0,1} is an oracle encoding the edge relation and x is the number of nodes of G written in binary. The nodes of G are 0, ... ,x-1 , written as bit strings of fixed length n . Given two nodes u and v of G , there is an edge between u and v iff O(uv) = 1 . (Since we consider strings of fixed length n , no separation symbol is needed.) In this representation, most of the information about G is stored in the oracle; the input x only encodes the size of the graph, and the running time of oracle Turing machines is measured in terms of x .

paper_title: Which graph motif parameters count?
statement_text: In our example of finding an induced copy of H in the graph G , we start with a binary type-2 relation IsIndSub _H(x,y,O) . The relation interprets y as an encoding of a set Y of k distinct nodes of G with k being the number of nodes of H . The relation then queries the oracle O to obtain the induced subgraph G[Y] . It then checks by brute force whether G[Y] and H are isomorphic. If yes, it returns the value 1 and otherwise 0 . This is clearly polynomial-time computable in |x| . The relation ∃ IsIndSub _H(x,O) now returns 1 if G contains an induced copy of H somewhere , and 0 if G does not contain such a copy. See also Lemma for a more formal proof.

statement_text: Underlying Graph: The underlying graph of a temporal graph G = ( V , E ) , denoted as G _U = ( V , E _U) , is a static graph where E _U = {(u, v) | ∃ t ∈ [0, T -1) such that e_ uv ^t is an instance of e_ uv ∈ E } .

paper_title: On Fixed-Parameter Tractability of Weighted 0-1 Timed Matching Problem on Temporal Graphs
statement_text: Bounded Degree Temporal Graph: A temporal graph G = ( V , E ) is a bounded degree temporal graph if the degree of each vertex v ∈ V in the underlying graph G _U is bounded by an integer Δ , i.e., deg(v) ≤ Δ .

statement_text: Temporal Tree: A temporal graph G = ( V , E ) is a temporal tree if the underlying graph G _U of G is a tree.

statement_text: Overlapping Edges: Two edges e_ uv , e_ vw ∈ E overlap each other if and only if both are incident at a vertex v and there is at least one timestep t when both the edges exist.

paper_title: On Fixed-Parameter Tractability of Weighted 0-1 Timed Matching Problem on Temporal Graphs
statement_text: 0-1 Timed Matching: A 0-1 timed matching M on a temporal graph, G = ( V , E ) is a subset of E such that any two edges in M are non-overlapping with each other.

paper_title: On Fixed-Parameter Tractability of Weighted 0-1 Timed Matching Problem on Temporal Graphs
statement_text: Maximum Weighted 0-1 Timed Matching: A maximum weighted 0-1 timed matching on a temporal graph G = ( V , E ) is a 0-1 timed matching, M ⊆ E such that the sum of weights of the edges in M are maximum among all such possible 0-1 timed matching on G .

paper_title: On Fixed-Parameter Tractability of Weighted 0-1 Timed Matching Problem on Temporal Graphs
statement_text: Edge-Overlap Graph: The edge-overlap graph of a temporal graph G = ( V , E ) is a static graph, G _O= (V_O,E_O) , where the vertex set V_O includes a vertex v_ uv for each edge e_ uv ∈ E and the edge set E_O includes the edge (v_ uv , v_ wx ) connecting v_ uv , v_ wx ∈ V_O when e_ uv , e_ wx are overlapping with each other.

label: thm: Cubical Complex
statement_text: Let F be a 3-SAT formula with n variables. The set of satisfying assignments S ⊆ {0,1}^n forms a cubical complex C(F) , where: Vertices correspond to satisfying assignments. k -faces correspond to k -dimensional subcubes where all 2^k assignments satisfy F . Topological queries about C(F) (e.g., connectedness, Betti numbers) reduce to 3-SAT instances.

paper_title: An Intrinsic Barrier for Resolving P = NP (2-SAT as Flat, 3-SAT as High-Dimensional Void-Rich)
label: thm:unstructured
statement_text: Let F be a random 3-SAT instance at clause density α>4.26 . Then with probability 1-o(1) : Its solution space S(F) decomposes into 2^ Ω(n) disconnected clusters. The cubical complex of S(F) has exponentially large Betti numbers (e.g.\ β_2(S(F))=2^ Ω(n) ). The primal constraint graph of F has treewidth Ω(n) . In particular, S(F) admits no global ordering or low-dimensional traversal.

label: lem:sat-4sat-to-3sat
title: Topological Admissibility of SAT to 3-SAT
statement_text: Let L = SAT and suppose R:L → threesat is a polynomial-time satisfiability-preserving reduction that is cubical and homologically faithful (discussion on this is delayed to Section 5.2 Conditions 1 and 2). If F ∈ L has a solution-space cubical complex S(F) with β_ 2 (S(F)) ≥ f(n) for some f(n)=ω(poly(n)) , then the reduced instance F^ prime =R(F) satisfies β_ 2 (S(F^ prime ) )\ ≥ \ β_ 2 (S(F) )\ =\ Ω(f(n)). In particular, the reduction from SAT to 3-SAT does not collapse exponential second Betti numbers.

label: thm:non-embedding-hardness
title: Topology-Destroying Reductions are Hard
statement_text: Computing β_k(K) for k ≥ 2 on a cubical complex K ⊆ {0,1}^N is \# P -hard under polynomial-time Turing reductions. In particular, unless \# P ⊆ FP , no algorithm in the standard Boolean decision-tree or subcube-query model can compute β_k(K) in worst-case time 2^ o(N) .

title: Proxies Don't Detect Hardness
statement_text: Fix a constant radius r ≥ 1 and let q( · ) be any polynomial. There exist two families of 3-CNF formulas {F^ easy _ n }_ n ≥ 1 , {F^ hard _ n }_ n ≥ 1 , and a function m_n → ∞ (which may be chosen as m_n=2^ c n for some c>0 ) with the following properties for every n : The final number of Boolean variables satisfies N_n=Θ(m_n) for both families (each gadget is constant-size). The incidence graphs of both families have treewidth O(1) . Local-indistinguishability: For any choice of at most q(n) vertex-centered radius- r neighborhoods, the induced labeled subgraphs of F^ easy _ n and F^ hard _ n are identical on all those neighborhoods. Hence any proxy that inspects at most q(n) radius- r views cannot distinguish the two families on input size n . Topological gap: β_2 l(S(F^ hard _ n ) r) ≥ m_n while β_2 l(S(F^ easy _ n ) r)=O(1) . In particular, choosing m_n=2^ c n yields an exponential gap in β_2 that local proxies of radius r and q(n) inspections fail to detect. Expressed in terms of the final variable count N_n=Θ(m_n) , one obtains β_2 l(S(F^ hard _ n ) r) ≥ 2^ c' N_n for some constant c'>0 .

statement_text: Let s := s(n) and c := c(n) . A catalytic Turing machine with space s and catalytic space c is a Turing machine M with a read-only input tape of length n , a write-only output tape, a read-write work tape of length s , and a second read-write work tape of length c called the catalytic tape , which will be initialized to an adversarial string τ . We say that M computes a function f if for every x ∈ {0,1}^n and τ ∈ {0,1}^c , the result of executing M on input x with initial catalytic tape τ fulfils two properties: 1) M halts with f(x) written on the output tape; and 2) M halts with the catalytic tape in state τ .

title: Matroid
statement_text: A matroid M is a tuple (S, I ) , where S is called the ground set, and I ⊆ 2^S is a collection of subsets of S , known as 'independent sets'. The following properties must hold for (S, I ) to be a matroid: ∅ ∈ I . The empty set is independent. If A ∈ I and B ⊆ A , then B ∈ I . The independent sets are downward closed. If A,B ∈ I where | A | > | B | , then there exists x ∈ A \ B such that B ∪ {x} ∈ I . The inclusion-wise maximal sets of I are referred to as the `bases' of M . The rank of M is defined to be the size of the largest independent set in I : rank (M) : = max _ I ∈ I | I | .

label: def:group-action
title: Group action
statement_text: Let G be a group and X be a set. A group action of G on X is a function α: G × X → X , denoted by α(g,x) = g · x , that satisfies the following properties: e · x = x for all x ∈ X , where e ∈ G is the identity element of G , and g · (h · x)=(gh) · x for all g,h ∈ G and x ∈ X .

paper_title: On the Bit Size of Sum-of-Squares Proofs for Symmetric Formulations
title: Orbits, Stabilizers, and Fixed Points
statement_text: Let a group G act on a set X . For x ∈ X , the set Orb_x = {g · x ∈ X \ | \ g ∈ G } is called the G -orbit of x . For x ∈ X , the set Stab_x = { g ∈ G \ | \ g · x = x } is called the stabilizer of x in G . The set of all distinct G -orbits of X is called the quotient set of X by G , denoted X/G . An element x ∈ X is a fixed point if its G -orbit consists only of x , i.e., Orb_x = {x} . Equivalently, x is a fixed point if its stabilizer is the entire group G , i.e., Stab_x = G .

label: def:action-on-poly
title: Action on Monomials and Polynomials
statement_text: Let G be a finite group that can act on the indices 1, ... , n (e.g., a subgroup of S_n ). For g ∈ G and a multi-index α = (α_1, ... , α_n) ∈ N ^n , we define the action of g on α as g · α = (α_ g^ -1 (1) , ... , α_ g^ -1 (n) ) . For a monomial m = x^ α , the action of G on m is defined for any g ∈ G as: g · m := x^ g · α = x_1^ α_ g^ -1 (1) ... x_n^ α_ g^ -1 (n) = x_ g(1) ^ α_1 ... x_ g(n) ^ α_n . This action extends linearly to the set of polynomials R [x_1, ... , x_n] . Thus, for a polynomial p(x) = Σ _ i=0 ^m a_i x^ α_i , the action of g ∈ G on p is defined as g · p = Σ _ i=0 ^m a_i (g · x^ α_i ) . A polynomial p is said to be G -invariant if g · p = p for all g ∈ G . If G=S_n , where S_n is the symmetric group on n elements, the polynomial is called symmetric .

The action of π ∈ S_n on Q is given by π * Q = P_ π' Q P_ π' ^top . Equivalently, the entries of π * Q satisfy (π * Q)_ x^α, x^β = Q_ π · x^α, π · x^β . Moreover, for any G subgroup of S_n , we say that Q is G -invariant if π * Q = Q for every π ∈ G .

title: informal

label: thm-informal:lpn_to_lsn
title: informal
statement_text: Fix any k ≥ 1 and p ∈ (0, 1) which is not necessarily a constant. There exists a reduction from lpn (lfloor np/6 rfloor , 2n, p/6) to lsn (k, n, p) . In particular, for a constant error probability p , constant rate lpn reduces to lsn with a single logical qubit.

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding
label: thm-informal:attack_algo
title: informal
statement_text: The existence of any sub-exponential time (in n ) algorithm which solves lsn at any rate frac k n implies a substantial breakthrough in classical cryptography in the form of a sub-exponential time algorithm for lpn at constant rate. Note that the runtime for lpn decoders is typically stated with respect to k , the length of the secret. In the case of lsn , it is more natural to think of the block length n as the relevant parameter. Since we consider constant rates, the asymptotics are the same either way. We discuss these differences in .

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding
title: informal
statement_text: Decision qncp and Decision qsdp are equivalent. Search qncp , Search qsdp , and Search recqncp are all equivalent in the sense that an efficient algorithm which solves any one problem with high probability exists if and only if an efficient algorithm which solves any other problem with high probability exists. Search recqncp reduces to Search errqncp .

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding
title: informal

statement_text: The quantum syndrome decoding problem qsdp (k,n,w) is characterized by integers k,n,w ∈ N . Given a symplectic stabilizer check matrix H ∈ Z _2^ (n-k) × 2n (as in Definition ) which implicitly defines a stabilizer subgroup S whose code distance d satisfies w ≤ lfloor (d-1)/(2) rfloor , we let · Search qsdp (k,n,w) be the task of finding, with probability at least (2)/(3) , an error e ' ∈ Z _2^ n-k such that Symp ^ -1 ( e + e ') ∈ S when given as input ( H , v ) with v = H Ω e \ ( mod \ 2) ∈ Z _2^ n-k and wt ( Symp ^ -1 ( e )) ≤ w ; and we let · Decision qsdp (k,n,w) be the task of determining, with probability at least (2)/(3) , if there exists an error e ' ∈ Z _2^ n-k such that Symp ^ -1 ( e + e ') ∈ S when given as input ( H , v ) with v = H Ω e \ ( mod \ 2) ∈ Z _2^ n-k and wt ( Symp ^ -1 ( e )) ≤ w .

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding
label: def:search-LSN
title: Learning Stabilizers with Noise, lsn
statement_text: The Learning Stabilizers with Noise problem, denoted by LSN (k, n, p) , is characterized by integers k,n ∈ N and a noise parameter p ∈ (0,1) . Here, both p and k can vary with n . We consider two variants: · Search LSN (k, n, p) is the following task: given as input a sample of the form ( C C _n, E C ket 0^ n-k , x ) where C is a random n -qubit Clifford operator and E D _p^ ⊗ n is an n -qubit Pauli error, and x Z _2^k is a random logical basis state, the task is to find x ; and · Decision LSN (k, n, p) is the following task: given as input a simple which is either overbrace ( C C _n, E C ket 0^ n-k , x ) ^ Structured sample or overbrace ( C C _n, frac I ^ ⊗ n 2^n ) ^ Unstructured sample where C is a random n -qubit Clifford, E D _p^ ⊗ n is an n -qubit Pauli, x Z _2^k is a random basis state and I _n is the n -qubit identity, the task is to distinguish which is the case. In addition, we also consider the multi-shot, or multi-sample, variant of the problem, denoted by LSN ^m(k, n, p) , which is characterized by an additional parameter m ∈ N . In the search variant, the input consists of many independent samples of the form { C _i C _n, E _i C _iket 0^ n-k , x }_ i=1 ^m , where E _i D _p^ ⊗ n are independently chosen Pauli errors, for i ∈ [m] , and the task is to recover x ∈ Z _2^k which appears in each of the samples. In the decision variant, the input either consists of the multi-sample instances above, or m copies of the identity matrix ( I _n/2^n)^ ⊗ m .

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding
label: lemma:secret_rerandomize
title: Secret re-randomization
statement_text: Suppose A is an algorithm which solves Search lsn ^m(k, n, p) with probability q . Let D be an arbitrary distribution over Z _2^k , and define Search lsn ^m(k, n, p, D ) to be the same task as Search lsn ^m(k, n, p) , but with x drawn from D . Then there is an algorithm which solves Search lsn ^m(k, n, p, D ) to probability q , using efficient quantum pre-processing and efficient classical post-processing, with a single call to A in between. The same statement holds for Decision lsn ^m(k, n, p) with advantage δ .

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding
label: def:search-sLSN
title: Learning Stabilizers with Noise, state variant slsn
statement_text: The state variant of the Learning Stabilizers with Noise problem, denoted by slsn ^m(k,n,p) , is characterized by integers k,n,m ∈ N and p ∈ (0,1) . Both p and k can vary with n . We consider two variants of the problem: · Search slsn ^m(k,n,p) is the following task: given as input samples of the form { C _i C _n, E _i C _iket 0^ n-k ,ψ }_ i=1 ^m , where C _i are random n -qubit Clifford operators, E _i D _p^ ⊗ n are n -qubit Paulis, and ket ψ μ _k is a Haar random k -qubit state, the task is to output a quantum state ρ within average fidelity at least (1)/(2^k)+frac 1 poly (n) of ket ψ over the choice of ket ψ μ_k ; that is, underset ket ψ μ_k E [braket ψ|ρ|ψ ] ≥ (1)/(2^k) + frac 1 poly (n) . · Decision slsn ^m(k,n,p) is the following task: given as input a sample which is either overbrace { C _i C _n, E _i C _iket 0^ n-k ,ψ }_ i=1 ^m ^ Structured samples or overbrace { C _i C _n, I _n/2^n }_ i=1 ^m ^ Unstructured samples where C _i are random n -qubit Cliffords, E _i D _p^ ⊗ n are n -qubit Paulis, ket ψ μ _k is a Haar random k -qubit state, and I _n is the n -qubit identity, the task is to distinguish which is the case with non-negligible advantage.

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding

statement_text: Let k,n ∈ N and p ∈ (0,1) be parameters. A quantum algorithm solves Decision slsn (k, n, p) with success probability q if and only if it solves Decision lsn (k, n, p) with success probability q .

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding
label: lem:designLSN
title: Relaxation to t -designs
statement_text: Let k,n ∈ N and p ∈ (0,1) be parameters. Then, the Search slsn ^m(k,n,p) problem is equivalent (in the sense that an efficient algorithm for one exists if and only if an efficient algorithm exists for the other) to a variant of the problem in which the encoded Haar state ket ψ μ_k is instead sampled according to a state t -design ensemble ν , whenever t ≥ m+1 .

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding
title: Search lsn to slsn with ≤ 2 samples

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding
label: def:classical-search-LSN
title: Learning Stabilizers with Noise, classical representation
statement_text: The classical formulation of lsn (k, n, p) , is characterized by integers k,n ∈ N and p ∈ (0,1) . We consider two variants: · Search lsn (k,n,p) : this is the task of finding y Z _2^k given as input a sample of the form ( A | B , A | B · r y + e ) where A ∈ Z _2^ 2n × n and B ∈ Z _2^ 2n × k are uniformly random matrices subject to the constraint that the columns of A and also of B , respectively, are pairwise symplectically orthogonal (as in Definition ) and that A | B is full-rank, where r Z _2^n is random, and where e ∈ Z _2^ 2n is a random depolarizing Pauli error in symplectic form. That is, e = Symp ( E ) for E D _p^ ⊗ n . · Decision lsn (k,n,p) : this is the task of distinguishing between samples of the form ( A | B , A | B · r y + e ) and ( A | B , u Z _2^ 2n ) where all variables are as before, and u ∈ Z _2^ 2n is a uniformly random vector. We refer to r as the junk and y as the secret . In the search variant , we say that a poly (n) (classical or quantum) algorithm solves the problem if it outputs x ∈ Z _2^k with probability at least (1)/(2^k) + frac 1 poly (n) , whereas in the decision variant of the problem we require a distinguishing advantage of at least frac 1 poly (n) . In addition, we also consider in the classical representation the multi-sample variant of both Search and Decision lsn (k,n,p) , which we denote by lsn ^m(k,n,p) ; this problem features an additional parameter m ∈ N which captures the number of independent samples. In the case of Search lsn ^m(k,n,p) , these consist of { ( A _i | B _i , A _i | B _i · r _i y + e _i ) }_ i ∈ [m] which are distributed as before, and where y Z _2^k is the same in each sample. In the case of Decision lsn ^m(k,n,p) , these are either m samples of the previous form, or m samples of the form { ( A _i | B _i , u _i Z _2^ 2n ) }_ i ∈ [m] . which are also independently distributed as in the single sample variant. We emphasize that, just like in the standard formulation of lsn , the secret is the same across samples. However, the junk is re-sampled each time.

title: Classical representation is equivalent to lsn

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding
label: thm:search2dec_sqncp
title: Search-to-decision reduction, qncp
statement_text: Let T = set P _1, ... , P _ n-k be a stabilizer tableau with code distance d such that w ≤ lfloor (d-1)/(2) rfloor . Let C ∈ C _n be the associated Clifford circuit and let S be the stabilizer subgroup generated by T . Suppose there exists an algorithm A ( T ) which solves Decision qncp (k, n, w') for all w' ≤ w with probability at least (2)/(3) . Then there exists an algorithm B ( T ) with input ( C , ket φ = E C ket 0^ n-k , ψ ) such that wt ( E ) ≤ w , finds E ∈ P _n such that E E ∈ S with probability (2)/(3) .

Then for any p = ω(( log n)/(n)) , ket C bra C ⊗ ( EC )ρ( EC )^dag is negligibly close in trace distance to ket C bra C ⊗ frac I ^ ⊗ n 2^n .

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding
label: def:random_self_reduction
title: Random self-reduction distribution
statement_text: Fix parameters n, k . Let D _ n, k, p = Unif ( Stab (n, k)) ⊗ D _ p ^ ⊗ n , where Stab (n, k) is set of llbracket n, k rrbracket stabilizer codes and D _ p ^ ⊗ n is the n -fold depolarizing channel with probability p . A ( V , ε, w, p) random self-reduction distribution is an efficiently sampleable distribution R _n over Cliffords C _n which satisfies mathop TV _ R R _n (( R C , R E R ^dag ), D _ n, k, p ) ≤ ε , for all C whose corresponding stabilizer code S is in V ⊆ C _n , and for all E such that wt ( E ) ≤ w .

title: Scrambling stabilizer tableaus scrambles the error
statement_text: If a distribution R _n over C _n takes every stabilizer tableau S _1, ... , S _ n-k corresponding to a stabilizer code S ∈ Stab (n, k) to a distribution R S _1 R ^ -1 , ... , R S _ n-k R ^ -1 for R R _n which has negligible distance to the uniform distribution over stabilizer tableaus (in TV distance), then R _n must also take every error E ∈ P _n by conjugation to have negligible distance from D _ 3/4 ^ ⊗ n .

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding
label: thm:no_w2a_general
title: No strong tableau-randomizing random-self-reduction for qncp
statement_text: There is no tableau-randomizing reduction ( V , ε, w, p) random self-reduction distribution, where V is the set of all stabilized tableaus, from qncp (k, n, w) with computational basis logical states to lsn (k, n, p) such that p = frac 34 - frac 1 poly (n) and ε = negl (n) .

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding
label: thm:w2a_nogo_sparse_Clifford
title: No random self-reduction from sparse Cliffords
statement_text: If k = n - Ω(n) , then number of stabilizer codes N = | Stab (n, k)| and the number of Cliffords M with column sparsity d = o(n) satisfy log (N) - log (M) = Ω(n^2) . Consequently, no sparse random self-reduction distribution exists for any ε < 1 - 2^ -o(n^2) , any error weight w ≥ 1 , and any probability parameter p .

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding
title: Optimistic and pessimistic mixing times
statement_text: Let M be an irreducible and aperiodic Markov chain on state space Ω with transition matrix Q and stationary distribution π . The optimistic mixing time is given by τ_*(ε) := min _ s ∈ S min set t ∈ Z _ ≥ 0 | TV (Q^t 1 _s, π) ≤ ε , and the pessimistic mixing time is given by τ^*(ε) := max _ s ∈ S min set t ∈ Z _ ≥ 0 | TV (Q^t 1 _s, π) ≤ ε , where 1 _s is the indicator vector on s . Note that τ^*(ε) coincides with the standard definition of the mixing time of an irreducible, aperiodic Markov chain and represents the minimum time at which, regardless of starting point, the distribution is ε -close to the stationary distribution. On the other hand, τ_* represents the minimum time at which some choice of starting state will have fully mixed.

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding
label: lemma:scrambling_gap
title: Small scrambling gap implies no tableau-randomizing reduction
statement_text: Let R _n be a distribution over C _n which defines a Markov chain M on non-identity Paulis by repeatedly conjugating an initial non-identity Pauli by independent samples R R _n . Assume this chain to be irreducible and aperiodic, such that the stationary distribution is a uniformly random non-identity Pauli. Let η(ε) > 0 be the pessimistic error when scrambling optimistically, which we call the scrambling gap . That is, η(ε) is defined implicitly via τ^*(η(ε)) = τ_*(ε) . By definition, η(ε) ≥ ε . If η(ε) = O( poly (n) · ε^b) for some constant b > 0 , then for any k, w and subset V ⊆ Stab (n, k) , there does not exist a positive integer d for which the distribution induced by applying d samples from R _n yields a ( V , ε, w, p) random self-reduction operator as defined in Definition , such that ε = negl (n) and p = frac 34 - frac 1 poly (n) .

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding
label: def:Clifford_random_chain
title: t -Clifford chain
statement_text: Let M be a Markov chain whose state space is Ω := set 0,1,2,3 ^n \ set 0^n and whose transitions are given by the following rule. Let the state be s ∈ Ω . Pick a random t -tuple (i_1, ... i_t) where i_j ∈ [n] and all i_j are distinct. If s_ i_j = 0 for all j ∈ [t] , do nothing. Otherwise, pick a random t -tuple (a_1, ... , a_t) ∈ set 0,1,2,3 ^t \ set 0^t and replace (s_ i_1 , ... , s_ i_t ) with (a_1, ... , a_t) .

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding
label: lemma:2-qubitClifford_upper_bound

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding
label: problem:coupon_collector
title: Coupon collector
statement_text: There are n distinct coupons in a bag, and we repeatedly draw t distinct coupons and then put them back. How many draws do we need for the probability that you collected coupon 1 to be at least 1 - ε ?

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding

statement_text: Fix any logical qubit function k(n) and weight function w(n) , and any subset of codes V (n) ⊆ C _n . Then there is no strong, non-trivial random self-reduction from qncp (k, n, w) (with computational basis logical states) to lsn (k, n, p) . More precisely, there is no ( V (n), ε, w(n), p(n)) random self-reduction distribution R _n on llbracket n, k rrbracket stabilizer codes, such that p = frac 34 - frac 1 poly (n) and ε = negl (n) , and R _n is a sequence of random t -local Cliffords.

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding
statement_text: There is no ( V , ε, w, p) tableau-randomizing random self-reduction operator (as defined in Definition ) for lsn , for any V ⊆ C _n , w ≥ 1 , such that ε = negl (n) and p = frac 34 - frac 1 poly (n) .

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding
title: symplpn
statement_text: The Symplectic Learning Parity with Noise problem, denoted by symplpn [n, p] , is characterized by an integer n ∈ N and p ∈ (0,1) . We distinguish between two variants of the problem: · Search symplpn [n, p] is the task of finding x Z _2^ n given as input a sample of the form ( A ∈ Z _2^ 2n × n , A x + e \ ( mod \ 2)) where A is random subject to the constraint that its n columns are linearly independent and symplectically orthogonal, and where e is a depolarizing error with probability parameter p , i.e. Symp ^ -1 ( e ) D _p^ ⊗ n . · Decision symplpn [n, p] is the task of distinguishing between the samples ( A ∈ Z _2^ 2n × n , A x + e \ ( mod \ 2)) or ( A ∈ Z _2^ 2n × n , u Z _2^ 2n ) where A , x , e are as before and u is a uniformly random bitstring.

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding

Then for any constant δ ∈ (0, 1) , there is an efficiently sampleable distribution μ_ n, m over Z _2^n such that mathop TV _ substack π S^n e ' μ_ n, m (π( e + e' ), Ber (p)^ ⊗ n ) = negl (n) . Here, p = (m)/(2n) (1 + δ ) and π is a uniformly random permutation drawn from the symmetric group S^n on n elements.

paper_title: Average-Case Complexity of Quantum Stabilizer Decoding
label: thm:lpn_to_symplpn
title: lpn to symplpn
statement_text: Let n, ℓ ∈ N be parameters and ε ∈ (0, 1) be a constant, such that ℓ (1+ε) ≤ n and ℓ = Ω(n^ ε ) . paper_title: Quantum Cryptography and Hardness of Non-Collapsing Measurements
title: OWPuzzs
statement_text: A one-way puzzle (OWPuzz) is a pair ( Samp , Ver ) of algorithms such that Samp (1^λ) → ( puzz , ans ): It is a QPT algorithm that, on input the security parameter λ , outputs a pair ( puzz , ans ) of classical strings. Ver ( puzz , ans ') → top /bot : It is an unbounded algorithm that, on input ( puzz , ans ') , outputs either top /bot . They satisfy the following properties. Correctness: Pr [top gets Ver ( puzz , ans ): ( puzz , ans )gets Samp (1^λ)] ≥ 1- negl (λ). Security: For any QPT adversary A , Pr [top gets Ver ( puzz , A (1^λ, puzz )): ( puzz , ans )gets Samp (1^λ)] ≤ negl (λ).

paper_title: Quantum Cryptography and Hardness of Non-Collapsing Measurements
title: DistOWPuzzs
statement_text: A uniform QPT algorithm Samp that takes the security parameter 1^λ as input and outputs a pair ( puzz , ans ) of bit strings is called an α -distributional one-way puzzle ( α -DistOWPuzz) if there exists a function α: N → [0,1] such that for any QPT adversary A , and for all sufficiently large λ ∈ N , SD ( { puzz , ans }_ ( puzz , ans )gets Samp (1^λ) , { puzz , A (1^λ, puzz )}_ ( puzz , ans )gets Samp (1^λ) ) ≥ α(λ). If Samp is a λ^ -c -DistOWPuzz for some constant c>0 , we simply say Samp is a DistOWPuzz.

paper_title: Quantum Cryptography and Hardness of Non-Collapsing Measurements
label: lem:DistOWPuzz_OWPuzz
statement_text: OWPuzzs exist if and only if DistOWPuzzs exist.

paper_title: Quantum Cryptography and Hardness of Non-Collapsing Measurements
title: Auxiliary-Input OWPuzzs
statement_text: An auxiliary-input one-way puzzle (auxiliary-input OWPuzz) is a pair ( Samp , Ver ) of algorithms such that Samp (x) → ( puzz , ans ): It is a QPT algorithm that, on input a bit string x , outputs a pair ( puzz , ans ) of classical bit strings. Ver (x, puzz , ans ') → top /bot : It is an unbounded algorithm that, on input (x, puzz , ans ') , outputs either top /bot . They satisfy the following properties. Correctness: Pr [top gets Ver (x, puzz , ans ): ( puzz , ans )gets Samp (x)] ≥ 1- negl (|x|). Security: For any QPT adversary A , there exists an infinite subset I ⊆ {0,1}^* such that for all x ∈ I , Pr [top gets Ver (x, puzz , A (x, puzz )): ( puzz , ans )gets Samp (x)] ≤ negl (|x|).

paper_title: Quantum Cryptography and Hardness of Non-Collapsing Measurements
title: Auxiliary-Input DistOWPuzzs
statement_text: A uniform QPT algorithm Samp that takes an advice bit string x ∈ {0,1}^* as input and outputs a pair ( puzz , ans ) of bit strings is called an auxiliary-input α -distributional one-way puzzle (auxiliary-input α -DistOWPuzz) if there exists a function α: N → [0,1] such that for any QPT adversary A , there exists an infinite subset I ⊆ {0,1}^* such that for all x ∈ I , SD ( { puzz , ans }_ ( puzz , ans )gets Samp (x) , { puzz , A (x, puzz )}_ ( puzz , ans )gets Samp (x) ) ≥ α(|x|). If Samp is an auxiliary-input λ^ -c -DistOWPuzzs for some constant c>0 , we simply say that Samp is an auxiliary-input DistOWPuzzs.

paper_title: Quantum Cryptography and Hardness of Non-Collapsing Measurements
label: lem:AI_DistOWPuzz_OWPuzz
statement_text: Auxiliary-input OWPuzzs exist if and only if auxiliary-input DistOWPuzzs exist.

paper_title: Quantum Cryptography and Hardness of Non-Collapsing Measurements
title: Non-Collapsing Measurement Oracle
statement_text: A non-collapsing measurement oracle Q is an oracle that behaves as follows: Take (a classical description of) a quantum circuit C=(U_1,M_1,...,U_T,M_T) and an integer ℓ >0 as input. Here each U_i is a unitary operator on ℓ qubits and each M_i is a computational-basis projective measurement on m_i qubits such that 0 ≤ m_i ≤ ℓ . (When m_i=0 , this means that no measurement is done.) Let |ψ_0 ⟩ :=|0^ ℓ ⟩ . Run C on input |ψ_0 ⟩ , and obtain (u_1,...,u_T) , where u_t ∈ {0,1}^ m_t is the outcome of the measurement M_t for each t ∈ [T] . Let τ_t:=(u_1,...,u_t) . For each t ∈ [T] , let |ψ_t^ τ_t ⟩ be the (normalized) post-measurement state immediately after the measurement M_t , i.e., |ψ_t^ τ_t ⟩ := frac (|u_t ⟩ ⟨ u_t| ⊗ I)U_t|ψ_ t-1 ^ τ_ t-1 ⟩ sqrt ⟨ ψ_ t-1 ^ τ_ t-1 |U_t^ † (|u_t ⟩ ⟨ u_t| ⊗ I)U_t|ψ_ t-1 ^ τ_ t-1 ⟩ . For each t ∈ [T] , sample v_t ∈ {0,1}^ ℓ with probability | ⟨ v_t|ψ_t^ τ_t ⟩ |^2 . Output (v_1,...,v_T) .

paper_title: Quantum Cryptography and Hardness of Non-Collapsing Measurements
title: PDQP
statement_text: A language L is in PDQP if there exists a polynomial-time classical deterministic Turing machine R with a single query to a non-collapsing measurement oracle Q such that For all x ∈ L , Pr [1gets R^ Q (x)] ≥ α(|x|) , For all x ∉ L , Pr [1gets R^ Q (x)] ≤ β(|x|) , where α,β are functions such that α(|x|)-β(|x|) ≥ 1/ poly (|x|) .

paper_title: Quantum Cryptography and Hardness of Non-Collapsing Measurements
title: Average-Case Hardness of PDQP
statement_text: We say that PDQP is hard on average if the following is satisfied: there exist a language L ∈ PDQP , a polynomial p , and a QPT algorithm E (1^λ) → {0,1}^λ such that for any QPT algorithm F and for all sufficiently large λ ∈ N , Pr _ xgets E (1^λ) [ F (x) ≠ L(x)] ≥ (1)/(p(λ)), where L(x) := 1 & x ∈ L 0 & x ∉ L.

paper_title: Quantum Cryptography and Hardness of Non-Collapsing Measurements
label: def:Samplingproblems
title: Sampling Problems
statement_text: A (polynomially-bounded) sampling problem is a collection {D_x}_ x ∈ {0,1}^* of probability distributions, where D_x is a distribution over {0,1}^ p(|x|) , for some fixed polynomial p .

paper_title: Quantum Cryptography and Hardness of Non-Collapsing Measurements
label: def:SampBQP
title: SampBQP
statement_text: SampBQP is the class of (polynomially-bounded) sampling problems {D_x}_ x ∈ {0,1}^* for which there exists a QPT algorithm B such that for all x and all ε>0 , SD ( B (x,1^ lfloor 1/ε rfloor ),D_x) ≤ ε , where B (x,1^ lfloor 1/εrfloor ) is the output probability distribution of B on input (x, 1^ lfloor 1/εrfloor ) .

paper_title: Quantum Cryptography and Hardness of Non-Collapsing Measurements
label: def:SampBQP

statement_text: SampPDQP is the class of (polynomially-bounded) sampling problems {D_x}_ x ∈ {0,1}^* for which there exists a classical deterministic polynomial-time algorithm B that makes a single query to the non-collapsing measurement oracle Q such that for all x and all ε>0 , SD ( B (x,1^ lfloor 1/ε rfloor ),D_x) ≤ ε , where B (x,1^ lfloor 1/εrfloor ) is the output probability distribution of B on input (x, 1^ lfloor 1/εrfloor ) .

paper_title: Quantum Cryptography and Hardness of Non-Collapsing Measurements
label: def:AHSampPDQP
title: Average-case Hardness of SampPDQP
statement_text: We say that SampPDQP is hard on average if the following is satisfied: there exist a sampling problem { D _x}_x ∈ SampPDQP , a polynomial p , and a QPT algorithm E (1^λ) → {0,1}^λ such that for any QPT algorithm F and for all sufficiently large λ , SD ( {x, F (x)}_ xgets E (1^λ) , {x, D _x}_ xgets E (1^λ) ) > (1)/(p(λ)).

paper_title: Quantum Cryptography and Hardness of Non-Collapsing Measurements

paper_title: Quantum Cryptography and Hardness of Non-Collapsing Measurements
title: Collision-Resistant Hashing (CRH)
statement_text: Let { H _λ : {0,1}^ n(λ) → {0,1}^ m(λ) }_ λ ∈ N be an efficient function family ensemble. Here m and n are polynomials such that m(λ) ≤ n(λ) for all λ ∈ N . We say that it is a collision-resistant hash (dCRH) function family if for any QPT algorithm A , Pr [h(x)=h(x') ∧ x ≠ x': hgets H _λ, (x,x')gets A (h)] ≤ negl (λ).

title: Distributional Collision-Resistant Hashing (dCRH)
statement_text: Let { H _λ : {0,1}^ n(λ) → {0,1}^ m(λ) }_ λ ∈ N be an efficient function family ensemble. Here n and m are polynomials. We say that it is a distributional collision-resistant hash (dCRH) function family if there exists a polynomial p such that for any QPT algorithm A , SD ({h, A (h)}_ hgets H _λ , {h, Col (h)}_ hgets H _λ ) ≥ (1)/(p(λ)) for all sufficiently large λ ∈ N . Here Col (h) is the following distribution. Sample xgets {0,1}^ n(λ) . Sample x'gets h^ -1 (h(x)) . Output (x,x') .

label: def:OSSDS
title: One-Shot Signatures
statement_text: A one-shot signature scheme is a set ( Setup , Gen , Sign , Ver ) of algorithms such that Setup (1^λ) → pp : It is a QPT algorithm that, on input the security parameter λ , outputs a public parameter pp . Gen ( pp ) → ( vk , sigk ): It is a QPT algorithm that, on input pp , outputs a quantum signing key sigk and a classical verification key vk . Sign ( sigk ,m) → σ: It is a QPT algorithm that, on input sigk and a message m , outputs a classical signature σ . Ver ( pp , vk ,σ,m) → top /bot : It is a QPT algorithm that, on input pp , vk , σ , and m , outputs top /bot . We require the following properties. @startsection paragraph 4 z@ -12p@ @plus -4p@ @minus -4p@ -0.5em @plus -0.22em @minus -0.1em Correctness: For any m , Pr [ top gets Ver ( pp , vk ,σ,m): rr pp gets Setup (1^λ) ( vk , sigk )gets Gen ( pp ) σgets Sign ( sigk ,m) ] ≥ 1- negl (λ). @startsection paragraph 4 z@ -12p@ @plus -4p@ @minus -4p@ -0.5em @plus -0.22em @minus -0.1em Security: For any QPT adversary A , Pr [ c m_0 ≠ m_1 ∧ top gets Ver ( pp , vk ,σ_0,m_0) ∧ top gets Ver ( pp , vk ,σ_1,m_1) : rr pp gets Setup (1^λ) ( vk ,m_0,m_1,σ_0,σ_1)gets A ( pp ) ] ≤ negl (λ).

statement_text: A one-shot message authentication code (MAC) scheme is a set ( Setup , Gen , Sign , Ver ) of algorithms such that Setup (1^λ) → ( pp , mvk ): It is a QPT algorithm that, on input the security parameter λ , outputs a public parameter pp and a master verification key mvk . Gen ( pp ) → ( vk , sigk ): It is a QPT algorithm that, on input pp , outputs a quantum signing key sigk and a classical verification key vk . Sign ( sigk ,m) → σ: It is a QPT algorithm that, on input sigk and a message m , outputs a classical signature σ . Ver ( pp , mvk , vk ,σ,m) → top /bot : It is a QPT algorithm that, on input pp , mvk , vk , σ , and m , outputs top /bot . We require the following properties. @startsection paragraph 4 z@ -12p@ @plus -4p@ @minus -4p@ -0.5em @plus -0.22em @minus -0.1em Correctness: For any m , Pr [ top gets Ver ( pp , mvk , vk ,σ,m): rr ( pp , mvk )gets Setup (1^λ) ( sigk , vk )gets Gen ( pp ) σgets Sign ( sigk ,m) ] ≥ 1- negl (λ). @startsection paragraph 4 z@ -12p@ @plus -4p@ @minus -4p@ -0.5em @plus -0.22em @minus -0.1em Security: For any QPT adversary A , Pr [ c m_0 ≠ m_1 ∧ top gets Ver ( pp , mvk , vk ,σ_0,m_0) ∧ top gets Ver ( pp , mvk , vk ,σ_1,m_1) : rr ( pp , mvk )gets Setup (1^λ) ( vk ,m_0,m_1,σ_0,σ_1)gets A ( pp ) ] ≤ negl (λ).

paper_title: Quantum Cryptography and Hardness of Non-Collapsing Measurements
title: Two-Message Honest-Statistically-Hiding Computationally-Binding Bit Commitments with Classical Communication
statement_text: A two-message honest-statistically-hiding and computationally-binding bit commitment scheme with classical communication is a set ( S _1, S _2, R _1, R _2) of algorithms such that R _1(1^λ) → (r_1,ψ_R): It is a QPT algorithm that, on input the security parameter λ , outputs a classical bit string r_1 and an internal quantum state ψ_R . S _1(r_1,b) → (s_1,ψ_S): It is a QPT algorithm that, on input r_1 and a bit b ∈ {0,1} , outputs a bit string s_1 and an internal state ψ_S . S _2(b,ψ_S) → s_2: It is a QPT algorithm that, on input b and ψ_S , outputs a bit string s_2 . R _2(ψ_R,s_1,s_2,b) → top /bot : It is a QPT algorithm that, on input ψ_R , s_1 , s_2 , and b , outputs top /bot . We require the following properties. @startsection paragraph 4 z@ -12p@ @plus -4p@ @minus -4p@ -0.5em @plus -0.22em @minus -0.1em Correctness. For all b ∈ {0,1} , Pr [top gets R _2(ψ_R,s_1,s_2,b):(r_1,ψ_R)gets R _1(1^λ),(s_1,ψ_S)gets S _1(r_1,b),s_2gets S _2(b,ψ_S)] ≥ 1- negl (λ). @startsection paragraph 4 z@ -12p@ @plus -4p@ @minus -4p@ -0.5em @plus -0.22em @minus -0.1em Honest statistical hiding. For all b ∈ {0,1} and for any (not-necessarily-efficient) algorithm A , Pr [bgets A (ψ_R,s_1):(r_1,ψ_R)gets R _1(1^λ),s_1gets S _1(r_1,b)] ≤ (1)/(2)+ negl (λ). @startsection paragraph 4 z@ -12p@ @plus -4p@ @minus -4p@ -0.5em @plus -0.22em @minus -0.1em Computational binding. For any QPT algorithm A , Pr [ c top gets R _2(ψ_R,s_1,s_2,0) ∧ top gets R _2(ψ_R,s_1,s_2',1) : r (r_1,ψ_R)gets R _1(1^λ) (s_1,s_2,s_2')gets A (r_1) ] ≤ negl (λ).

paper_title: A Polynomial Space Lower Bound for Diameter Estimation in Dynamic Streams
label: thm:lb
statement_text: For any c ≥ 1 , there exists a metric M = ([n], d ) such that any dynamic streaming algorithm that computes a c -approximation to diam _ M (x) for all x ∈ {0,1}^n must use Ω (n^ 1/(2lceil c rceil - 1) ) bits of space.

paper_title: A Polynomial Space Lower Bound for Diameter Estimation in Dynamic Streams
label: thm:ub
statement_text: For any metric space M = ([n], d ) and any c > 6 , there is a dynamic streaming algorithm that computes a c -approximation to diam _ M (x) with O (n^ 1 / lfloor (c-2)/4rfloor ) bits of space. We assume, for convenience, that final frequency vectors have entries with magnitude at most poly (n) (to support frequency vectors of magnitude m , we pay a multiplicative O( log m) in the bit-complexity). Furthermore, we assume for convenience, that the metric M has aspect ratio poly (n) (to support aspect ratio Δ , we pay an additive polylog (nΔ) factor in the bit-complexity).

paper_title: A Polynomial Space Lower Bound for Diameter Estimation in Dynamic Streams
label: def: L0 sampler
title: ℓ _0 -sampler
statement_text: For δ > 0 , a δ -error ℓ _0 -sampler over Z^n is a randomized streaming algorithm with the following behavior: on input x ∈ Z^n , it fails with probability at most δ ; conditioned on not failing, it either returns a uniformly random index i supp (x) , where supp (x) := {i ∈ [n] : x_i ≠ 0} , or declares x = 0 if supp (x) = ∅ .

paper_title: A Polynomial Space Lower Bound for Diameter Estimation in Dynamic Streams
label: thm: L0 sampler
title: Theorem 2 of
statement_text: For any δ > 0 , there exists a δ -error ℓ _0 -sampler that uses O( log n log (1/δ) log (mn)) bits of space, where m is an upper bound on the magnitude of the coordinates of the input vector. Moreover, the algorithm can be implemented as a linear sketch using an s × n matrix with s = O( log n log (1/δ)) whose entries are in {-1,0,1} .

paper_title: A Polynomial Space Lower Bound for Diameter Estimation in Dynamic Streams
title: Dynamic Stream
statement_text: A dynamic stream σ for Z^n of length u ∈ N is a sequence of u updates of the form Add (i) or Remove (i) for i ∈ [n] , defining an implicit frequency vector x ∈ Z^n . The vector x is initialized to zero, an Add (i) update increments x_i by 1, while a Remove (i) update decrements x_i by 1.

paper_title: A Polynomial Space Lower Bound for Diameter Estimation in Dynamic Streams
label: def:randomized-streaming-alg
title: Randomized Streaming Algorithm
statement_text: A randomized streaming algorithm A is specified by a Turing machine with state space S and two distinguished states s, t ∈ S denoting the start and end of an update's processing. The machine has access to three tapes: Input Tape : A read-only, one-way tape containing a dynamic stream σ . Working Tape : A two-way tape storing memory from W ⊂ {0,1}^* . Random Tape : A read-only, two-way tape containing a fixed string ρ ∈ {0,1}^ r of random bits. The parameter r is the randomness complexity of A (see Definition ). A configuration after processing an update is a tuple (w, ρ) , where w ∈ W is the working tape and ρ is the random tape. Output Function: There is a function Dec : W × {0,1}^r → {0,1} that produces the output from the final configuration.

paper_title: A Polynomial Space Lower Bound for Diameter Estimation in Dynamic Streams
title: Correctness
statement_text: For a function g : Z^n → {0,1,*} , a randomized streaming algorithm A computes g with error probability at most δ if, for any stream σ with frequency vector x ∈ Z^n , Pr _ ρ [g(x) ∈ {0,1} and A (σ) ≠ g(x) ] ≤ δ.

paper_title: A Polynomial Space Lower Bound for Diameter Estimation in Dynamic Streams
label: def:space

statement_text: The local Hamiltonian problem is a decision problem that asks whether the ground state energy of a K -local Hamiltonian is greater or less than given energy thresholds. Outputs: Z ∈ R such that (1-δ)Z ≤ Z ≤ (1+δ)Z, where Z:= Tr (e^ -β H ) . We say an algorithm A_ QPF solves kQPF(H, β, δ) if A_ QPF outputs such Z on the inputs H, β, δ .

paper_title: A (Very) Nearly Optimal Sketch for $k$-Edge Connectivity Certificates
title: k -Connectivity Certificate
statement_text: Let G = (V, E) be a graph on n vertices and let k be a positive integer. A k -connectivity certificate is one of the following: If G is k -edge-connected, the certificate is a spanning subgraph H of G such that H itself is k -edge-connected. If G is not k -edge-connected, the certificate consists of a cut (S, S ) whose cut size is strictly less than k , along with the explicit list of edges crossing the cut denoted by E(S, S ) .

paper_title: A (Very) Nearly Optimal Sketch for $k$-Edge Connectivity Certificates
title: SupportFind
statement_text: Let n,m, and k be positive integers with m ≤ poly (n) , and δ ∈ (0,1) be the error parameter. The dynamic streaming problem SupportFind (k, n, m, δ) is defined as follows: Let x_1, ... , x_n ∈ Z ^m be vectors, each initialized to 0^m at the beginning of the stream. Each stream updates are of the form (i, Δ) ∈ [n] × Z ^m , where |Δ|_ ∞ ≤ poly (n) and the update modifies x_i arrow x_i + Δ . At the end of the stream, given a query set S ⊆ [n] , the algorithm must return min {k, |x_S|_0} distinct indices from the support of x_S , with probability at least 1 - δ , where x_S := Σ _ i ∈ S x_i .

Specifically, there exists a sketch M consisting of n sub-sketches sk (x_1), ... , sk (x_n) , and a query algorithm A with the following properties: Each sk (x_i) is a sketch of vector x_i that supports a sequence of updates to x_i . Moreover, each sk (x_i) uses O(t log ^2 m) bits of space. Upon querying a set S ⊆ [n] , the algorithm A operates on sk (x_1), ... , sk (x_n) and S , and returns min {k, |x_S|_0} distinct indices in the support of x_S with probability at least 1 - δ .

paper_title: Adversarial Barrier in Uniform Class Separation
statement_text: Accordingly, the final barrier can be read as a meta --separation phenomenon: once one is permitted to quantify over Prob without stratification, the distinction between enquote solving and enquote certifying a solution can be made to fold back onto itself. In particular, one can define meta-questions whose instances include their own classification interface as admissible input, so that any attempted resolution protocol becomes susceptible to the same adversarial recipe. The point is not that enquote P vs.\ NP is undecidable constitutes a resolution, but that the validity of any proposed resolution schema can be arranged to depend on the very self-application that diagonalization exploits. In such a regime, the predicate enquote this is a valid polynomially checkable resolution is no longer transparently simpler than the underlying resolution task: its verification inherits the same intensional dependency on the code of the interface. Thus the mechanism can be iterated: one may quantify over uniform separation tasks themselves and ask for uniform meta-classifications of those tasks, and the same adversarial loop reappears at the next level. The common source is unbounded, untyped quantification over enquote problems together with internal certification demands, which jointly supply the self-availability needed for diagonal inversion.

statement_text: Let C=(V, E) be a circuit, with V denoting the set of gates and the directed edge set is E . A weight assignment for C is a mapping w: V → N . paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:finite-envelope-polytime
title: Finite envelopes are simulable in poly-time
statement_text: Any finite N-Frame envelope O_n=(U_n,V_n,Z_n,T,B,Π^ * ,t(n)) with polynomial CEW and polynomial time budget t(n) induces a uniform deterministic polynomial-time procedure deciding the same language.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:observer-separation-agents
title: Observer separation as boundary-limited agents
statement_text: The following are equivalent: No finite boundary-limited agent (x,b,t) decides the hard family (g_m) . No finite N-Frame envelope decides the hard family (g_m) . P ≠ NP .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:cew-invariance
title: CEW invariance under the N-Frame encoding regime
statement_text: For any two compiler-equivalent encodings of the same observer O at length n , their CEW values coincide: Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ (Π^ * [P_ O ,n ] ) = Γ^ B' _ κ, ℓ (Π^ * ' [P'_ O ,n ] ), for all admissible changes (B,Π^ * ,P)mapsto (B',Π^ * ' ,P') induced by the compiler templates.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:spdp-separation-compiled
title: SPDP separation in the compiled (blocked) model
statement_text: Fix (κ, ℓ )=Θ( log n) and the radius-- 1 block partition B induced by the uniform compiler templates. Field convention: The NP-side lower bound uses a coefficient-space identity minor with diagonal entries ± 1 , which is invertible over any field---hence no characteristic restriction is required for the lower bound. The P-side upper bound and Width ⇒ Rank theorem are stated over characteristic 0 (or prime p > poly (n) ) to ensure that multilinearization and polynomial identity arguments hold without cancellation issues. For the separation conclusion, any fixed choice of such a field suffices. Then the following three facts (proved in this manuscript) imply P ≠ NP : (P-side compiled upper bound) For every deterministic machine M ∈ DTIME (n^c) , the uniformly compiled family {P_ M,n } satisfies Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ (P_ M,n ) ≤ n^ O(1) . (Item (1) holds uniformly for all polynomial time bounds by the universal-machine unrolling (Section ), hence applies to every L ∈ P .) (NP-side explicit compiled lower bound) There exists an explicit uniform 3 SAT witness family {Φ_n} such that the associated coupled clause-sheet polynomials {Q^ × _ Φ_n } satisfy Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ (Q^ × _ Φ_n ) ≥ n^ Θ( log n) . (The identity minor has ± 1 diagonal entries, so this holds over any field.) (See Theorem and Lemma .) (Instance-uniform, witness-free extraction and rank monotonicity) For every instance Φ there is an instance-uniform map T_Φ (depending only on Φ , not on any witness) such that T_Φ(P_ M',N(Φ) ) = Q^ × _Φ and Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ (T_Φ(p)) ≤ Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ (p) \ for all polynomials p. Consequently, P ≠ NP .
bounds: DTIME(n^c); \Theta(\log n); poly(n); O(1); n^c; n^{O(1)}; n^{\Theta(\log n)}

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:cew-observer
title: Observer-capacity (CEW)
statement_text: The Contextual Entanglement Width of an observer/machine M at input length n is CEW _ κ, ℓ ^ B (M;n) := Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ (P_ M,n ), where Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ ( · ) is the SPDP rank invariant defined in Definition .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: prop:cew-is-spdp
title: CEW is exactly SPDP rank
statement_text: For every machine M and input length n , CEW _ κ, ℓ ^ B (M;n) = Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ (P_ M,n ).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:god-move
title: N-Frame God-Move (codimension-collapse projection)
statement_text: The N-Frame God-Move is the canonical block-local global projection Π_Φ: F [u,v] → F [u] (computed uniformly from Φ and the fixed compiler templates) obtained by: (i) restricting administrative/tableau blocks v to fixed constants, (ii) projecting to the clause-sheet blocks u , and (iii) applying a fixed block-local relabeling/basis normalization. We also refer to Π_Φ as the codimension-collapse projection .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:god-move-properties
title: God-Move correctness and rank monotonicity
statement_text: For every instance Φ , Π_Φ(P_ M',N(Φ) ) = Q^ × _Φ and Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ (Π_Φ(p)) ≤ Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ (p). Moreover, Π_Φ is instance-uniform and witness-free.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:god-move-gauge
title: Global God-Move Gauge (Global gauge projection map)
statement_text: A global gauge is a canonical diagonal basis Π^+=A under which every compiled program has radius-1 locality and acts within the same finite local type algebra Σ . This gauge choice unifies the representation of all computational families so that SPDP-rank and contextual-entanglement width are invariant under basis changes within the gauge.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:observer-separation
title: Observer-class separation under the Global God-Move gauge
statement_text: Fix (κ, ℓ )=Θ( log n) and the universal gauge Π^ * . Then the following two statements hold: (Polynomial-time observers have polynomial CEW). For every deterministic polynomial-time machine M ∈ DTIME (n^ c ) , the induced observer O _M satisfies CEW ^ B _ κ, ℓ ( O _M;n) ≤ n^ O(1) . (An explicit NP witness family has superpolynomial CEW). There exists an explicit family of NP witnesses {Φ_n} (e.g.\ Ramanujan--Tseitin / identity-minor family) such that the induced observers O _ Φ_n satisfy CEW ^ B _ κ, ℓ ( O _ Φ_n ;n) ≥ n^ Ω( log n) .
bounds: \Theta(\log n); O(1); \Omega(\log n); n^{c}; n^{O(1)}; n^{\Omega(\log n)}

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:p-neq-np-from-observers
title: P ≠ NP (standard complexity consequence)
statement_text: If P=NP , then the NP witness family in Theorem (2) would be decidable by a polynomial-time machine, hence would induce a polynomial-time observer with polynomial CEW, contradicting Theorem (2). Therefore P ≠ NP .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:global-god-move
title: Holographic Upper-Bound Principle
statement_text: There exist a constant C ≥ 1 and a fixed deterministic projection Π_N (uniform per input length N ) such that for every Boolean function f ∈ P , rk _ SPDP (E(f); r(n) ) ≤ n^ O(1) for r(n) = ( log n)^C, κ ≤ r(n).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:uniform-projection
title: Global God Move / Uniform Projection
statement_text: For every n and κ , there is an explicit, polytime projection Π_n onto the binom n κ monomials m_S = Π _ i ∉ S x_ i,i such that Π_n M_ κ,0 ( perm _n) = I_ binom n κ . In particular, M_ κ,0 ( perm _n) contains an identity minor of size binom n κ , hence Γ_ κ,0 ( perm _n) ≥ binom n κ = 2^ Ω(n) . The map Π_n is uniformly realizable by PAC.compile (n,κ) . The identity claim admits a dual Lagrangian/Farkas certificate: for each S , v = e_ m_S solves Π_n M v = e_S and no y with A^top y = 0 separates e_S , where A = Π_n M .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:main-final
title: Unconditional separation via SPDP collapse vs explicit minor witness
statement_text: There exists an explicit family of 3 CNF formulas {Φ_n} such that for the matched SPDP parameters (κ, ℓ )=Θ( log n) and the fixed compiled block partition B induced by the uniform compiler templates, the following holds: ( P-side collapse ) For every deterministic Turing machine M running in time n^ O(1) , the compiled object associated to M and input length n has SPDP rank at most n^ O(1) after applying the canonical restriction/projection pipeline. ( NP-side non-collapse ) The explicit witness family {Φ_n} yields compiled objects whose SPDP rank is n^ Ω( log n) (in particular, superpolynomial) under the same parameters (κ, ℓ ) and the same compilation/pipeline. Consequently, P ≠ NP .
bounds: \Theta(\log n); O(1); \Omega(\log n); n^{O(1)}; n^{\Omega(\log n)}

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:semantic-closure-compiled
title: Semantic closure of the compiled normal form under P -decidability
statement_text: Fix the compiler template family C (radius--1 blocks, diagonal basis, and Π^+ ) and parameters (κ, ℓ )=Θ( log n) . For each Boolean function f_n:{0,1}^n → {0,1} , let C (f_n) denote the compiler's canonical compiled representation of f_n (i.e.\ the unique normal-form output of C on any description of f_n within the admitted source class, modulo the equivalences listed below). The compiler satisfies the following representation invariance properties (as proved in Theorem and Corollary ): (Normal-form invariance.) If two admitted source descriptions D,D' compute the same Boolean function f_n , then the canonical compiled outputs C (D) and C (D') are equivalent under a finite sequence of the compiler equivalence moves listed in Definition (Appendix ), i.e. C (D) ≡ _ comp C (D'). (Rank invariance under compiler equivalences.) If P ≡ _ comp P' , then Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ (P') ≤ poly (n) · Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ (P), and the same bound holds with P,P' swapped. In particular, no compiler equivalence can turn an n^ Ω( log n) SPDP-rank lower bound into an n^ O(1) bound. Therefore, if f_n ∈ P , the canonical compiled representation C (f_n) satisfies Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ ( C (f_n)) ≤ n^ O(1) .
bounds: \Theta(\log n); poly(n); \Omega(\log n); O(1); n^{\Omega(\log n)}; n^{O(1)}

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: CEW - Contextual Entanglement Width
statement_text: For a Boolean function f: {0,1}^n → {0,1} and observer O , the Contextual Entanglement Width is: CEW _O(f) = max _ t ≤ 2^n dim ( span {O_t(x) : x ∈ {0,1}^n}) where O_t represents the observer's state after t computation steps.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:structural-cew
title: Structural CEW
statement_text: For a compiled program in the diagonal holographic basis, the structural CEW CEW (p) is defined as the maximum, over all time steps t , of the number of block interfaces simultaneously touched by primitive operations at time t , under the fixed, input-independent access schedule produced by the compiler.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:spdp-cew
title: SPDP-based CEW (Appendix-only)
statement_text: In some appendix sections we introduce an alternative, purely algebraic notion of CEW: for fixed derivative parameters (κ, ℓ ) we define CEW _ κ, ℓ (p) to be the minimum w such that there exists a universal restriction ρ^ * with Γ_ κ, ℓ (p upharpoonright ρ^ * ) ≤ w . This SPDP-based CEW is used only as an equivalent characterisation of low-width behaviour.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: CEW
statement_text: For a straight-line program P on n inputs and window w , with r(n)=( log n)^C , CEW _w(P) is the maximum support size of any intermediate of formal degree ≤ r(n) encountered in window w . The global CEW is CEW (P)=max _w CEW _w(P) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:cew-subadd
title: Subadditivity
statement_text: If P=g(P_1, ... ,P_t) with bounded fan-in t ≤ t_0 , then CEW (P) ≤ C_1(t_0) Σ _i CEW (P_i)+C_2(t_0) n^ c_0 .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:cew-mono
title: Monotonicity
statement_text: For any input restriction ρ , CEW (P upharpoonright _ρ) ≤ CEW (P) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:cew-depth4
title: Depth--4/log--degree
statement_text: If f has a size- n^k deterministic circuit, then f admits a ΣΠΣΠ form with each factor multilinear and deg , vars ≤ ( log n)^C , hence CEW (f) ≤ n^ c_2k .
