paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:splitter
title: Combinatorial isolating family for κ -sets
statement_text: Let [N] index variables/blocks with N=Θ(n) . Fix κ=α log n for any constant α>0 . There exists a family H ={h_1, ... ,h_t} of hash functions h_j:[N] → [m] with m:=c_0 κ^2 and t:=c_1(κ log N+10) (for absolute constants c_0,c_1 ) such that for every κ -subset S ⊆ [N] there is some j with h_j injective on S .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:identity-minor
title: DEPRECATED - Identity minor for additive clause SoS
statement_text: Let F be a field of characteristic 0 or prime p > poly (n) . Let Q_ Φ_n =1- Σ _ C ∈ Φ_n V_C(x)^2 be the clause-violation SoS for a fixed 3 SAT instance family (Ramanujan/Tseitin-based or any with bounded degree and clause locality). With κ=α log n and ℓ =β log n , there exists a set R of binom N κ row indices and a matching set C of column monomials such that the SPDP submatrix M_ κ, ℓ (Q_ Φ_n )[ R , C ] is the identity.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:isolating-family-deprecated
title: DEPRECATED - Isolating Family for additive sheet (INCORRECT)
statement_text: Let Q_ Φ_n (x)=1- Σ _ C ∈ Φ_n V_C(x)^2 be the clause--sheet SoS polynomial for a 3SAT/Tseitin instance on N=Θ(n) block--variables, with each clause block depending on O(1) local variables (radius 1 ). Fix constants 0<w<1 and c>0 , and set k:=lfloor w log nrfloor , ℓ :=lfloor c log nrfloor . There exists a family S ⊆ binom [N] κ of κ -subsets of blocks, with | S | = n^ Θ( log n) , and for each S ∈ S a monomial x^ β(S) of degree ≤ ℓ , such that in the SPDP matrix M_ κ, ℓ (Q_ Φ_n ) the submatrix indexed by rows {(S,1):S ∈ S } and columns {x^ β(S) :S ∈ S } is the identity. In particular, Γ_ κ, ℓ (Q_ Φ_n )\ ≥ \ | S |\ =\ n^ Θ( log n) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:np-identity-minor
title: Identity-minor lower bound
statement_text: Let F be a field of characteristic 0 or prime p > poly (n) . Let {Φ_n} be a Ramanujan--Tseitin family compiled to the same local SoS form Q_ Φ_n (x)=1- Σ _ C ∈ Φ_n V_C(x)^2 with the same block partition B . There exist constants K,β>0 such that for κ=lfloor K log nrfloor and ℓ =lfloor β log nrfloor , Γ_ κ, ℓ (Q_ Φ_n ) ≥ n^ Θ( log n) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:3sat-combinatorial-lb
title: \#3SAT SPDP lower bound
statement_text: Let φ be a 3-CNF on n variables with at least k ≥ 2^ n/2 satisfying assignments. Let χ_φ be its characteristic multilinear polynomial. Then over any field of characteristic 0 or sufficiently large prime, rk _ SPDP , ℓ (χ_φ)\ ≥ \ 2^ Ω(n) for any fixed ℓ ≥ 1 ; in particular rk _ SPDP , ℓ (χ_φ) ≥ k ≥ 2^ n/2 .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:entropy-weight
title: Entropy/weight bound, one-line form
statement_text: Let a random partition [n]=Y ∪ Z ∪ W place each coordinate independently into Y,Z,W with probability 1/3 . Then Pr l[\ l||Y|-tfrac n 3 r|>ε n or l||Z|-tfrac n 3 r|>ε n or l||W|-tfrac n 3 r|>ε n\ r]\ ≤ \ 2^ -Ω(ε^2 n) . In particular, with probability 1-2^ -Ω(n) all three parts have size Θ(n) ; a union bound over 2^ O(n) candidate structures still leaves 2^ -Ω(n) failure probability.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:hard-family-recalled
title: recalled, hard family
statement_text: There exists ε>0 such that rk _ SPDP , ℓ (χ_ φ_n )\ ≥ \ 2^ ε n for all sufficiently large n .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:p-upper-recalled
title: recalled, P-side upper bound
statement_text: If L ∈ P , then for each input length n the length- n slice L_n has a multilinear representative f_ L,n with rk _ SPDP , ℓ (f_ L,n )\ ≤ \ n^c for some constant c=c(L, ℓ ) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:3sat-hard-rank
title: Exponential SPDP rank on hard 3-SAT instances
statement_text: There exists ε>0 such that rk _ SPDP , ℓ (χ_ φ_n )\ ≥ \ 2^ ε n for all large n .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:rank-projection
title: SPDP rank under projection and submatrices
statement_text: Let f be multilinear on variables split as (x,y) with disjoint supports. If we delete all SPDP columns whose monomials use any y -variable, the resulting submatrix of M_ ℓ (f) has rank ≤ rk _ SPDP , ℓ (f) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:product-dummy
title: Product with a dummy factor
statement_text: Let f(x) be multilinear on x and D(d) be any multilinear polynomial on disjoint dummy variables d , and fix ℓ ≥ 0 . For every S ⊆ vars (x) with |S|= ℓ and every shift α(x) on x (no d -variables), α(x) · partial _S l(f(x) D(d) r)\ =\ l(α(x) · partial _S f(x) r) D(d). Consider the block of M_ ℓ (f · D) whose columns are restricted to monomials on x only (i.e., ignoring any column that uses a d -variable). That block equals M_ ℓ (f) multiplied on the right by a diagonal matrix with the nonzero scalar D(0, ... ,0) on its diagonal if we project the dummy variables to d=0 . In particular, if D is a nonzero multilinear polynomial (e.g., a nonzero constant or a single dummy variable evaluated at 1 ), then the rank of that block is rank (M_ ℓ (f)) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:block-lower-tri
title: Block-lower-triangular sum
statement_text: If a matrix M is block-lower-triangular with diagonal blocks B_1, ... ,B_t , then rank (M)\ ≥ \ Σ _ i=1 ^t rank (B_i).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:unit-dummy-pad
title: Unit-dummy padding
statement_text: Given a 3-CNF φ(x) , define pad (φ) on (x,d) by adding (a polynomial number of) unit clauses d_j for fresh dummies d=(d_1, ... ,d_t) , and do not introduce any clause that mixes d with x . Then the satisfying assignments of pad (φ) are precisely the pairs (a, 1 ) with amodels φ and d= 1 . Consequently, the characteristic polynomial factors as χ_ pad (φ) (x,d)\ =\ χ_φ(x) · Π _ j=1 ^t d_j.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:no-padding-unit
title: No-padding under unit-dummy padding
statement_text: For unit-dummy paddings pad as above, rk _ SPDP , ℓ l(χ_ pad (φ) r)\ ≥ \ rk _ SPDP , ℓ (χ_φ).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:padding-robust
title: Robustness of the lower bound
statement_text: If rk _ SPDP , ℓ (χ_ φ_n ) ≥ 2^ ε n then rk _ SPDP , ℓ l(χ_ pad (φ_n) r) ≥ 2^ ε n for any unit-dummy padding.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:round-trip-nc0
title: Round-trip NC ^0 padding
statement_text: There exist NC ^0 maps pad : 3CNF (n) → 3CNF (n+O(n log n)), unpad : 3CNF (n+O(n log n)) → 3CNF (n), such that for every φ : (Satisfiability preservation) φ is satisfiable iff pad (φ) is satisfiable. (Assignment recovery) Any satisfying assignment to pad (φ) maps (in NC ^0 ) to a satisfying assignment to φ . (Rank preservation) rk _ SPDP , ℓ l(χ_ pad (φ) r) ≥ rk _ SPDP , ℓ (χ_φ)/ poly (|φ|) . (Independence) The dummy variables in pad (φ) do not appear together with original variables in any clause beyond trivial unit clauses, so the SPDP matrix acquires a block-lower-triangular structure.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:separation-3sat
title: Separation on 3-SAT
statement_text: 3 - SAT ∉ P . In particular, P ≠ NP .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:cnf-zero-test
title: CNF zero--test polynomial
statement_text: Set the clause sum S_j(x)\ :=\ ℓ _ j,1 (x)+ ℓ _ j,2 (x)+ ℓ _ j,3 (x), and the CNF polynomial P_n(x)\ :=\ Π _ j=1 ^m S_j(x).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:poly-decides-sat
title: Polynomial decides SAT
statement_text: For every assignment a ∈ {0,1}^n , amodels Φ_n Longleftrightarrow P_n(a) ≠ 0.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:num-monomials
title: Number of monomials
statement_text: Expanding P_n yields exactly 3^m multilinear monomials: P_n(x)\ =\ Σ _ s ∈ {1,2,3}^m Π _ j=1 ^m ℓ _ j,s_j (x). Each choice string s=(s_1, ... ,s_m) picks one literal from each clause and determines a distinct monomial.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:selector-independence
title: Selector assignments ⇒ independence
statement_text: Assume the base field has characteristic 0 or a prime >3 . Then the 3^m monomials l{ M_s(x):= Π _ j=1 ^m ℓ _ j,s_j (x) m| s ∈ {1,2,3}^m r} are linearly independent.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:global-spdp-exp
title: Global SPDP rank is exponential
statement_text: Over any field of characteristic 0 or >3 , rk _ SPDP , all (P_n)\ ≥ \ 3^m\ =\ 2^ Ω(n) for m=Θ(n) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:cnf-hard-lang
title: CNF-Hard language
statement_text: CNF - Hard _n\ :=\ l{ a ∈ {0,1}^n : P_n(a) ≠ 0 r}\ =\ SAT (Φ_n). Then CNF - Hard := cup_n CNF - Hard _n is in NP (witness: a satisfying assignment), and by Corollary the associated polynomial family {P_n} has exponential global SPDP rank whenever m=Θ(n) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:universal-tableau-reduction
title: Uniform tableau family reduction
statement_text: For each k there exists k'=k+O(1) and a uniform Cook--Levin tableau polynomial UconfPoly _k(n) (for U_k on inputs of length n'= poly (n) ) such that for every deterministic M ∈ DTIME (n^k) there is a restriction ρ_M (fixing the code bits encoding ⟨ M ⟩ ) with UconfPoly _k(n) upharpoonright ρ_M ≡ confPoly (M,n), up to a harmless renaming of tableau variables. In particular, for any further restriction ρ , rk _ SPDP , ℓ l( confPoly (M,n) upharpoonright ρ r) ≤ rk _ SPDP , ℓ l( UconfPoly _k(n) upharpoonright ρ r) ( restriction monotonicity ).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:codim-collapse
title: Codimension collapse; deterministic (fixed exponent)
statement_text: Fix a constant k ≥ 1 . There exists a computable map n longmapsto s^ * _k(n) ∈ {0,1}^ O( log n) such that the restriction ρ^ * _ n,k :=ρ_ s^ * _k(n) satisfies, for every deterministic M ∈ DTIME (n^k) , rk _ SPDP , ℓ ( confPoly (M,n) upharpoonright ρ^ * _ n,k ) ≤ n^ 6 for each fixed ℓ ∈ {2,3}.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:np-restriction
title: Uniform NP-side rank lower bound
statement_text: Let V be any polynomial-time verifier for a language L ∈ NP , and let {p_ x } be the compiled workloads produced by the deterministic radius- 1 compiler (in the diagonal basis with Π^+=A ) on inputs x of length n . There exist absolute constants c_0,c_1>0 and a canonically defined restriction ρ^ * (the universal restriction) such that, for all sufficiently large n , Γ_ κ, ℓ (p_ x upharpoonright _ ρ^ * )\ ≥ \ n^ c_0 log n for some x with |x|=n , and with κ, ℓ =c_1 log n. In particular, the NP-side SPDP rank is super-polynomial under the same (κ, ℓ ) used on the P-side.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:explicit-id-minor
title: Explicit identity-minor under the universal restriction
statement_text: Work over characteristic 0 (or prime p> poly (n) ). After the universal restriction ρ^ * , each block B exposes a constant-size interface consisting of a live private literal x_B and its attached parity edge bit y_B . There exist: a set of κ=Θ( log n) vertex-disjoint lanes L _1, ... , L _κ in the expander scaffold (each lane is a disjoint set of blocks), and for each lane L _j , a block subset S_j ⊆ L _j with |S_j| ≥ n^ Ω(1) , such that the SPDP evaluation submatrix indexed by R \ =\ { (τ_ j,s ,u_ j,s ) : j ∈ [κ],\ s ∈ S_j } and C \ =\ { s =(s_1, ... ,s_κ): s_j ∈ S_j } contains a diagonal (identity) minor of size Π _ j=1 ^κ |S_j|\ =\ n^ Θ( log n) . Here (τ_ j,s ,u_ j,s ) denotes the local derivative coordinate at block u_ j,s ∈ S_j chosen as below. Consequently, rk _ SPDP , ℓ (p upharpoonright _ ρ^ * )\ ≥ \ n^ Θ( log n) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:annihilator
title: Deterministic annihilator
statement_text: There is a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that outputs a nonzero vector w_n such that ⟨ w_n,\ g( · +e) ⟩ = 0 for all g ∈ V_n and all shifts e ∈ {0,1}^n, while ⟨ w_n,\ h( · +e^ † ) ⟩ ≠ 0 for at least one NP-witnessed hard instance h( · )= jointPoly (V^ † ,n) upharpoonright ρ_ * [w^ † ] from Theorem (some fixed witness w^ † and shift e^ † ).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:cew-equiv
title: Equivalence
statement_text: For every Boolean f , CEW _ ℓ (f)= rk _ SPDP , ℓ (p_f upharpoonright ρ_ * ) . Moreover, multilinearization and the choice of ρ_ * do not increase the rank.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:codim-collapse
title: Codimension Collapse
statement_text: For every deterministic Turing machine M running in time t(n)=n^k and every input length n , there exists a seed s_* ∈ {0,1}^ O( log n) such that for ρ_ s_* we have, for each fixed ℓ ∈ {2,3} , rk _ SPDP , ℓ ( confPoly (M,n) upharpoonright ρ_ s_* ) ≤ n^ 6 .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:Fnk
title: Template-local constraint family F _ n,k
statement_text: Let F _ n,k be the set of all width- ≤ 5 CNF constraints obtained by instantiating the compiler's finite template library (for exponent k ) at every legal tableau position for input length n and time bound t(n)=n^k .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:canonical-dtdepth
title: Canonical decision-tree depth
statement_text: Fix a deterministic procedure CanTree (Ψ) which, given a CNF Ψ , constructs a decision tree by repeatedly selecting the first clause in a fixed ordering that is not yet forced by the partial assignment and querying the first unassigned literal in it. Let cDTdepth (Ψ) denote the depth of this canonical tree (or + ∞ if it does not halt).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:cdtdepth-check-poly
title: Polynomial-time depth check for cDTdepth
statement_text: For a width- w CNF Ψ , the predicate cDTdepth (Ψ) ≤ d can be decided in time poly ( size (Ψ)) · (O(w))^ d by explicitly expanding the canonical tree to depth d and evaluating Ψ at each node. In particular, for w=O(1) and d=O( log n) this is n^ O(1) time.
bounds: poly(size(\Psi)); O(w); O(1); O(\log n); n^{O(1)}

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:canonical-switching
title: Canonical switching lemma bound (CNF)
statement_text: Fix width w ≥ 1 and let Ψ be a width- w CNF. Under a p -random restriction ρ (independently star each variable with probability p , otherwise fix uniformly), the canonical decision-tree depth satisfies Pr _ ρ l[ cDTdepth (Ψ upharpoonright ρ) > d r] ≤ (C · p w)^ d for an absolute constant C>0 (equivalently, (pw)^ Ω(d) ).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:enumerate-Fnk
title: Template enumeration of the bounded-width family
statement_text: For each fixed time exponent k , the set F _ n,k of all bounded-width CNF subformulas arising from the (universal) tableau unrolling for U_k (Section ) can be enumerated in time poly (n) , and satisfies | F _ n,k | ≤ n^ c_F(k) for some constant c_F(k) depending only on k .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:depth-check-runtime
title: Depth-check runtime
statement_text: Let Ψ be a width- w CNF of size at most m(n)=n^ c_2(k) . Given a restriction ρ_s and a depth threshold d=O( log n) , the predicate cDTdepth (Ψ upharpoonright ρ_s) ≤ d can be decided in time poly (m(n)) · 2^ O(d) = n^ O(1) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:det-universal-restriction-fixed-M
title: Deterministic universal restriction (fixed M )
statement_text: Fix w:=5 , p:=1/(8w)=1/40 , and d:=12w( log n+1)=Θ( log n) . Fix a machine M with t(n) ≤ n^c , and let F _n(M) be as in Lemma . There exists a restriction ρ^ * =ρ^ * (M,n):[N(n)] → {0,1, * } with star-rate p such that simultaneously for all Ψ ∈ F _n(M) , cDTdepth (Ψupharpoonright ρ^ * ) ≤ d. Moreover, ρ^ * can be found deterministically in time n^ O(1) by enumerating an explicit restriction family S _ n,c of size n^ O(1) (from the derandomized switching lemma/PRG) and testing the depth predicate using Lemma .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:pr-switching
title: Pseudorandom switching lemma (explicit restrictions)
statement_text: Fix width w=O(1) and star-rate p ∈ (0,1) (e.g.\ p=1/(40w) ). There exists an explicit restriction generator Gen with seed length s= O ( log m+ log (1/ε)) such that for every width- w CNF Ψ of size at most m , if ρ arrow Gen (U_s) then Pr [ cDTdepth (Ψ upharpoonright _ρ) > d ] ≤ ε, where d = O(w log (m/ε)). Moreover, ρ is computable in poly (N,m,1/ε) time from the seed.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:universal-restriction
title: Explicit universal restriction for the machine-independent family F _ n,k
statement_text: Fix a constant time exponent k ≥ 1 . Fix w=O(1) and let F _ n,k be the machine-independent family of width- w CNFs produced by the compiler templates at input length n and time bound n^k (Definition ), with | F _ n,k | ≤ n^ c_2(k) and each Ψ ∈ F _ n,k of size ≤ n^ c_Φ(k) . Set ε := n^ -10 and let d:=O( log n) be as in Theorem . Then there exists a seed s^ * _k(n) such that the restriction ρ^ * _ n,k := Gen (s^ * _k(n)) satisfies cDTdepth (Ψ upharpoonright _ ρ^ * _ n,k ) ≤ d for all Ψ ∈ F _ n,k . Furthermore, such an s^ * _k(n) (hence ρ^ * _ n,k ) can be found deterministically in time n^ O(1) by enumerating all seeds and checking the canonical decision tree depth up to d for each Ψ ∈ F _ n,k .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:explicit-prg-width5
title: Explicit pseudorandom restriction family for width- 5 formulas
statement_text: Fix constants w:=5 and p:=1/40 . For each n and fixed time exponent k , there exists an explicit family S _ n,k of restrictions ρ:[N(n)] → {0,1, * } with star-rate p and | S _ n,k | ≤ n^ a(k) such that the following holds. Let F _ n,k be the (machine-independent) family of width- 5 CNF formulas arising from the radius-- 1 compiler at length n and time bound t(n) ≤ n^k (as in Lemma ). (Switching/PRG bounds are stated for bounded-width CNF/DNF in the literature; throughout we use only the CNF case.) Then there exists ρ^ * ∈ S _ n,k such that for all Ψ ∈ F _ n,k , cDTdepth (Ψ upharpoonright ρ^ * )\ ≤ \ d where d:=12w( log n+1)=O( log n). Moreover, such a ρ^ * can be found deterministically in n^ O(1) time by enumerating S _ n,k and checking the predicate cDTdepth (Ψ upharpoonright ρ) ≤ d for all Ψ ∈ F _ n,k using Lemma .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:explicit-restriction-family-proof
title: Explicit restriction family for a polynomial-size width- w CNF family
statement_text: Fix a constant width w ≥ 1 and a star-rate p ∈ (0,1) . Let F _ n,k be any family of width- w CNF formulas over N=N(n) variables such that | F _ n,k | ≤ n^ a(k) for some constant a(k) depending only on k . Fix a depth parameter d=d(n) and an error parameter ε=ε(n) . Assume there is an explicit distribution D _ n,k over p -restrictions ρ:[N] → {0,1, * } with the following two properties: For every Ψ ∈ F _ n,k , | Pr _ ρ D _ n,k [ cDTdepth (Ψ upharpoonright ρ)>d ] - Pr _ ρ R _ p [ cDTdepth (Ψ upharpoonright ρ)>d ] | \ ≤ \ ε, where R _ p denotes the truly random p -restriction distribution. The support S _ n,k := supp ( D _ n,k ) satisfies | S _ n,k | ≤ n^ b(k) for some constant b(k) depending only on k , and S _ n,k can be enumerated deterministically in time n^ O(1) . Suppose further that the (random) switching lemma bound yields, for all Ψ ∈ F _ n,k , Pr _ ρ R _ p [ cDTdepth (Ψ upharpoonright ρ)>d ] \ ≤ \ δ and δ+ε\ ≤ \ n^ -10-a(k) . Then there exists a restriction ρ^ * ∈ S _ n,k such that ∀ Ψ ∈ F _ n,k , cDTdepth (Ψ upharpoonright ρ^ * )\ ≤ \ d. Moreover, such a ρ^ * can be found deterministically in time n^ O(1) by enumerating S _ n,k and checking the predicate cDTdepth (Ψ upharpoonright ρ) ≤ d for all Ψ ∈ F _ n,k .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:per-constraint-monomials
title: Per-constraint monomial bound
statement_text: There exists a constant a ≥ 1 such that, for all large n and all Ψ ∈ F _n , \# Mon ( ML (Ψ upharpoonright ρ^ * _n) ) ≤ n^a.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:global-rank-bound-confpoly
title: Global compiled SPDP-rank bound for the configuration polynomial
statement_text: Fix compiled SPDP parameters (κ, ℓ )=(K log n, K log n) for a fixed constant K . For every M ∈ DTIME (n^ c ) (for any fixed constant c ), the compiled configuration polynomial family satisfies Γ^B_ κ, ℓ ( confPoly (M,n) )\ ≤ \ n^ O(1) . Moreover, for any restriction ρ , Γ^B_ κ, ℓ ( confPoly (M,n) upharpoonright ρ )\ ≤ \ Γ^B_ κ, ℓ ( confPoly (M,n) ).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:restricted-dnf-size
title: Size bound from depth bound
statement_text: If cDTdepth (Ψ upharpoonright ρ) ≤ d , then DNF (Ψ,ρ) has at most 2^ d terms and is constructible in time polynomial in |Ψ| · 2^ d . In particular, for d=Θ( log n) this yields a polynomial-size DNF.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: clm:restricted-cnf-dnf-size
title: Restricted width-5 CNF has polynomial-size DNF under bounded-depth decision tree
statement_text: Let Ψ be a width- 5 CNF formula and let ρ be a restriction such that the canonical decision tree SwitchTree (Ψ upharpoonright ρ) has depth at most d = O( log n) . Then: The restricted formula Ψ upharpoonright ρ has a DNF representation of size at most 2^d = poly (n) ; The DNF is explicitly constructible from Ψ and ρ in time polynomial in |Ψ| · 2^d ; No global CNF-to-DNF expansion is needed---this DNF is extracted directly from the canonical decision tree under a fixed variable order (e.g., FoL/twistor sweep).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:det-switching
title: Deterministic Switching
statement_text: Let Φ be a width- w CNF over N variables. Set p:=(1)/(8w) and d:=12w( log n+1) . There is a deterministically constructible restriction ρ^ † :[N] → {0,1, * } that fixes at least (1-p)N ≥ N/2 variables such that cDTdepth (Φupharpoonright ρ^ † )\ ≤ \ d, and ρ^ † can be computed in time n^ O(1) given oracle access sufficient to evaluate Φ on partial assignments.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:bounded-width-formula-count
title: Counting bounded-width tableau subformulas (fixed machine)
statement_text: Fix a deterministic machine M and a time bound t(n) ≤ n^c . Let F _n(M) denote the family of width- 5 CNF subformulas that occur as local tableau constraints (local unrollings) inside the configuration polynomial confPoly (M,n) . Then | F _n(M)| ≤ n^ c_0(M,c) for all sufficiently large n , for some constant c_0(M,c) depending only on M and c (not on n ).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: clm:tableau-width-cnf
title: Tableau predicate as bounded-width CNF (no CNF → DNF expansion)
statement_text: For a time bound t(n)=n^k and input length n , the accepting-tableau predicate can be expressed as a CNF Φ_ M,n in which every clause has width at most w_0 for a fixed constant w_0 ≤ 5 , and whose total size is size (Φ_ M,n ) ≤ n^ c_Φ(k) for some constant c_Φ(k) depending only on the fixed time-exponent k and the chosen normal form for machines.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:np-spdp-lb
title: NP Exponential Lower Bound
statement_text: Fix ℓ ∈ {2,3} and the universal ρ_ * from S 17.7.4. Let V_ can be the canonical 3SAT verifier of Definition for inputs of length n with witness length m=n , and let J(x,w)\ :=\ jointPoly (V_ can ,n) be the multilinear polynomial encoding the accepting tableaux of V_ can on input x ∈ {0,1}^n and witness w ∈ {0,1}^n . Then there exists a witness w such that rk _ SPDP , ℓ (J upharpoonright ρ_ * [w] )\ =\ 2^ Ω(n) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:uniform-np-restriction
title: Uniform NP restriction with explicit growth
statement_text: Fix k ≥ 1 . Let V be any time- n^k verifier and n ≥ 16 . Let ρ^ * _ n,k be the universal restriction from S 17.7.4 with seed length O( log n) . There exists a witness w_ * (n) of length m=Θ(n log n) such that, for ℓ =3 and any κ=lceil α log nrceil with α ≤ (1)/(2) , rk _ SPDP , ℓ ( jointPoly (V,n) upharpoonright ρ^ * _ n,k [w_ * (n)] )\ ≥ \ 2^ (1)/(4) n log n .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:spdp-am
title: SPDP--rank is AM--verifiable
statement_text: Fix a derivative order ℓ ≥ 0 . Let L_ rank \ :=\ {(p,r): rk _ SPDP , ℓ (p) ≥ r}. Then L_ rank ∈ AM .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:rank-cert-circuitsat
title: Rank certificates for Circuit--SAT
statement_text: In our separation, the NP witnesses induce explicit SPDP rows/indices (under the universal restriction), so Circuit--SAT instances admit polynomial-size rank certificates verifiable in polynomial time (equivalently, in AM, hence in NP / poly ).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:det-rank-col-oracle
title: Deterministic low-rank decision under a column--oracle
statement_text: Fix ℓ ≥ 0 . Let M_ ℓ (p) be the order- ℓ SPDP matrix of a multilinear p . Suppose we are given a column-application oracle that, on input a Boolean assignment x ∈ {0,1}^n , returns z(x)\ :=\ V χ(x)\ ∈ F ^r in time poly (n,r) , where M_ ℓ (p)=U V is a (promised) rank factorization over F , χ(x) is the monomial-evaluation vector, and r is an a-priori upper bound on the rank (e.g., r ≤ n^6 for the compiled classes under our universal restriction). Then there is a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that decides whether rk M_ ℓ (p) ≤ r .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:machine-exact-compiler
title: Machine-Exact Compiler Spec with Coupled Verifier Sheet
statement_text: For every uniform polynomial-time decider M of 3SAT (running in time n^c ), there exists a deterministic compiler that produces an instrumented machine M' with the following properties: Clause-gadget prepending with coupling structure. The compiled polynomial P_ M',n can be extracted to a coupled verifier sheet via a deterministic map. Specifically, there exists a local wiring z=ζ(u,v) (setting each selector z_C to 0 or 1 based on the God-Move projection) such that P_ M',n (u, v) = Q_Φ^ × (u,z) |_ z=ζ(u,v) + R_ M',Φ (v), where u represents clause variables, v represents computation variables, Q_Φ^ × (u,z) = Π _ C ∈ Φ (1 - z_C · V_C(u)^2) is the coupled verifier polynomial (Definition ), and R_ M',Φ (v) encodes the Turing machine tableau. For the selected clause-set S = S (n) exposed by the God-Move projection Π_n , we obtain the activated coupled sheet Q_ Φ, S ^ × (u) = Π _ C ∈ S (1-V_C(u)^2). paragraph Choice of the activated clause set. Throughout the separation proof we take S :=C_ disj (Φ) to be the canonical greedy disjoint-clause subfamily guaranteed by Lemma (and used in the identity-minor lower bound). The local wiring z=ζ(u,v) is defined so that z_C=1 iff C ∈ C_ disj (Φ) , yielding Q^ × _ Φ, S =Q^ × _ Φ,C_ disj (Φ) . Locality preservation. Each clause gadget V_C uses only radius- 1 (adjacent-cell) interactions, maintaining CEW (Q_ Φ, S ^ × ) = O(1) . Rank inheritance. The SPDP submatrix induced by the activated coupled sheet satisfies Γ_ κ, ℓ (Q_ Φ, S ^ × ) ≤ Γ_ κ, ℓ (P_ M',n ) ≤ n^ O(1) , for κ, ℓ = Θ( log n) . Acceptance equivalence. For all inputs x , M' accepts x if and only if M accepts x .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:witness-free-restriction
title: Witness-free restriction step
statement_text: Fix any field constants c for the v -variables (e.g.\ set all v:=0 ). Then P_ M',N(Φ) (u,c) = Q^ × _ Φ (u) + const . In particular, restricting v to constants is witness-free and does not require knowledge of any accepting computation.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:tphi-rank-stages
title: Rank monotonicity per stage
statement_text: Each stage in the definition of T_ Φ is rank-preserving or rank-nonincreasing: basis changes and block-local invertible affine relabelings preserve Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ , while restrictions/projections do not increase it.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:extraction-map-wf
title: Extraction map T_ Φ (witness-free)
statement_text: Fix an instance polynomial Φ(u) over the verification variables u . Define T_ Φ to be the substitution/projection operator acting on any compiled polynomial P(u,z,v) by: (Instance wiring) identify the instance-wires in P carrying Φ with the u -variables (as per the uniform compiler wiring of Φ ). (Drop computation scaffold) set all computation variables to a fixed constant string, e.g.\ v arrow 0 . (Drop aux verification tags) set auxiliary tag variables z to their fixed compiler constants, e.g.\ z arrow 0 .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:extraction-no-witness
title: Extraction preserves Φ without a witness
statement_text: Let P_ M',n (u,z,v) be the compiled verifier polynomial for the compiled machine M' at length n , and let Φ(u) be the embedded instance polynomial. Under Lemma , there exist a nonzero polynomial Q_ M',n (u) and a constant Δ_ M',n ∈ F such that T_ Φ (P_ M',n )(u) = Q_ M',n (u) · Φ(u) + Δ_ M',n . Moreover, the definition of T_ Φ uses only fixed substitutions (e.g.\ v arrow 0 ), so it is witness-free and instance-uniform.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:rank-monotone-extraction
title: Rank monotonicity under extraction
statement_text: For the SPDP rank invariant Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ , Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ (T_ Φ (P_ M',n ) ) ≤ Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ (P_ M',n ), i.e.\ extraction cannot increase SPDP rank.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:extraction-normalization
title: Normalization of extraction output
statement_text: Fix (κ, ℓ )=Θ( log n) with κ ≥ 1 . Under the canonical verifier wiring, the extraction output of Lemma can be normalized by rank-nonincreasing block-local operations so that the coupled clause-sheet polynomial is obtained exactly. More precisely, there exists a block-local map N (composition of restrictions, affine relabelings, and block-supported projections) such that for every instance Φ , (N ∘ T_Φ)(P_ M',n ) = Q^ × _Φ, and for all polynomials p , Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ ((N ∘ T_Φ)(p) ) ≤ Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ (p).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:instance-uniform-extraction
title: Instance-Uniform Extraction Map
statement_text: For each 3SAT instance Φ with m clauses and n variables, there exists a block-local extraction map T_Φ : P_ M',n longrightarrow Q^ × _Φ with the following properties: Composition. T_Φ decomposes as a composition of block-local stages T_Φ = ( basis change ) ∘ ( affine relabeling ) ∘ ( restriction ) ∘ ( projection ). Rank monotonicity. Each stage is rank non-increasing, hence Γ_ κ, ℓ (Q^ × _Φ) = Γ_ κ, ℓ (T_Φ(P_ M',n )) ≤ Γ_ κ, ℓ (P_ M',n ). Instance uniformity / witness-free. T_Φ depends only on the clause structure of Φ and does not depend on any satisfying assignment or accepting computation. Computability. T_Φ is computable in poly (n,m) time from Φ .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:canonical-verifier
title: Canonical 3SAT verifier V_ can
statement_text: Fix a standard encoding of 3CNF formulas on n Boolean variables, say Φ(x_1, ... ,x_n) with m = m(n) clauses. We define a verifier V_ can that, on input (Φ,w) where w ∈ {0,1}^n , proceeds as follows: Witness loading phase. For j = 1, ... ,n in order, V_ can reads the j -th bit w_j of the putative witness from the input tape and copies it to a dedicated witness register cell u_j on a separate work tape. This is done using a fixed constant-length sequence of local transitions: move the head to the j -th witness position, read w_j ∈ {0,1} , move to cell u_j on the witness tape and write w_j , return the head to a canonical ``base'' position. The internal control state distinguishes the substeps of this loop, so the loading of each w_j occupies a fixed constant number L_0 of time steps. Deterministic evaluation phase. Having made a local copy of the witness in (u_1, ... ,u_n) , V_ can now deterministically scans the clauses of Φ one by one. For each clause C_ ℓ = ( ℓ _ ℓ ,1 ∨ ℓ _ ℓ ,2 ∨ ℓ _ ℓ ,3 ) it: queries the appropriate witness-register cells u_ i( ℓ ,r) , checks whether at least one literal ℓ _ ℓ ,r is satisfied by the stored bits, if any clause is unsatisfied, enters a rejecting sink state; otherwise continues. If all clauses are satisfied, V_ can enters an accepting sink state. It is immediate that V_ can runs in time T(n) = O(n + m(n)) and verifies satisfiability of Φ in the usual sense: there exists w with V_ can (Φ,w) accepting if and only if Φ is satisfiable.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:witness-neighborhoods
title: Witness-local neighborhoods in the tableau
statement_text: Let T (Φ,w) denote the Cook--Levin space--time tableau of V_ can on input (Φ,w) : a grid of cells indexed by time t and tape position i , each recording the local symbol and control state. For each j ∈ {1, ... ,n} , let t_j be a fixed time step in the witness-loading phase at which the verifier has just completed copying w_j into the register cell u_j and has returned the head to the base position. We define the j -th witness neighborhood to be the set N_j := {(t,i) : |t - t_j| ≤ R,\ |i - i_0| ≤ S}, where (t_j,i_0) is the space--time coordinate of the head in the base position at time t_j , and R,S are fixed constants chosen large enough to contain the entire local transition pattern used to read and write w_j in Phase (1). We call (R,S) the radius of the neighborhood.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:slack-multiplicity
title: Unconditional accepting-witness multiplicity
statement_text: For every satisfiable Φ and every satisfying assignment w_ sat models Φ , the verifier accepts (Φ,(w_ sat ,w_ slack )) for every w_ slack ∈ {0,1}^ s(n) . Hence every satisfiable instance admits at least 2^ s(n) =2^ Ω(n) accepting witnesses.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:block-local-control
title: Block-local witness control (no distributional assumptions)
statement_text: Fix the canonical verifier V_ can (Definition ) and constants R,S from the verifier normal form. There exists a constant β>0 and, for each n , an index set J_n ⊆ [n] of size |J_n| ≥ β n such that the following holds. Let Φ be any satisfiable 3CNF instance on n variables in the padded-hard family (defined below), and fix any satisfying assignment wmodels Φ . Then there exist pairwise-disjoint constant-radius neighborhoods N_j (for j ∈ J_n ) in the space--time diagram of V_ can such that: (Disjointness) The neighborhoods {N_j}_ j ∈ J_n are disjoint and each has radius (R,S) . (Two local patterns) For each j ∈ J_n and each bit b ∈ {0,1} , there exists a locally consistent filling of the cells in N_j corresponding to the witness-loading behavior with w_j=b , while keeping the exterior configuration partial N_j := T (Φ,w) upharpoonright _ outside N_j fixed. (Guaranteed global extension) For each j ∈ J_n and each b ∈ {0,1} , the local pattern from (ii) extends to a globally consistent accepting tableau of V_ can on a satisfying assignment w^ (j,b) satisfying: w^ (j,b) _i = w_i for all i ≠ j, and w^ (j,b) _j = b.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:block-normal-form
title: Verifier block-normal form for the NP-hard family
statement_text: Let Q^ × _ Φ_n be the SPDP-encoded coupled polynomial family associated with the canonical 3SAT instances and verifier V_ can as above. Then, for each input length n , there is a collection N_1, ... ,N_ β n of pairwise disjoint, constant-radius neighborhoods in the Cook--Levin tableau of V_ can such that: each N_j admits two locally consistent fillings corresponding to the two choices w_j ∈ {0,1} at the j -th witness position, and these local degrees of freedom induce 2^ β n distinct monomials in Q^ × _ Φ_n that can be arranged into an identity minor in the SPDP matrix at the parameters (κ', ℓ ') used in the NP-side lower bound. In particular, the `` β n disjoint, locally controlled neighborhoods'' hypothesis used in the proof of Lemma holds for the canonical 3SAT verifier V_ can .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:p-poly-bound
title: P--polynomial bound
statement_text: For every language L ∈ P there is a constant c such that for all input lengths n , rk _ SPDP , ℓ (p_ L_n upharpoonright ρ_ * )\ ≤ \ n^c, where p_ L_n is any multilinear polynomial that agrees with L on {0,1}^n , and ρ_ * is the universal restriction of S 17.7.4. In particular, by Theorem 17.1 (codimension collapse), one may take c=6 .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:observer-spdp-bridge
title: Observer--SPDP bridge
statement_text: For every Boolean f :{0,1}^n → {0,1} , min _ O computes f CEW _ ℓ (O)\ =\ rk _ SPDP , ℓ (p_fupharpoonright ρ_ * )\ =\ CEW _ ℓ (f).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:bp-cew-observer
title: Width-5 BP ⇒ CEW-bounded observer
statement_text: Let B be a width-5 branching program computing f . Then there is an observer O_B with CEW _ ℓ (O_B)=Θ( rk _ SPDP , ℓ (p_fupharpoonright ρ_ * )) that computes f and whose fan-out is ≤ 5 .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:cew-hardness
title: NP-hardness of CEW
statement_text: Given a succinct description of a multilinear polynomial g (e.g., monomial list or sum-of-products circuit), deciding whether CEW _ ℓ (g) ≤ k is NP-hard (already for ℓ =3,4 ).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:superpoly-spdp-gap
title: Superpolynomial SPDP gap
statement_text: There exists f ∈ NP such that, for the universal restriction ρ_ * , rk _ SPDP , ℓ (p_fupharpoonright ρ_ * )\ >\ n^6.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:separation-via-cew
title: Separation via CEW
statement_text: P \ =\ { f | CEW _ ℓ (f) ≤ n^6 } and NP \ ⊇ \ { f | CEW _ ℓ (f) ≥ 2^ Ω(n) }. In particular, P ≠ NP .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:barrier-immunity
title: Barrier immunity
statement_text: The SPDP--rank method simultaneously avoids the two standard barriers: (Non-naturalness.) The property P _c\ =\ l{ f: rk _ SPDP , ℓ (p_f upharpoonright ρ_ * ) ≤ n^c r} has density at most 2^ -Ω(2^n) among Boolean functions on {0,1}^n . (Non-algebrization.) If k/F is any field extension with the same characteristic (either 0 or a sufficiently large fixed prime), then for every f , rk _ SPDP , ℓ ,k (p_f upharpoonright ρ_ * ) \ =\ rk _ SPDP , ℓ ,F (p_f upharpoonright ρ_ * ). Hence the separation does not fall to the Razborov--Rudich natural-proofs barrier nor to algebrization , and uses no oracles.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:rank-gap-implies-pnp
title: Rank gap ⇒ P ≠ NP
statement_text: Suppose there exists {f_n} ⊆ NP and a fixed restriction ρ^ * such that rk _ SPDP , ℓ (p_ f_n upharpoonright ρ^ * )\ ≥ \ n^ ω(1) , while every g ∈ P satisfies rk _ SPDP , ℓ (p_ g_n upharpoonright ρ^ * )\ ≤ \ n^ O(1) . Then P ≠ NP .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:holographic-transform
title: Holographic Transform Π^+
statement_text: The fixed holographic transform Π^+ acts as a block-diagonal linear map on the local variable neighborhoods of a compiled polynomial p(x) : p^ Π^+ (x) = p(Ux), where U is a unitary block matrix, block-local with radius r=1 , satisfying U^top U = I . Each block corresponds to a local ``tile'' in the time × tape layout. Π^+ preserves the total degree and maps Boolean constraints x_i^2 - x_i = 0 to orthogonal projectors on each block subspace.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:local-diagonalization
title: Local Diagonalization
statement_text: For any compiled polynomial p generated by the deterministic oblivious-access compiler (radius r=1 ), Π^+ diagonalizes all block-local quadratic constraints and decouples their higher-order derivative supports. Consequently, every partial derivative of order κ = Θ( log n) in the SPDP matrix M_ κ, ℓ (p^ Π^+ ) is supported on at most O(κ) disjoint blocks.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:holo-upper-bound
title: Holographic Upper-Bound Principle
statement_text: Let p = P_ M,n be the SoS polynomial compiled from any uniform DTM M ∈ DTIME (n^t) . Under the holographic transform Π^+ , Γ_ κ, ℓ (p^ Π^+ ) ≤ n^ O(1) for κ, ℓ = Θ( log n).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:god-move-equivalence
title: God-Move Equivalence
statement_text: A God-Move is a uniform transformation G such that both the P-side and NP-side polynomials are expressed in the same holographic representation, allowing their SPDP ranks to be directly compared: G(P_ M,n ) = P_ M,n ^ Π^+ , G(Q^ × _ Φ_n ) = (Q^ × _ Φ_n )^ Π^+ .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:holo-godmove
title: Holographic God-Move Separation
statement_text: Under the holographic transform Π^+ , Γ_ κ, ℓ (P_ M,n ^ Π^+ ) ≤ n^ O(1) , Γ_ κ, ℓ ((Q^ × _ Φ_n )^ Π^+ ) ≥ n^ Θ( log n) , for κ, ℓ = Θ( log n) . Thus the separation persists in the shared holographic frame.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:spdp-framework-recalled
title: SPDP framework, recalled
statement_text: For a polynomial p(x) and parameters κ, ℓ , the SPDP-matrix M_ κ, ℓ (p) = [partial _S p(x^T)]_ |S|=κ, |T|= ℓ defines the rank measure Γ_ κ, ℓ (p) = rank M_ κ, ℓ (p) . All subsequent constructions occur within ZFC and use only finite combinatorics and algebraic identities.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:self-contained-det-compiler
title: Self-Contained Deterministic Compiler
statement_text: There exists a uniform, deterministic, input-independent compilation pipeline Comp _ det : M longmapsto P_ M,n with the following properties: Locality. Each gate is replaced by constant-radius ( r=1 ) SoS gadgets arranged as layered-wires or time × tape tiles. Complexity. For every M ∈ DTIME (n^t) , the compiled polynomial has size n^ O(1) and contextual entanglement width CEW (P_ M,n ) = O( log n). Rank bound. For κ', ℓ ' = Θ( log n) , Γ_ κ', ℓ ' (P_ M,n ) ≤ n^ O(1) .
bounds: DTIME(n^t); O(1); O(\log n); \Theta(\log n); n^t; n^{O(1)}

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:machine-exact-verifier-norm
title: Machine-Exact Verifier Normalization with Coupling
statement_text: For every uniform decider M of 3SAT (time n^c ), the compiler can be extended---without changing acceptance---to an instrumented machine M' that prepends a static clause-gadget sheet consisting of O(m) disjoint, radius- 1 blocks with coupling selectors, computing the coupled verifier polynomial V_C(x) = OR ( ℓ _1, ℓ _2, ℓ _3), Q_Φ^ × (x,z) = Π _ C ∈ Φ (1 - z_C · V_C(x)^2). Compilation preserves polylog CEW and polynomial rank: Γ_ κ, ℓ (P_ M',n ) ≤ n^ O(1) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:instance-uniform-extraction
title: Instance-Uniform Extraction T_Φ for Coupled Sheets
statement_text: For each instance Φ of 3SAT, there exists a block-local transformation T_Φ = ( basis ) ∘ ( affine relabel ) ∘ ( restriction ) ∘ ( projection ) computable in poly (n) time from Φ alone, such that T_Φ(P_ M',|ρ(Φ)| ) = Q_ Φ, S ^ × and Γ_ κ, ℓ (Q_ Φ, S ^ × ) ≤ Γ_ κ, ℓ (P_ M',|ρ(Φ)| ), where S = S (n) is the activated clause-set from the God-Move projection. Each stage is rank-preserving or non-increasing by the Monotonicity Lemmas (Section ); see Lemma for the combined properties.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:coupled-sheet-extraction
title: Coupled Sheet Extraction with Rank Monotonicity
statement_text: The instrumented polynomial P_ M',n from Lemma admits an extraction to the coupled verifier sheet: there exists a deterministic local wiring z=ζ(u,v) such that for all inputs (u, v) where u represents clause variables and v represents computation variables, P_ M',n (u, v) = Q_Φ^ × (u,z) |_ z=ζ(u,v) + R_ M',Φ (v), where Q_Φ^ × (u,z) = Π _ C ∈ Φ (1-z_C · V_C(u)^2) is the coupled verifier sheet (Definition ) and R_ M',Φ depends only on v (the TM tableau). For the activated clause-set S = S (n) from the God-Move projection, this yields Q_ Φ, S ^ × (u) = Π _ C ∈ S (1-V_C(u)^2) , and the SPDP submatrix induced by the u -blocks satisfies Γ_ κ, ℓ (Q_ Φ, S ^ × ) ≤ Γ_ κ, ℓ (P_ M',n ).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:global-god-move-pnp
title: Global God Move (Global gauge projection map) ⇒ P ≠ NP
statement_text: Assume the premises above. Suppose for contradiction P = NP . Then a polytime decider M for 3SAT exists. By Theorem and Lemma we obtain P_ M',n with Γ_ κ, ℓ (P_ M',n ) ≤ n^ O(1) . Applying Lemma yields for each Φ_n : Γ_ κ, ℓ (Q^ × _ Φ_n ) ≤ n^ O(1) . However, by the NP-side identity-minor lower bound (Section ), Γ_ κ, ℓ (Q^ × _ Φ_n ) ≥ n^ Θ( log n) , a contradiction. Hence boxed P ≠ NP .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:zfc-status
title: Closure and ZFC Status
statement_text: All constructions above---sorting-network compiler, CEW accounting, SPDP rank theory, and instance-uniform extraction---are finitely definable and verifiable within ZFC. No additional axioms, randomness, or oracles are required. Formally verifying the chain in Lean or Coq would therefore constitute a machine-checked ZFC-level proof of P ≠ NP within the SPDP--holographic framework.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:universal-p-to-polyspdp
title: Universal P → poly--SPDP bridge
statement_text: Fix any deterministic Turing machine M ∈ DTIME (n^t) . There exists a uniform , input-independent compiler C _ det producing a multilinear polynomial P_ M,n over a field F (of characteristic 0 , or prime p sufficiently large), such that: ( Uniformity ) P_ M,n is computable from the finite description of M and n in time poly (n) (no dependence on the particular input x ). ( Locality ) P_ M,n is assembled from constant-radius ( r=1 ) local gadgets arranged in a time × tape (or layered-wire) layout. ( Bounded interface types by construction ) in every canonical window, only O(1) gadget types occur, so the induced profile alphabet is finite and independent of the window length κ . ( CEW bound ) CEW (P_ M,n ) = O( log n) . ( SPDP rank bound ) for κ'=α log n and ℓ '=β log n (with fixed constants α,β>0 ), Γ_ κ', ℓ ' (P_ M,n )\ ≤ \ n^ O(1) . Consequently, every language in P admits a polynomial-SPDP-rank representation.

statement_text: Any bounded-fanin Boolean circuit of size poly (n) can be transformed uniformly in poly (n) time into an equivalent bounded-fanin, bounded-fanout circuit of size poly (n) (e.g.\ fanout ≤ 2 ), by replacing each high-fanout wire with a binary tree of copy/buffer gates.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:compiler-bounded-degree
title: Compiler output has bounded local incidence
statement_text: Let M ∈ DTIME (n^t) be deterministic and let C _ det (M,1^n) be the self-contained deterministic compiler of Theorem . Then the induced constraint object (CNF/tableau/gadget system) φ_ M,n : has constant clause/gadget arity w=O(1) , and has bounded incidence degree Δ=O(1) in its clause--variable incidence graph (or equivalently bounded-degree in its local gadget interaction graph).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:uniform-bounded-profile-diversity
title: Uniform bounded profile diversity in Θ( log n) canonical windows
statement_text: Let φ be any constraint object whose incidence graph has bounded degree Δ=O(1) and bounded arity/width w=O(1) (Lemma ). Fix a canonical-window rule that selects a radius- R neighborhood W(v) around an interface variable v in the incidence graph, where R=Θ( log n) . Assume the (interface-anonymous) profile signature has constant description length (as in Definition ). Then the number of distinct profiles realized within any W(v) satisfies P(W(v))\ ≤ \ n^ O(1) , uniformly over all φ and all choices of v , and independent of the SPDP derivative parameter κ .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:cew-to-admissible
title: CEW/log-window ⇒ SPDP-admissible
statement_text: Let P_ M,n be the compiler output polynomial of Theorem . If CEW (P_ M,n )=O( log n) , then the induced canonical-window feature scheme is SPDP-admissible (Definition ) and P_ M,n ∈ C _ coll (n) (Definition ).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:universal-p-to-spdp-consolidated
title: Universal P-to-SPDP Collapse (Consolidated)
statement_text: For every deterministic polynomial-time Turing machine M ∈ DTIME (n^t) , the self-contained deterministic compiler of Theorem produces an SPDP polynomial P_ M,n such that: Object identity: P_ M,n coincides with the SPDP polynomial object used in the Codimension/Collapse Theorem (the compiled polynomial is the same mathematical object analyzed for rank bounds). CEW implies SPDP-admissibility: The CEW bound CEW (P_ M,n ) = O( log n) implies P_ M,n ∈ C _ coll (n) by Lemma . Rank collapse: Consequently, for the parameter regime of Theorem (in particular κ=Θ( log n) and ℓ as specified there), Γ_ κ, ℓ (P_ M,n ) ≤ n^ O(1) . Thus, the universal inclusion P ⊆ C _ coll holds in ZFC, with all quantifiers discharged by explicit uniform construction.
bounds: DTIME(n^t); O(\log n); \Theta(\log n); O(1); n^t; n^{O(1)}

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:width-to-rank-formal
title: Width ⇒ Rank at (κ, ℓ )=Θ( log n)
statement_text: Let p be a local SoS polynomial compiled by the deterministic pipeline with: radius r=1 , local gadget degree O(1) , and contextual entanglement width CEW (p) ≤ C log n. Then for κ = lfloor K log n rfloor , ℓ = lfloor β log n rfloor , Γ_ κ, ℓ (p) ≤ n^ O(1) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:np-identity-minor-formal
title: Identity-Minor Lower Bound
statement_text: Let F be a field of characteristic 0 or prime p > poly (n) . Let Q_ Φ_n ^ × (u,z) = Π _ C ∈ Φ_n l(1 - z_C · V_C(u)^2 r) be the coupled verifier sheet polynomial (Definition ) corresponding to a Ramanujan--Tseitin family on n vertices with log-size activation | S | = Θ( log n) (Global God-Move regime). There exist indices κ, ℓ = Θ( log n) and row/column sets in M_ κ, ℓ (Q_ Φ_n ^ × ) forming an identity submatrix of size n^ Θ( log n) . Hence Γ_ κ, ℓ (Q_ Φ_n ^ × ) ≥ n^ Θ( log n) . The identity-minor construction uses the multiplicative coupling structure which preserves cross-block mixed partials (unlike the additive formulation; see Remark ).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:det-compiler-formal
title: Deterministic Compiler Locality
statement_text: The deterministic oblivious-access compiler maps any M ∈ DTIME (n^t) to a local SoS polynomial P_ M,n with radius 1, degree O(1) , and contextual entanglement width CEW (P_ M,n ) ≤ C log n.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:pi-plus-formal
title: Π^+ Invariance
statement_text: For any block-local positive-cone map Π^+ , Γ_ κ, ℓ (Π^+[p]) = Γ_ κ, ℓ (p).

label: lem:basis-formal
title: Block-Local Basis Invariance

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:mono-formal
title: Restriction/Projection Monotonicity
statement_text: For block-local restrictions ρ or block-supported submatrices, Γ_ κ, ℓ (p|_ρ) ≤ Γ_ κ, ℓ (p).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:template-partition
title: Template partition
statement_text: The compiler template library is partitioned as T = T _ ver dot ∪ T _ comp , where every T ∈ T _ ver uses only verification/interface variables (e.g.\ u,z ) and every T ∈ T _ comp uses only computation variables (e.g.\ v ). No template contains both (u,z) and v variables in the same gadget.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:additive-separability
title: Additive separability (no cross monomials)
statement_text: For every compiled instance P_ M,n there exist polynomials V_ M,n and R_ M,n such that P_ M,n (u,z,v) = V_ M,n (u,z) + R_ M,n (v), and V_ M,n contains no v -variables while R_ M,n contains no (u,z) -variables. In particular, P_ M,n has no mixed monomials involving both (u,z) and v .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:tphi-formal
title: Instance-Uniform Extraction
statement_text: For every 3SAT instance Φ with n variables, there exists a block-local transformation T_Φ = ( basis ) ∘ ( affine relabeling ) ∘ ( restriction ) ∘ ( projection ) such that T_Φ(P_ M^*,|ρ(Φ)| ) = Q^ × _Φ, Γ_ κ, ℓ (T_Φ( · )) ≤ Γ_ κ, ℓ ( · ). Moreover, T_Φ is uniformly computable with the following properties: Time bound: The description of T_Φ can be computed from Φ in time poly (n) . Description length: The representation of T_Φ has size poly (n) . Instance-independence: The structure of T_Φ depends only on the size n and parameters (κ, ℓ ) , not on the specific satisfying assignment or accepting computation. The map is determined entirely by the clause structure of Φ and the fixed compiler templates from Section . Rank monotonicity: Each stage (basis change, affine relabeling, restriction, projection) preserves or decreases SPDP rank by Lemma ; see also Lemma for the combined God-move properties.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:sheet-formal
title: Coupled Sheet Separability
statement_text: In the compiled machine-exact polynomial P_ M',|x| , verifier-sheet variables (u,z) and compute variables v factor block-locally: P_ M',|x| (u,z,v) = Q^ × _Φ(u,z) + R_ M',Φ (v), where Q^ × _Φ(u,z) = Π _C (1 - z_C · V_C(u)^2) is the coupled verifier sheet (Definition ), and no cross-constraints couple (u,z) and v .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:spdp-admissible-feature-scheme
title: SPDP-admissible feature scheme
statement_text: A polynomial p over N= poly (n) variables admits an SPDP-admissible feature scheme if it satisfies: Bounded local degree: p decomposes into local gadgets of degree O(1) , uniformly across all canonical windows; Canonical window structure / bounded incidence: there is a canonical windowing rule producing windows of radius R=Θ( log n) in the clause--variable (or gadget-interaction) incidence graph, and this incidence graph has maximum degree Δ=O(1) ; Bounded profile diversity: the number of distinct interface-anonymous profiles (Definition ) realized within any canonical window is at most N^ O(1) , independent of the derivative parameter κ ; Parameter compatibility: for κ, ℓ =Θ( log n) , all shifted partials used to form M_ κ, ℓ (p) remain within the degree regime required by the collapse theorem; equivalently, the effective degree after |S| ≤ κ differentiation and ℓ -shift is O( log n) . These conditions ensure that the SPDP Codimension/Collapse Theorem (Theorem ) applies with parameters κ, ℓ =Θ( log n) .
bounds: poly(n); O(1); \Theta(\log n); O(\log n); N^{O(1)}

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:collapsing-class
title: Collapsing SPDP class C _ coll
statement_text: Fix parameters κ=lceil α log nrceil and ℓ =lceil β log nrceil . A multilinear polynomial p over N= poly (n) variables is in C _ coll (n) if there exists a canonical window decomposition and interface-anonymous profile representation satisfying: Local canonical windows: p decomposes into local windows of radius O(1) after the canonicalization map of Section . Bounded interface diversity: within each window, the number of realizable interface-anonymous profiles is at most n^ O(1) (equivalently, profile compression removes any κ -dependence as in Lemma ). SPDP-admissibility: the induced feature scheme is SPDP-admissible in the sense of Definition (and hence satisfies the Codimension/Collapse hypotheses).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:collapse-for-class

statement_text: If p ∈ C _ coll (n) , then Γ_ κ, ℓ (p)\ ≤ \ n^ O(1) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:tm-to-uniform-circuit
title: Uniform circuit normal form for polynomial-time machines
statement_text: Fix c ≥ 1 . For every deterministic M ∈ DTIME (n^c) there exists a logspace-uniform family of bounded-fanin Boolean circuits {C_ M,n }_ n ≥ 1 of size n^ O(c) such that for all x ∈ {0,1}^n , C_ M,n (x)=M(x). Moreover, the map (M,n)mapsto C_ M,n is effective (uniform) in the standard sense.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:circuit-to-radius1-templates
title: Radius-- 1 template encoding yields bounded-incidence local constraints
statement_text: Fix the compiler template library T (radius-- 1 tiles/gadgets) and block partition B . Given a bounded-fanin Boolean circuit C_ M,n of size n^ O(1) , the compiler front-end produces in time n^ O(1) a local constraint system (equivalently, a multilinear polynomial P_ M,n in the compiler gauge) such that: each constraint/gadget touches O(1) variables and has degree O(1) ; the resulting gadget–variable incidence graph has maximum degree Δ=O(1) ; the construction is uniform in (M,n) and uses only templates from the fixed finite set T .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:uniform-p-to-spdp
title: Uniform P-to-SPDP Collapse Compiler
statement_text: There exists a uniform polynomial-time compilation map C :\ (M,1^n)\ mapsto \ p_ M,n such that for every deterministic polynomial-time Turing machine M deciding a language L ∈ P and for all input lengths n : Soundness of representation: p_ M,n is the SPDP polynomial associated to the computation of M on length- n inputs under the compiler semantics of Section (i.e.\ the compiler is machine-exact). Membership in the collapsing class: p_ M,n ∈ C _ coll (n) . Uniform rank collapse: consequently, Γ_ κ, ℓ l(p_ M,n r)\ ≤ \ n^ O(1) . Equivalently, under the same fixed parameters κ=Θ( log n) and ℓ =Θ( log n) , P\ ⊆ \ C _ coll .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:np-complete-witness-bookkeeping
title: NP-completeness bookkeeping for the witness family
statement_text: Let 3SAT ⊆ {0,1}^ * denote the standard NP-complete language of satisfiable 3-CNF formulas under the usual binary encoding (e.g.\ listing clauses as triples of signed variable indices). Let {Φ_n} be the explicit 3-CNF family used in Section (e.g.\ the expander/Tseitin/Ramanujan--Tseitin construction), with |Φ_n|= poly (n) and each Φ_n a bona fide 3-CNF formula over n primary variables and poly (n) auxiliary variables. Then: Φ_n is a standard 3SAT instance. For every n , the formula Φ_n is a syntactically valid 3-CNF formula, and its encoding length satisfies | enc (Φ_n)|= poly (n) . Uniform constructibility. The map nmapsto enc (Φ_n) is computable in time poly (n) (indeed logspace/uniform, if desired), so {Φ_n} forms an explicit uniform family of inputs to 3SAT . Same encoding regime for SPDP objects. Let C be the uniform compiler/encoding map fixed in Theorem (or Theorem ). Define the NP-side SPDP object by q_n := C (Φ_n). Then q_n is exactly the SPDP polynomial associated to the standard 3SAT input Φ_n under the same compilation/feature-scheme/canonical-window regime used on the P-side. NP-complete witness role. Consequently, any claimed separation that proves a rank lower bound for the family {q_n} (e.g.\ Γ_ κ, ℓ (q_n) ≥ n^ Ω( log n) for κ, ℓ =Θ( log n) ) is a rank lower bound for a uniform family of standard 3SAT instances under the paper's fixed encoding.

label: def:np-witness-family
title: NP witness family in SPDP form
statement_text: Let Φ_n be a canonical 3 -CNF family (e.g.\ the expander/Tseitin or characteristic-polynomial hard family of Section ). Let q_n denote its associated SPDP polynomial (e.g.\ χ_ φ_n or the God-Move extracted coupled sheet Q^ × _ Φ_n ).

statement_text: For the family {q_n} of Definition , Γ_ κ, ℓ (q_n)\ ≥ \ n^ Θ( log n) (or stronger, e.g.\ 2^ Ω(n) , depending on the construction). In particular, q_n ∉ C _ coll (n) for all sufficiently large n .

label: thm:universal-separation-criterion
title: Universal collapse vs explicit non-collapse yields P ≠ NP
statement_text: Assume Theorem (universal bridge) and Theorem (NP-side non-collapse). Then P ≠ NP .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:godmove-formal
title: Global God-Move ⇒ P ≠ NP (coupled-sheet form)
statement_text: Fix κ=lceil K log nrceil and ℓ =lceil β log nrceil for constants K,β>0 . Assume for contradiction that P=NP . Then for the verifier-restricted machine M' deciding 3SAT, the compiled polynomial satisfies Guard (no extraction from Φ alone). The extraction operator T_ Φ is applied only to the compiled machine-exact polynomial P_ M',n produced by the assumed polytime decider M' on input length n ; it is not an operator that outputs Q^ × _ Φ from Φ in isolation. The compiled polynomial satisfies Γ_ κ, ℓ (P_ M',n ) ≤ n^ O(1) by the P-side width ⇒ rank upper bound (Theorem ). By the coupled extraction map (Lemma ), Γ_ κ, ℓ (Q^ × _ Φ_n ) \ ≤ \ Γ_ κ, ℓ (P_ M',n ) \ ≤ \ n^ O(1) . On the other hand, by the coefficient-space identity minor for coupled sheets (Theorem , which applies to Q^ × _ Φ_n ), Γ_ κ, ℓ (Q^ × _ Φ_n )\ ≥ \ n^ Θ( log n) , a contradiction for large n . Hence P ≠ NP .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:uniform-extraction-verifier-sos
title: Uniform Block-Local Extraction of the Verifier SoS
statement_text: There exists a deterministic, instance-uniform map E : (Φ, M) longmapsto (Q^ × _Φ, P_ M,n ) with the following properties: P-side compilation. For any polytime decider M of 3SAT, the compiler produces P_ M,n with Γ_ κ, ℓ (P_ M,n ) ≤ n^ O(1) , κ, ℓ = Θ( log n). Verifier extraction. For each 3SAT instance Φ with n variables and m clauses, the map extracts Q^ × _Φ (the coupled clause-gadget SoS polynomial, Definition ) such that Γ_ κ, ℓ (Q^ × _Φ) ≤ Γ_ κ, ℓ (P_ M,n ) ≤ n^ O(1) . Block-locality. The extraction T_Φ : P_ M,n mapsto Q^ × _Φ decomposes as a finite composition of block-local operations (restriction, projection, affine relabeling, basis change), each operating within radius O(1) blocks. NP-side lower bound. For sufficiently hard 3SAT instances Φ_n (derived from the permanent via Valiant--Vazirani reduction or direct construction), Γ_ κ, ℓ (Q^ × _ Φ_n ) ≥ n^ Θ( log n) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:sheet-extract
title: Clause-sheet separability and extraction
statement_text: In the instrumented compilation, the coupled verifier sheet occupies disjoint blocks tagged VER . Selecting rows whose derivatives touch only VER variables (including coupling selectors z ) and projecting to columns supported on VER blocks yields a block-supported submatrix. By Lemma , this projection cannot increase rank, and after the instance-uniform affine relabeling of literal pads, the extracted polynomial equals Q^ × _Φ exactly.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:oracle-invariance
title: Oracle-invariance of SPDP rank
statement_text: Let p ∈ F [x_1, ... ,x_n] be any polynomial and κ, ℓ ≥ 0 . For any oracle O ⊆ {0,1}^* (or any Turing-relativized model), define the ``relativized'' SPDP rank Γ_ κ, ℓ ^O(p) to be the rank of the same shifted partial-derivative matrix M_ κ, ℓ (p) computed over F (i.e., the definition does not refer to oracle answers). Then Γ_ κ, ℓ ^O(p) = Γ_ κ, ℓ (p) for all O.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:non-largeness
title: Non-largeness of high-SPDP property
statement_text: For κ(n), ℓ (n) = O( log n) and any fixed α > 0 , there is c > 0 such that Pr _ f U({0,1}^ 2^n ) [f ∈ P _n] ≤ 2^ -c · 2^n for all sufficiently large n . In particular, P _n is not large in the Razborov--Rudich sense.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:natural-avoided
title: Non-largeness achieved unconditionally
statement_text: The SPDP-based property P _n is unconditionally non-large (Theorem ). In the Razborov--Rudich framework, non-largeness is the key condition preventing a ``natural'' proof from succeeding against PRF-computable functions. We mention this only as context; no cryptographic assumption enters our separation proof.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: prop:algebraic-oracle-invariance
title: Formal insensitivity to algebraic oracles for fixed p
statement_text: Let A be any algebraic oracle (collection of low-degree polynomials in fresh variables Z ). For a fixed base polynomial p(x) independent of Z , define p^A(x,Z) := p(x) (i.e., the oracle does not modify p ). Then Γ_ κ, ℓ (p^A) = Γ_ κ, ℓ (p).

title: Permanent monomial
statement_text: Fix n ≥ 1 . For σ ∈ S_n , define the monomial m_σ(x) = Π _ i=1 ^n x_ i,σ(i) , where we regard the variable x_ i,j as the single variable x_ (i-1)n+(j-1) in a flattened index.

statement_text: For σ, τ ∈ S_n : If x_ i,σ(i) = x_ j,τ(j) (as flattened variables), then i = j and σ(i) = τ(i) . vars (m_σ) = vars (m_τ) iff σ = τ . vars (m_σ) ∩ vars (m_τ) = { x_ i,σ(i) : σ(i) = τ(i) } .

statement_text: A convenient multilinear extension is p_ PAR _n (x) = Π _ i=1 ^n (1 - 2x_i). On {0,1}^n , each factor is ± 1 , and the product is (-1)^ Σ _i x_i ∈ { ± 1} . Hence the value set is {-1, +1} ⇒ valrank (p) = 2 .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: Majority, n = 2k+1
statement_text: Let MAJ _ 2k+1 (x) = 1 [ Σ _i x_i > k] and p_ MAJ its multilinear extension. For Hamming weight t ∈ {0, ... ,2k+1} , the restriction of p_ MAJ to the weight- t layer is constant and equals the probability (over a uniformly random completion consistent with fixing those t ones) that a random point has majority 1. As t varies from 0 to 2k+1 , these constants form a strictly monotone list with exactly k+2 distinct values (from 0 up to 1 in steps that occur at the threshold), hence valrank (p) = k+2 = Θ(n) .

statement_text: Fix derivative order ℓ and c ∈ N . There exists c_0 > 0 such that, for uniform f : {0,1}^n → {0,1} , Pr [ SPDP-rank _ ℓ (p_f) ≤ n^c] ≤ 2^ -c_0 2^n .

title: PRG-resistance of low-rank
statement_text: Under the truth-table model (strings of length 2^n ), low-rank functions are computationally indistinguishable from PRG outputs for poly-size distinguishers; advantage ≤ 2^ -Ω(2^n) . (Proof: S 2.4.2, App. A.M, App. A.O.)

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:inherently-algebraic
title: Inherently algebraic; method does not algebrize
statement_text: SPDP lower bounds talk about the multilinear p_f and linear-algebraic independence over a base field (and extensions). These arguments are not captured by standard algebrizing frameworks for relativized classes. (Discussion: S 2.4, App. A.3--A.4, S 29.9.2--29.9.3.)
