title: Linear independence
statement_text: The set { partial _ S,τ_S perm _n : S ∈ binom [n] κ } is linearly independent over the base field. Reason: each polynomial in the family contains its ``signature'' monomial m_S that does not occur in any other member; a nontrivial linear relation would force the coefficient of m_S to vanish, contradiction.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:rank-test
title: Storjohann-Wiedemann Rank Test
statement_text: Given a matrix M ∈ Q ^ m × n with entries of bit-size at most B , there exists a deterministic algorithm that computes rank (M) in time O(mn^ ω-1 · log ^2(nB)) where ω < 2.373 is the matrix multiplication exponent.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:canonical-window-vocabulary
title: Canonical window vocabulary
statement_text: Fix the radius-- 1 compiler template family (finite local tile alphabet, neighborhood shape, block partition B , diagonal-basis conventions, administrative tag scheme, and the fixed gauge Π^+ ). The canonical window vocabulary is the finite template language determined by these fixed compiler parameters, in which compiled objects are represented as multisets/sequences of local constraints indexed by canonical window coordinates, with deterministic tie-breaking conventions for ordering and naming.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:admitted-source-descriptions
title: Admitted source descriptions
statement_text: A source description D (machine/circuit/tableau description) is admitted if the compiler front-end contains an explicit deterministic normalization map Win (D) ∈ L _ win into the canonical window vocabulary L _ win (Definition ), computed using only syntactic rewrites that preserve the computed Boolean function (e.g.\ standard uniform simulation steps, fixed template expansion, and deterministic naming/order conventions).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:window-normalization-degrees
title: Front-end determinism: only (E1)--(E4),(E6) remain after window normalization
statement_text: Let D_1,D_2 be admitted source descriptions computing the same Boolean function f_n . Then their normalized window forms Win (D_1) and Win (D_2) differ only by the syntactic degrees of freedom listed in Definition , i.e., moves (E1)--(E4) and (E6) (and padding only if explicitly invoked).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:compiler-equivalence-moves
title: Compiler equivalence moves
statement_text: Fix the compiler template family Comp (radius-- 1 blocks, diagonal basis, and Π^+ ). We write p ≡ _ comp p' (or p p' ) if p' is obtained from p by a finite sequence of the following moves (and their inverses where applicable): (E1) Block-local invertible changes. Blockwise invertible linear changes of variables within blocks, and block-local variable renamings (permutations) consistent with the block partition B . (E2) Tag specialization / administrative normalization. Deterministic specialization, coalescing, or elimination of administrative tags introduced by the compiler front-end, in a way that preserves the Boolean semantics of the compiled instance. (E3) Deletion of identically-zero components (only). Removal of constraints/cells whose compiled polynomial is identically 0 after deterministic normalization. No other notion of ``semantically inactive'' is permitted. (E4) Commutation / reordering of independent cells. Reordering (permutation) of commuting factors, independent cells, or disjoint local constraints, including deterministic tie-breaking conventions. (E6) Positive-cone closure Π^+ . Applying the canonical ``positive-cone'' linear map Π^+ used in the final canonicalization layer. By definition of the compiler, Π^+ is chosen block-local and invertible on each block, hence is a special case of (E1) (recorded separately because it is used repeatedly in the narrative).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:padding-equivalence
title: Padding equivalence (optional, not in core)
statement_text: Write p ≡ _ pad p' if p' is obtained from p by applying the (uniform) round-trip NC ^0 padding transformation from Theorem (or its inverse), together with the induced renaming of auxiliary variables. This move is not part of the core equivalence ≡ _ comp and contributes at most a poly (n) factor to rank.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:each-move-rank-exact
title: Core compiler moves preserve blocked SPDP rank exactly
statement_text: If p ≡ _ comp p' (i.e.\ p' is obtained from p by moves (E1)--(E4), (E6)), then Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ (p') = Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ (p).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:padding-rank-benign
title: Padding is rank-benign up to poly (n)
statement_text: If p ≡ _ pad p' , then Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ (p') ≤ poly (n) · Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ (p) and Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ (p) ≤ poly (n) · Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ (p').

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:canonical-compiled-rep
title: Canonical compiled representative
statement_text: Fix the compiler pipeline Comp ( · ) described in S , including the final canonicalization layer (tag normalization, block-basis choice, and Π^+ application). For an admitted source description D , write NF (D)\ :=\ Comp (D) for the compiler output after canonicalization.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model

title: (I1) Normal-form invariance
statement_text: Let D_1,D_2 be admitted source descriptions computing the same Boolean function f_n . Then NF (D_1) NF (D_2) . Equivalently, the compiler output is well-defined as a normal form modulo .

title: (I2) Representation invariance of SPDP rank
statement_text: Under the hypotheses of Theorem , Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ ( NF (D_1)) = Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ ( NF (D_2)). If padding is additionally invoked, the two ranks are within a poly (n) factor by Lemma .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:finite-family
title: Finite compiled formula family F_ n,c
statement_text: Fix a runtime exponent c . Let F_ n,c be the set of all bounded-width CNF constraints generated by instantiating the compiler's local templates over all legal placements (time layer, tape index, and local neighborhood) in the Cook--Levin tableau for computations of length ≤ n^ c .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:enumerability
title: Enumerability bound
statement_text: For fixed template library T and fixed c , the family F_ n,c can be enumerated in time n^ O(c) , and |F_ n,c | ≤ n^ O(c) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:hoeffding-bernstein
title: Hoeffding-Bernstein MGF bound
statement_text: Let X be a real-valued random variable such that E [X] = μ and |X - μ| ≤ b almost surely. Then for every |t| ≤ 1/b , E [exp (t(X - μ))] ≤ exp ((t^2σ^2)/(2) ) where σ^2 = Var (X) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:spdp-rank-hard
title: Hardness of exact SPDP rank on succinct inputs
statement_text: Fix SPDP parameters (κ, ℓ ) with κ ≥ 1 . Consider the function problem RANK _ SPDP : f longmapsto Γ_ κ, ℓ (f), where f is specified by a succinct arithmetic (or Boolean) circuit computing its multilinear extension p_f . Then RANK _ SPDP is \#P-hard under polynomial-time Turing reductions.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: prop:low-rank-not-large
title: Low-rank property is not large
statement_text: For each fixed k there exists a constant c_k ∈ (0,1) such that, for all sufficiently large n , at most 2^ c_k 2^n Boolean functions on n variables satisfy P_ rank ,k (f) . In particular, P_ rank ,k is not large in the Razborov--Rudich sense.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:spdp-appg
title: SPDP Matrix
statement_text: Let p ∈ Bbb F[x_1, ... ,x_N] and let B={B_1, ... ,B_m} be a partition of {1, ... ,N} into blocks of size ≤ b=O(1) . Fix κ, ℓ ∈ Bbb N . Rows are indexed by pairs (τ,u) with multi-index τ ∈ Bbb N^N of weight |τ|=κ whose block support supp _ B (τ):={j: ∃ i ∈ B_j,\ τ_i>0} satisfies | supp _ B (τ)| ≤ κ , and u a monomial of degree ≤ ℓ . Columns are monomials x^β with deg x^β ≤ deg (p)-κ+ ℓ (empty set if negative). Define M^ B _ κ, ℓ (p) [(τ,u),x^β ] := coeff _ x^β (u · partial ^τ p ), Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ (p):= rank _Bbb F (M^ B _ κ, ℓ (p) ).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:width-to-rank-appg
title: Width ⇒ Rank at κ, ℓ =Θ( log n)
statement_text: Let p be a constant-degree multilinear polynomial with contextual entanglement width CEW (p) ≤ R:=C( log n)^c for absolute constants C,c>0 . If deg (p)-κ+ ℓ <0 then M_ κ, ℓ (p)=0 . Otherwise, for κ, ℓ =Θ( log n) we have Γ_ κ, ℓ (p) ≤ n^ O(1) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:splitter-appg
title: Combinatorial isolating family for κ -sets
statement_text: Let [N] index variables/blocks with N=Θ(n) and fix κ=α log n for any constant α>0 . There exists a family H ={h_1, ... ,h_t} of hash functions h_j:[N] → [m] with m:=c_0 κ^2 and t:=c_1(κ log N+10) (absolute constants c_0,c_1 ) such that for every κ -subset S ⊆ [N] there is some j with h_j injective on S .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:isolator
title: DEPRECATED - Isolating Family for additive sheet
statement_text: Let N be the number of clause--blocks/variable--pads in Q_ Φ_n and let κ=α log n for a fixed α>0 . There exists a family H of κ -perfect hash functions h:[N] → [κ] of size | H | ≤ C_0 κ^κ log N = n^ O(1) with the following property: for every κ -subset S ⊆ [N] there is an h ∈ H that is injective on S . For each S choose the unique monomial x^ β(S) that selects, in the SoS clause gadget for Q_ Φ_n , exactly the κ literal--wires indexed by S and no others (feasible because each block exposes private pads and the gadgets are block-separable). Then the SPDP submatrix with rows indexed by the κ -tuples S and columns by the x^ β(S) is the identity. Consequently, Γ_ κ, ℓ (Q_ Φ_n ) ≥ binom N κ = n^ Θ( log n) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:identity-minor-appg
title: DEPRECATED - Identity minor for additive clause SoS
statement_text: Let Q_ Φ_n =1- Σ _ C ∈ Φ_n V_C(x)^2 be the clause-violation SoS for a fixed 3 SAT family with bounded degree and clause locality (e.g., Ramanujan/Tseitin-based). With κ=α log n and ℓ =β log n , there exist sets R , C of size binom N κ =n^ Θ( log n) such that M_ κ, ℓ (Q_ Φ_n )[ R , C ] is the identity matrix.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:tphi-appg
title: Rank-monotone extraction
statement_text: There exists an instance-uniform, block-local transformation T_Φ such that T_Φ(P_ M,n )=Q_ Φ_n and for all κ, ℓ , Γ_ κ, ℓ (T_Φ(P_ M,n ) ) ≤ Γ_ κ, ℓ (P_ M,n ) . The transformation is witness-free in the sense of Lemma .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:identity-minor-explicit
title: Explicit identity minor and absence of cancellations
statement_text: Let Φ_n be the Ramanujan--Tseitin instance on a fixed d -regular expander G_n = (V_n,E_n) with |V_n| = m and |E_n| = N = Θ(n) , and let p_n be the associated multilinear polynomial in edge-variables {x_e : e ∈ E_n} constructed above. For parameters κ = α log n and ℓ = β log n as in the main text, there exist: a set R of binom N κ = n^ Θ( log n) SPDP rows, indexed by mixed partials partial ^ τ concentrating on κ -tuples of vertices with pairwise disjoint neighbourhoods, and a matching set C of binom N κ columns, indexed by monomials x^ α selecting one incident edge per such vertex, such that the submatrix M(p_n)[R,C] is a signed identity matrix. In particular, rank M(p_n) ≥ binom N κ and there are no cancellations among the corresponding monomials.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:spdp-matrix-formal
title: SPDP matrix
statement_text: Let F be a field and p ∈ F [x_1, ... , x_N] a polynomial. Fix parameters κ, ℓ ∈ N with κ ≤ N . Define: S _κ := {S ⊆ [N] : |S| = κ} (the set of all κ -subsets of variable indices), T _ ℓ := { monomials m in x_1, ... , x_N : deg m ≤ ℓ } , For S ∈ S _κ , define the partial derivative operator partial _S := Π _ i ∈ S (partial )/(partial x_i) , For m ∈ T _ ℓ , define the shift operator x^m : p mapsto m · p . The SPDP matrix M_ κ, ℓ (p) is the matrix with rows indexed by (S, m) ∈ S _κ × T _ ℓ and columns indexed by monomials in the standard monomial basis, where the (S,m) -th row is the coefficient vector of m · partial _S p expressed as a linear combination of monomials. The SPDP rank is defined as Γ_ κ, ℓ (p) := rank _ F M_ κ, ℓ (p).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:cew-formal
title: CEW and additive composition law
statement_text: Let p be a polynomial representing a Boolean function or circuit. The Contextual Entanglement Width CEW (p) is the minimal w such that after a universal restriction ρ_ * (defined via deterministic switching lemma), the SPDP rank satisfies Γ_ κ, ℓ (p upharpoonright ρ_ * ) ≤ w for fixed parameters (κ, ℓ ) = Θ( log n) . For compositional systems (e.g., layered circuits), CEW satisfies the additive composition law : CEW (f ∘ g) ≤ CEW (f) + CEW (g) + O(1), where the O(1) accounts for interface gadgets.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:batcher-network
title: Batcher odd--even merge network
statement_text: The Batcher sorting network for N inputs is a fixed comparison network defined recursively: Base case : For N = 1 , the network is trivial (identity). Recursive case : For N > 1 , split into two halves of size lceil N/2 rceil and lfloor N/2 rfloor , recursively sort each half, then merge using the odd--even merge gadget. The network has: Depth : D(N) = O( log ^2 N) , Width : Constant (each comparison gate operates on exactly 2 wires), Size : S(N) = O(N log ^2 N) comparisons.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:compiled-width-rank
title: Compiled Width ⇒ Rank via profile compression (load-bearing)
statement_text: Under the compiler setting of Section (bounded type set |T|=O(1) , radius-- 1 locality, and at most R= polylog (n) live interfaces throughout the sweep), the compiled SPDP rank satisfies Γ^ B _ κ, ℓ (p) ≤ R^ O(1) = ( log n)^ O(1) for (κ, ℓ )=Θ( log n).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:restriction-monotonicity
title: Restriction monotonicity
statement_text: Let p ∈ F [x_1, ... , x_N] and ρ : F ^N → F ^ N' be a restriction (fixing some variables to constants). Then Γ_ κ, ℓ (p upharpoonright ρ) ≤ Γ_ κ, ℓ (p).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:submatrix-monotonicity
title: Submatrix monotonicity
statement_text: If M' is a submatrix of M_ κ, ℓ (p) obtained by selecting a subset of rows, then rank (M') ≤ Γ_ κ, ℓ (p).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:basis-Piplus-invariance
title: Block-local affine/basis invariance and Π^+
statement_text: Let p ∈ Bbb F[x_1, ... ,x_N] and fix κ, ℓ . Suppose a block-local change of variables x mapsto Ax+b acts on each block by an invertible linear map A (so det A ≠ 0 on each block), and let Π^+ denote the fixed positive-cone map used in the compilation (acting block-locally and invertibly on the column space induced by the local basis). Then left/right multiplication of M_ κ, ℓ (p) by the corresponding block-diagonal change-of-basis matrices is invertible, hence Γ_ κ, ℓ (p) = Γ_ κ, ℓ (p ∘ (Ax+b) ) = Γ_ κ, ℓ (Π^+[p] ).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:basis-invariance-appg
title: Basis invariance
statement_text: The rank Γ_ κ, ℓ (p) does not depend on the choice of monomial ordering or coordinate system (up to linear isomorphism).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: prop:monotonicity-parameters-cumulative
title: Monotonicity in parameters (cumulative variant)
statement_text: Fix an ambient coefficient convention (monomial bases) for each parameter choice. If ℓ ' ≥ ℓ then Γ_ κ, ℓ (p) ≤ Γ_ κ, ℓ ' (p) . If κ' ≥ κ then Γ_ ≤ κ, ℓ (p) ≤ Γ_ ≤ κ', ℓ (p) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: Splitters / κ -perfect hash family
statement_text: A family H of functions h:[N] → [L] is κ -injective if for every κ -subset S ⊆ [N] there exists h ∈ H such that h|_ S is injective (i.e., assigns distinct colors in [L] to all elements of S ).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:k-injective-family
title: Existence of small κ -injective families
statement_text: Fix κ ≤ c log n and set L:=2κ . There exists a κ -injective family H={h_1, ... ,h_T} with T = O (κ log N ) such that for every S ∈ binom [N] κ some h_t is injective on S .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:private-literal-unique
title: Private literal uniqueness
statement_text: For each witness block B_i used in the NP construction, there exists a designated literal pad variable ℓ _i such that: ℓ _i occurs in the NP polynomial Q_ Φ_n only inside the unique local gadget factor associated with B_i , and no other local gadget contains ℓ _i .

label: def:treedepth
title: treedepth
statement_text: definedhere td A treedepth decomposition of a connected graph G is a rooted tree T such that V(T) = V(G) , and for every edge {u, v} ∈ E(G) , vertex u is an ancestor of vertex v in T , or vice versa. A treedepth decomposition of a disconnected graph is just a disjoint union of treedepth decompositions for its connected components. The treedepth of G , denoted by td (G) , is the minimum depth (in number of vertices) of a treedepth decomposition of G .

label: def:minor-model
title: minor model
statement_text: A minor model of a graph H in a graph G is a mapping φ : V(H) → subsets V(G) assigning a branch set φ(v) ⊆ V(G) to each vertex v ∈ V(H) , such that: G[φ(v)] is non-empty and connected for all v ∈ V(H) , φ(v) ∩ φ(u) = ∅ for all u ≠ v ∈ V(H) , and if {u,v} ∈ E(H) , then there exist u' ∈ φ(u) and v' ∈ φ(v) such that {u',v'} ∈ E(G) . For a vertex set S ⊆ V(H) , we define φ(S) coloneqq cup_ v ∈ S φ(v) to be the branch set of S . A minor model is minimal if there is no minor model that results from removing a single vertex from a branch set φ(v) for some v ∈ V(H) .

label: clm:sq-biclique
statement_text: Let r' be an RSQ, t and t' be k -cliques in G , and s ∈ Σ^* be a string that does not contain centoldstyle _2 11 centoldstyle _1 as a substring. Then, r_ conn ,k^2 ler' ⟩ matches CNG (t) s CLG (t') if and only if t ∪ t' is a 2k -clique in G and r' matches s .

paper_title: Hardness of Regular Expression Matching with Extensions
label: cor:clique-rsq
statement_text: Let ω be the exponent of square matrix multiplication. If RSQ matching on a string of length n and an RSQ of length m can be solved in n^ ω - ε 2^ o(m) time for some ε > 0 , then k -Clique on a graph of n vertices can be solved in O(n^ ω k / 3 - ε' ) time for some sufficiently large integer k and some ε' > 0 , and the k -Clique Hypothesis is false.
bounds: o(m); O(n^{\omega k / 3 - \varepsilon'}); n^{\omega - \varepsilon}; 2^{o(m)}; n^{\omega k / 3 - \varepsilon'}

paper_title: Hardness of Regular Expression Matching with Extensions
label: cor:comb-clique-rsq
statement_text: If RSQ matching on a string of length n and an RSQ of length m can be solved combinatorially in n^ 3 - ε 2^ o(m) time for some ε > 0 , then k -Clique on a graph of n vertices can be solved combinatorially in O(n^ k - ε' ) time for some sufficiently large integer k and some ε' > 0 , and the Combinatorial k -Clique Hypothesis is false.

paper_title: Hardness of Regular Expression Matching with Extensions
statement_text: A jumping machine P = (P, p_0, π) consists of set P of states, an initial state p_0 , and a jumping map π : [0,n-1] × P → ([1,n] × P) ∪ {bot } with the property that for any i ∈ [0,n-1] and any p ∈ P , if π(i, p) = (j, p') , then i < j . Given i ∈ [0,n] and p ∈ P , we let π_ p (i) = {j | ∃ p' ∈ P. ∃ l ≥ 1. π^ l (i, p) = (j, p')} . Here, π^ l (i, p) = π^ l-1 (π(i, p)) if π(i, p) ≠ bot , and π^ l (i, p) = bot otherwise for l ≥ 2 , and π^ 1 (i, p) = π(i, p) . Given a word w = a_1 ... a_n and an ERE r , we say that P = (P, p_0, π) is a jumping machine for w and r if for any i ∈ [0,n-1] , we have π_ p_0 (i) = {j ∈ [i+1,n] | a_ i+1 ... a_ j ∈ r}.

paper_title: Hardness of Regular Expression Matching with Extensions
label: lem:rosu
statement_text: Let w = a_1 ... a_n be a string and r be an ERE. Let j be a position such that a_ i+1 ... a_j ∈ r for all i ∈ [0,j-1] . Let C(w, r, j) be the number of distinct sets in the collection {ξ(i) | i ∈ [0,j-1]} , where ξ(i) = {j' ∈ [j+1,n] | a_ i+1 ... a_ j' ∈ r}. Then, any jumping machine for w and r must have at least C(w, r, j) states.

statement_text: For any function f(m) = 2^ 2^ o(m) , there are a string w and an ERE r of length m such that any jumping machine for w and r must have f(m) states. Consequently, the claim is false.

statement_text: For arbitrary 0 < ε < 1/2 , an algorithm computing the number of copies of a given k -pattern with n^ (1/2-ε) · k -multiplicative error in f(k) · n^ o(k/ log k) time would refute ETH.

statement_text: Left PPM is W [1] -hard with respect to k , and unless ETH fails, it cannot be solved in time f(k) · n^ o(k/ log k) for any function f , where k is the length of the pattern and n is the length of the text.

paper_title: Inapproximability of Counting Permutation Patterns
label: thm:sppm-hard
statement_text: There is no algorithm that counts the number of copies of a given k -pattern in time f(k) · n^ o(k/ log k) for any function f , unless ETH fails.

label: thm:gap-hard

paper_title: Lower Bounds in Algebraic Complexity via Symmetry and Homomorphism Polynomials
label: def:symmetric-ckts
title: Symmetric circuits
statement_text: Let Γ be a group acting on X . An algebraic circuit C over X is Γ -symmetric if every π ∈ Γ on the input gates X extends to an automorphism of C .

paper_title: Lower Bounds in Algebraic Complexity via Symmetry and Homomorphism Polynomials
title: Symmetric formulas
statement_text: A symmetric formula is a symmetric circuit C without multiedges such that the subgraph of C induced by the internal gates is a tree.

paper_title: Lower Bounds in Algebraic Complexity via Symmetry and Homomorphism Polynomials
label: def:skew-ckts
title: Symmetric skew circuits
statement_text: An algebraic circuit is skew if for every multiplication gate, at most one of its children is an internal (or a non-input) gate. A symmetric skew circuit is a symmetric circuit that is additionally skew.

paper_title: Lower Bounds in Algebraic Complexity via Symmetry and Homomorphism Polynomials
title: restate=rigidify, label=lem:rigidification, name=Rigidification
statement_text: Let Γ be a group acting on a variable set X , and let K be a field. Let C be a Γ -symmetric circuit over X ∪ K . There exists a Γ -symmetric rigid circuit C' with ‖ C' ‖ ≤ ‖ C ‖ that computes the same polynomial as C . If C is a symmetric formula, then C' is a symmetric formula with multiedges. If C is a symmetric skew circuit, then so is C' .

This linear combination is obtained by observing that Π _ v,w ∈ [n] x_ v,w is the subgraph polynomial for the pattern K_ n,n and applying M\"obius inversion . In particular, tw (K_ n,n ) ∈ Θ(n) .

label: def:w-counting-width
statement_text: Let w be an N -valued graph parameter. A family of matrix-symmetric polynomials (p_n) has w -counting width at most k ∈ N if, whenever two (n,n) -vertex bipartite graphs G and H are homomorphism indistinguishable over all graphs F such that w(F) < k , then p_n(G) = p_n(H) .

paper_title: Lower Bounds in Algebraic Complexity via Symmetry and Homomorphism Polynomials

label: def:supportDepth
title: Support depth
statement_text: Let C be a Sym _n × Sym _m -symmetric circuit. Let P denote the set of all paths from the root of C to an input gate. The support depth of a Sym _n × Sym _m -symmetric circuit C is supDp (C) coloneqq max _ P ∈ P supDp (P).

paper_title: Quantum Interactive Oracle Proofs
title: Quantum IOP systems; informal version of Definition
statement_text: A quantum interactive oracle proof (quantum IOP) system, parameterized by functions q(n) and l(n): Z _+ → Z _+ , consists of a quantum verifier V satisfying the following conditions for any input of size n : The verifier interacts with the prover for at most poly (n) rounds. In each round, the prover sends a quantum message to the verifier. The message length may vary between rounds. In each round, the verifier: applies a quantum circuit to his private qubits and to portions of the prover’s message, including qubits received in the current round as well as those retained from previous rounds, stores part of the prover’s message registers for use in later rounds. After each interaction, the verifier returns the remainder of the prover's quantum message (i.e., the part not stored) and may optionally send back part of their own private quantum register. At the end of the protocol, the verifier outputs a single decision bit. The main complexity parameters are: The query complexity q(n) : the total number of qubits from the prover's messages accessed by the verifier across all rounds. The communication complexity l(n) : the total number of qubits in the prover's messages across all rounds. We refer to such a system as a quantum IOP if q(n) is bounded by a constant. In the formal Definition , we refer to this as the general quantum IOP to distinguish it from the restricted and strong variants. We define the following variants of a quantum IOP : A system is called a restricted quantum IOP if the private register sent back by the verifier is required to be classical . It is called a strong quantum IOP if the verifier must return the entire prover's message register in each round (i.e., does not store any part of the message).

paper_title: Hardness and Tractability of T_{h+1}-Free Edge Deletion
label: defvc
statement_text: A set S ⊆ V(G) is a vertex cover of G if every edge in E(G) has at least one endpoint in S . The size of a smallest vertex cover of G is the vertex cover number of G .

paper_title: Bounds for Hardness Condensation in the Query Model
label: defi:fbs
title: Fractional Block Sensitivity
statement_text: Let W (f,x):={B ⊆ [n] | f(x^ B ) ≠ f(x)} denote the set of all sensitive blocks for an input x ∈ {0,1}^ n . The fractional block sensitivity of f at x , denoted fbs (f,x) , is the value of the linear program, maximize & Σ _ B ∈ W (f,x) y_B, subject to & Σ _ B : i ∈ B y_B ≤ 1, ∀ i ∈ [n], & 0 ≤ y_B ≤ 1, ∀ B ∈ W (f,x). The fractional block sensitivity fbs (f) of f is then defined as fbs (f):=underset x ∈ {0,1}^ n max fbs (f,x) .

title: Certificate Complexity
statement_text: The certificate complexity of a function f on an input x , denoted C (x, f) , is the size of the smallest f(x) -certificate that is consistent with x . The certificate complexity of f , denoted C (f) , is max _x{ C (f,x)} . Further, define C _ 0 (f) = max _ x : f(x)=0 { C (f,x)} and C _ 1 (f) = max _ x : f(x)=1 { C (f,x)} .

statement_text: Fix b ∈ {0,1} . We then define UC _ b (f) to be the minimum value of max _ p ∈ U |p| over all choices of such collections U . Further, define UC (f):= max { UC _ 0 (f), UC _ 1 (f)} and UC_ min (f):= min { UC _ 0 (f), UC _ 1 (f)} .

statement_text: Let f : {0,1} ^ n → {0,1} be a Boolean function. Let A be a deterministic algorithm that computes f by making queries to the bits of an unknown input x . Further, let cost (A,x) be the number of queries made by A on the input x , and cost (A)=max _x cost (A,x) . Then, the deterministic decision tree complexity (also known as query complexity) of f , denoted D (f) , is min _A{ cost (A)} , where the minimum is over all deterministic algorithm computing f .

statement_text: A randomized query algorithm A is said to compute f with error at most 1/3 (or, bounded-error), if Pr [A(x)=f(x)] ≥ 2/3 for all x ∈ {0,1}^n , where the probability is taken over the (internal) randomness of A . We then define R (f) to be the minimum number of queries required by any randomized query algorithm to compute f with error at most 1/3 . We will also consider a zero-error model in the randomized case. We say that a randomized decision tree computes f with zero-error if it never gives an incorrect answer, but it may output ``don't know'', with probability at most 1/2 for every input. Let R _0(f) denote the minimum number of queries required by any zero-error randomized algorithm computing f .

statement_text: A T -query quantum algorithm has the form A=U_TO_xU_ T-1 ... O_xU_1O_xU_0 , where the U_k 's are fixed unitary transformations independent of the input x . A query is the application of the unitary transformation O_x that maps O_x : |i,b,z ⟩ mapsto |i,b ⊕ x_i,z ⟩ , where i ∈ [n] , b ∈ {0,1} , and x ∈ {0,1}^n is an unknown input. The z -part corresponds to the workspace, which is not affected by the query. The final state A|0 ⟩ depends on x via the T applications of O_x . The output of the algorithm is determined by measuring the rightmost qubit of the final state. We say that a quantum query algorithm computes f exactly (resp., with bounded-error ) if its output equals f(x) with probability 1 (resp., at least 2/3 ), for all x ∈ {0,1}^n . Then, define Q _ E (f) (resp., Q (f) ) to be the minimum number of queries made by a quantum query algorithm computing f exactly (resp., with bounded-error).

paper_title: A Theory for Probabilistic Polynomial-Time Reasoning
title: Standard Models
statement_text: Let P : {0,1}^* × {0,1}^* → {0,1}^* be any correct approximate counting function , i.e., P (C,Δ) outputs (the encoding of) a rational number q ∈ [0,1] within the interval [p-1/|Δ|, p+1/|Δ|] for every circuit C:{0,1}^* → {0,1} and Δ ∈ {0,1}^* , where p is the acceptance probability of C and q is of length at most |C| · |Δ|^2 ; and P (C,Δ) outputs the correct value in {0,1} whenever the input circuit C satisfies IsConst (C) . We say that M (P ) is a standard model of APX .

paper_title: A Theory for Probabilistic Polynomial-Time Reasoning
title: Admissible Models
statement_text: Let P : {0,1}^* × {0,1}^* → {0,1} be a function. We say that M (P ) is an admissible model of APX if it satisfies all axioms and rules of APX .

title: Brute Force Counting Lemma
statement_text: APX _1 proves the following statement. For every n ∈ Log Log , circuit C ∈ B_n , and δ^ -1 ,β^ -1 ∈ Log , let t be the number of accepting inputs of C . Then |P _δ(C)-t/2^n| ≤ δ+β . In particular, if δ ≤ 2^ -n-1 , t is the nearest integer to P _δ(C) · 2^n .

paper_title: A Theory for Probabilistic Polynomial-Time Reasoning

statement_text: APX _1 proves the following statement. Let n ∈ Log , C ∈ B_n be a circuit, and P_0,P_1, ... ,P_n be circuits that output rational numbers such that P_i is of input length i . paper_title: A Theory for Probabilistic Polynomial-Time Reasoning
title: Random Variable
statement_text: Let V be an explicit set of rational numbers, n ∈ Log , and C be a multi-output circuit. We say that (V,n,C) defines a random variable X over V if ∀ x ∈ {0,1}^n C(x) ∈ V . The set V is called the support of X , C is called the sampler of X , and n is called the seed length of X .

paper_title: A Theory for Probabilistic Polynomial-Time Reasoning

statement_text: Let (V,n,C) be a tuple defining a random variable X over V , and δ^ -1 ∈ Log . paper_title: A Theory for Probabilistic Polynomial-Time Reasoning
label: prop: indicator variable
statement_text: APX _1 proves the following statement. Let n,δ^ -1 ∈ Log and C:{0,1}^n → {0,1} be a Boolean circuit. Let I_Ctriangleq ({0,1}, n,C) be the indicator random variable for C(x) = 1 . Then for any β^ -1 ∈ Log , |P _δ(C) - E _δ[I_C]| ≤ 2δ + β .

paper_title: A Theory for Probabilistic Polynomial-Time Reasoning

statement_text: APX _1 proves the following statement. Let n,δ_1^ -1 ,δ_2^ -1 ∈ Log , C:{0,1}^n → Q , V ⊆ Q be an explicit set such that ∀ x ∈ {0,1}^n C(x) ∈ V . Then for every β^ -1 ∈ Log , | E _ δ_1 [X] - E _ δ_2 [X] | ≤ (δ_1+δ_2+β) · |V|, where |V|triangleq Σ _ v ∈ V |v| is the ℓ _1 -norm of V and |v| denotes the absolute value of the rational v .

paper_title: A Theory for Probabilistic Polynomial-Time Reasoning

statement_text: APX _1 proves the following statement. Let n,δ^ -1 ∈ Log , C:{0,1}^n → Q , V ⊆ Q be an explicit set such that ∀ x ∈ {0,1}^n C(x) ∈ V . Let X be the random variable defined by (V,n,C) . Then for every β^ -1 ∈ Log , | E _ δ [X] - frac E _ δ [X|_0] + E _ δ [X|_1] 2 | ≤ (2δ+β) · |V|, where |V|triangleq Σ _ v ∈ V |v| is the ℓ _1 norm of V , and for b ∈ {0,1} , X|_b denotes the random variable defined by (V,n-1, Fix _b(C)) .

paper_title: A Theory for Probabilistic Polynomial-Time Reasoning

paper_title: A Theory for Probabilistic Polynomial-Time Reasoning
label: prop: permutation exp
statement_text: APX _1 proves the following statement. Let n,δ^ -1 ,β^ -1 ∈ Log , C:{0,1}^n → Q , V ⊆ Q be an explicit set such that ∀ x ∈ {0,1}^n C(x) ∈ V . paper_title: A Theory for Probabilistic Polynomial-Time Reasoning
label: thm: linearity exp
title: Linearity of Expectation
statement_text: APX _1 proves the following: Let n,m,δ^ -1 ,β^ -1 ∈ Log , C_1, ... ,C_m:{0,1}^n → Q be a list of circuits, λ = (λ_1, ... ,λ_m) be a list of length m such that λ_i ∈ Q for i ∈ [m] , γ ∈ Q , and V ⊆ Q be an explicit set such that: For any x ∈ {0,1}^n and i ∈ [m] , C_i(x) ∈ V . For any x ∈ {0,1}^n , γ + λ_1 · C_1(x) + λ_2 · C_2(x) + ... + λ_m · C_m(x) ∈ V . Then: | E _δ[Y] - (γ + λ_1 · E _δ[X_1] + ... + λ_m · E _δ[X_m]) | ≤ (2δ + β) · |V| · |λ|, where |V| and |λ| are the ℓ _1 -norm of V and λ , respectively.

paper_title: A Theory for Probabilistic Polynomial-Time Reasoning

statement_text: APX _1 proves the following statement. Let n,m,δ^ -1 ,β^ -1 ∈ Log , C_1, ... ,C_m ∈ B_n be single-output circuits, V={0,1} . Suppose that ∀ x ∈ {0,1}^n and i ∈ [m] , C_i(x) ∈ V , and let Y,X_1, ... , X_m be random variables defined as follows. For each i ∈ [m] , X_i is defined by (V,n,C_i) . Y is defined by (V,n,S) , where S(x) ∈ {0,1} is a circuit such that S(x) ≤ C_1(x) ∨ ... ∨ C_m(x) . Then we have E _δ[Y] ≤ E _δ[X_1] + ... + E _δ[X_m] + (2δ+β) · m .

paper_title: A Theory for Probabilistic Polynomial-Time Reasoning
label: thm: markov
title: Markov's Inequality
statement_text: The following statement is provable in APX _1 . Let X be a random variable defined by (V,n,C) , where V is an explicit set of non-negative rational numbers, n ∈ Log , and C:{0,1}^n → Q is a circuit. Let δ^ -1 ,β^ -1 ∈ Log , μ ∈ Q with μ ≥ E _δ[X] and μ > 0 , k ∈ Q with k > 0 , and T(x) be the circuit that outputs 1 if C(x) ≥ k · μ , and outputs 0 otherwise. Then P _δ(T) ≤ δ + k^ -1 · (1+δ · μ^ -1 · |V|) + β · (μ^ -1 · |V|+1), where |V| is the ℓ _1 -norm of V .

paper_title: A Theory for Probabilistic Polynomial-Time Reasoning
title: Approximate Variance
statement_text: Let X be a random variable defined by the tuple (V,n,C) , δ^ -1 ∈ Log . The approximate variance of X with precision parameter δ , denoted by Var _δ[X] , is defined as Var _δ[X] triangleq E _δ[(X-μ)^2] where μ triangleq E _δ[X] ∈ Q .

paper_title: A Theory for Probabilistic Polynomial-Time Reasoning
label: prop: variance alternative def
statement_text: APX _1 proves the following statement. Let X be a random variable defined by the tuple (V,n,C) , where V ⊆ Q is an explicit set, n ∈ Log , and C:{0,1}^n → Q satisfies ∀ x ∈ {0,1}^n C(x) ∈ V . Let μtriangleq E _δ[X] ∈ Q . Then for any δ^ -1 ,β^ -1 ∈ Log , | Var _δ[X] - ( E _δ[X^2] - μ^2)| ≤ (2δ +β) · (1+|μ|) · |V|, where V = V ∪ (V-μ)^2 ∪ V^2 ∪ {1} .

paper_title: A Theory for Probabilistic Polynomial-Time Reasoning
title: Chebyshev's Inequality
statement_text: APX _1 proves the following statement. Let X be a random variable defined by the tuple (V,n,C) , δ^ -1 ∈ Log , where V ⊆ Q is an explicit set, n ∈ Log , and C:{0,1}^n → Q is a circuit such that ∀ x ∈ {0,1}^n C(x) ∈ V . Let μtriangleq E _δ[X] ∈ Q , σ^2triangleq Var _δ[X] , and T(x) be the circuit that outputs 1 if (C(x)-μ)^2 ≥ k · σ^2 , and outputs 0 otherwise. Then for any β^ -1 ∈ Log and k ∈ Q , where k > 0 , we have that P _ δ (T) ≤ δ + k^ -1 · (1 + δ · σ^ -2 · |V|) + β · (σ^ -2 · |V| + 1), where V = (V-μ)^2 = {(v-μ)^2 | v ∈ V} .

paper_title: A Theory for Probabilistic Polynomial-Time Reasoning
title: Covariance
statement_text: Let X_1 and X_2 be the random variables defined by the tuples (V_1,n,C_1) and (V_2,n,C_2) , respectively, where V_1,V_2 ⊆ Q are explicit sets, n ∈ Log , and C_1,C_2:{0,1}^n → Q are circuits. Let δ^ -1 ∈ Log , V_1V_2triangleq {v_1 · v_2 | v_1 ∈ V_1,v_2 ∈ V_2} , Y(x) be the circuit computing C_1(x) · C_2(x) , and Y be the random variable defined by the tuple (V_1V_2,n,Y) . The δ -approximate covariance of X_1 and X_2 , denoted by Cov _δ(X_1,X_2) , is defined as Cov _ δ (X_1,X_2) triangleq | E _ δ [Y] - E _ δ [X_1] · E _ δ [X_2]|.

paper_title: A Theory for Probabilistic Polynomial-Time Reasoning

statement_text: Let δ^ -1 ∈ Log , ε ∈ Q . Random variables X_1 and X_2 are said to be ε -almost δ -approximately independent if Cov _ δ (X_1,X_2) ≤ ε .

paper_title: A Theory for Probabilistic Polynomial-Time Reasoning
title: Pairwise Independence
statement_text: Let n,m ∈ Log , C_1, ... ,C_m:{0,1}^n → Q be circuits, and V ⊆ Q be an explicit set such that ∀ i ∈ [m] ∀ x ∈ {0,1}^n C_i(x) ∈ V . Let X_1, ... , X_m be random variables, where for each i ∈ [m] , X_i is defined by the tuple (V,n,C_i) , and let δ^ -1 ∈ Log and ε ∈ Q . The sequence X_1, ... ,X_m of random variables is said to be ε -almost δ -approximately pairwise independent if for every pair (i,j) with i,j ∈ [m] and i ≠ j , X_i and X_j are ε -almost δ -approximately independent.

paper_title: A Theory for Probabilistic Polynomial-Time Reasoning
statement_text: The following statement is provable in APX _1 . Let n,m ∈ Log , C_1, ... ,C_m:{0,1}^n → Q be circuits, and V ⊆ Q be an explicit set such that the following holds: ∀ i ∈ [m] ∀ x ∈ {0,1}^n C_i(x) ∈ V ; ∀ x ∈ {0,1}^n C_1(x) + C_2(x) + ... + C_m(x) ∈ V . Let X_1, ... , X_m be random variables, where for each i ∈ [m] , X_i is defined by the tuple (V,n,C_i) . Let Y be the random variable defined by the tuple (V,n,S) , where S(x) is the circuit computing C_1(x) + C_2(x) + ... + C_m(x) . Let δ^ -1 ,β^ -1 ∈ Log and ε ∈ Q . Suppose that X_1, ... ,X_m are ε -almost δ -approximately pairwise independent. Then | Var _δ[Y] - ( Var _δ[X_1] + ... + Var _δ[X_m]) | ≤ (ε +3δ · |V|^2) · m^2 + β · (|V|+1)^3, where |V|= Σ _ v ∈ V |v| is the ℓ _1 -norm of V .

paper_title: A Theory for Probabilistic Polynomial-Time Reasoning
title: Explicit Independence
statement_text: Let X and X' be random variables defined by (V,n,C) and (V,n,C') , respectively. We say that X and X' are explicitly independent if C and C' read disjoint bits of the n -bit seed; that is, there is a partition π_1 ∪ π_2 of [n] such that for any seed x ∈ {0,1}^n , C only reads x_ π_1 and C' only reads x_ π_2 , where x_ π denotes the bits of x with indices in π .

paper_title: A Theory for Probabilistic Polynomial-Time Reasoning
title: Explicitly i.i.d. RVs
statement_text: Let n,m ∈ Log , C:{0,1}^n → Q be a circuit, V ⊆ Q be an explicit set such that ∀ x ∈ {0,1}^n C(x) ∈ V . paper_title: Separating Quantum and Classical Advice with Good Codes
title: Modified from
statement_text: We use the phrase ``an oracle'' to refer to a function O ∶ {0, 1}^ * → {0, 1} . A quantum query algorithm is a quantum circuit that interacts with an oracle O ∶ {0, 1}^ * → {0, 1} via a query gate ket x, b → ket x, b ⊕ O (x) , which acts on an |x|+1 -qubit query register for various x . The algorithm is described by an alternating sequence of unitaries (drawn from any fixed gate set) and query gates. After all gates are applied, a designated qubit is measured in the standard basis to determine acceptance. The circuit has ancilla qubits which are initialized to ket 0 and all intermediate unitaries may act on an arbitrary (but finite) number of qubits. A quantum query algorithm may also receive an auxiliary witness or advice as input. A quantum witness/advice state is a state ket ψ on some (finite) number of qubits, while a classical witness/advice string is a (finite) bitstring w , treated as a computational basis state. The algorithm's acceptance probability may depend on both the oracle and the witness.

paper_title: Separating Quantum and Classical Advice with Good Codes
statement_text: We denote a family of quantum oracle circuits/algorithms by { A _ λ }_ λ ∈ N , where the index λ corresponds to the length of the explicit input to the computational problem. { A _ λ }_ λ ∈ N is P -uniform if there exists a deterministic polynomial-time Turing machine M that, on input 1^ λ , outputs a full classical description of the circuit A _ λ . The runtime of M implies that A _ λ has at most poly (λ) gates (oracle or elementary), queries O at lengths of at most poly (λ) , and receives witnesses/advice of length at most poly (λ) .

paper_title: Separating Quantum and Classical Advice with Good Codes
title: Oracle QCMA
statement_text: A promise language L ^ O = ( L _ yes , L _ no )^ O ⊆ {0, 1}^ * is in QCMA ^ O if there exists a P -uniform family of quantum oracle circuits A _ λ with A _ λ accepting a witness of length t(λ) , such that for every input x of length λ = |x| , x ∈ L _ yes ⇒ ∃ w ∈ {0, 1}^ t(λ) s.t. Pr [ A _ λ ^ O (x, w) = 1] ≥ (2)/(3) , x ∈ L _ no ⇒ ∀ w ∈ {0, 1}^ t(λ) , Pr [ A _ λ ^ O (x, w ) = 1] ≤ (1)/(3) .

Pr [ A _ λ ^ O (x, ket ψ ) = 1] ≥ (2)/(3) , x ∈ L _ no ⇒ ∀ ket * ψ ∈ ( C ^2)^ ⊗ t(λ) , Pr [ A _ λ ^ O (x, ket * ψ ) = 1] ≤ (1)/(3) .

If t(λ) = 0 then we say L ^ O ∈ BQP ^ O .

statement_text: A code of length n ∈ N over an alphabet Σ is a subset C ⊆ Σ^n . C ⊆ Σ^n is said to be F _q -linear if its alphabet Σ = F _q^s for some field F _q and a positive integer s ≥ 1 and C is an F _q -linear subspace of Σ^n . Equivalently, this means that for any two codewords x, y ∈ C and scalar α ∈ F _q , both x+y and α · x are in C . For an F _q -linear code C , the dual code of C is the code C^ perp ⊆ ( F _q^s)^n containing all strings c' ∈ ( F _q^s)^n which satisfy Σ _ i = 1 ^n Σ _ j = 1 ^s (c'_i)_j · (c_i)_j = 0 for all c ∈ C . Observe that C^ perp is always F _q -linear, and that |C| · |C^ perp | = |Σ|^n if and only if C is F _q -linear.

We define the i 'th formal and Hasse derivatives of f(X) as the linear operators which take f(X) to the polynomials f^ [i] (X) = Σ _ j = i ^n (j!)/((j-i)!) a_j X^ j-i and f^ (i) (X) = Σ _ j = i ^n binom j i a_j X^ j-i , respectively. Note that f^ [i] (X) = i! f^ (i) (X) for all i and f .

The univariate multiplicity code Mult _ s, F _q (α_1, ... , α_n; k) is the code over the alphabet Σ = F _q^s of length n which associates each polynomial f(X) ∈ ( F _q)_ <k [X] to the codeword c ∈ Σ^n such that for i ∈ [n] , c_i = (f^ (0) (α_i), f^ (1) (α_i), ... , f^ (s−1) (α_i)), where f^ (j) is the j 'th Hasse derivative of f . statement_text: A bipartite graph with N left-vertices, M right-vertices, and left-degree D is specified by a function Γ : [N] × [D] → [M] , where Γ(x, y) denotes the y ’th neighbor of x . For a set X ⊆ [N] , we write Γ(X) to denote its set of neighbors cup_ x ∈ X, y ∈ [D] Γ(x, y) . For a set T ⊆ [M] , we write LIST _ Γ (T) = { x: Γ(x) ⊆ T } . We say that Γ is a (K, A) -expander if for every set X ⊆ [N] of size at most K , |Γ(X)| ≥ A · |X| . Note that if Γ is a (K, A) -expander then for all B ≤ K and all sets T such that |T| < AB , | LIST _ Γ (T)| < B .

Then, for sufficiently large λ , for a (1)/(4000Q^2) fraction of x ∈ {0, 1}^ λ , measuring a random query of A ^ G (for randomly sampled G ) will produce x with probability at least (1)/(3200Q^2) .

statement_text: For a function H : [n] × Σ → {0, 1} and a code C ⊆ Σ^n , define the code intersection relation R_ C, H ⊆ {0, 1}^n × Σ^n by R_ C,H = { ( x , v ) = (x_1, ... , x_n, v_1, ... , v_n) : ((v_1, ... , v_n) ∈ C) ∧ ( ∀ i ∈ [n], H(i, v_i) = x_i) }.

The trace function is F _r -linear: for all a, b ∈ F _r and x, y ∈ F _q , Tr (ax+ by) = aTr (x) + bTr (y) . In addition, for any x ∈ F _q^n , Σ _ y ∈ F _q^n ω_r^ Tr (x · y) = 0 , where ω_r := e^ 2π i/r .

title: Multi-control-NOT gate and Toffoli gate
statement_text: A multi-control gate, denoted by C^k not , is a quantum gate that acts on k+1 qubits. Let C be a k -qubit register and T be a one-qubit register. label: def:klocalH
title: Local Hamiltonian
statement_text: We say a Hamiltonian H acting on n qubits is k -local if H can be written as H = Σ _ i=1 ^m H_i for m= poly (n) and for all i , the following holds. H_i is a Hamiltonian. H_i non-trivially acts on at most k qubits. |H_i| ≤ poly (n) .

paper_title: Fine-Grained Complexity for Quantum Problems from Size-Preserving Circuit-to-Hamiltonian Constructions
label: def:LHP
title: k -local Hamiltonian ( k - LH ) problem
statement_text: The local Hamiltonian problem is a decision problem that asks whether the ground-state energy of a k -local Hamiltonian is greater or less than given energy thresholds. Inputs: a k -local Hamiltonian H such that acting on n qubits where k=O(1) , and two energy thresholds E_ yes ,E_ no satisfying E_ no -E_ yes ≥ Ω(1) . Outputs: YES, if there exists a quantum state ket ψ ∈ C ^ 2^n such that ⟨ ψmiddle rvertH middle | ψ ⟩ ≤ E_ yes . NO, if ⟨ ψmiddle rvertH middle | ψ ⟩ ≥ E_ no for all ket ψ ∈ C ^ 2^n . In other words, the k - LH problem asks to decide whether λ(H) ≤ E_ yes or λ(H) ≥ E_ no . We say an algorithm A _ LH solves k - LH (H, E_ yes , E_ no ) if A _ LH decides (H,E_ yes ,E_ no ) correctly.

paper_title: Fine-Grained Complexity for Quantum Problems from Size-Preserving Circuit-to-Hamiltonian Constructions
label: def:QPF
title: Approximating quantum partition function of k -local Hamiltonian ( k - QPF ) problem
statement_text: The quantum partition function problem is to approximate the partition function of a k -local Hamiltonian up to a multiplicative error under a certain temperature. Inputs: a k -local Hamiltonian H acting on n qubits where k=O(1) , an inverse temperature β ≤ poly (n) , and an error parameter δ ∈ (0,1) . Outputs: Z ∈ R such that (1-δ)Z ≤ Z ≤ (1+δ)Z, where Z:= tr [e^ -β H ] . We say an algorithm A _ QPF solves k - QPF (H, β, δ) if A _ QPF outputs such Z on the inputs H, β, δ .

paper_title: Fine-Grained Complexity for Quantum Problems from Size-Preserving Circuit-to-Hamiltonian Constructions
label: def:kCNF
title: Conjunctive normal form (CNF) formula
statement_text: Let Φ be a Boolean formula that consists of n variables x_1,x_2, ... , x_k . We say Φ is a k CNF formula if Φ is in the form of m= poly (n) smaller formulas connected by ∧ . Each smaller formula contains at most k variables, and the variables are connected by ∨ . To be more precise, Φ=φ_1 ∧ φ_2 ∧ ... ∧ φ_m where m= poly (n) , and for all i ∈ [m] , the following constrains hold. φ_ i = ( ℓ _ i,1 ∨ ℓ _ i_2 ∨ ... ∨ ℓ _ i,k_ i ) , where ℓ _ i,p can be x_j or ¬ x_j for all p ∈ [k_i] and j ∈ [n] . k_i ≤ k . For each j ∈ [n] , x_j and ¬ x_j do not appear in φ_i at the same time; x_j , ¬ x_j appears in φ_i at most once. We say φ_i is a clause of Φ for all i ∈ [m] .

label: def:kSAT
title: Satisfiability for k - CNF ( k - SAT ) problem
statement_text: The satisfiability problem is a decision problem that asks whether there is an assignment satisfying the given k CNF formula. Inputs: a k - CNF formula Φ that contains n variables. The number of clauses of Φ is m= poly (n) . Outputs: YES, if there exists an assignment x ∈ {0,1}^n such that Φ(x)=1 . No, if Φ(x)=0 for all x ∈ {0,1}^n . We say an algorithm A _ SAT solves k - SAT (Φ) if A _ SAT decides Φ correctly.

title: ε - RePolymatrix
statement_text: In a general polymatrix game, there are n players with m_i actions for player i ∈ [n] . Let a_i ∈ [m_i] be the action of player i . The payoff of player i from the sub-game associated with player j ≠ i is determined by the matrix A^ ij , where player i gets a payoff of A^ ij _ a_i a_j from this subgame if i plays a_i and j plays a_j . Given the actions of all agents (a_1, ... , a_n) , the utility of player i is equal to Σ _ j ≠ i A^ ij _ a_i a_j . We make the following additional assumptions to restrict the class of polymatrix games we use in our reductions: Each player has exactly two actions: a_i ∈ {0, 1} for all i . All the payoffs are from the set {0, 1, 2} : A^ ij ∈ {0, 1, 2}^ 2 × 2 for all i and j ≠ i . All payoff matrices are either diagonal or anti-diagonal: for every i and j ≠ i , either A^ ij _ 01 = A^ ij _ 10 = 0 or A^ ij _ 00 = A^ ij _ 11 = 0 . The game is bipartite : We can view the polymatrix game as a directed graph, where the vertices are the players, and there is an edge from player j to player i if A^ ij ≠ 0 . We assume that the underlying undirected graph of this directed graph is bipartite. The in-degree is at most two: The payoff of any player depends upon at most two other players, i.e., for every player i , there exist at most two players k and k' such that A^ ij = 0 for all j ∉ { k, k' } . The out-degree is at most two: Any player can affect the payoff of at most two other players, i.e., for every player i , there exist at most two players k and k' such that A^ ji = 0 for all j ∉ { k, k' } . The ε - RePolymatrix problem is to find an ε -WSNE of a polymatrix game satisfying the assumptions given above, for a given ε > 0 .

statement_text: Let H= Σ _e h_e be a k -local, degree- D Hamiltonian on n qubits with |h_e| ≤ J . Fix a real target time t>0 . For η ∈ (0,1) , let σ := σ_η / t where σ_η is taken from . paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
title: Adjacency matrix
statement_text: The adjacency matrix of G is the symmetric matrix A_G ∈ {0,1}^ n × n with (A_G)_ ij =1 if and only if {i,j} ∈ E(G) .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
title: Graph Laplacian
statement_text: The combinatorial Laplacian of G is L_G=D_G-A_G , where D_G= diag (deg (1), ... ,deg (n)) is the degree matrix. The normalized Laplacian is L _G=D_G^ -1/2 L_G D_G^ -1/2 .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
title: Graph isomorphism
statement_text: Graphs G and H on [n] are isomorphic , written Gcong H , if there exists a bijection π ∈ S _n such that {u,v} ∈ E(G) ⟺ {π(u),π(v)} ∈ E(H) .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: def:edit-distance
title: Edit distance
statement_text: For graphs G and H on [n] and a permutation π ∈ S _n , define ed _π(G,H) = l| l{{u,v} ∈ tbinom [n] 2 : (A_G)_ uv ≠ (A_H)_ π(u)π(v) r} r|. The edit distance is ed (G,H)=min _ π ∈ S _n ed _π(G,H) .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
title: Quantum query complexity
statement_text: The quantum query complexity of a decision problem P with oracle access to input x is the minimum number of queries to O_x required by a quantum algorithm that computes P(x) correctly with probability at least 2/3 on every input.

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: thm:grover
title: Grover search,
statement_text: Given quantum query access to f : [N] → {0,1} with t marked elements ( f(x)=1 ), a marked element can be found with probability ≥ 2/3 using O ( sqrt N/t ) queries.

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: thm:amp-est
title: Amplitude estimation,
statement_text: Given a quantum circuit A such that measuring the output of A |0 ⟩ yields |1 ⟩ with probability p , there exists a quantum algorithm that outputs p satisfying | p -p| ≤ δ with probability ≥ 2/3 using O (1/δ) applications of A and A ^ † .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: def:szegedy
title: Szegedy walk
statement_text: Let P be the transition matrix of an ergodic, reversible Markov chain on state space X with | X |=N and stationary distribution μ . Define the Szegedy walk operator W(P) on C ^N ⊗ C ^N by W(P) = ref (B) ref (A), where A= span {|ψ_x ⟩ : x ∈ X } , B= span {|φ_x ⟩ : x ∈ X } , with |ψ_x ⟩ =|x ⟩ Σ _ y sqrt P(x,y) |y ⟩ and |φ_y ⟩ = Σ _x sqrt P(x,y) |x ⟩ |y ⟩ , and ref (S)=2Π_S-I is the reflection about subspace S .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: thm:szegedy-spectral
title: Szegedy spectral theorem,
statement_text: Let P be a reversible Markov chain with eigenvalues 1=λ_1 ≥ λ_2 ≥ ... ≥ λ_N ≥ -1 . The eigenvalues of W(P) corresponding to each classical eigenvalue λ_j are e^ ± iarccos (λ_j) . In particular, the spectral gap δ of P (defined as δ=1-λ_2 ) gives rise to a phase gap Δ=Θ( sqrt δ ) in W(P) .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: thm:qwalk-search
title: Quantum walk search,
statement_text: Let P be an ergodic, reversible Markov chain on X with stationary distribution μ , spectral gap δ , and let M ⊆ X be a set of marked vertices with μ(M)=ε . There exists a quantum algorithm that finds a marked vertex (if one exists) with O (1/ sqrt ε ) applications of the Szegedy walk operator W(P) , each requiring one step of the walk, plus setup cost S , update cost U , and checking cost C , giving total complexity O (frac 1 sqrt ε (frac 1 sqrt δ · U + C )+S ).

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: lem:hoeffding
title: Hoeffding's inequality
statement_text: Let X_1, ... ,X_m be independent random variables with X_i ∈ [a_i,b_i] . Then for X =(1)/(m) Σ _ i=1 ^ m X_i , Pr l[ | X - E [ X ] | ≥ t r] ≤ 2exp (-frac 2m^2 t^2 Σ _ i=1 ^m(b_i-a_i)^2 ).

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: lem:matrix-chernoff
title: Matrix Chernoff bound,
statement_text: Let X_1, ... ,X_m be independent random symmetric matrices with 0preceq X_ipreceq I and let μ_ min =λ_ min ( E [ Σ _i X_i]) . Then Pr [λ_ min ( Σ _ i=1 ^m X_i ) ≤ (1-δ)μ_ min ] ≤ n · (frac e^ -δ (1-δ)^ 1-δ )^ μ_ min for any δ ∈ [0,1) .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: lem:gentle
title: Gentle measurement lemma,
statement_text: If a measurement on state ρ yields outcome k with probability 1-ε , then the post-measurement state ρ_k satisfies |ρ-ρ_k |_1 ≤ 2 sqrt ε .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: prob:agi
title: (ε_1,ε_2) -Approximate Graph Isomorphism
statement_text: Given two graphs G and H on n vertices with 0 ≤ ε_1<ε_2 ≤ 1 , and quantum query access to O_G and O_H as in , distinguish: YES case: ed (G,H) ≤ ε_1 (i.e., ed (G,H) ≤ ε_1binom n 2 ); NO case: ed (G,H) ≥ ε_2 (i.e., ed (G,H) ≥ ε_2binom n 2 ). The algorithm must succeed with probability at least 2/3 on every input satisfying the promise.

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: lem:perm-recovery
title: Vertex defect bound
statement_text: Let G,H be graphs on [n] with ed (G,H) ≤ k , and let π^* ∈ S _n be an optimal permutation achieving ed _ π^* (G,H)=k . Define the defect of vertex v under π^* as d(v) = l|{u ∈ [n] \ {v} : (A_G)_ vu ≠ (A_H)_ π^*(v)π^*(u) } r|. Then d(v)< sqrt k for all but at most 2 sqrt k vertices v .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: lem:local-consistency
title: Local consistency propagation
statement_text: Let G,H be graphs on [n] drawn from G (n,1/2) conditioned on ed _π(G,H) ≤ k for a permutation π ∈ S _n . Suppose the vertex-image pairs {(v_1,π(v_1)), ... ,(v_s,π(v_s))} are known, where each v_i is a low-defect vertex drawn uniformly at random from L , and s ≥ C log n for a sufficiently large constant C>0 . Then with probability ≥ 1-1/ poly (n) over the randomness of G,H and the choice of seeds, the permutation π is uniquely determined on all of L .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: cor:seeds
title: Seed count for reconstruction
statement_text: Under the hypotheses of Lemma , to reconstruct π on all low-defect vertices, it suffices to obtain O ( log n) correct seed pairs (v,π(v)) where each v ∈ L is low-defect. In our algorithm, these correct pairs are produced by Phase 1 (MNRS quantum walk search, Section ), which returns matching vertices with high probability; incorrect candidates are filtered out by the marking oracle (Definition ). The remaining ≤ 2 sqrt k high-defect vertices must be resolved separately (see Phase 2, Section ).

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: def:product-graph
title: Product graph
statement_text: Given graphs G and H on [n] , define the compatibility product graph Γ=Γ(G,H) with: Vertex set: V(Γ)=[n] × [n] , where vertex (i,j) represents the candidate pairing of vertex i ∈ V(G) with vertex j ∈ V(H) . Edge set: {(i_1,j_1),(i_2,j_2)} ∈ E(Γ) if and only if: i_1 ≠ i_2 and j_1 ≠ j_2 (the pairing is injective), and (A_G)_ i_1 i_2 =(A_H)_ j_1 j_2 (the pairing is edge-consistent). The product graph Γ has N=n^2 vertices.

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: def:approx-clique
title: Matching set
statement_text: For a permutation π ∈ S _n , define the matching set M_π = {(i,π(i)) : i ∈ [n]} ⊆ V(Γ). If ed _π(G,H)=k , then M_π induces a subgraph with exactly binom n 2 -k internal edges (a near-clique missing k edges out of binom n 2 ).

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: lem:deg-matching
title: Degree of matching vertices
statement_text: Let π ∈ S _n with ed _π(G,H)=k . For vertex (i,π(i)) ∈ M_π , its degree within Γ[M_π] (the subgraph induced by M_π ) is exactly n-1-d(i) , where d(i) is the defect of vertex i (Lemma ). For low-defect vertices ( d(i)< sqrt k , of which there are ≥ n-2 sqrt k ), the internal degree is at least n-1- sqrt k .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: lem:deg-nonmatching
title: Total degree of matching vs.\ non-matching vertices
statement_text: For G,H G (n,1/2) conditioned on ed _π(G,H)=k : A low-defect matching vertex (i,π(i)) has total degree deg _Γ(i,π(i)) ≥ n-1- sqrt k within M_π alone. Including edges to non-matching vertices, deg _Γ(i,π(i))=Θ(n^2) . A non-matching vertex (i,j) with j ≠ π(i) has expected total degree E [deg _Γ(i,j)]=(n-1)^2/2 ± O (n) .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: def:product-walk
title: Product graph walk
statement_text: Define the Markov chain P on V(Γ)=[n] × [n] as follows. From state (i,j) : With probability 1/2 , stay at (i,j) (lazy step). With probability 1/2 , choose i' ∈ [n] \ {i} and j' ∈ [n] \ {j} uniformly at random. If (A_G)_ ii' =(A_H)_ jj' , move to (i',j') . Otherwise, stay at (i,j) .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: lem:stationary
title: Reversibility and stationary distribution
statement_text: The walk P is ergodic, aperiodic, and reversible with respect to the uniform distribution μ(i,j)=1/n^2 for all (i,j) ∈ [n] × [n] .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: thm:spectral-gap
title: Spectral gap of the product walk
statement_text: For G,H G (n,1/2) , the random walk P on Γ(G,H) has spectral gap δ ≥ Ω(1) with high probability.

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: cor:phase-gap
title: Phase gap of the Szegedy walk
statement_text: The Szegedy walk W(P) corresponding to the product graph walk P has phase gap Δ ≥ Ω(1) .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: def:marking
title: Marking oracle
statement_text: A vertex (i,j) ∈ V(Γ) is marked if its empirical consistency score exceeds a threshold. Concretely, we implement a probabilistic marking check : sample r=Θ( log n/ε^2) pairs (i',j') independently and uniformly from ([n] \ {i}) × ([n] \ {j}) , query (A_G)_ ii' and (A_H)_ jj' , and mark (i,j) if the fraction of consistent pairs (i.e., those satisfying (A_G)_ ii' =(A_H)_ jj' ) exceeds 1/2+ε/4 .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: lem:marking-correct
title: Marking oracle correctness
statement_text: For G,H G (n,1/2) with ed _ π^* (G,H) ≤ k=εbinom n 2 : Every low-defect matching vertex (i,π^*(i)) ∈ M_ π^* with d(i)< sqrt k is marked with probability ≥ 1-1/ poly (n) . Every non-matching vertex (i,j) with j ≠ π^*(i) is marked with probability ≤ 1/ poly (n) . Each invocation of the marking oracle uses r= O ( log n/ε^2) queries.

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: lem:walk-impl
title: Walk implementation
statement_text: One step of the Szegedy walk W(P) on the product graph can be implemented using O (1) queries to O_G and O_H and O ( log n) auxiliary gates.

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: prop:find-marked
title: Finding a marked vertex
statement_text: If ed (G,H) ≤ εbinom n 2 and G,H G (n,1/2) , a single marked vertex in Γ(G,H) can be found using O (n^ 3/2 /ε) queries, with constant probability.

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: lem:seed-sufficiency
title: Seed sufficiency
statement_text: For G,H G (n,1/2) with ed (G,H) ≤ εbinom n 2 , s= O ( log n) seed pairs (i,π^*(i)) from low-defect vertices suffice to reconstruct π^* on all low-defect vertices, w.h.p.

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: lem:reconstruction
title: Reconstruction procedure
statement_text: Given s= O ( log n) seed pairs from Phase 1, the following procedure reconstructs π^* on all of [n] using O (n log n+ sqrt k sqrt n ) additional queries: Signature computation: For each non-seed vertex v , compute the signature σ_ v,w for each candidate w ∈ [n] with respect to the seeds. This costs 2s queries per candidate (query (A_G)_ v,v_i and (A_H)_ w,π^*(v_i) for each seed v_i ). Over n vertices and n candidates: O (n^2 s) queries naively, but only O (ns)= O (n log n) queries if we fix v and iterate over w (since the (A_G)_ v,v_i entries are shared across all w , costing s queries, and (A_H)_ w,π^*(v_i) for w=1, ... ,n costs ns queries total across all v ). Matching: For each v ∈ L , select π(v)=arg min _w|σ_ v,w | . By Lemma , π(v)=π^*(v) for all v ∈ L w.h.p. Resolving high-defect vertices: For each of the ≤ 2 sqrt k high-defect vertices, use Grover search (Theorem ) over the n candidate images to find the one minimizing local edit distance. Each search costs O ( sqrt n ) queries, for a total of O ( sqrt k · sqrt n ) queries. Total: O (n log n+ sqrt k sqrt n )= O (n log n+n sqrt ε · sqrt n ) = O (n log n+n^ 3/2 sqrt ε ) . For constant ε , this is O (n^ 3/2 ) .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: lem:verification
title: Quantum verification
statement_text: Given π , one can estimate ed _ π (G,H) to within additive error δ with probability ≥ 2/3 using O (1/δ) queries.

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: thm:main-upper
title: Quantum upper bound for approximate graph isomorphism
statement_text: There exists a quantum algorithm that solves (ε, 2ε) -Approximate Graph Isomorphism (Problem ) on graphs G,H G (n,1/2) with n vertices using O (frac n^ 3/2 log n ε ) queries to the adjacency oracles O_G, O_H , succeeding with probability at least 2/3 .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: thm:classical-lower
title: Classical lower bound
statement_text: Any classical randomized algorithm that solves (ε,2ε) -Approximate Graph Isomorphism (Problem ) with success probability ≥ 2/3 for constant ε ∈ (0,1/8) requires Ω(n^2) queries to the adjacency oracles.

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: def:dyes
title: YES distribution D _ yes
statement_text: Sample (G,H) as follows: Draw G G (n,1/2) (ErdH o s--R\'enyi random graph). Draw π Uniform ( S _n) . Set H_0=π(G) (the graph obtained by relabeling G according to π ). Independently flip each edge of H_0 with probability p=ε/2 : for each {i,j} ∈ binom [n] 2 , set (A_H)_ ij =(A_ H_0 )_ ij ⊕ B_ ij where B_ ij Bernoulli (p) independently. Output (G,H) .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: lem:dyes-valid
statement_text: Under D _ yes , we have ed (G,H) ≤ ε with probability ≥ 1-e^ -Ω(n^2) .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: def:dno
title: NO distribution D _ no
statement_text: Sample (G,H) as follows: Draw G G (n,1/2) independently. Draw H G (n,1/2) independently. Output (G,H) .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: lem:dno-valid
statement_text: Under D _ no , we have ed (G,H) ≥ 2ε with probability ≥ 1-e^ -Ω(n^2) for ε<1/8 .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: lem:indistinguishable
title: Query transcript indistinguishability
statement_text: Let A be any deterministic adaptive algorithm making q queries in total, of which q_G go to A_G and q_H=q-q_G go to A_H . Let T_ yes and T_ no denote the distributions over query-answer transcripts under D_ yes and D_ no respectively. Provided q ≤ binom n 2 /2 , d_ TV (T_ yes , T_ no ) ≤ frac ε q_G q_H binom n 2 -q ≤ (4ε q^2)/(n^2).

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: subclm:ind
title: Independence on no collision
statement_text: For every t ∈ [q] , conditioned on F _ t-1 and on the event E_t that step t does not produce a collision, the conditional distribution of the answer A_t is Bern (tfrac 1 2 ) under both D_ yes and D_ no .

paper_title: Quantum Algorithms for Approximate Graph Isomorphism Testing
label: lem:hard

title: The class PLS
statement_text: A local search problem P is in the class color defblue PLS , if there are three polynomial time algorithms A_ P , \ B_ P , \ C_ P such that Given an instance I ∈ D_P , A_ P returns a solution s ∈ F_ P (I) ; Given an instance I ∈ D_ P and a solution s ∈ F_ P (I) , B_ P computes the objective value f_ P (s,I) of s ; and Given an instance I ∈ D_P and a solution s ∈ F_ P (I) , C_ P returns a neighbor of s with strictly better objective value, if it exists, and ``locally optimal", otherwise.

A problem Q ∈ PLS is color defblue PLS -complete if for every problem P ∈ PLS , there exists a PLS reduction from P to Q .

paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
label: def:tight_pls_complete
title: Tight PLS -reduction
statement_text: A color defblue tight PLS -reduction from a problem P ∈ PLS to a problem Q ∈ PLS is a PLS -reduction (h,g) from P to Q such that for every instance I ∈ D_P , we can choose a subset R of F_Q(h(I)) that satisfies: R contains all local optima of h(I) ; For every solution s_p ∈ F_ P (I) , we can construct in polynomial time a solution s_q ∈ R so that g(I,s_q) = s_p ; If there is a path from s_q ∈ R to s'_q ∈ R in the transition graph T_ h(I) such that the path contains no other element of R , then either there is an edge from the solution g(I,s_q) to the solution g(I,s'_q) in the transition graph T_I or these two solutions are identical. A problem Q ∈ PLS is color defblue tightly PLS -complete if for every problem P ∈ PLS , there exists a tight PLS -reduction from P to Q .

In addition, for i ∈ {1, ... , p} , the XOR gadget contains vertex disjoint paths of length two with a_i and b_i as endpoints. A color defblue subtour of the XOR gadget is a spanning path with two endpoints in the set {a_1, a_p, b_1, b_p} . For convenience, when p = 0 , both the XOR gadget of order zero and its only subtour are defined to be the empty graph.

The second-set case: The tour uses all the doors and the right second-set edge of x and does not use the left and right first-set edges of x . It also uses the subtour in the XOR gadget assigned to x incident to the right second-set edge of x and the closest door to x_r . Further, all parity gadgets related to x are engaged at x .

paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
label: lem:x-change
statement_text: For an H -vertex x , an x -change is a swap of at least k edges. Further, it is a swap of exactly k edges, if and only if the x -change only involves standard subtour changes.

paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
label: lem:phi_bijection
statement_text: The function φ is a bijection between the standard tours in G and the cuts in H . Further, for any cut γ of H , φ^ -1 (γ) can be constructed in polynomial time.

paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
label: lem:correspondence_13_1
statement_text: Let τ_1 be a standard tour of G , and let γ_1 := φ(τ_1) . Then for any cut γ_2 obtained from γ_1 by an improving flip, the tour φ^ -1 (γ_2) can be obtained from τ_1 by an improving k -swap.

paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
label: lem:correspondence_13_2
statement_text: Let τ_1 be a standard tour of G , and let γ_1 = φ(τ_1) . Then for any standard tour τ_2 , obtained from τ_1 by performing an improving k -swap, the cut φ(τ_2) can be obtained from γ_1 by an improving flip.

paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
label: lem:correspondence
statement_text: The transition graph of the Max-Cut instance (H,w) is isomorphic to the subgraph of the transition graph of the TSP/ k -Opt instance (G_ ∞ , c_ ∞ ) induced by the standard tours of G .

paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
label: lem:forcing_a
statement_text: In a tour of G , if a parity gadget is strict at one related H -vertex, then it is also strict at the other related H -vertex.

paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
label: lem:forcing_b
statement_text: Suppose x is an H -vertex with degree d(x) . If d(x)-1 parity gadgets related to x are strict at x in a tour of G , then the remaining parity gadget related to x is also strict at x .

paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
label: lem:strict_flexible_gadgets
statement_text: If the H -edges corresponding to the flexible gadgets form a forest in H , then all parity gadgets are strict at their related H -vertices in any tour of G .

paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
label: cor:no_nonstandard
statement_text: All tours of G are standard tours.

paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
label: lem:degrees
statement_text: The following holds for the graph G : Each vertex of G has degree two, three, or four. Every vertex in G is either a degree-two vertex or adjacent to one. Every degree-four vertex in G is in a parity gadget. Every strict gadget in G has four degree-four vertices (namely, Z, Z', a , and Y' ). Every flexible gadget in G also has four degree-four vertices (namely, Z, Z', X' , and Y' ).

paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
label: obs:improving3swap
statement_text: Let (E_1, E_2) be a 3-swap in (G_ ∞ , c_ ∞ ) such that E_1 contains a non-edge e_1 with c_ ∞ (e_1) > max _ e ∈ E_2 c_ ∞ (e) . Suppose that performing the swap (E_1, E_2) from a tour τ of (G_ ∞ , c_ ∞ ) results in another tour. Then this swap is improving.

paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
label: lem:no_infty_local_optima
statement_text: Let τ be a tour of (G_ ∞ , c_ ∞ ) containing a non-edge . Then there exists an improving 3 -swap for τ .

paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
label: claim:3_swap_from_infty
statement_text: Suppose there exist a non-edge v v' in τ and an edge u v in τ^* but not in τ . Further suppose that for any vertex v'' ≠ u, v , if v'' is not τ^* -consistent, then λ(v'') < λ( v ) . Then there exists an improving 3-swap that removes v v' .

paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
label: thm:tight_reduction
statement_text: There exists a tight PLS -reduction from Max-Cut/Flip with maximum degree five to TSP/ k -Opt for any k ≥ 15 .

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
label: thm:small-embedding
title: Informal
statement_text: Under the 3 - OV Hypothesis or SETH , any algorithm computing L layer, H head transformers with summation aggregation and embedding dimension m = Ω ( log N ) requires LHN^ 2 - o(1) time. The lower bound holds even if the transformer has no MLPs.

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
label: thm:linear-embedding
title: Informal
statement_text: Any extended arithmetic circuit computing L -layer H -head transformers with summation aggregation and embedding dimension m = Ω(N) has size at least L H N^ ω - o(1) when ω > 2 . The lower bound holds even if the transformer has no MLPs.

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
label: def:arithmetic-circuit
statement_text: An arithmetic circuit ( AC ) is a sequence of operations {g_1, dotsc , g_ s } such that each g_ j gets y ∘ z for ∘ ∈ {+, -, × , / } and y, z ∈ {g_ i }_ i < j ∪ {x_ i } ∪ R with a subset of gates {g_ i_k } denoted the output gates. Given input x , denote C (x) as the values on the output gates. An arithmetic circuit C computes F: R ^ n → R ^ m if C (x) = F(x) for all x ∈ R ^ n .

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
label: def:extended-arithmetic-circuit
statement_text: An extended arithmetic circuit ( eAC ) computing F: R ^ n → R is a sequence of operations {g_1, dotsc , g_ s } such that each g_ j is one of the following forms: g_ j gets y ∘ z for ∘ ∈ {+, -, × , / } and y, z ∈ {g_ i }_ i < j ∪ {x_ i } ∪ R . g_ j gets exp (y) for y ∈ {g_ i }_ i < j ∪ {x_ i } ∪ R . g_ j gets ln (y) for y ∈ {g_ i }_ i < j ∪ {x_ i } ∪ R _ > 0 .

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
label: def:attn
title: Attention
statement_text: A self-attention head is a mapping f_ Q, K, V : R ^ N × d_ in → R ^ N × m defined by f_ Q, K, V (X)= softmax (Q(X) K(X)^top ) V(X) and parameterized by row-wise query , key , and value embeddings Q, K, V : R ^ N × d_ in → R ^ N × m (e.g., Q(X) = (Q(X_1), ... , Q(X_N)) . Let Att ^ N _ m, d_ in denote the set of all self-attention heads with input dimension d_ in , embedding dimension m and input length N . When m = d_ in , we denote this as Att ^ N _ m .

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
label: def:hardmax-attn
title: Hardmax Attention
statement_text: A hardmax-attention head is a mapping f^ hard _ Q, K, V : R ^ N × d_ in → R ^ N × m defined by f^ hard _ Q, K, V (X)= hardmax (Q(X) K(X)^top ) V(X) .

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
label: def:mlp
statement_text: An MLP is a continuous function Ψ: R ^ m_1 → R ^ m_2 for m_1, m_2 > 0 .

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
label: def:tran
title: Transformer
statement_text: A transformer is a mapping T: R ^ N × d_ in → R ^ N × d_ out specified by attention heads {f_ ℓ , h }_ ℓ , h = 1 ^ L, H and element-wise MLP layers Ψ_ ℓ : R ^ m → R ^ m for ℓ ∈ [L] . Upon input X ∈ R ^ N × d_ in , the transformer computes intermediate embeddings X^ (1) , ... , X^ (L) with X^ ( ℓ ) = Ψ_ ℓ (X^ ( ℓ - 1) + Σ _ h=1 ^ H f_ ℓ ,h (X^ ( ℓ -1) ) ) ∀ ℓ ∈ [L], and returns T(X) = Ψ_O(X^ (L) ) for an output MLP Ψ_O: R ^m → R ^ d_ out (let X^ (0) := X for notational convenience). A hardmax transformer is defined analogously, replacing each attention head with a hardmax-attention head.

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
label: def:alg-compute-tran
statement_text: An algorithm computes transformers with context length N , embedding dimension m , L layers, H heads in each layer, input dimension d_ in and output dimension d_ out if given any such transformer T and any input X ∈ R ^ N × d_ in , the algorithm outputs T(X) .

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
label: def:circuit-compute-tran
statement_text: Let T be a transformer with context length N , embedding dimension m , L layers, H heads in each layer, input dimension d_ in and output dimension d_ out . Suppose T has weights W and input X . A circuit C computes T if for any input X ∈ R ^ N × d_ in and any weights W , C (X, W) = T_ W (X) .

label: lem:softmax-sim-hardmax

Then there exists an attention unit f' ∈ Att ^ N _ m satisfying lVertf '(X) - hardmax (A(X)) V(X) ‖ _ ∞ ≤ frac 1 poly (N) for an arbitrarily small inverse polynomial.

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
title: Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis ( SETH )
statement_text: For any ε>0 , there exists a positive integer k such that k - SAT requires Ω(2^ (1-ε)n ) time, where n is the number of variables in the CNF.
