label: hyp:k-ov

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
label: hyp:unbalanced-k-ov
title: Unbalanced k - OV Hypothesis

label: lemma:unbalanced-k-OV
statement_text: Let 0 < s_ 2 dotsc , s_ k ≤ 1 . Let A_1, ... A_ k ⊂ {0, 1 }^ d for d = Θ( log n) with |A_ 1 | = n and |A_ i | = n^ s_ i for all i > 1 . In particular, the Unbalanced k - OV Hypothesis holds under the k - OV Hypothesis.

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
label: thm:small-embedding-formal

statement_text: Let m = Θ( log N) and L, H = poly (N) . Any algorithm computing transformers with input length N , embedding dimension m , L layers, H heads in each layer, and input and output dimension m up to entry-wise additive error (1)/(10N) requires LHN^ 2 - o(1) time under the 3 - OV Hypothesis. paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers

statement_text: Suppose there exists an algorithm A that computes any transformer with input length N+1 , embedding dimension 2d+2 , L layers, H heads in each layer, input and output dimension 2d+2 , up to entry-wise additive error (1)/(10N) in time B , then there exists an algorithm that solves unbalanced 3 - OV with dimension d and size N,N,LH in time O (LHd+B) .

statement_text: Under the 3 - OV Hypothesis, any transformer with linear time embedding and MLP maps computing d -dimensional 3 - OV requires LHm = N^ 1 - o(1) .

statement_text: Let F: R ^ n → R be a function and F' = (frac partial F partial x_ 1 , ... , frac partial F partial x_ n ) . If there is an AC of size s computing F , there is an AC of size O(s) computing F' .

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers

statement_text: Let F: R ^ n → R be a function and let F' = {frac partial F partial x_ 1 , dotsc , frac partial F partial x_ n } . If there is an eAC of size s computing F , there is an eAC of size O(s) computing F' .

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
label: lem:independent-product-lb
statement_text: For any integer ℓ ≥ 1 , any arithmetic circuit computing ℓ independent n × n × n matrix products has size ℓ · n^ ω - o(1) .

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
label: def:denormalized-attn
title: Denormalized Attention

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
label: lem:denormalized-attn

label: def:glu

Let T be a transformer with input length N , embedding dimension m , L layers, H heads, input dimension d_ in , output dimension d_ out with no MLPs. paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
label: lem:relu-simulates-no-mlp
statement_text: Let T be a transformer with input length N , embedding dimension m , L layers, H heads, input dimension d_ in , output dimension d_ out with no MLPs. Then, there is a transformer T' with input length N , embedding dimension m , L layers, H heads, input dimension d_ in , output dimension d_ out and MLPs with d_ hid = 2m and ReLU activation functions such that T'(X) = T(X) for all inputs X .

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
label: def:gap-preserving-activation
statement_text: An activation function σ: R → R is gap-preserving if the following hold: σ(0) ≠ σ(1) , There exists c^* such that for all x ≤ c^* - 1 , σ(x) ≤ σ(c^* - 1) < σ(c^*) .

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
label: prop:small-embedding-sigmoid
statement_text: Let m = Θ( log N) and L, H = poly (N) . Any algorithm computing transformers with input length N , embedding dimension m , L layers, H heads in each layer, input dimension m , and output dimension 1 up to entry-wise additive error (1)/(10N) requires LHN^ 2 - o(1) time under the 3 - OV Hypothesis. The lower bound holds even if the transformer has MLPs with hidden dimension O(m) and gap-preserving activation function.

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
label: def:differentiable-activation
statement_text: An activation function σ: R → R is eAC gradient efficient if the following hold: σ(0) ≠ σ(1) , σ^ -1 can be implemented with an eAC of size O(1) . σ'(x) = h(σ(x)) for some h such that both σ, h can be implemented with an eAC of size O(1) .

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
label: prop:large-embedding-sigmoid

Any eAC computing T has size at least L H N^ ω - o(1) - O (LHN^2 ) . The lower bound holds even when T has MLPs with d_ hid = O(m) and eAC gradient efficient activation functions.

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
label: lem:sigmoid-recover-derivatives
statement_text: Recall that we index k ∈ [LH] as (h, ℓ ) . For all 0 ≤ ℓ ≤ L , there is an eAC of size O(H(L - ℓ )N^2) that computes {A_ k B_ k ^ top } for k = (h, p) with p ≥ ℓ , { Π _ p = t ^ L σ' (Y^ (p) _ i_0, 1 ) }_ t ∈ [ ℓ - 1, L], i_0 , and { Π _ p = t ^ L σ' (Y^ (p) _ i_0, i_0 + 1 ) }_ t ∈ [ ℓ - 1, L], i_0 .

paper_title: On the Computational Hardness of Transformers
label: prop:concat-sims-sum
statement_text: Assume H ≤ m divides m . Suppose T is a transformer with input length N , embedding dimension m/H , L layers, H heads per layer, and summation aggregation. Then, there is a transformer T' with input length N + 1 , embedding dimension m + H , L layers, H heads per layer and concatenation aggregation such that there is a linear function f: R ^ m → R ^ m such that f(T'(X)) = T(X) for all inputs X . Furthermore, the following hold: If T is computable by an eAC , so is T' . If each embedding map of T is computable by an AC of size O(m/H) , then all embedding maps of T in one layer are computable by an AC of size O(m) . If T has no MLPs, then neither does T' . If T has MLPs or GLU MLPs with d_ hid = O(m/H) and activation function σ , then T' has an MLP with d_ hid = O(m) and activation function σ (see and ).

paper_title: Tight (S)ETH-based Lower Bounds for Pseudopolynomial Algorithms for Bin Packing and Multi-Machine Scheduling

label: ex:pigeonhole
title: Pigeonhole principle
statement_text: Consider the following CNF formula ¬ onto PHP _n , consisting of clauses over propositional variables p_ ij , where i ∈ [n+1] and j ∈ [n] : vee_j p_ ij , one clause for each i ; ¬ p_ i_1 j ∨ ¬ p_ i_2 j , one clause for each triple i_1 < i_2 and j ; ¬ p_ i j_1 ∨ ¬ p_ i j_2 , one clause for each triple i and j_1 < j_2 ; vee_i p_ ij , one clause for each j . The variable p_ ij is intended to express that pigeon i is assigned to hole j . The clauses in (1) and (4) assert that every pigeon is assigned to some hole and that every hole contains at least one pigeon, respectively. Clauses in (2) and (3) enforce that no two pigeons are assigned to the same hole and that no pigeon is assigned to more than one hole. Clearly, ¬ onto PHP _n is unsatisfiable, since the number of pigeons exceeds the number of holes. In fact, the formula remains unsatisfiable even if only clauses (1) and (2) are retained. This weaker principle is known as the weak pigeonhole principle , denoted ¬ PHP _n . We introduce this example because of the following well-known result due to Ajtai, which establishes super-polynomial lower bounds for bounded-depth Frege proofs. Let d ≥ 2 and let 0 < δ < 5^ -d . Then for all sufficiently large n the following holds. Every F_d -refutation of ¬ ontoPHP _n (that is, every F_d -proof of bot from ¬ ontoPHP _n ) contains at least 2^ n^δ pairwise different subformulas. In particular, any such refutation has size at least 2^ n^δ .

statement_text: Let R be an (A,B) -ribbon with vertex set V(R) and edge set W_R . A set Q ⊆ V(R) (not necessarily disjoint from supp (A) ∪ supp (B) ) is a separator if removing Q disconnects supp (A) from supp (B) in the graph (V(R),W_R ∪ E _ A,B ) . Let sep (R) be the minimum size of a separator. By convention, separators are allowed to intersect the endpoint sets supp (A) and supp (B) . Consider the following communication problem DIHP. Communication structure : There are T players named Player _t for t ∈ [T] . This is a one-way communication game; the players speak in order from 1 to T . Input type: Each player Player _t gets a k -partite hypermatching M_t ∈ M ^ m,k _ n and a noisy signal Z_t ∈ Z _q^ m × k . (I.e., each player can be viewed as a function Player _t : M ^ m,k _ n × Z _q^ m × k × {0,1}^s → {0,1}^s .) Input distributions: The goal is to distinguish between the YES and NO input distributions. In both cases, the inputs M _t are uniformly random and independent. The two cases are defined as follows: In the NO case, Z _t is also picked uniformly and independently for every t ∈ [T] . paper_title: Automatic constraint satisfaction problem
statement_text: (AutCSP instance) \ We call the tuple (V, D, C , A ) an AutCSP instance I or an automatic CSP instance , where V is a set of variables, D is a finite domain, C is a finite set of constraints, and A is a finite automaton over D . paper_title: Automatic constraint satisfaction problem
statement_text: Based on the representations of AutCSP instances, we define the following classes of CSP. The automatic constraint satisfaction problem , written AutCSP , is the problem of finding solutions to instances I=(V, D, C, A ) where the automaton A is counted as a part of the input. The constraint satisfaction problem that corresponds to Γ_ A is denoted by AutCSP( A ) . For the AutCSP( A ) instances, the automaton A is a fixed parameter and it is not part of the input. Hence we can write these instances in the form (V, D, C ) as Γ_ A is given by A .

statement_text: In these examples D={0,1} is Boolean: Consider CSP (Γ) , where Γ consists of finitely many relations of pairwise different arities. This is an AutCSP as finite languages are regular . paper_title: Automatic constraint satisfaction problem
label: dfn:polymorphisms
statement_text: Let R be a relation of arity k on D . A polymorphism of R is an operation f:D^t → D that satisfies the following condition. For all tuples (x_ 1,1 , ... , x_ 1, k ) ∈ R , ... , (x_ t,1 , ... , x_ t, k ) ∈ R we have (f(x_ 1,1 , x_ 2,1 , ... , x_ t,1 ), ... , f(x_ 1,k , x_ 2,k , ... , x_ t,k )) ∈ R . statement_text: Let Γ be a (possibly infinite) set of relations over D = {0,1} . paper_title: Kernelization Bounds for Constrained Coloring
label: def:R-CC

label: thm:equiv-lit
title: Equivalence Class Theorem for CSP (Γ)
statement_text: Let n ∈ N and Γ be a constraint language containing k -ary relations over the domain [q] . For a,b ∈ [q]^n , define (a,b) ∈ E if every instance of CSP (Γ) on n variables that is satisfied by a is also satisfied by b . Then E is an equivalence relation on [q]^n . As a consequence, for every a ∈ [q]^n , there exists an instance P_a of CSP (Γ) such that Sat (P_a) = [a]_ E , where [a]_ E denotes the equivalence class of a under E .

paper_title: Characterizing Streaming Decidability of CSPs via Non-Redundancy

For a,b ∈ {0,1}^n , define (a,b) ∈ E if every instance of the positive CSP (Γ) on n variables that is satisfied by a is also satisfied by b . Then the restriction of E to the non-constant assignments {0,1}^n \ {0^n,1^n} is an equivalence relation.

statement_text: Let us consider the PMMSNP problem with template ( F _3^ (2) , F _4^ (2) ) . In this problem, we are given a graph G = (V, E) and must decide whether it has a 2-colouring that avoids monochromatic triangles, or not even a 2-colouring that avoids monochromatic 4-cliques. We will show that something slightly more strict is possible: if we assume the input graph has a 2-colouring avoiding all monochromatic triangles, we will find a 2-colouring avoiding all monochromatic 4-cliques. (Thus, if our algorithm successfully outputs a 2-colouring avoiding all monochromatic 4-cliques we may answer Yes , otherwise we must answer No .) To do this, construct a 4-uniform hypergraph whose vertices coincide with the vertices of G , and whose hyperedges are given by the 4-cliques of G . Call this hypergraph H = (V, E') . The condition that G has a 2-colouring avoiding all monochromatic triangles implies that there exists a 2-colouring c : V → {0, 1} of H that, for every (x, y, z, t) ∈ E' , colours half of x, y, z, t with 0 and the other half with 1 . We must output a colouring d : V → {0, 1} that leaves no edge of H monochromatic. This is just the problem PCSP ( 2 - in - 4 , NAE 4 ) , well-known from the PCSP literature, which admits a poly-time solution via the Affine Integer Programming (AIP) relaxation . Let us quickly present this algorithm. By assumption, there exists c : V → {0, 1 } such that ∀ (x, y, z, t) ∈ E' : c(x) + c(y) + c(z) + c(t) = 2. Of course, it is NP -hard to find this mapping; however, it is possible to solve the system of equations in over Z , by computing the Smith normal form ; suppose c is our solution. Now, consider any edge (x, y, z, t) . It is not possible that all of c (x), c (y), c (z), c (t) are ≤ 0 (or else the sum would be ≤ 0 < 2 ); nor is it possible that all are > 0 (or else the sum would be at least 4 > 2 ). Hence, if we set v ∈ V to 1 or 0 depending on whether c (v) ≥ 1 or c (v) ≤ 0 , we can find the desired solution in NAE 4 .

statement_text: Consider a multiset of linear equations (C_1,C_2, ... , C_m) over variables {x_1,x_2, ... ,x_n|x_i ∈ G} for a group G . Each constraint consists of a tuple of exactly k literals and will be considered satisfied when their sum/product over G is in S ⊆ G . The Max-E k -LIN _ S (G) problem is to find an assignment to {x_1,x_2, ... ,x_n} that maximizes the number of satisfied constraints.

label: thm:main
statement_text: Fix any finite group G and S ⊆ G . Let H_S is the smallest normal subgroup such that [G,G] ⊆ H_S S ⊆ gH_S for some g ∈ G , i.e., S is a subset of some coset of H_S . then the problem Max-E k -LIN _ S (G) is approximable within a factor of (|S|)/(|H_S|) on satisfiable instances. Furthermore, if S^ -1 S generates H_S , assuming P ≠ NP , for every ε>0 , it is NP -hard to approximate Max-E k -LIN _ S (G) within a factor of (|S|)/(|H_S|)+ε .

label: def:label-cover
title: Label Cover
statement_text: An instance Ψ=(U,V,E,[L], [R],{π_e}_ e ∈ E ) of the Label Cover constraint satisfaction problem consists of a bi-regular bipartite graph (U,V,E) , alphabets [L] and [R] and a surjective projection map π_e : [L] → [R] for every edge e ∈ E . Given a labeling ℓ : U → [L], ℓ :V → [R] , an edge e = (u,v) is said to be satisfied by ℓ if π_e( ℓ (u)) = ℓ (v) . Ψ is said to be satisfiable if there exists a labeling that satisfies all the edges. Ψ is said to be at most δ -satisfiable if every labeling satisfies at most a δ fraction of the edges.

title: Layered Label Cover
statement_text: An T - Layered Label Cover \ instance, given by H =( V ={V_1, ... ,V_T}, {Π_ i,j }_ 1 ≤ i < j ≤ T }, {[R_i]_ i ∈ [T] } consist of T sets of vertices V ={V_1, ... ,V_T} . The label set of vertices in layer i is denoted by [R_i] . Every pair of layers 1 ≤ i<j ≤ l has a set of constraints Π_ i,j between the vertices in V_ i and V_ j . The constraint between v ∈ V_ i and u ∈ V_ j (if it exists in Π_ i,j ) is denoted by π_ vu . Moreover, every constraint between a pair of vertices is a projection constraint: for every assignment k ∈ [R_ i ] to v ∈ V_ i , there is a unique assignment to u ∈ V_ j that satisfies the constraint π_ vu .

statement_text: For any constant parameters T ≥ 2 , r ∈ Z , the following problem is NP-hard. label: thm:intro-tbalanced
title: Upper-Bound criterion ; informal
statement_text: Let R ⊆ {0,1}^r and let t ≥ 1 . Then R is t -balanced if and only if every falsifying tuple f ∉ R is captured by a multilinear polynomial of degree at most t over some commutative ring with identity. Consequently, every n -variable instance of CSP (R) has an equivalent subinstance with O(n^t) constraints, and hence NRD _ n (R) =O(n^t) .

label: ex:nae-upper-1
statement_text: Consider R= NAE _3 , so W (R) ={1,2} . The falsifying tuples are 000 and 111 . The polynomial p(x)=(x_1+x_2+x_3-1)(x_1+x_2+x_3-2) vanishes on all tuples of Hamming weight 1 or 2 , and is nonzero on tuples of Hamming weight 0 or 3 . Thus this degree- 2 polynomial captures both falsifying tuples. For t=2 , the lift is ν_2(x)=(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_1x_2,x_1x_3,x_2x_3) . The lifted relation R^ (2) consists of the six vectors obtained from the accepting tuples: c|c x & ν_2(x) hline 100 & (1,0,0,0,0,0) 010 & (0,1,0,0,0,0) 001 & (0,0,1,0,0,0) 110 & (1,1,0,1,0,0) 101 & (1,0,1,0,1,0) 011 & (0,1,1,0,0,1). The falsifying tuples lift to ν_2(000)=(0,0,0,0,0,0) and ν_2(111)=(1,1,1,1,1,1) . After multilinearization, p becomes p(x)=2-2(x_1+x_2+x_3)+2(x_1x_2+x_1x_3+x_2x_3) , which is a linear expression in the lifted coordinates. This illustrates why degree- t capturing polynomials can be studied through linear conditions after the degree- t lift.

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
title: Continuing
statement_text: The previous example showed the polynomial side of the lift. We now use the same relation to illustrate the integer-span test actually used in the implementation. The two rejected lifted points are ν_2(000)=(0,0,0,0,0,0) and ν_2(111)=(1,1,1,1,1,1) . To test 2 -balancedness, we check whether either rejected point lies in the integer span of the accepted lifted points after adding a leading 1 coordinate. For b=ν_2(000) , membership would mean that there are integers z_ 100 ,z_ 010 ,z_ 001 ,z_ 110 ,z_ 101 ,z_ 011 such that Σ _ a ∈ R^ (2) z_a ext (a)= ext (b)=(1,0,0,0,0,0,0). Looking at the three degree- 2 coordinates forces z_ 110 =z_ 101 =z_ 011 =0 . Then the three degree- 1 coordinates force z_ 100 =z_ 010 =z_ 001 =0 , contradicting the leading-coordinate equation Σ _a z_a=1 . Hence ext (ν_2(000)) is not in the integer span. Similarly, for b=ν_2(111) , the three degree- 2 coordinates force z_ 110 =z_ 101 =z_ 011 =1 . The degree- 1 coordinates then force z_ 100 =z_ 010 =z_ 001 =-1 . But the leading-coordinate sum is then -1-1-1+1+1+1=0 , not 1 . Hence ext (ν_2(111)) is also not in the integer span. Therefore neither rejected lifted point lies in the integer span, so the integer-span test certifies that NAE _3 is 2 -balanced.

label: ex:kcube
statement_text: For example, when k=2 , the input rows are indexed by 11,10,01 . The operation f_2 has arity 3 and is defined on the following column types: c|c column & f_2( column ) hline 000 & 0 111 & 1 110 & 0 001 & 1 101 & 0 010 & 1. Here 110 and 101 are the two coordinate columns of the nonzero 2 -cube, and 001 and 010 are their complements. As a concrete failure, take R= NAE _3 , so W (R) ={1,2} . Consider the following three input rows, indexed by 11,10,01 : c|ccc|c & coord. 1 & coord. 2 & coord. 3 & weight hline 11 & 1 & 1 & 0 & 2 10 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1 01 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 1. All three rows belong to NAE _3 . Now look at the columns: they are 110 , 101 , and 000 . By the table above, f_2 maps these columns to 0 , 0 , and 0 , respectively. paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
statement_text: Consider again the case k=2 . The column types in the domain of f_2 are 000,111,110,001,101,010 , with outputs 0,1,0,1,0,1 , respectively. Suppose R= NAE _3 , so W (R) ={1,2} . Since R has arity 3 , a multiplicity vector assigns three coordinates among these six column types. Take the multiplicity vector that uses 110 once, 101 once, and 000 once, and uses all other column types zero times. The three input rows then have weights 2,1,1 : the row indexed by 11 sees the entries 1,1,0 , the row indexed by 10 sees 1,0,0 , and the row indexed by 01 sees 0,1,0 . All these weights lie in W (R) ={1,2} . The output row has entries 0,0,0 , hence output weight 0 , which does not lie in W (R) . Therefore this multiplicity vector witnesses failure of preservation, and the lower-bound criterion succeeds for R= NAE _3 and k=2 .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
title: Relative balancedness
statement_text: Let A ⊆ X ⊆ {0,1} ^N . We say that A is balanced relative to X if for every odd integer m ≥ 1 and every tuple a^ (1) ,a^ (2) , ... ,a^ (m) ∈ A , it holds that if the coordinatewise alternating sum u := a^ (1) - a^ (2) + a^ (3) - ... - a^ (m-1) + a^ (m) belongs to X , then u ∈ A .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: def:tbal
title: t -lift and t -balancedness
statement_text: Fix integers r ≥ 1 and t ≥ 1 , and let S_ r,t :={S ⊆ [r]:1 ≤ |S| ≤ t} . The degree- t lift is the map ν_t:{0,1}^r → {0,1}^ S_ r,t defined by ν_t(x)_S:= Π _ i ∈ S x_i . For a relation R ⊆ {0,1}^r , let X_t:=ν_t({0,1}^r) and R^ (t) :=ν_t(R) . We say that R is t -balanced if R^ (t) is balanced relative to X_t .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
title: Capturing polynomial
statement_text: Let R ⊆ {0,1} ^r and let f ∈ {0,1} ^r \ R . A polynomial p over a ring E captures f with respect to R if p(y)=0 for all y ∈ R, and p(f) ≠ 0. Equivalently, we may write p\ captures _R\ f .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: lem:bal-latt
statement_text: Let A ⊆ X ⊆ {0,1} ^N , and define ext (v) := (1,v) ∈ Z ^ N+1 . Then the following are equivalent. A is balanced relative to X . For every u ∈ X , if ext (u) ∈ span _ Z l({ ext (a): a ∈ A} r), then u ∈ A .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: thm:linrel
statement_text: Let A ⊆ X ⊆ {0,1} ^N . Then the following are equivalent. A is balanced relative to X . For every u ∈ X \ A , there exists a prime-power q_u := p^a (for some prime p ) and a linear polynomial ℓ _u(z_1, ... ,z_N)=α_0+α_1 z_1+ ... +α_N z_N over Z /q_u Z such that ℓ _u\ captures _A\ u . Moreover, if A is not balanced relative to X , then there exists some u ∈ X \ A that is not capturable by any linear polynomial over any commutative ring with identity.

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: thm:t-balanced-main
statement_text: Let R ⊆ {0,1}^r and let t ≥ 1 . Then the following are equivalent. R is t -balanced . For every f ∈ {0,1}^r \ R , there exists a prime-power q_f and a multilinear polynomial p_f over Z/q_fZ of degree at most t such that p_f captures f with respect to R . Moreover, if R is not t -balanced , then there exists f ∈ {0,1}^r \ R that is not captured by any degree- ≤ t multilinear polynomial over any commutative ring with identity.

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: thm:cjp-general-capture
title: Theorem 3.5,
statement_text: Let R ⊆ {0,1} ^r be a fixed Boolean relation. Suppose that for every u ∈ {0,1} ^r \ R , there exists a ring E_u which is either Q or a Z /q_u Z for some q_u ∈ N _ >1 and a polynomial p_u over E_u of degree at most t such that p_u captures u with respect to R . Then there exists a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a set of R -constraints on n variables, outputs an equivalent subset of O(n^t) constraints.

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: def:fgppdef
title: fgpp-definition
statement_text: Let Γ be a constraint language over a finite domain D , and let R ⊆ D^m be a relation. We say that R is fgpp-definable from Γ if there is a formula R(x_1, ... ,x_m) ≡ ∃ y_1, ... ,y_q ψ(x_1, ... ,x_m,y_1, ... ,y_q), where ψ is a conjunction of constraints over Γ together with functional guards of the form Q_g(u,v) , where g : D → D is a unary map and Q_g:={(a,g(a)):a ∈ D}. We write ⟨ Γ ⟩ _ fg for the set of all relations fgpp-definable from Γ .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
title: Polymorphism pattern and pattern partial operation
statement_text: A polymorphism pattern of arity s is a set of pairs ((x_1, ... ,x_s),x), where (x_1, ... ,x_s) is a tuple of variables and x is one of the variables appearing in it. Given a finite domain D , the interpretation of such a pattern P on D is the partial operation f_P^D defined as follows: its domain consists of all tuples of the form (φ(x_1), ... ,φ(x_s)) arising from a pair ((x_1, ... ,x_s),x) ∈ P and an assignment φ of the variables to D , and on such a tuple we set f_P^D(φ(x_1), ... ,φ(x_s)):=φ(x). A partial operation obtained in this way is called a pattern partial operation .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
title: Pattern partial polymorphisms
statement_text: Let R ⊆ D^r be a relation and let f be a k -ary partial operation on D . We say that f is a partial polymorphism of R if for every choice of tuples t^ (1) , ... ,t^ (k) ∈ R such that f is defined coordinatewise on these tuples, the tuple obtained by applying f coordinatewise also belongs to R . If in addition f is a pattern partial operation, then we call it a pattern partial polymorphism of R . For a constraint language Γ , we write p^2Pol (Γ) for the set of all pattern partial polymorphisms of every relation in Γ .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: thm:carbonnel-duality
title: Carbonnel
statement_text: Let Γ_1,Γ_2 be finite constraint languages over the same finite domain. Then p^2Pol (Γ_1) ⊆ p^2Pol (Γ_2) Longleftrightarrow Γ_2 ⊆ ⟨ Γ_1 ⟩ _ fg . In particular, for a relation R and any relation S over the same domain, S ∈ ⟨ {R} ⟩ _ fg Longleftrightarrow p^2Pol ({R}) ⊆ p^2Pol ({S}).

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: def:universal-k-cube
title: Universal k -cube pattern
statement_text: Fix k ≥ 2 . Let c_1, ... ,c_ 2^k-1 be the lexicographic ordering of the tuples in {x,y}^k \ {(y, ... ,y)} with respect to y>x . The universal k -cube pattern P_k^u of arity 2^k-1 is the set of pairs (t_i,y) for all 1 ≤ i ≤ k , where t_i := l(c_1[i],c_2[i], ... ,c_ 2^k-1 [i] r). Its interpretation on the Boolean domain is denoted by f^ {0,1} _ P_k^u .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: thm:carbonnel-lower-bound

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: thm:positive-nrd
statement_text: Let D be a domain of size |D|=q , let Γ be a fixed finite constraint language containing r -ary relations over D . Let U be a finite set of unary maps D → D containing the identity map. Then, for every n ≥ 1 , we have NRD ^ simp _ n (Γ) ≤ NRD ^ + _ n (Γ) ≤ NRD ^ lit _ n (Γ) ≤ NRD ^ simp _ O_ r,q (n) (Γ) . Consequently, for fixed D,Γ , and U , the three models have the same asymptotic non-redundancy up to constant-factor changes in the number of variables.

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: def:balance
statement_text: A Boolean predicate P ⊆ {0,1}^r is balanced if for all k ∈ N and all tuples t_1, hdots , t_ 2k+1 ∈ P (some possibly equal), if we compute (over Z ) the r -tuple t := t_1 - t_2 + t_3 - ... + t_ 2k+1 and t ∈ {0,1}^r , then t ∈ P .

statement_text: Assume that P is an I -substructure of Q and that CSP (P) has an infinite family of (|E|^ ε , I) - shrinking instances . Then, NRD (Q, n) = Ω(n^ (1)/(1-ε) ) .

label: thm:boolbck-intro

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: def:NRD
statement_text: Given a predicate P ⊆ D^r , we say that an r -uniform hypergraph H = (V, E) is a non-redundant (NRD) instance of CSP (P) if for every edge e ∈ E , there exists an assignment ψ_e : V → D such that ψ_e satisfies e' for every e' ∈ E \ {e} , but ψ_e does not satisfy e . We define NRD (P, n) to be the size of the largest non-redundant instance of CSP (P) on n vertices.

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: def:conditional-nrd
statement_text: Given predicates P ⊊ Q ⊆ D^r , we say that an r -uniform hypergraph H = (V, E) is a (conditionally) non-redundant instance of CSP (P | Q) if for every edge e ∈ E , there exists an assignment ψ_e : V → D such that ψ_e P -satisfies e' for every e' ∈ E \ {e} , but e is Q \ P -satisfied by ψ_e . We define NRD (P | Q, n) to be the size of the largest non-redundant instance of CSP (P | Q) on n vertices.

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: lem:NRD-triangle
title: Triangle inequality
statement_text: For any predicates P ⊊ Q ⊊ R ⊆ D^r and n ∈ N , we have that NRD (P | R, n) ≤ NRD (P | Q, n) + NRD (Q | R, n). In particular, if R = D^r , we have that NRD (P, n) ≤ NRD (P | Q, n) + NRD (Q, n).

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: def:projection
statement_text: Consider predicates P ⊊ Q ⊆ D_1^ r_1 and R ⊊ S ⊆ D_2^ r_2 . Given a sequence I = (I_1, hdots , I_ r_2 ) of subsets of [r_1] , we say that P | Q is an I -substructure of R | S if there exist maps {g_j : D_1^ I_j → D_2 | j ∈ [r_2]} (called the witnessing maps ) such that the following two conditions are true. ∀ x ∈ P &, (g_1(π_ I_1 x), g_2(π_ I_2 x), hdots , g_ r_2 (π_ I_ r_2 x)) ∈ R, ∀ x ∈ Q \ P &, (g_1(π_ I_1 x), g_2(π_ I_2 x), hdots , g_ r_2 (π_ I_ r_2 x)) ∈ S \ R.

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: prop:projection-compact
statement_text: Consider predicates P ⊊ Q ⊆ D_1^ r_1 and R ⊊ S ⊆ D_2^ r_2 . Given a sequence I = (I_1, hdots , I_ r_2 ) of subsets of [r_1] , we have that that P | Q is an I -substructure of R | S if and only if there exists a map Σ : Q → S subject to the following conditions Σ(P) ⊆ R and Σ(Q \ P) ⊆ S \ R . For all i ∈ [r_1] and j ∈ [r_2] , if i ∉ I_j and x, y ∈ Q differ only in coordinate i , then Σ(x)_j = Σ(y)_j .

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: def:shrink
statement_text: Given an r -partite hypergraph H = (V_1, hdots , V_r, E) , a family of sets I of subsets of [r] , and a parameter λ ≥ 1 , we say that H is (λ, I) -shrinking if for all I ∈ I , we have that |π_I E| ≤ |E| / λ . We say that H is λ -shrinking if H is (λ, I) -shrinking for all I ⊊ [r] .

label: def:projection-hypergraph
statement_text: Given an r -partite hypergraph H = (V_1, hdots , V_r, E) and a family of sets I = (I_1, hdots , I_ ℓ ) of subsets of [r] (possibly with repetition), define the ℓ -partite projection hypergraph pr _ I H = (π_ I_1 E, hdots , π_ I_ ℓ E, pr _ I (E)) , where pr _ I (E) = { pr _ I e := (π_ I_1 e, hdots , π_ I_ ℓ e) | e ∈ E}.

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: lemma:projection-NRD
statement_text: Consider predicates P ⊊ Q ⊆ D_1^ r_1 and R ⊊ S ⊆ D_2^ r_2 . Given a sequence I = (I_1, hdots , I_ r_2 ) of subsets of [r_1] , assume that that P | Q is an I -substructure of R | S with witnessing maps g_1, hdots , g_ r_2 . If H = (V_1, hdots , V_ r_1 , E) is a non-redundant instance of CSP (P | Q) , then pr _ I H = (π_ I_1 E, hdots , π_ I_ r_2 E, pr _ I (E)) is a non-redundant instance of CSP (R | S) .

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: thm:shrink-lb
statement_text: Consider predicates P ⊊ Q ⊆ D_1^ r_1 and R ⊊ S ⊆ D_2^ r_2 . Given a sequence I = (I_1, hdots , I_ r_2 ) of subsets of [r_1] , assume that that P | Q is an I -substructure of R | S . Further let H_1 = (V_1, E_1), H_2 = (V_2, E_2), hdots be an infinite sequence of non-redundant instances of CSP (P | Q) with the following properties. Assume there exists absolute constants C_1, C_2, ε > 0 (with ε < 1 ) such that the following conditions hold for all i ≥ 1 : H_i is (C_1 · |E_i|^ -ε , I) -shrinking, and 1 ≤ |E_ i+1 | / |E_ i | ≤ C_2 . Then, NRD (R | S, n) = Ω(n^ (1)/(1-ε) ), where Ω hides constant factors dependent on |E_1|, C_1, C_2, r_1,r_2, ε.

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances

paper_title: Quantum-Classical Equivalence for AND-Functions

For every assignment α ∈ {0,*}^V , there exists a unique ρ ∈ D such that ρ(x_i) = α(x_i) for all x_i ∈ V . Equivalently, D consists of all restrictions obtained by assigning each variable in V either 0 or * , while fixing all variables outside V as a function of this assignment.

statement_text: The monotone block sensitivity of a Boolean function f : {0,1}^n → {0,1} , denoted MBS (f) , is a variant of block sensitivity that only considers flipping 0’s to 1’s. paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: thm:busy-beaver-transfer
statement_text: For a sound theory S ⊇ S^1_2 , the following are equivalent. There exists a true sentence φ such that, for every constant c > 0 , Scenternot sststile n^c Con _ S + φ (n) . For all sufficiently large k and every constant c > 0 , Scenternot sststile n^c Con _ S^1_2 + φ_ BB (k) (n) .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: conj:kolmogorov-hardness
statement_text: ( Kolmogorov Hardness (KH) ) Let S ⊇ S^1_2 be a sound, finitely axiomatized, sequential theory. For every x ∈ R in the standard model, one has S sststile n^ O(1) Con _ S + (x ∈ R) (n) if and only if EA vdash Con _ S → Con _ S + (x ∈ R) . We expect the hardness direction of KH to extend to sound computably axiomatized ambient theories, whose sufficiently long true randomness facts remain inaccessible by Chaitin incompleteness.

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: theoremHRCImpliesKH
statement_text: HRC implies KH . Moreover, assume HRC , let S ⊇ S^1_2 be a sound, finitely axiomatized, sequential theory, and let x ∈ R hold in the standard model. If EA + Con _ S not vdash x ∈ R , then Scenternot sststile n^ O(1) Con _ S + (x ∈ R) (n) .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: lem:no-access-no-relative-consistency
statement_text: For each fixed string x , if EA + Con _ S not vdash x ∈ R , then EA not vdash Con _ S → Con _ S + (x ∈ R) .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: thm:robustness
statement_text: Let U,U' be universal machines with Kolmogorov invariance constant c=c(U,U') , so that |K_U(x)-K_ U' (x)| ≤ c for every x . Fix d ≥ 3 and write R_U^ (d) :={x:K_U(x) ≥ |x|-d log |x|} . Then, for all sufficiently long x , x ∈ R_U^ (d) Longrightarrow x ∈ R_ U' ^ (d+1) and x ∈ R_ U' ^ (d) Longrightarrow x ∈ R_U^ (d+1) . Consequently, the density estimates and conclusions depending only on those estimates are robust under changing the universal machine, after increasing the logarithmic-deficiency parameter and disregarding finitely many lengths.

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: def:simulation-game
title: Simulation game
statement_text: Let C_ fs be the class of sound, finitely axiomatized sequential theories extending S^1_2 , and let Φ be a family of true sentences. In the game G(Φ) , Nature selects S ∈ C_ fs ; the Theorist, seeing S , selects φ ∈ Φ . Nature wins the round if S sststile n^ O(1) Con _ S + φ (n) , and the Theorist wins if, for every constant c , Scenternot sststile n^c Con _ S + φ (n) . Exactly one player wins each round.

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: def:explanation
title: Explanation and hidden information
statement_text: A position (S,φ) is explained if EA vdash Con _ S → Con _ S + φ ; the EA -proof is the explanation, a certificate any third party can check without reference to the internals of S . Nature holds hidden information at (S,φ) if Nature wins at an unexplained position.

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: prop:explained-wins
title: Explained positions are Nature wins
statement_text: If S is finitely axiomatized and sequential and the position (S,φ) is explained, then Nature wins at (S,φ) , by the canonical strategy: the explanation yields an interpretation of S + φ in S , whose proof translation supplies the required bounded-consistency proofs.

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: prop:random-strategy
title: The random-string strategy
statement_text: Assume HRC , and let the Theorist play true random axioms, Φ = {x ∈ R:x ∈ R\ is true } . Then against every Nature move S , at most finitely many rounds are Nature wins.

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: lem:finite-certified-randomness
statement_text: The set C_ rel ^ S is finite. Hence there is an integer k_R^ S such that, whenever |x| > k_R^ S and x ∈ R is true, one has EA not vdash Con _ S → Con _ S + (x ∈ R) .

label: theoremdensity

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: cor:no-intermediate-density
statement_text: Assume SETH-K-Finite . For every m > k_R^ S and every ε with 0 < ε < 1 , there exists N_ R,m,ε ^ S such that, for every n > N_ R,m,ε ^ S , one has |H_ m,n,ε ^ S | ≥ (1 - O(m^ -d ))2^m .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: cor:dense-small-hard-tautologies
statement_text: Assume SETH-K-Finite , and assume that for some constant a the chosen feasible correspondence between the bounded-consistency formalization and its propositional translation carries every propositional proof of τ_ x,n of size s to an S -proof of Con _ S + (x ∈ R) (n) of size at most s · (m + n)^a . For every m > k_R^ S and every ε with 0 < ε < 1 , there exists N_ R,m,ε ^ S such that, for every n > N_ R,m,ε ^ S , at least (1 - O(m^ -d ))2^m strings x ∈ {0,1}^m index tautologies τ_ x,n of size (m + n)^ O(1) that require size greater than 2^ (1-ε)n in the propositional proof system associated with S .

label: theoremPairwiseRelativeConsistencyImpliesAccess
statement_text: For every pair of strings x,y , if EA vdash Con _ S + (y ∈ R) → Con _ S + (x ∈ R) , then EA + Con _ S + (y ∈ R) vdash x ∈ R .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: corollaryPairwiseFactualNoAccess
statement_text: For every pair of strings x,y , if EA + Con _ S + (y ∈ R) not vdash x ∈ R , then EA not vdash Con _ S + (y ∈ R) → Con _ S + (x ∈ R) .

label: conjectureConditionalFactualNoAccess

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: theoremConditionalNoAccess
statement_text: Assume Conditional Factual No Access . Then, for every m > k_ R, access ^ S and every x,y ∈ {0,1}^m satisfying x mathrel perp _R y , one has EA not vdash Con _ S + (y ∈ R) → Con _ S + (x ∈ R) and EA not vdash Con _ S + (x ∈ R) → Con _ S + (y ∈ R) .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: conjecturePairwiseSETHKFinite

There exists k_ R, hard ^ S such that, for every m > k_ R, hard ^ S and every ε with 0 < ε < 1 , there exists N_ R,m,ε ^ S, pair such that, for every x,y ∈ {0,1}^m satisfying x mathrel perp _R y and every n > N_ R,m,ε ^ S, pair , one has S + (y ∈ R)vdash _ ≤ 2^ (1-ε)n Con _ S + (x ∈ R) (n) Longleftrightarrow EA vdash Con _ S + (y ∈ R) → Con _ S + (x ∈ R) .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: theoremNoMutualHelp
statement_text: Assume Conditional Factual No Access and Pairwise SETH-K-Finite , and let k_ R, pair ^ S := max {k_ R, access ^ S ,k_ R, hard ^ S } . Then, for every m > k_ R, pair ^ S and every ε with 0 < ε < 1 , there exists N_ R,m,ε ^ S, pair such that, for every x,y ∈ {0,1}^m satisfying x mathrel perp _R y and every n > N_ R,m,ε ^ S, pair , one has S + (y ∈ R)nvdash _ ≤ 2^ (1-ε)n Con _ S + (x ∈ R) (n) and S + (x ∈ R)nvdash _ ≤ 2^ (1-ε)n Con _ S + (y ∈ R) (n) .

label: lemmaMutuallyRandomPairsDense

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption

For every sufficiently large m > k_ R, pair ^ S and every ε with 0 < ε < 1 , there exists N_ R,m,ε ^ S, pair such that, for every n > N_ R,m,ε ^ S, pair , at least (1 - O(m^ -d ))2^ 2m ordered pairs (x,y) ∈ {0,1}^m × {0,1}^m satisfy S + (y ∈ R)nvdash _ ≤ 2^ (1-ε)n Con _ S + (x ∈ R) (n) and S + (x ∈ R)nvdash _ ≤ 2^ (1-ε)n Con _ S + (y ∈ R) (n) .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: lem:finite-ph-coding
statement_text: For every i ≥ 1 and every polynomial time bound t , the predicate Q_i^t lies uniformly in Π_ i+1 ^p . Moreover, if Π_i^p = Π_ i+1 ^p , then Q_i^t is decidable by a polynomial-time Turing machine with oracle access to Π_i^p .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: ass:algph
title: SETH-K-PH
statement_text: For every i ≥ 1 , there exists a polynomial time bound t_i such that the canonical finite predicate Q_i^ t_i , whose YES-set is R_i^ t_i , is not decidable by any polynomial-time Turing machine with oracle access to Π_i^p .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: thm:phnoncollapse
statement_text: Assume SETH-K-PH . Then Π_i^p ≠ Π_ i+1 ^p for every i ≥ 1 . Consequently, PH does not collapse.

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: cor:circuit-consequences

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: thm:ph-density
statement_text: Assume SETH-K-PH . For every i ≥ 1 , let t_i be the time bound supplied by the assumption. Then: (Explicitness.) The predicate Q_i^ t_i is an explicit language in Π_ i+1 ^p \ P ^ Π_i^p . In particular, it witnesses Π_i^p ≠ Π_ i+1 ^p . (Density.) Its YES-set R_i^ t_i has density at least 1 - n^ -d inside {0,1}^n . Thus almost every length- n string is a YES-instance. (Sparse-side localization.) Every polynomial-time Π_i^p -oracle machine that is correct on all of R_i^ t_i for all sufficiently large n must err, for infinitely many n , on some string in the sparse complement R_i^ t_i .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: ass:feref
title: Certified Feasible Reflection at Level i
statement_text: For every i ≥ 1 , let T_i := S + Π_i^ true . Let t be a polynomial time bound, and let M be a polynomial-time Turing machine with oracle access to Π_i^p . Suppose that, for a sufficiently long string x ∈ R_i ∩ R_i^t , the theory T_i certifies that M accepts x and that this acceptance is correct for Q_i^t(x) . Then T_i vdash x ∈ R_i .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: ass:level-respecting-certification-bridge
title: Level-Respecting Certification Bridge
statement_text: For every i ≥ 1 , let T_i := S + Π_i^ true . If a polynomial-time Turing machine M with oracle access to Π_i^p correctly decides Q_i^t , then, for every sufficiently long string x ∈ R_i ∩ R_i^t , the theory T_i , rather than T_ i+1 , certifies that M accepts x and that this acceptance is correct for Q_i^t(x) .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: thm:reflection-bridge-implies-seth-k-ph

label: prop:full-versus-certified-random-oracle

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: def:boundary-exposure-main
title: Boundary-exposure predicate
statement_text: For a theory S and a threshold N , let E_ S (x,N) := ∃ m ≤ N ¬ Con _ S + (x ∈ R) (m) . Equivalently, E_ S (x,N) holds if there is a contradiction proof of length at most N from the extension S + (x ∈ R) .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: thm:liu-pass-main
title: Liu--Pass
statement_text: For every polynomial time bound t satisfying t(n) ≥ (1 + δ)n for some constant δ > 0 , one-way functions exist if and only if K^t is mildly hard on average over the uniform distribution: there is a polynomial p such that no probabilistic polynomial-time algorithm computes K^t(x) correctly on more than a 1 - 1/p(n) fraction of strings x ∈ {0,1}^n for all sufficiently large n .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: ass:avg-boundary-reflection-main
title: Average-Case Boundary Reflection
statement_text: There exist a computable polynomial time bound t , a polynomial N(n) , and a polynomial-time samplable ensemble D = {D_n} supported on R_t ∩ {0,1}^n such that both Pr _ x D_n [x ∈ R] and Pr _ x D_n [x ∈ R_t \ R] are bounded away from 0 uniformly in n , and such that the following reflection principle holds: if some probabilistic polynomial-time algorithm decides E_ S (x,N(n)) on x D_n with success probability 1 - o(1) , then for almost every x D_n with x ∈ R , one has EA + Con _ S vdash x ∈ R .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: prop:avg-boundary-hardness-main

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: ass:boundary-calibration-main
title: Boundary Calibration
statement_text: The ensemble D , the threshold N(n) , and the time bound t are chosen so that two conditions hold. First, on D the boundary-exposure predicate E_ S ( · ,N(n)) tracks t -time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity up to a polynomial-time computable reindexing. Second, this correspondence bridges D to the uniform distribution on which Liu--Pass operates: any average-case algorithm computing K^ t over the uniform distribution on {0,1}^n that is strong enough to violate the Liu--Pass hardness condition yields, through the reindexing, a 1 - o(1) -success heuristic for E_ S ( · ,N(n)) on x D_n .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: thm:owf-from-boundary-main
statement_text: Assume Average-Case Boundary Reflection and Boundary Calibration . Then one-way functions exist.

statement_text: There are constants α,ε with 0 < α,ε < 1 such that every Boolean circuit deciding L_ α ^ KT on inputs of length N has size at least 2^ ε N for all sufficiently large N .

statement_text: Consider n, m, t ∈ Z and η, θ ∈ (0,1) such that t^2θ^2m < 1 . paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
title: Two neighbors
statement_text: Let X_2 ⊆ V(G) be the set of vertices having exactly two non-consecutive neighbors on the cycle: A_2 : adjacent to {b, e} , B_2 : adjacent to {a, c} , C_2 : adjacent to {b, d} , D_2 : adjacent to {c, e} , E_2 : adjacent to {d, a} .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
title: Zero neighbor vertices
statement_text: Let X_0 ⊆ V(G) be the set of vertices at distance 2 from V(C) . A_0 is a set of vertices adjacent to A_2 , and similarly we define B_0,C_0,D_0,E_0 . Note that every vertex x of distance two from C is not adjacent to any vertex in A_1 ∪ B_1 ∪ C_1 ∪ D_1 ∪ E_1 , which will be proved later.

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: lem:distance-2

label: X1-X2-dichotomy

statement_text: If none of X_1, X_2, Y_1 is empty, where X_1 and Y_1 are not consecutive (i.e. (X_1,X_2,Y_1)=(A_1,A_2,C_1) then X_2=X^1_2 ∪ X^2_2 so that X^2_2 is complete to X_1 and independent from Y_1 , and X^1_2 is complete to Y_1 and independent from X_1 .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: A1~A2--B2
statement_text: Suppose X_1,X_2 and Y_2 are not empty where X_2 and Y_2 are consecutive. Let X^2_2 be a subset of X_2 with neighbors in X_1 . Then X^2_2 is complete to Y_2 .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: A1!~A2--B1!~B2--C1
statement_text: Suppose X_1, X_2, Y_1, Y_2, Z_1 are non-empty where X_1 and X_2 are independent, Y_1 and Y_2 are independent, and Z_1 is not next to X_1, Y_1 . Then X_2 and Y_2 are independent.

label: B0!~A1
statement_text: Every vertex x of distance two from C is not adjacent to any vertex in A_1 ∪ B_1 ∪ C_1 ∪ D_1 ∪ E_1 .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: 2-disjoint-cycle
statement_text: Let G be a connected (P_6, C_3) -free graph. If G contains two vertex-disjoint induced 5-cycles C^1 and C^2 , then there exists at least one edge with one endpoint in V(C^1) and the other in V(C^2) .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: A1-C2
statement_text: Suppose X_1 and Y_2 are not empty where X_1,Y_1 are not consecutive (i.e. A_1 and C_2 are not empty or A_1 and D_2 are not empty). Then for every two vertices x_1,x'_1 ∈ X_1 , N(x_1) ∩ Y_2 = N(x'_1) ∩ Y_2 .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: A1~C2_2
statement_text: Suppose X_1 and Y_2 are not empty where X_1 and Y_1 are not consecutive (e.g. A_1 and C_2 ). Then Y_2= Y^1_2 ∪ Y^2_2 so that X_1 and Y_2^2 forms a clique and X_1 ∪ Y^1_2 is independent.

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: A1-D2-C2
statement_text: Suppose X_1,Y_2,Z_2 (say A_1,D_2,C_2) are not empty where X_1 is not consecutive with Y_1 and not consecutive with Z_1 ( Y_1,Z_1 consecutive). Then Y_2=Y^2_2 ∪ Y^1_2 , and Z_2=Z^1_2 ∪ Z^2_2 so that : X_1 is complete to Y^2_2 and Z^2_2 . X_1 is independent of Y^1_2 and Z^1_2 . Z^1_2 and Y^2_2 form a complete bipartite graph. Y^1_2 and Z^2_2 form a complete bipartite graph.

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: A0-A2-B2
statement_text: If X_0 , X_2 , and Y_2 ( X_2,Y_2 are consecutive) are not empty then the following hold. For every two vertices a_0,a'_0 ∈ X_0 with a common neighbor in X_2 , N(a_0) ∩ Y_2 = N(a'_0) ∩ Y_2 . For every two vertices a_0,a'_0 ∈ X_0 with a common neighbor in Y_2 , N(a_0) ∩ X_2 = N(a'_0) ∩ X_2 . For every two vertices a_2,a'_2 ∈ X_2 with a common neighbor in X_0 , N(a_2) ∩ Y_2 = N(a'_2) ∩ Y_2 .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: chain-switch
statement_text: Let a_1, a_2 ∈ V_j and b_1, b_2 ∈ V_ j+1 . Suppose that a_1b_1 ∈ E(H) , a_2b_2 ∈ E(H) , and b_1a_2 ∈ E(H) , but a_1b_2 ∉ E(H) (a `Z' shape). Then: N(b_2) ∩ V_ j+2 ⊆ N(b_1) ∩ V_ j+2 , N(a_1) ∩ V_ j-1 ⊆ N(a_2) ∩ V_ j-1 .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs

Then H_j is partitioned into A_1, A_2, A_3 where A_1 and A_2 are connected and contain a_1b_1 and a_2b_2 (respectively), and A_1 and A_2 are independent. A_3 is complete to both A_1 and A_2 . statement_text: Let k ≥ 6 be an integer. There is a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a P_k -free graph G , outputs an OCT, S such that |S| ≤ (k-3) · OPT (G) when k is even and |S| ≤ (k-2) · OPT (G) when k is odd. Here OPT (G) denotes the size of a minimum OCT of G .

label: tm:k-odd-main

title: Ring Partition

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: thm:ring-structure
statement_text: For k ≥ 8 , the graph H forms a ring of k-1 independent sets V_0, V_1, ... , V_ k-2 , where edges exist only between consecutive sets V_j and V_ j+1 (indices modulo k-1 ).

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
statement_text: The OCT problem on G reduces to breaking the odd-length macroscopic ring H . Because k-1 is odd, any valid odd cycle transversal must remove all vertices from at least one partition V_j , or sever the connections between V_j and V_ j+1 . Since V_j and V_ j+1 are independent sets, the subgraph H[V_j ∪ V_ j+1 ] is bipartite. Breaking the ring optimally is equivalent to computing the Minimum Vertex Cover for the bipartite graph H[V_j ∪ V_ j+1 ] for each j ∈ {0, ... , k-2} , and taking the global minimum. This can be computed exactly in polynomial time.

paper_title: Probabilistically Checking Quantum Proofs, with Interaction
title: Main result, informal
statement_text: Every language in QMA has a ( poly , polylog , polylog ) -qIOP. In addition, the qIOP has completeness exponentially close to 1 and the honest prover is efficient, i.e.\ it can be executed in quantum polynomial time provided it is initially given access to the right quantum witness.

paper_title: Probabilistically Checking Quantum Proofs, with Interaction
label: def:ltc
title: Classical locally testable codes
statement_text: Let C = ker (H) be a classical code, where H ∈ F _2^ m × n is a parity-check matrix. We say that C is locally testable with soundness ρ if for all x ∈ F _2^n , it holds that (1)/(m) |Hx| ≥ ρ (d_H(x, C))/(n) , where |x| denotes the Hamming weight (number of nonzero coordinates) of x and d_H(x, C) denotes the Hamming distance between x and the code C .

paper_title: Probabilistically Checking Quantum Proofs, with Interaction
label: def:local-tester
title: Local tester for a classical LTC
statement_text: Let c ∈ Z _+ . Let C = ker (H) be a classical locally testable code, where H ∈ F _2^ m × n is a parity-check matrix. Define the local tester T for the code C as the following procedure: Given input w ∈ F _2^n , Randomly sample i_1, ... , i_c ∈ _R [m] , Compute r = H_ i_1 vdots H_ i_c · w ∈ F _2^c, Reject if vee_ j ∈ [c] r_j = 1 (i.e., any parity constraint is violated).

paper_title: Probabilistically Checking Quantum Proofs, with Interaction
label: lem:ltc_amp
statement_text: Let C = ker (H) be a locally testable code with soundness ρ , where each row of H has weight at most R . Let κ > ρ . Then, there exists a code tester for C with query complexity Q such that for all x ∈ F _2^n , Pr [ verifier rejects x] ≥ 1 - (1 - ρ · (d_H(x, C))/(n) )^ Q/R . title: CSS Code
statement_text: An [n, k, d] quantum CSS code on n qubits is a subspace C ⊆ H = ( C ^2)^ ⊗ n . It is defined by a pair of parity-check matrices H_X, H_Z such that Im (H_X^top ) perp Im (H_Z^top ) . paper_title: Probabilistically Checking Quantum Proofs, with Interaction
title: PCPs of Proximity (PCPPs),
statement_text: Let s, δ: Z ^+ → [0, 1] be functions. A verifier V is said to be a probabilistically checkable proof of proximity (PCPP) system for a pair language L with proximity parameter δ and soundness error s if, for every pair of strings (x, y) , the following conditions hold: Completeness: If (x, y) ∈ L , then there exists a proof string π such that V(x) accepts the oracle y ∘ π with probability 1 . Soundness: If y is δ(|x|) -far from L(x) , then for every π , the verifier V(x) accepts the oracle y ∘ π with probability strictly less than s(|x|) . If s and δ are not explicitly specified, they are assumed to be constants in the interval (0, 1) .

paper_title: Probabilistically Checking Quantum Proofs, with Interaction
label: def:qiop
title: Quantum interactive probabilistically checkable proof system
statement_text: Let n ∈ Z _+ denote the instance size, and let m : Z _+ → Z _+ be a non-decreasing, even-valued function representing the total number of messages as a function of the instance size. Define h(n) := m(n)/2 . An m -message quantum interactive probabilistically checkable proof system (qIPCP) is specified by a tuple of quantum algorithms V = ( V _1, V _2, ... , V _ h+1 ) . For each i ∈ [h+1] , the verifier’s algorithm V _i takes x as input and acts on registers as follows: (( R _ i-1 ), ( R _1, ... , R _ i-2 , W _i, ... , W _h) ) longrightarrow (( W _i, J _i), ( R _1, ... , R _ i-1 , W _ i+1 , ... , W _h) ), where R _i is the quantum prover’s message register, for each i ∈ {-1, 0, ... , h} , W _i is the quantum witness register, for each i ∈ {1, ... , h+1} , J _i is the verifier’s classical message register, for each i ∈ {1, ... , h+1} . R _ -1 , R _0 , and W _ h+1 are all empty registers. The register J is initialized to the all-zero classical string. The register W =( W _i)_ i ∈ [h] is initialized to a quantum witness for the input x . Each verifier algorithm V _i must be implementable in polynomial time. Let I = {1, ... , h} . A prover strategy is defined by a collection of quantum channels { P _i}_ i ∈ I (possibly depending on x ) and a private quantum register P initialized with an quantum state, where each P _i acts as: (( W _i, J _i), P ) longrightarrow ( R _i, P ). The first (classical) bit of the register J _ h+1 in the output of V _ h+1 represents the verifier’s final decision to accept or reject. Let ω( V , ket φ ) denote the value of the interactive game defined by V _x when the initial state of the entire system is ket φ . That is, ω( V , ket φ ) is the maximum acceptance probability of V over all prover strategies { P _i}_ i ∈ I , where ket φ is defined on the joint quantum register WP . paragraph Resource bounds. We define the resource complexity of the system as follows: Communication complexity: The verifier V has communication complexity l : Z _+ → Z _+ if l(n) ≥ Σ _ i ∈ [h(n)] l_i(n), where l_i(n) is the total size (in qubits) of the registers R _i, J _i, W _i . Query complexity: The verifier V has query complexity q : Z _+ → Z _+ if q(n) ≥ Σ _ i ∈ [h(n)+1] q_i(n), where q_i(n) is the number of qubits accessed by V _i in the registers ( R _1, ... , R _ i-1 , W _i, ... , W _h) .

title: Quantum interactive probabilistically checkable proof systems for a promise problem
statement_text: A quantum interactive probabilistically checkable proof system for a promise problem (S_ yes , S_ no ) satisfies the following: Let ω( V , ket φ _ WP ) be defined as in Definition . The system must satisfy: Completeness: There exists a constant c ∈ (0,1] such that for all x ∈ S_ yes , the maximum acceptance probability satisfies max _ ket ψ ω( V , ket ψ _ W ket 0 _ P ) ≥ c . That is, there exists a quantum witness ket ψ and an honest prover strategy under which the verifier accepts with probability at least c . Soundness: There exists a constant s ∈ [0, c) such that for all x ∈ S_ no , the maximum acceptance probability satisfies max _ ket φ ω( V , ket φ _ WP ) ≤ s . That is, no combination of prover strategy, prover's initial state, and jointly entangled quantum witness can cause the verifier to accept a no-instance with probability greater than s .

Moreover, we say that the protocol is succinct if there exists a fixed polynomial p(λ) such that, for any ε = 1/ poly (λ) , the total communication is bounded by p(λ,1/ε) and V 's run-time is bounded by |Q| · p(λ,1/ε) .

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
label: def:commitment
title: Commitment.
statement_text: A (two-message) commitment scheme with message space cM , randomness space cR , commitment space COM , and a public parameter space PP consists of two classical PPT algorithms ( Setup , Com ) : The setup algorithm takes the security parameter 1^λ as input and outputs a public parameter pp ∈ PP . The committing algorithm takes a public parameter pp ∈ PP and a message m ∈ M as input and outputs a commitment com ∈ COM . We say that a commitment scheme is non-interactive if a public parameter pp generated by Setup (1^λ) is always just the security parameter 1^λ . For such a scheme, we omit to write Setup . We define the following security notions for a commitment scheme. paragraph Statistical/Computational Hiding. For an adversary cA , we consider an experiment Exp _ cA ^ hiding (1^λ) defined below: cA is given the security parameter 1^λ and sends a (possibly malformed) public parameter pp ∈ PP and (m_0,m_1) ∈ M ^2 to the challenger The challenger randomly picks bgets {0,1} , computes com gets Com ( pp ,m_b) , and sends com to cA . cA is given a commitment com and outputs b' ∈ {0,1} . The experiment outputs 1 if b=b' and 0 otherwise. We say that a commitment scheme satisfies statistical (resp. computational) hiding if for any unbounded-time (resp. non-uniform QPT) adversary cA , we have |Pr [1gets Exp _ cA ^ hiding (1^λ)]-1/2|= negl (λ). paragraph Binding. Computational Binding. We say that a non-interactive commitment scheme satisfies statistical (resp. computational) binding if for any non-uniform QPT adversary cA , we have Pr [ Com ( pp ,m;r)= Com ( pp ,m';r') ∧ m ≠ m' : pp gets Setup (1^λ),(m,m',r,r')gets cA ( pp )]= negl (λ). Pr [ ll & Com ( pp ,m;r)= Com ( pp ,m';r') & ∧ m ≠ m' : ll & pp gets Setup (1^λ), &(m,m',r,r')gets cA ( pp ) ]= negl (λ). We say that a scheme satisfies perfect binding if the above probability is 0 for all unbounded-time adversary cA . Collapse-Binding. For an adversary cA , we define an experiment Exp _ cA ^ clbinding (1^λ) as follows: The challenger generates pp gets Setup (1^λ) . cA is given the public parameter pp as input and generates a commitment com ∈ COM and a quantum state σ over registers ( M , R , A ) where M stores an element of M , R stores an element of cR , and A is cA 's internal register. Then it sends com and registers ( M , R ) to the challenger, and keeps A on its side. The challenger picks bgets {0,1} If b=0 , the challenger does nothing and if b=1 , the challenger measures registers ( M , R ) in the computational basis. The challenger returns registers ( M , R ) to cA cA outputs a bit b' . The experiment outputs 1 if b'=b and 0 otherwise. We say that cA is a valid adversary if we we have Pr [ Com ( pp ,m;r)= com : pp gets Setup (1^λ),( com ,σ)gets cA ( pp ),(m,r) arrow M_ M , R ∘ σ]=1. We say that a commitment is strongly collapse-binding if for any non-uniform QPT valid adversary cA , we have |Pr [1gets Exp _ cA ^ clbinding (1^λ)]-1/2|= negl (λ).

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
label: def:crh
title: Collision Resistance
statement_text: H is post-quantum collision resistant if for every QPT adversary cA , Pr [ c x ≠ x' ∧ h(x) = h(x') middle vert r h gets H_ λ (x,x') gets cA (h) ] = negl (λ).

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
label: def:collapsing
title: Collapsing
statement_text: H is collapsing if for every QPT adversary cA , | Pr [ HCollasingExp (0,λ,cA ) = 1] - Pr [ HCollasingExp (1,λ,cA ) = 1] | ≤ negl (λ). For b ∈ {0,1} the experiment HCollasingExp (b,λ,cA ) is defined as follows: The challenger samples h gets H_ λ and sends h to cA . cA replies with a (classical) binary string y ∈ {0,1}^ ℓ (λ) and a λ -qubit quantum state on register cX . (The requirement that y is classical can be enforced by having the challenger immediately measure these registers upon receiving them.) The challenger computes h in superposition on the λ -qubit quantum state, and measures the bit indicating whether the output of h equals y . If h does not equal y , the challenger aborts and outputs bot . If b = 0 , the challenger does nothing. If b = 1 , the challenger measures the λ -qubit state in the standard basis. The challenger returns contents of the registers cX to cA . cA outputs a bit b' , which is the output of the experiment.

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
label: claim:collapsing-crhf
statement_text: If H is collapsing then H is post-quantum collision resistant.

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
label: def:AoK
title: State-Preserving AoKs for NP
statement_text: A state-preserving argument of knowledge (AoK) for NP is an interaction between a QPT prover and PPT verifier on input an instance x {top ,bot } gets ⟨ P(1^λ,x),V(1^λ,x) ⟩ , where {top ,bot } is the verifier's output. For any language cL in NP, the following properties hold. Succinctness. When invoked on a security parameter λ and instance size n and a relation decidable in time T , the communication complexity of the protocol is poly (λ, log T ) . The verifier computational complexity is poly (λ, log T ) + Tilde O (n) . Extraction. There exists an extractor Ext (x, ε) with running in time poly (n, λ, 1/ε) outputting a classical transcript τ and a classical string w , such that the following holds. For any ε = 1/ poly (λ) , any QPT adversarial prover cA = {cA _λ}_ λ ∈ N , any QPT distinguisher cD = {cD _λ}_ λ ∈ N , and any advice state ρ_ A,E = {ρ_ λ,A,E }_ λ ∈ N , consider the following games. ExpREAL [cA ,ρ] Run ⟨ cA (A, x),V(1^λ,x) ⟩ and let τ be the classical transcript and A the residual state on the input register. Output (τ,A,E) . ExpIDEAL [ Ext ,ε,ρ] Run (τ, w, A) gets Ext (x, ε)^ A (A,x) . Output (τ,A,E) . Then, g| Pr [cD ( ExpREAL [cA ,ρ]) = 1] - Pr [cD ( ExpIDEAL [ Ext ,ε,ρ]) = 1] g| ≤ ε. Furthermore, the probability that τ is an accepting transcript but w is not a witness for x is bounded by ε + negl (λ) .

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
statement_text: OSP implies classical verification of quantum computation.

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
label: def:OSP
title: Oblivious State Preparation
statement_text: Oblivious state preparation (OSP) is a protocol that takes place between a PPT sender S with input b ∈ {0,1} and a QPT receiver R : (s, ⟩ * ψ ) gets OSP ⟨ S(1^λ,b),R(1^λ) ⟩ , where s ∈ {0,1} is the sender's output and ⟩ * ψ is the receiver's output. It should satisfy the following properties. Correctness. For any b ∈ {0,1} , let Π_b coloneqq Σ _ s ∈ {0,1} ketbra * s ⊗ H^bketbra * s H^b. Then for any b ∈ {0,1} , E [|Π_b ⟩ * s ⟩ * ψ | : (s, ⟩ * ψ ) gets OSP ⟨ S(1^λ,b),R(1^λ) ⟩ ] = 1- negl (λ). Security. For any QPT adversary {cA _λ}_ λ ∈ N , |&Pr [b_cA = 0 : (s,b_cA ) gets OSP ⟨ S(1^λ,0),cA _λ ⟩ ] &- Pr [b_cA = 0 : (s,b_cA ) gets OSP ⟨ S(1^λ,1),cA _λ ⟩ ] | = negl (λ).

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
label: def:RSPV
title: Verifiable State Preparation
statement_text: Verifiable state preparation (VSP) for a state family { ⟩ ψ_i }_ i ∈ [K] is a protocol that takes place between a PPT sender S and a QPT receiver R : (i, ⟩ * ψ_i ) gets VSP ⟨ S(1^λ,ε),R(1^λ,ε) ⟩ , where ε is an error parameter, i ∈ [K] ∪ {bot } is the sender's output, and ⟩ * ψ_i is the receiver's output. It should satisfy the following properties. Correctness. For any ε = 1/ poly (λ) , TD ( VSP ⟨ S(1^λ,ε),R(1^λ,ε) ⟩ ,(1)/(K) Σ _ i ∈ [K] ketbra i ⊗ ketbra ψ_i ) = negl (λ). Security. For any ε = 1/ poly (λ) , any QPT adversarial receiver cA = {cA _λ}_ λ ∈ N , and any advice state ρ_ A,E = {ρ_ λ,A,E }_ λ ∈ N , there exists a QPT simulator Sim = { Sim _λ}_ λ ∈ N such that for any QPT distinguisher cD = {cD _λ}_ λ ∈ N , the following holds. Define the following games. ExpREAL [cA ,ε,ρ] Run (i,A) gets VSP ⟨ S(1^λ,ε),cA (A) ⟩ . Output (i,A,E) . ExpIDEAL [ Sim ,ε,ρ] Run (b,A) gets Sim (1^λ,ε,A) . If b = 1 , sample i gets [K] , otherwise if b = 0 , set i = bot and ⟩ ψ_i = 0 . Run A gets Sim (1^λ,ε,A, ⟩ ψ_i ) . Output (i,A,E) . Then, g| Pr [cD ( ExpREAL [cA ,ε,ρ]) = 1] - Pr [cD ( ExpIDEAL [ Sim ,ε,ρ]) = 1] g| ≤ ε.

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
label: thm:claw-state-RSP
title: VSP for Claw States
statement_text: Assuming OSP, there exists VSP for the ``claw state'' family {frac 1 sqrt 2 ( ⟩ 0,x_0 + ⟩ 1,x_1 ) }_ x_0,x_1 ∈ {0,1}^ m(λ) for any polynomial m(λ) .

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
label: lemma:OSP-VSP
statement_text: Assuming OSP, there exists VSP for the ``BB84 state'' family {H^θ ⟩ x }_ x,θ ∈ {0,1}^ n(λ) for any polynomial n(λ) .

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
label: lemma:CHSH
statement_text: Let X be a classical register, Z be an arbitrary-size quantum register, and B be a single-qubit register. Let ρ^ (0) _ Z,B,X , ρ^ (1) _ Z,B,X be any two states such that Tr _X (ρ^ (0) ) ≈ _c Tr _X (ρ^ (1) ) and (1)/(4)Tr (Π^ (0,0) _ B,X ρ^ (0) ) + (1)/(4)Tr (Π^ (0,1) _ B,X ρ^ (0) ) + (1)/(4)Tr (Π^ (1,0) _ B,X ρ^ (1) ) + (1)/(4)Tr (Π^ (1,1) _ B,X ρ^ (1) ) ≥ cos ^2(π/8) - δ. Then, there exists σ_Z such that ((1)/(2)ρ^ (0) ⊗ ketbra 0 _T + (1)/(2)ρ^ (1) ⊗ ketbra 1 _T ) ≈ _ c, poly (δ) σ_Z ⊗ (1)/(4) Σ _ x,θ ∈ {0,1} (H^θketbra x H^θ )_B ⊗ ketbra x _X ⊗ ketbra θ _T .

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
statement_text: For any polynomial m(λ) , there exists a polynomial n(λ) such that the following holds. Assuming VSP for the BB84 state family {H^θ ⟩ x }_ x,θ ∈ {0,1}^ n(λ) , there exists VSP for the claw state family {frac 1 sqrt 2 ( ⟩ 0,x_0 + ⟩ 1,x_1 ) }_ x_0,x_1 ∈ {0,1}^ m(λ) .

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
title: Projective measurements
statement_text: Pure basis measurements. In the Pauli braiding test (Protocol ), and also in the b=0 case of the mixed versus pure basis test (Protocol ), Bob is asked a single-bit question corresponding to a basis ( X or Z ). For each basis W ∈ {X,Z} , we notate Bob's projective measurement after receiving question W as a set of projectors {P^ W _u}_ u with outcomes u ∈ {0,1}^n . Mixed basis measurements. In the mixed versus pure basis test (Protocol ), Bob receives a question w ∈ {\1, X, Z}^n corresponding to n Pauli bases (one for each of n qubits). For each Pauli string w ∈ {\1, X,Z}^n , we notate Bob's projective measurement after receiving question w as a set of projectors {M^ w _u}_ u ∈ {0,1}^n . We can assume without loss of generality that Bob always answers ``0'' on indices where he was asked to measure the identity, i.e. formally we can assume that M^w_u = 0 if there exists an index i ∈ [n] for which w_i = \1 but u_i = 1 . The reason that this assumption is without loss of generality is that we can always replace Bob's measurements by a post-processed version that has this property; since the verifier ignores all indices for which w_i = \1 , this post-processing affects neither Bob's success probability nor any of the rigidity statements we show below.

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
title: Pure basis observables
statement_text: For W ∈ {X, Z} and a ∈ {0,1}^n , define the binary observable W(a) := Σ _ u (-1)^ u · a P^W_u.

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
title: Mixed basis observables
statement_text: For w ∈ {\1, X,Z}^n and a ∈ {0,1}^n , define the binary observables O^w(a) &= Σ _ u ∈ {0,1}^n (-1)^ a · u M^w_u , O^w_W(a) &= Σ _ u ∈ {0,1}^n (-1)^ 1_ w = W ∧ a = 1 · u M^w_u . We also write O^w = O^w(1) and O^w_W = O^w_W(1) .

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
label: def:state_dep_inner_product
title: State-dependent inner product and norm
statement_text: Let H be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space and A, B ∈ L( H ) be linear operators on H . Let ψ ∈ Pos ( H ) . We define the state-dependent (semi) inner product of A and B w.r.t ψ as ⟨ A, B ⟩ _ψ = Tr [ A^ † B ψ ] . This induces the state-dependent (semi) norm norm A _ψ^2 = ⟨ A, A ⟩ _ψ = Tr [ A^ † A ψ ] .

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
label: lem:state_dep_norm_props
title: Basic properties of the state dependent norm
statement_text: For all (not necessarily normalised) states ψ, ψ' ∈ Pos ( H ) and linear operators A, B ∈ L( H ) on some finite-dimensional Hilbert space H : norm A _ B ψ B^ † = norm AB _ ψ . norm A B _ ψ ≤ norm A _ ∞ norm B _ ψ , where Vert A Vert _ ∞ : = sup _ Vert v Vert = 1 Vert Av Vert For any unitary U , norm UA _ψ = norm A _ψ . Linearity of the squared norm in the state: norm A _ ψ + ψ' ^2 = norm A _ ψ ^2 + norm A _ ψ' ^2 . Triangle inequality for the squared norm: norm A+B _ψ^2 ≤ 2 norm A _ψ^2 + 2 norm B _ψ^2 .

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
label: lem:state_replace
title: Lemma 2.9 in
statement_text: For an observable A on H and two states ψ, ψ' on H with norm ψ - ψ' _1 ≤ ε , we have that norm A _ ψ ^2 ≈ _ norm A _ ∞ ^2 ε norm A _ ψ' ^2 .

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
label: def:hamiltonian-problem
title: Hamiltonian problem
statement_text: We refer to a tuple of the form (H, α, β) , where H is a Hermitian operator and α and β are both real numbers, as a Hamiltonian problem . We may refer to such a tuple where H acts on n qubits as an n -qubit Hamiltonian problem.

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
title: Deciding a Hamiltonian problem
statement_text: Given a tuple of the form (H, α, β) , where H is a Hermitian operator and α and β are both real numbers, we refer to the problem of deciding whether the ground energy of H is ≤ α (yes case) or ≥ β (no case) as the problem of deciding (H, α, β) .

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
title: Family of Hamiltonians
statement_text: We will use the notation H = { H (n)}_ n ∈ N to refer to a family of Hamiltonians, i.e., a collection of sets H (n) (one for every value of n ∈ N ) such that the n th set H (n) contains only n -qubit Hamiltonian problems. We assume that the length of the binary description of (H, α, β) for any (H, α, β) ∈ H (n) is poly (n) .

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
title: QMA-completeness of a family of Hamiltonians
statement_text: We say a family of Hamiltonians H = { H (n)}_ n ∈ N is QMA-complete if, for every promise problem cL = (cL _ yes , cL _ no ) in QMA , and every instance x ∈ {0,1}^* , the problem of deciding whether x ∈ cL _ yes or x ∈ cL _ no can be Karp reduced in polynomial time (in |x| , given as input x and also the algorithm C which characterizes the verifier for cL ) to the problem of deciding some element of H (n) for n = poly (|x|) .

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
label: thm:qma-to-hamiltonian
title: Lemma 6.18
statement_text: Let C be a QMA verification algorithm for a QMA promise problem cL = (cL _ yes , cL _ no ) , and let x be an input of length n . Then there is a Hamiltonian problem (H, α(n), β(n)) that can be efficiently computed from the input (x, C) , such that if x ∈ cL _ yes , then H is a YES instance of the Hamiltonian problem, and if x ∈ cL _ no , then H is a NO instance, and β(n) - α(n) = 1 - negl (n) . Moreover, H has the following form: H = \1 - underset w D E Σ _ a ∈ T(w) π^w_a, where D is a distribution over {\1,X,Z}^ poly (n) which can be efficiently sampled, and T(w) ⊆ {0,1}^ poly (n) is a set for which membership can be decided in time polynomial in n .

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
label: def:blind-computation
title: Blind Classical Delegation of Quantum Computation
statement_text: Let H _V, H _W be Hilbert spaces of arbitrary dimension, and let Q: {0,1}^* × H _V → H _W be a polynomial-size quantum circuit that takes as input a classical string x and a state on register V , and outputs a state on register W . A protocol for blind classical delegation of quantum computation consists of an interaction (W,(r,s)) gets ⟨ S(1^λ,Q,V),C(1^λ,Q,x) ⟩ between a QPT server S(1^λ,Q,V) with input the security parameter 1^λ , circuit Q , and state on register V , and a PPT client C(1^λ,Q,x) with input the security parameter 1^λ , circuit Q , and classical string x . At the end of the interaction, the server outputs a state on register W and the client outputs classical strings (r,s) . The protocol must satisfy the following properties. Correctness. For any circuit Q and input x , let IDEAL [Q,x] be the map from V → W defined by Q(x, · ) , and let REAL [Q,x]_λ be the map from V → W induced by running the protocol (W,(r,s)) gets ⟨ S(1^λ,Q,V),C(1^λ,Q,x) ⟩ and then applying X^r Z^s to W . Then for any Q and x , D_diamond ( REAL [Q,x]_λ, IDEAL [Q,x] ) = negl (λ). Security. For any circuit Q , QPT adversary { A _λ}_ λ ∈ N , and two strings x_0,x_1 , it holds that & g| Pr [b_ A = 0 : (b_ A ,(r,s)) gets ⟨ A _λ,C(1^λ,Q,x_0) ⟩ ] &-Pr [b_ A = 0 : (b_ A ,(r,s)) gets ⟨ A _λ,C(1^λ,Q,x_1) ⟩ ] g| = negl (λ), where b_ A denotes a single bit output by A _λ after the interaction (which could result from an arbitrary QPT operation applied to its state after the interaction).

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
label: thm:osp_imply_blind
statement_text: OSP ( ) implies blind classical delegation of quantum computation ( ).

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
label: claim:blind_depend_depth
statement_text: The round complexity of the blind classical delegation of quantum computation protocol from is poly (D, λ) , where D is the depth of the quantum circuit Q (in fact, the T -depth) and λ is the security parameter.

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
title: Nonlocal game
statement_text: A nonlocal game G = (Q,V) is specified by a distribution Q over pairs (x,y) ∈ {0,1}^ n_1 × {0,1}^ n_2 and a verification predicate V(x,y,a,b) ∈ {0,1} , where a ∈ {0,1}^ m_1 and b ∈ {0,1}^ m_2 . A family of nonlocal games G ( = ) { G ( _ )λ}_ λ ∈ N is a set of games parameterized by λ , where each G ( _ )λ is itself a set of games G ∈ G ( _ )λ . Each game G ∈ G ( ) is defined by a distribution Q_G over pairs (x,y) ∈ {0,1}^ n_ 1,G × {0,1}^ n_ 2,G and a verification predicate V_G(x,y,a,b) ∈ {0,1} , where a ∈ {0,1}^ m_ 1,G and b ∈ {0,1}^ m_ 2,G . For any game G ∈ G ( ), we define λ_G to be the choice of λ such that G ∈ G ( _ )λ . We say that the family of games is efficient if there exists a polynomial p( · ) and a procedure that, for any G ∈ G ( ), samples from Q_G and computes V_G in time p(λ_G) .

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
label: def:nonlocal_strategy
title: Non-local Strategy
statement_text: A nonlocal strategy S for game G consists of the following. A state ⟩ ψ ∈ H _cA ⊗ H _cB . For every x ∈ {0,1}^ n_1 , a projective measurement {A_a^x}_ a acting on H _A with outcomes a ∈ {0,1}^ m_1 . For every y ∈ {0,1}^ n_2 , a projective measurement {B_b^y}_ b acting on H _B with outcomes b ∈ {0,1}^ m_2 . The value of this strategy is given by ω(G, S ) coloneqq E _ (x,y) gets Q Σ _ a,b V(x,y,a,b) ⟨ ψ A_a^x ⊗ B_b^y ⟩ ψ . A strategy S for a family of games G ( ) consists of a strategy S _G = ( ⟩ ψ_G ,{A^x_ a,G }_a,{B^y_ b,G }_b ) for each G ∈ G ( ). We say that S is efficient if ⟩ ψ is QPT-preparable and {A_ a,G ^x}_a and {B_ b,G ^y}_b are QPT-implementable.

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
label: def:generalized_KLVY-compiler
title: Generalized KLVY Compiler
statement_text: Let G ( ) be a family of nonlocal games, let Π = ⟨ S,C ⟩ be a blind classical delegation of quantum computation protocol, and let S be an efficient nonlocal strategy for G ( ). For each G ∈ G ( ), let A_G : {0,1}^ n_ 1,G × H _ cA → {0,1}^ m_ 1,G be the QPT circuit that performs the Alice measurement of S _G and B_G : {0,1}^ n_ 2,G × H _ cB → {0,1}^ m_ 2,G be the QPT circuit that performs the Bob measurement of S _G . The KLVY-compiled protocol KLVY [ G ( , )Π, S ] is an interaction between a QPT prover Prove and a PPT verifier Verify that is parameterized by a game G ∈ G ( _ )λ ⊂ G ( ), and operates as follows. The verifier samples (x,y) gets Q_G . Let ⟩ ψ_G ∈ H _ cA ⊗ H _ cB be the initial state used in S _G . The prover and verifier engage in a blind classical delegation of quantum computation protocol (with classical output, see ) a gets ⟨ S(1^λ,A_G, ⟩ ψ_G ), C(1^λ,A_G,x) ⟩ , with the prover playing the role of the server S and the verifier playing the role of the client C . The verifier sends y to the prover. The prover runs b gets B_G(y,cB ) and sends b to the verifier. The verifier outputs V_G(x,y,a,b) . This interaction is denoted b_ Verify gets ⟨ Prove (1^λ,G), Verify (1^λ,G) ⟩ , where b_ Verify denotes the bit output by Verify . The completeness of KLVY [ G ( , )Π, S ] is defined by a function c(G) coloneqq Pr [b_ Verify = 1 : b_ Verify gets ⟨ Prove (1^λ,G), Verify (1^λ,G) ⟩ ], and KLVY [ G ( , )Π, S ] has soundness s(G) if for any QPT adversary { A _λ}_ λ ∈ N Pr [b_ Verify = 1 : b_ Verify gets ⟨ A _ λ_G (1^λ,G), Verify (1^λ,G) ⟩ ] ≤ s(G).

paper_title: A Modular Approach to Succinct Arguments for QMA
label: def:comp-non-local
title: Computationally nonlocal strategy
statement_text: A computationally nonlocal strategy C for a family of games G ( = ) { G ( _ )λ}_λ consists of the following for each G ∈ G ( ). A QPT-preparable state ⟩ ψ_G ∈ H _ cA ,G ⊗ H _ cB ,G . For every x ∈ {0,1}^ n_ 1,G , a QPT-implementable unitary U^x_G acting on H _ cA ,G ⊗ H _ cB ,G . For each a ∈ {0,1}^ m_ 1,G , define A^x_ a,G coloneqq ketbra a a U^x_G, where the projection ketbra a a is applied to some specified sub-register of H _ cA ,G .
