label: lem:multigraph-to-simple
title: Simple-Graph Transformation
statement_text: Let I=(G,χ,b) be a loopless instance with |V| ≥ 2 and b ≤ p . In polynomial time, one can construct an instance on a simple edge-labeled graph I^sharp =(G^sharp ,χ^sharp ,b) such that I is a Yes -instance Longleftrightarrow I^sharp is a Yes -instance . Moreover, OPT (G^sharp ,χ^sharp )= OPT (G,χ).

paper_title: An Exponent-Tight Conditional Lower Bound for Global Label Min-Cut
label: cor:simple-graph-hardness
title: Conditional Lower Bound for Simple Graphs
statement_text: Suppose that a hard family of multigraph instances satisfies m ≤ (np)^ O(1) and p ≤ n^ O(1) . If Global Label Min-Cut on edge-labeled simple graphs admitted a deterministic algorithm with running time (np)^ o( log n) poly (|E|), then this would yield an algorithm in the same asymptotic running-time class on the original multigraph family.

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
title: OVH
statement_text: For every δ>0 there is a constant c=c(δ) such that any algorithm that, given two sets of n Boolean vectors in dimension c log n , determines whether there is a pair of orthogonal vectors cannot run in time O(n^ 2-δ ) .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: thm:main-intro
title: Informal
statement_text: Under OVH or SETH, Furthest Pair, Bichromatic Closest Pair, Maximum Inner Product, and Hopcroft’s problem (also known as Z -OV) require n^ 2-o(1) time for any efficiently constructible dimension d = ω(1) .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:constructible
title: Constructible dimension function
statement_text: A function D:Z_ ≥ 1 → Z_ ≥ 1 is constructible if D(n) can be computed exactly in n^ o(1) time.

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: thm:prime-number
title: Prime Number Theorem
statement_text: Let π(n) denote the number of primes ≤ n . Then, lim _ n → ∞ (π(n))/(n/ log n) = 1 .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: thm:chinese-remainder
title: Chinese Remainder Theorem
statement_text: Given d pairwise co-prime integers q_1,q_2, ... ,q_d , and d integers r_1,r_2, ... ,r_d , there is exactly one integer 0 ≤ t < Π _ i = 1 ^ d q_i such that t ≡ r_i pmod q_i for all i ∈ [d] . We call this the Chinese remainder representation (or the CRR encoding) of the r_i ’s (with respect to these q_i ’s). We also denote t = CRR ({ r_i }; { q_i }) for convenience. We sometimes omit the sequence { q_i } for simplicity, when it is clear from the context. Moreover, t can be computed in polynomial time with respect to the total bits of all the given integers.

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: lem:nonuiform-local-lean
statement_text: There exist absolute constants K_0, L_0, w_0 such that for all integers b ≥ 1 and L ≥ L_0 , there exist functions α, β: { 0, 1 }^ b → Z_ ≥ 0 ^ w_0 and V ⊆ Z_ ≥ 0 satisfying the following properties. Let B = lceil L^ K_0 b sqrt L rceil . Then: (Entry Bound) For all a ∈ { 0, 1 }^ b and k ∈ [w_0] , α(a)_ k , β(a)_ k < B and for all v ∈ V , v ≤ B . Also, |V| ≤ B . (Product Bound) For all x, y ∈ { 0, 1 }^ bL , let x_i, y_i denote the i -th block of size b in x, y respectively. Then Σ _ i = 1 ^ L α(x_i) · β(y_i) ≤ B (Correctness) For all x, y ∈ { 0, 1 }^ bL and x_i, y_i as above, x · y = 0 Longleftrightarrow Σ _ i = 1 ^ L α(x_i) · β(y_i) ∈ V .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:number-field
title: Number field
statement_text: A number field is a finite-dimensional field extension K/Q . Its degree, denoted [K:Q] , is the dimension of K as a vector space over Q .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
title: Real embedding
statement_text: An embedding of K/Q into C is a homomorphism σ: K hookrightarrow C that fixes Q . An embedding is real if its image is contained in the real numbers: σ(K) ⊆ R and complex otherwise.

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
title: Totally real and totally imaginary field
statement_text: A number field K is totally real if every embedding σ:K hookrightarrowC is real. A number field K is totally imaginary if every embedding σ:K hookrightarrowC is complex.

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
title: Infinite Place
statement_text: An infinite place of K/Q into C is an equivalence class of embeddings σ:KhookrightarrowC , where two embeddings σ and τ are equivalent if τ=σ or τ= σ . An infinite place is real if σ(K) ⊆ R for one (equivalently every) representative embedding σ and complex otherwise.

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: lem:num-embeddings-ub
statement_text: Let K/Q be a finite extension of degree [K:Q] . Then, there are exactly [K:Q] embeddings of K into C .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:cm-field
title: CM field ( )
statement_text: A CM field is a totally imaginary quadratic extension K/L of a totally real field. The nontrivial automorphism of K/L , also known as the complex conjugation automorphism, is denoted c . If K = L(i) with L totally real, then for every complex embedding σ: K hookrightarrow C , σ(c(α)) = σ(α) .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
title: Ring of integers
statement_text: Let K be a number field. Its ring of integers is O_K = { x ∈ K : x satisfies a monic polynomial with coefficients in Z }.

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
title: Ideal
statement_text: Given a ring R , a subset I ⊆ R is an ideal if: (i) a + b ∈ I for all a, b ∈ I and (ii) r a ∈ I for all r ∈ R and a ∈ I . An ideal is proper if I ⊊ R . An ideal is principal if it is generated by a single element.

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
title: Prime and Maximal ideals
statement_text: A proper ideal I ⊊ R is prime if for all a, b ∈ R , ab ∈ I implies that a ∈ I or b ∈ I . A proper ideal I ⊊ R is maximal if there is no proper ideal I' satisfying I ⊊ I' ⊊ R .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: fact:prime-ideal-maximal
title: Theorem 3.1 of
statement_text: Every non-zero prime ideal p of O_ K is maximal. Since quotients by maximal ideals are fields, O_ K / p is a field.

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
title: Local ring
statement_text: Let K be a number field and let p be a prime ideal of O_K . The local ring of K at p is O_ K,p := { (a)/(b) : a,b ∈ O_K, b ∉ p } .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
title: Residue field
statement_text: If p is a prime ideal of O_K , the field O_K/p is the residue field of p .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
title: Residue degree
statement_text: Let K be a number field and let q be a rational prime. For a prime ideal p above q , the residue degree of p over q is f(p | q) := [O_K/p : F_q] .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
title: Splitting completely (as in Definition A.2 of )
statement_text: Let q be a rational prime. We say that q is unramified in K if qO_K = Π _ i = 1 ^ g p _ i ^ e(p_i|q) . where the prime ideals p_i are distinct and the exponents (called ramification indices) e(p_ i | q) = 1 . We say q splits completely if it further satisfies g = [K:Q] or equivalently f(p_i | q) = 1 i.e. each residue field is O_K/p_i cong F_q .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:unramified
title: Definition A.2 of
statement_text: An infinite ramification of an extension K/F is a real place v: F → C such that there is a complex place w: K → C lying above v . An extension K/F is everywhere unramified if there is no finite ramification (i.e. all finite primes of F are unramified) and no infinite ramification.

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:conjugate-prime
title: Conjugate prime ideals
statement_text: Let c be the complex conjugation automorphism of a CM field K . If p is a prime ideal of O_K , then c p = { c(x) | x ∈ p } is also a prime ideal. The pair { p,cp } is called a conjugate pair of prime ideals .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:valuation
title: Valuation at a prime ideal (see e.g. Chapter 3 of )
statement_text: Let p be a prime ideal of O_K . For a nonzero element x ∈ K^ × , the valuation val _ p (x) is the exponent of p appearing in the factorization of the principal ideal (x) .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: lem:valuation-complex
statement_text: Let K be a CM field with complex conjugation automorphism c and p a prime in O_ K . Then, for any z ∈ K^ × , val _ p (c(z)) = val _ c p (z) .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: prop:codebook
title: Medium-Prime Norm-One Codebook
statement_text: There exist absolute constants C_0>0 and T ≥ 16 such that the following holds for all sufficiently large L and b . Put Y:= lceil 4 sqrt L rceil . There exist: a CM field K with complex conjugation c and degree [K:Q] ≤ C_0b ; T distinct rational primes q_1, ... ,q_T ∈ [Y,2Y] , each splitting completely in K , and Q:= Π _ t=1 ^Tq_t ; for each block bit j ∈ [b] , two prime ideals p_ j,1 ,p_ j,2 ⊆ O_K lying above two distinct rational primes q_ j,1 ,q_ j,2 ∈ {q_1, ... ,q_T} , with q_ j,1 q_ j,2 >L ; for every a ∈ {0,1}^b , an element u_a ∈ K^ × ; with the following properties. For every a ∈ {0,1}^b , u_ac(u_a)&=1, |σ(u_a)|&=1 for every complex embedding σ:KhookrightarrowC , Q^2u_a& ∈ O_K. Moreover, for every selected prime ideal p_ j,r , val _ p_ j,r (u_a)&=2a_j val _ cp_ j,r (u_a)&=-2a_j . Because each selected rational prime splits completely in K , one also has O_K/p_ j,r cong F_ q_ j,r .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: lem:valuation-table
title: Valuation Table
statement_text: Let p_ j,r lie above the rational prime q_t . Then, for every block a , val _ p_ j,r (F_t(a))=2E_t(1-a_j). Consequently, for any blocks a, b , val _ p_ j,r (F_t(a)F_t(b)) = 2E_t(2-a_j-b_j). In particular, this product has valuation 0 exactly when a_j=b_j=1 , and has valuation at least 2E_t otherwise.

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: lem:anticancel
title: Multi-Characteristic Anti-Cancellation
statement_text: For x,y ∈ {0,1}^ bL , written in L blocks of length b , the following are equivalent: x · y=0 Longleftrightarrow for all t and all selected p_ j,r | q_t, val _ p_ j,r (K_t(x,y)) ≥ 2E_t . In particular, if x · y=0 and x' · y'>0 , then (K_1(x,y), ... ,K_T(x,y)) ≠ (K_1(x',y'), ... ,K_T(x',y')).

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: lem:product-separation
title: Product-Formula Separation
statement_text: There is an absolute constant C_3 such that if (K_1(x,y), ... ,K_T(x,y)) ≠ (K_1(x',y'), ... ,K_T(x',y')), then, for some t , |σ(K_t(x,y)-K_t(x',y'))| ≥ exp (-C_3b sqrt L log L).

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: prop:int-gadget
title: Nonuniform Finite Integer Block Gadget
statement_text: There are absolute constants C_5 and L_* ≥ 2 such that, for every b ≥ 1 and every L ≥ L_* , there exist two blockwise maps Φ_A,Φ_B:{0,1}^ bL → Z^r, r=O(L), and a finite set V_ b,L ⊆ Z such that x · y=0 Longleftrightarrow Φ_A(x) · Φ_B(y) ∈ V_ b,L . Here blockwise means that there are local maps α_ b,L ,β_ b,L :{0,1}^b → Z^ w , with w=O(1) , such that Φ_A(x_1, ... ,x_L)=(α_ b,L (x_1), ... ,α_ b,L (x_L)) and similarly for Φ_B . Moreover, |Φ_A(x)|_ ∞ , |Φ_B(y)|_ ∞ , max _ v ∈ V_ b,L |v| & ≤ 2^ C_5 b sqrt L log L , |V_ b,L |& ≤ 2^ C_5 b sqrt L log L .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:local-red
title: Local Bichromatic Nonnegative Reduction
statement_text: A local bichromatic nonnegative (b,L,κ) -reduction of width w=O(1) consists of maps α,β:{0,1}^b → {0,1, ... , lceil L^ κ b rceil -1}^ w and a set V ⊆ Z_ ≥ 0 such that |V| ≤ lceil L^ κ b rceil , max _ v ∈ V v ≤ lceil L^ κ b rceil , every possible full dot product is at most lceil L^ κ b rceil , and for all block vectors x=(x_1, ... ,x_L) and y=(y_1, ... ,y_L) , x · y=0 Longleftrightarrow Σ _ i=1 ^Lα(x_i) · β(y_i) ∈ V. It is uniform if α,β can be evaluated and V can be generated in time L^ O(κ b) poly (b) .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: cor:nonuniform-local
statement_text: There are absolute constants K_0 and L_0 ≥ 2 , and a fixed width w_0=O(1) , such that, for every b ≥ 1 and every L ≥ L_0 , there is a (possibly nonuniform) local bichromatic nonnegative (b, L, K_0 sqrt L ) -reduction of width w_0 , consisting of maps α_ b, L , β_ b, L and a set V_ b, L .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: lem:crt-composition
title: CRT Composition for Local Two-Map Reductions
statement_text: There is an absolute constant C_ crt with the following property. Suppose κ ≥ 1 and there is a local bichromatic nonnegative (m,L,κ) -reduction (called the micro-reduction) of constant width w . Let B ≥ m and put q:= lceil B/m rceil . If q ≤ L^ κ m , then there is a local bichromatic nonnegative (B,L,C_ crt κ) -reduction of the same constant width. If the micro-reduction is given uniformly, the composed reduction can be evaluated and its value set generated in time L^ O(κ B) poly (B) plus the corresponding micro-reduction construction time.

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: lem:base-search
title: Base Search
statement_text: For every fixed C>0 and absolute integer width bound W ≥ 1 , there are thresholds L_ bs =L_ bs (C,W) and b_ bs =b_ bs (C,W) with the following property. Let L ≥ L_ bs and b ≥ b_ bs , and assume m,L ≤ C log log log b, 1 ≤ κ ≤ ( log log log b)^ C . Suppose a local bichromatic nonnegative (m,L,κ) -reduction of width at most W exists. Then exhaustive search over widths at most W finds a local bichromatic nonnegative (m,L,C_ bs κ) -reduction, for a constant C_ bs =C_ bs (W) , in time b^ o(1) ≤ L^ O(κ b) for the ranges used in .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: lem:two-param-uniformization
title: Two-Parameter Uniformization
statement_text: There are absolute constants K_1,L_1,B_1 such that, for every L ≥ L_1 and b ≥ B_1 with 2 ≤ L ≤ log log log b, there is a uniform local bichromatic nonnegative (b,L,K_1 sqrt L) -reduction. The maps can be evaluated and the value set can be generated in time L^ O(b sqrt L) poly (b)=2^ O(b sqrt L log L) poly (b).
bounds: O(b\sqrt L); poly(b); O(b\sqrt L\log L); 2^{O(b\sqrt L\log L)}

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: prop:to-zov
title: Dimensionality Reduction to Z -OV
statement_text: For all sufficiently large L and sufficiently large b , let 2 ≤ L ≤ d , b=lceil d/Lrceil , and assume L ≤ log log log b . Boolean OV_ n,d reduces in time n · 2^ O(b sqrt L log L) +2^ O(b sqrt L log L) poly (b) to 2^ O(b sqrt L log L) instances of Z -OV on two sets of n vectors in dimension O(L) , with entry bit-length O(b sqrt L log L) .
bounds: O(b\sqrt L\log L); poly(b); O(L); 2^{O(b\sqrt L\log L)}

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: thm:main
title: Main Theorem
statement_text: Assume OVH or SETH. Let D(n)=ω(1) be a constructible dimension function. Then, for every fixed δ>0 , Z -OV on two n -point sets in dimension at most D(n) , with O( log n) -bit entries, has no O(n^ 2-δ ) -time algorithm.

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:normal
title: Normal Extension (Chapter 13 of )
statement_text: The extension field K/F is called a splitting field for the polynomial f(x) if f(x) factors completely into linear factors (or splits completely) in K[x] (i.e. splits into degree- 1 polynomials with coefficients in K ) and f(x) does not factor completely into linear factors over any proper subfield of K containing F . An extension K/F is normal if K is the splitting field for some collection of polynomials. The normal closure of an extension K/F is the smallest normal extension K/F ⊆ N/F .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:separable
title: Separable (Chapter 13 of )
statement_text: A polynomial over F is called separable if it has no multiple roots (i.e., all its roots are distinct). The field K is said to be separable (or separably algebraic) over F if every element of K is the root of a separable polynomial over F (equivalently, the minimal polynomial over F of every element of K is separable).

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:galois
title: Galois Extension ( )
statement_text: A finite extension K/F is Galois if | Aut (K/F)| = [K:F] . In this case, the Galois group of K/F is Gal (K/F) = Aut (K/F) .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:fixed-field
title: Fixed Field
statement_text: If H is a subgroup of Aut (K/F) , the subfield of K fixed by all the elements of H is called the fixed field of H , denoted K^ H .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:p-group
statement_text: A finite group G is a p -group if every element has order that is a power of p .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:inverse-limit
title: Inverse Limits
statement_text: A partially ordered set (J, preceq ) is an inverse system if for any i,j ∈ J there is some k ∈ J such that k preceq i and k preceq j . An inverse system of groups (J, preceq ) consists of: (1) group G_j for each j ∈ J and, whenever i preceq j , we have some homomorphism φ_ ij : G_ i → G_ j such that φ_ ii = id _ G_ i and φ_ ik = φ_ jk ∘ φ_ ij when i preceq j preceq k . The inverse limit of an inverse system of groups (more informally, the inverse limit of the groups G_ j ) is the group, denoted underset arrow lim G_ j , of sequences (g_ j )_ j ∈ J such that g_ j ∈ G_ j for all j and φ_ ij (g_ i ) = g_ j for all i preceq j .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:pro-p-group
title: Pro- p Groups
statement_text: Let p be a prime. A pro- p group is an inverse limit of an inverse system of finite p -groups.

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:compositum
title: Maximal unramified pro-p extension (Definition A.3 of )
statement_text: For a number field F , F^ ur ,p denotes the compositum of all finite everywhere-unramified Galois extensions of F whose Galois groups are finite p -groups. Its Galois group Gal (F^ ur ,p /F) is a pro- p group, and its finite quotients correspond to finite everywhere-unramified Galois p -group extensions of F .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
statement_text: Let (G_j)_ j ∈ J be an inverse system of finite groups. Endow each G_j with the discrete topology (every subset is open and closed), and give Π G_j the product topology (open sets are the full group G_j in all but finitely many coordinates). The topology on underset arrow lim G_j ⊆ Π G_j is the subspace topology.

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:frattini
title: Frattini Subgroup (Definition 4.1.1 of )
statement_text: The Frattini subgroup of group G , denoted Φ(G) , is the intersection of all maximal proper subgroups of G .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
title: Generator rank
statement_text: Let G be a topological group and let S be a subset of G . We say S is a (topological) generating set for G if the subgroup ⟨ S ⟩ generated by S is a dense subgroup of G . The group G is (topologically) finitely generated if it has a finite topological generating set. The generator rank of G , denoted d(G) , is the minimum size of a (topological) generating set.

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:relation-rank
title: Relation rank (Section 5.4.2 of )
statement_text: Let G be a topologically finitely generated pro- p group, and let d(G) denote its minimal number of topological generators. A finite pro- p presentation of G is an isomorphism G cong F/ ⟨ ⟨ R ⟩ ⟩ , where F is a finitely generated free pro- p group and ⟨ ⟨ R ⟩ ⟩ denotes the closed normal subgroup of F topologically normally generated by R . The relation rank of G , denoted r(G) , is the minimum cardinality of such a set R , taken over pro- p presentations of G in which F is freely generated by d(G) elements.

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:trace-norm
title: Trace (see e.g. Corollary 2.20 of )
statement_text: Let L/K be a separable extension so that there are n = [L:K] distinct embeddings of L fixing K , denoted { σ_ i } . Then, define for x ∈ L , Tr _ L/K (x) = Σ _ i = 1 ^ n σ_ i (x) .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:relative-discriminant
title: Relative Discriminant ( )
statement_text: Let L/K be a separable extension of degree n = [L:K] and x_1, ... , x_ n ∈ L . Then their discriminant is disc (x_1, ... , x_n) = det ( Tr _ L/K (x_i x_j)) . The relative discriminant d_ L/K is the ideal of O_ K generated by disc (x_1, ... , x_n) for all x_1, ... , x_n ∈ O_ L .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:absolute-discriminant
title: Absolute Discriminant ( )
statement_text: The absolute discriminant of a number field K/Q is defined |Δ_ K | = | disc (x_1, ... , x_n)| where { x_i } is (any) Z -basis of O_ K .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:discriminant
title: Discriminant (Definition A.6 of )
statement_text: The root discriminant of a number field K/Q is rd (K) = |Δ_ K |^ 1/[K:Q] . Finite unramified extensions preserve root discriminant. For an extension M/F , the relative discriminant d_ M/F is an ideal of O_F , and the tower formula is |Δ_M|= |Δ_F|^ [M:F] N_ F/Q (d_ M/F ). Thus d_ M/F = O_ F is equivalent to no finite ramification in M/F . Here, N_ F/Q (a) = [O_ F : a] denotes the absolute norm of an ideal a .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:fractional=ideal
title: Fractional Ideal
statement_text: A fractional ideal of K is a finitely generated O_ K -submodule a ≠ 0 of K . The ideal group of K , denoted J_K is the group of fractional ideals of K , with identity O_ K and inverse a^ -1 = { x ∈ K | x a ⊆ O_ K } . The fractional principal ideals of K , denoted P_ K , form a subgroup of J_K .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:class-number
title: Class Number
statement_text: The class group of K is the group J_K/P_K . The class number of K , denoted h (K) is h (K) = |J_K/P_K| .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
label: def:frobenius
title: Frobenius Representative
statement_text: Let L/K be a Galois extension. Let p be a prime ideal of O_ K that is unramified in L/K , and P a prime lying above p in O_ L . The Frobenius automorphism of P , denoted φ_ P is the unique φ ∈ Gal (L/K) such that φ_ P (α) ≡ α^ |O_ K /p| pmod P for all α ∈ O_ L .

paper_title: Furthest Pair Requires Quadratic Time in Superconstant Dimension under SETH
title: Decomposition Group
statement_text: Let L/K be an extension and p a prime ideal in O_ K . For a prime P above p in O_ L , the decomposition group D(P | p) is the set of automorphisms in Gal (L/K) satisfying σ(P) = P . title: Informal, see
statement_text: Let F(x_1, ... , x_n) = C_1 ∧ C_2 ∧ ... ∧ C_m be an unsatisfiable CNF formula, and let R ∈ TFNP be any total NP search problem. An ⟨ EF, R ⟩ refutation of F is a tuple (C, D, Π) , where C and D are polynomial-size circuits encoding a mapping reduction from Search _F to R , and Π is an Extended Frege proof that C and D are a correct mapping reduction. We call (C, D, Π) an EF -provable mapping reduction from Search _F to R .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_text: A propositional proof system P is given by a polynomial-time algorithm V: {0,1}^* × {0,1}^* → {0,1} , known as its verifier, such that for every CNF formula F , ∃ Π : V(F,Π) = 1 ⟺ F is unsatisfiable . Given two propositional proof systems P , Q , with verifiers V_P and V_Q , we say that P polynomially-simulates Q , written P ≥ _p Q , if there is a polynomial-time computable function f such that V_Q(F, Π) ⇒ V_P(F, f(F, Π)) for all F and Π .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_text: Let C_1, ... C_m, D be a collection of clauses. A Resolution proof of D from C_1, ... , C_m is a sequence of clauses Π = (D_1, D_2, ... , D_s) where D_s = D and, for each i ≤ s , either D_i = C_j for some j , or D_i is derived from earlier clauses in the sequence by one of the following two rules: Resolution C ∨ x, D ∨ ¬ x vdash C ∨ D Weakening C vdash C ∨ D The proof is a refutation if D = bot (the empty clause).

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_text: Let Π=L_1, ... , L_t be a Frege-derivation using variables x_1, ... , x_n . The extension rule allows one to add the line L_ t+1 := e ↔ A , where A is any formula over the variables x_1, ... , x_n , and the extension variable e is not among these variables.

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
label: def:reflection
statement_text: For a proof system P with verifier V , its reflection principle is the family of tautologies Refl _ P,n,m,s (F,Π,x) := ¬ Proof _ n,m,s (F,Π) ∨ SAT _ n,m (F,x) where Proof _ n,m,s is a formula (using the definition of V_ n,m,s ) asserting that Π is a P -proof that F is a tautology, and SAT _ n,m is the CNF formula claiming that x is a satisfying assignment to F . This captures the soundness of the proof system P : it asserts that if Π is a P -proof of F then every assignment satisfies F . If the parameters n, m, s are clear from context, then we will suppress the subscripts and call the formula Refl _P . A Σ^q_1 -formula is a quantified boolean formula of the form ∃ y G(x, y) , where G is unquantified. The reflection principle for Σ^q_1 -formulas is defined similarly by changing SAT (F,x) to SAT _ Σ^q_1 (F,x) , asserting that F , a Σ^q_1 -formula, is satisfied by assignment x . The formula SAT _ Σ^q_1 (F,x) may itself be written as a Σ^q_1 -formula in the natural way. We will denote this version of reflection as Σ^q_1 - Refl _P .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_text: The proof system [EF, Resolution ] is defined as follows. If F(x_1, ... , x_n) = C_1 ∧ ... ∧ C_m is an unsatisfiable CNF formula, then a refutation in [EF, Resolution ] of F is given by a pair (C, Π) , where C is an implicit encoding of a Resolution refutation of F , and Π is an Extended Frege proof that C is correctly encoded.

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_text: A relation R ⊆ { 0,1 } ^* × { 0,1 } ^* is Total , if for all x ∈ { 0,1 } ^* there is a y ∈ { 0,1 } ^* such that (x, y) ∈ R . Polynomially bounded , if there is a polynomial ℓ (n) such that for all (x, y) ∈ R , |y| ≤ ℓ (n) . An NP search problem is a polynomial-time computable, polynomially bounded relation R ⊆ { 0,1 } ^* × { 0,1 } ^* . The class of all total NP search problems is denoted TFNP .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
label: def:tfnp-cnf-encoding
statement_text: Let R ∈ TFNP and let n, ℓ be positive integers. Define V_ R, n, ℓ to be a polynomial-size circuit such that V_ R, n, ℓ (x, y) = R(x, y) . If the parameters n and ℓ are clear from context, then we will omit them and write V_R(x, y) .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
label: def:mapping-reduction
statement_text: Let R, S ∈ TFNP . A mapping reduction from R to S is given by two polynomial-time computable functions f and g such that for all x, y ∈ { 0,1 } ^* , S(f(x), y) ⇒ R(x, g(y)). If R is mapping reducible to S we write R ≤ _m S .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_text: The iterlong problem, also denoted iter , is defined as follows. For any positive integer n , let ℓ (n) = n^ O(1) be a polynomially-bounded input parameter. The input to the problem is a size parameter 1^n and a circuit S: { 0,1 } ^n × { 0,1 } ^ ℓ → { 0,1 } ^ ℓ of size polynomial in n . Given n and S , a string y ∈ { 0,1 } ^ ℓ is a valid solution if either y = 0^ ℓ , if S(x, 0^ ℓ ) = 0^ ℓ , or y ≠ 0^ ℓ , if S(x, y) <_ lex y , or y ≠ 0^ ℓ , if S(x, y) >_ lex y and S(x, S(x, y)) = S(x, y) . Above <_ lex denotes the usual lexicographic ordering on strings. The class of all search problems mapping reducible to iterlong is denoted by PLS .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_text: If F(x_1, ... , x_n) = C_1 ∧ ... ∧ C_m is an unsatisfiable CNF formula, the false-clause search problem Search _F associated with F is the total relation Search _F := { (x, i) ∈ {0,1}^n × [m]: C_i(x) = 0 }.

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_text: Let n be a positive integer. A black-box search problem is any total relation R^ dt _n ⊆ { 0,1 }^ n × O_n, where O_n is a polynomial-sized set of feasible solutions. The class TFNP ^ dt contains all sequences R^ dt = { R^ dt _n }_n of black-box search problems such that the following holds: there is a universal constant c such that for each input length n , and each o ∈ O_n , there is a O(( log n)^c) -depth decision tree T_o satisfying T_o(x) = R^ dt _n(x,o) .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
label: def:formulation
statement_text: Let S^ dt _m ⊆ {0,1}^m × O_S, R^ dt _n ⊆ {0,1}^n × O_S be black-box search problems. A decision-tree reduction from S^ dt _m to R^ dt _n is given by functions f = {f_i: { 0,1 } ^m → {0,1}}_ i ∈ [n] and g = {g_o: { 0,1 } ^n → O_S}_ o ∈ O_R each computable by decision trees T_ f_i , T_ g_o , such that for every x ∈ {0,1}^m and o ∈ O_R , (T_f(x), o) ∈ R^ dt ⇒ (x, T_ g_o (x)) ∈ S^ dt . where T_f(x) denotes the n -bit string obtained by evaluating T_ f_1 (x), ... ,T_ f_n (x) . The depth of the reduction is the maximum depth of any of the decision trees { T_ f_i }_i ∪ { T_ g_o }_o . The complexity of the reduction to be: Σ _ i=1 ^n |T_ f_i | + Σ _ o ∈ O_S |T_ g_o |. We extend this definition to sequences as follows. If R ^ dt = {R^ dt _n} is a sequence of search problems, then R^ dt (S^ dt _m) is the minimum complexity of a reduction from S^ dt _m to any problem in R^ dt . If S^ dt = {S^ dt _m} is also a sequence of search problems, then we write S^ dt ≤ ^ dt _m R ^ dt if R ^ dt (S^ dt _m) is polynomially-bounded in m .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_text: Let N = 2^k be a positive integer. The problem iter _N^ dt is defined as follows. As input, for each element u ∈ [N] , we are given a successor s_u ∈ [N] , interpreted as naming the successor node of u , and which we can think of as being encoded by a string of k bits. The goal of the search problem is to output any of the following 1 if s_1 = 1 (inactive distinguished source) u ≠ 1 , if s_u < u , (decreasing successor) u , if u is active and s_u is a proper sink. (proper sink)

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
label: def:unsat-cnf
statement_text: Let F(x_1, ... , x_n) = C_1 ∧ C_2 ∧ ... ∧ C_m be a CNF formula. The formula UNSAT _F(x_1, ... , x_n, z_1, ... , z_m) is defined to be UNSAT _F(x, z) := ( vee_ i=1 ^m z_i ) ∧ wedge_ i=1 ^m ( ¬ z_i ∨ ¬ C_i). If F = { F_i }_i is a sequence of unsatisfiable CNF formulas, then let UNSAT _ F = { UNSAT _ F_i }_i be the corresponding sequence of formulas.

statement_text: If F is a polynomial-time uniform sequence of unsatisfiable CNF formulas, then UNSAT _ F , interpreted as a total search problem, is in FP .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
label: def:non-uniform mapping reduction
statement_text: Let R ∈ TFNP and let F(x_1, ... , x_n) = C_1 ∧ ... ∧ C_m be an unsatisfiable CNF formula. Let ℓ (n) denote the polynomial upper bound on the length of any solution to R on inputs of length n . A non-uniform mapping reduction from Search _F to R is given by two circuits C : {0,1}^n → {0,1}^s, D : { 0,1 } ^n × { 0,1 } ^ ℓ (s) → { 0,1 } ^m , such that R(C(x), y) ⇒ UNSAT _F(x, D(x, y)).

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_text: Let n, m be positive integers, let R ∈ TFNP , and let F(x_1, ... , x_n) = ∧ _ i=1 ^m C_i be a CNF formula. Let ℓ be a polynomial bound on the certificate length of R . If R ∈ TFNP and F(x_1, ... , x_n) = ∧ _ i=1 ^m C_i , then Reduction _ R, n, m, S, s (C, D, F) is the boolean formula defined as follows. We introduce several helper formulas which can easily be represented in CNF. isCkt _S(C) is satisfied iff the variables in C encode a valid boolean circuit with S gates. Eval _ n, S, s (C, x, t) is satisfied iff C encodes a boolean circuit with n inputs, S gates, and s outputs, and t ∈ { 0,1 } ^s is the output of C on input x ∈ { 0,1 } ^n . Then Reduction _ R, n, m, S, s (C, D, F):= isCkt (C) ∧ isCkt (D) ∧ Eval (C, x, x') ∧ Eval (D, (x, y), z) ∧ Eval (V_R, x', y) → UNSAT _F(x, z). For readability, we have omitted parameter subscripts above, and we will continue to do so when those parameters are clear from context. The circuit C has n inputs, S gates, and s outputs, and the circuit D has n+ ℓ (s) inputs, S gates, and m outputs.

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
label: def:ef-mapping-r
statement_text: (Defining ⟨ EF,R ⟩ ) For any R ∈ TFNP , the propositional proof system ⟨ EF, R ⟩ is defined as follows. For any unsatisfiable CNF formula F(x_1, ... , x_n) = C_1 ∧ ... ∧ C_m , a refutation of F in ⟨ EF, R ⟩ is given by an EF -provable reduction from Search _F to R . Formally, such a reduction is a tuple (C, D, Π) , where (C, D) are circuits computing a non-uniform mapping reduction from Search _F to R , and Π is an Extended Frege proof of a boolean formula Reduction _R(C, D, F) .

statement_text: The class Σ^q_0 = Π^q_0 consists of all (quantifer-free) propositional formulas. The class of Σ^q_1 formulas are of the form ∃ x_1, ... ,x_n A(x_1, ... ,x_n,y) where A(x,y) ∈ Σ^q_0 , and y=y_1, ... ,y_m .

statement_text: [Witnessing for G_1 ] Let F= ∃ y A(x,y) , where A is a Σ^q_0 formula, and let Π be a G_1 proof of F . Then G_1 vdash ∃ i (llbracket i = 1 rrbracket ∨ ... ∨ llbracket i = m rrbracket ) ∧ ( (llbracket i = 1 rrbracket → ¬ C_1) ∧ ... ∧ ( llbracket i = m rrbracket → ¬ C_m) ). statement_text: WrongProof _P:= { WrongProof _ P,n,m,s }_ n,m,s is the false clause search problem associated with the unsatisfiable formula ¬ Refl _P , which asserts that a formula has both a P -proof and a falsifying assignment. Formally, WrongProof _ P,n,m,s (x,z) :&= UNSAT _ ¬ Refl _ P,n,m,s (x,z) &= UNSAT _ Proof _ P,n,m,s (x,z_1) ∨ UNSAT _ ¬ SAT _ n,m (x,z_2), Recalling that we use a one-hot encoding in UNSAT , z_1 are the bits that represent the clauses of Proof , while z_2 are those belonging to SAT . As well, x=(α,F,Π) is a tuple encoding an assignment, a formula (claimed to be a tautology), and a proof Π . Recall from that this is a problem in TFNP .

label: def:pk
title: Gentzen's PK: Propositional Calculus
statement_text: Let all formulas be propositional and under the DeMorgan basis. A PK proof uses the following rules. l l (Ax) inferrule *[right=Ax] A → A & (Cut) inferrule *[right=Cut] Γ → A Δ, A → B Γ, Δ → B (WL) inferrule *[right=WL] Γ → A Γ, B → A & (WR) inferrule *[right=WR] Γ → A Γ → A, B (CL) inferrule *[right=CL] Γ, A, A → B Γ, A → B & (CR) inferrule *[right=CR] Γ → A, A Γ → A (EL) inferrule *[right=EL] Γ, A, B, Δ → C Γ, B, A, Δ → C & (ER) inferrule *[right=ER] Γ → A, B, Δ Γ → B, A, Δ (neg L) inferrule *[right=neg L] Γ → A, Δ Γ, ¬ A → Δ & (neg R) inferrule *[right=neg R] Γ, A → Δ Γ → ¬ A, Δ (and L) inferrule *[right=and L] Γ, A, B → Δ Γ, A ∧ B → Δ & (and R) inferrule *[right=and R] Γ → A, Δ Γ → B, Δ Γ → A ∧ B, Δ (or L) inferrule *[right=or L] Γ, A → Δ Γ, B → Δ Γ, A ∨ B → Δ & (or R) inferrule *[right=or R] Γ → A, B, Δ Γ → A ∨ B, Δ

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
label: def:G
title: G and G_i Subsystems
statement_text: We adapt Frege to allow quantified formulas introduced by the following rules: l l ( ∀ -left ) inferrule * A(B), Γ → Δ ∀ x A(x), Γ → Δ & ( ∀ -right ) inferrule * Γ → Δ, A(p) Γ → Δ, ∀ x A(x) ( ∃ -left ) inferrule * A(p), Γ → Δ ∃ x A(x), Γ → Δ & ( ∃ -right ) inferrule * Γ → Δ, A(p) Γ → Δ, ∃ x A(x) For the ∀ -right and ∃ -left rules, the variable p is called an eigenvariable and cannot appear in the bottom sequent. The G proof system is simply PK with these additional rules. For i ≥ 0 , G_i is a restriction of G to only allow cuts on (Σ^q_i ∪ Π^q_i ) -formulas. (That is, the cut rule for G_i can only be applied to formulas with at most i alternations of ∀ and ∃ quantifiers.) While the G systems can prove validity of general QBF formulas, it is also interesting to understand their strength with respect to Boolean formulas. Since G (and even G_1 ) has all of EF rules plus additional rules, G can trivially p-simulate EF (with respect to Boolean formulas). And it is known that the tree-like version of G_1 , called G_1^* is p-equivalent to EF. On the other hand, it is unknown whether or not G_1 is stronger than EF (with respect to Boolean formulas), and it is generally conjectured to be more powerful wrt p-simulations.

title: local subinstance reducibility for SAT
statement_text: Let F _N be a family of CNF formulas over N Boolean variables. A local subinstance H of size at most N^c comprises at most N^c evaluated clauses; all variables occurring within these evaluated clauses are also regarded as seen by H . The information in H is measured by the number of variables in H . We refer to information of order O(N^ 1-δ ) with δ>0 as local information. We call F _N reducible if there exist a constant 0<c<1 and a local subinstance H of size at most N^c such that the information in H suffices to determine the satisfiability of every formula in F _N . In this setting, we say that local information is sufficient for solving formulas in F _N . Conversely, F _N is irreducible whenever, for every 0<c<1 and every such H , there are two formulas inducing the same H but with opposite satisfiability status. In this case, local information is insufficient. Hence, we say that solving formulas in F _N requires global information.

For every local subinstance H of size at most N^c , there exists a formula F' such that H(F)=H(F'), but F ∈ UniqueSAT , F' ∈ UNSAT . The quantifier order is ∀ F ( in the good event ) ∀ H , so the statement is uniform: a single conditioned formula F defeats every local subinstance of size at most N^c simultaneously. In particular, the result holds against adaptive evaluators that choose H after examining F . Thus, the family of native logarithmic-width self-referential SAT formulas is irreducible in the local subinstance-evaluation sense, meaning solving such formulas inherently requires global information.

title: Challenge excursions
statement_text: Fix an edge e={x,y} and a vertex x ∈ e . Suppose Phase 1 has been completed, so in particular the edge o_e → r_e has already been used. If the x -side of G_e was traversed during Phase 1, then every challenge move q_x → μ^x_ e,i → x_e is immediately losing for Player 2, because all forward edges out of x_e have already been exhausted. If the x -side of G_e was not traversed during Phase 1, then after any challenge move q_x → μ^x_ e,i → x_e the token reaches x_e with Player 2 to move. From that point on, every non-losing continuation has the following form: Player 2 repeatedly chooses unused forward edges x_e → ξ^x_ e,j ; after each such move, Player 1 is forced to move to x'_e ; at x'_e , Player 2 may either use an unused backward edge x'_e → δ^x_ e,j' (if one exists), or choose a ζ -edge x'_e → ζ^x_ e, ℓ ; if Player 2 moves to m^x_e , then Player 1 is forced to o_e and Player 2 immediately loses, because o_e → r_e has already been used; if Player 2 moves to some ζ^x_ e, ℓ , then Player 1's only non-losing reply is ζ^x_ e, ℓ → x^ out _ e, ℓ , since choosing x^ esc _ e, ℓ leads to an immediate loss; after that, Player 2 is forced to move to v_x^ return . The parent-side label of p is defined as λ_i^uparrow (p):=iota _ par (i) (x_p) , and the child-side label of p is defined as λ_i^downarrow (p):=iota _i(y_p) . Thus each non-root node i determines an interface (P_i,λ_i^uparrow ,λ_i^downarrow ) .

paper_title: Edge Geography is XNLP-hard for Pathwidth and in XP for Tree-Partition Width
title: Labeled interface
statement_text: A labeled interface is a pair (P,λ) where P ⊆ Π_k and λ:P → [k] . Its rank is |P| .

paper_title: Edge Geography is XNLP-hard for Pathwidth and in XP for Tree-Partition Width
title: Ambient type universe
statement_text: For each labeled interface (P,λ) we define recursively a finite set T (P,λ) of ambient types . If P= ∅ , then T (P,λ)={bot } . Suppose |P|=r>0 , and that all sets T (P',λ') with |P'|<r have already been defined. Fix an entry port a ∈ P . Define Ω(P,λ,a) to be the set of all triples (q,τ,b) , where q ∈ P \ {a} , τ ∈ T (P \ {a,q},λ|_ P \ {a,q} ) , b ∈ { same , opp } . An ambient type σ ∈ T (P,λ) is a family σ= l((A_a^σ,Φ_a^σ) r)_ a ∈ P , where for every a ∈ P : A_a^σ ⊆ Ω(P,λ,a) is the set of exit labels declared attainable from entry through a , Φ_a^σ:{0,1}^ A_a^σ → {0,1} is a Boolean function.

paper_title: Edge Geography is XNLP-hard for Pathwidth and in XP for Tree-Partition Width
title: Rank of an ambient type
statement_text: Let σ ∈ T (P,λ) . The rank of σ , denoted rk (σ) , is rk (σ):=|P| . Equivalently, rk (σ) is the rank of the underlying labeled interface of σ .

paper_title: Edge Geography is XNLP-hard for Pathwidth and in XP for Tree-Partition Width
label: lem:finitely-many-types
statement_text: For every fixed k , the ambient type universe T _k := uplus_ P ⊆ Π_k \ uplus_ λ:P → [k] T (P,λ) is finite.

paper_title: Edge Geography is XNLP-hard for Pathwidth and in XP for Tree-Partition Width
title: Residual child subinstance
statement_text: A residual child subinstance of i consists of: a residual game position arising inside the subtree of some child of i , its parent-facing labeled interface (P_H,λ_H) , where λ_H:P_H → [k] is expressed relative to the labeling iota _i of the parent bag X_i , and its already defined ambient type τ(H) ∈ T (P_H,λ_H) .

paper_title: Edge Geography is XNLP-hard for Pathwidth and in XP for Tree-Partition Width
title: Expanded residual configuration
statement_text: An expanded residual configuration at node i is a triple Γ =(U,F,C) , where U ⊆ P_i is the set of unused parent ports, F ⊆ E(G[X_i]) is the set of unused edges inside the bag X_i , C is a multiset of residual child subinstances of i . Its parent-facing labeled interface is (U,λ_i^uparrow |_U) .

paper_title: Edge Geography is XNLP-hard for Pathwidth and in XP for Tree-Partition Width
title: Measure of an expanded residual configuration
statement_text: Let Γ =(U,F,C) be an expanded residual configuration. Its measure is μ( Γ ) := |U|+|F|+ Σ _ H ∈ C rk (τ(H)).

title: Entry state
statement_text: Let Γ =(U,F,C) be an expanded residual configuration at node i , and let a ∈ U . Let z_a ∈ X_i be the unique vertex satisfying iota _i(z_a)=λ_i^downarrow (a) . The entry state for entry through a is S_a^0 := (z_a, U \ {a}, F, C, opp ) .

paper_title: Edge Geography is XNLP-hard for Pathwidth and in XP for Tree-Partition Width
title: Expanded local state
statement_text: Fix an expanded residual configuration Γ =(U,F,C) and an entry port a ∈ U . An expanded local state relative to a is a tuple S=(z,U',F',C',π) , where z ∈ X_i is the current token position, U' ⊆ U \ {a} is the set of currently unused parent ports, F' ⊆ F is the set of currently unused edges inside X_i , C' is a multiset of residual child subinstances, π ∈ { same , opp } records whether the player to move is the same as or opposite to the player who originally entered through a .

paper_title: Edge Geography is XNLP-hard for Pathwidth and in XP for Tree-Partition Width
title: Legal moves from an expanded local state
statement_text: Let S=(z,U',F',C',π) be an expanded local state. A legal move from S is one of the following. Internal move. If {z,z'} ∈ F' , then traversing this edge yields the successor state (z',U',F' \ {{z,z'}},C', π ) . Exit move. If q ∈ U' satisfies λ_i^downarrow (q)=iota _i(z) , then play may leave the current subtree through the port q . Child excursion. If H ∈ C' has an entry port b ∈ P_H satisfying λ_H(b)=iota _i(z) , then play may enter the residual child subinstance H through b .

paper_title: Edge Geography is XNLP-hard for Pathwidth and in XP for Tree-Partition Width
title: Measure of an expanded local state
statement_text: The measure of an expanded local state S=(z,U',F',C',π) is μ(S) := |U'|+|F'|+ Σ _ H ∈ C' rk (τ(H)).

paper_title: Edge Geography is XNLP-hard for Pathwidth and in XP for Tree-Partition Width
title: Parent-side successor induced by a returning child excursion
statement_text: Let S=(z,U',F',C',π) be an expanded local state, and let H ∈ C' be a residual child subinstance entered through a port b ∈ P_H with λ_H(b)=iota _i(z) . Suppose a legal excursion inside H , entered through b , returns to the parent bag with exit label (q,τ',c) ∈ A_b^ τ(H) . Let H' denote the residual child subinstance produced by that excursion, so that τ(H')=τ' . Let z_q ∈ X_i be the unique vertex satisfying iota _i(z_q)=λ_H(q) . The corresponding parent-side successor state is S[q,H',c] := (z_q, U', F', (C' \ {H})uplus {H'}, π ∘ c).

statement_text: Fix an expanded residual configuration Γ =(U,F,C) and an entry port a ∈ U . Consider the directed graph whose vertices are the expanded local states reachable from the entry state S_a^0 , and whose arcs are the successor states arising from internal moves and from returning child excursions. Then this graph is acyclic.

statement_text: Let S=(z,U',F',C',π) be an expanded local state reachable from S_a^0 , and suppose that q ∈ U' satisfies λ_i^downarrow (q)=iota _i(z) . Then exiting through q produces the smaller expanded residual configuration Γ _S^q:=(U' \ {q},F',C') . The corresponding exit label is ℓ _S(q):=(q,τ( Γ _S^q), π ) .

statement_text: Let Γ _1=(U,F,C_1),\ Γ _2=(U,F,C_2) be two expanded residual configurations that differ only in that one residual child subinstance H_1 ∈ C_1 is replaced by another residual child subinstance H_2 ∈ C_2 . title: Ambient valuation

label: lem:joint

statement_text: Let i be a node of the rooted tree partition. For every expanded residual configuration Γ =(U,F,C) at node i , there exists a uniquely defined ambient type τ( Γ ) ∈ T (U,λ_i^uparrow |_U) . Let Γ _1=(U,F,C_1), Γ _2=(U,F,C_2) be expanded residual configurations that differ only in that one residual child subinstance H_1 ∈ C_1 is replaced by another residual child subinstance H_2 ∈ C_2 with τ(H_1)=τ(H_2) . statement_text: Let (P,λ) be a labeled interface. A type σ ∈ T (P,λ) is realizable if there exists an expanded residual configuration Γ with parent-facing labeled interface (P,λ) such that τ( Γ )=σ . We write T(P,λ) ⊆ T (P,λ) for the set of all realizable interface types on (P,λ) .

paper_title: Edge Geography is XNLP-hard for Pathwidth and in XP for Tree-Partition Width

title: Compressed local state
statement_text: Let Γ=(U,F,m) be a compressed residual configuration at node i , and let a ∈ U . A compressed local state relative to a is a tuple S=(z,U',F',m',π) , where z ∈ X_i is the current token position, U' ⊆ U \ {a} is the set of currently unused parent ports, F' ⊆ F is the set of currently unused internal edges of X_i , m' ≤ m is a multiplicity vector on T_k , π ∈ { same , opp } records the player to move relative to the player who originally entered through a .

title: Compressed transitions
statement_text: Let S=(z,U',F',m',π) be a compressed local state. Compressed internal move. If {z,z'} ∈ F' , then traversing this edge yields the successor state (z',U',F' \ {{z,z'}},m', π ) . Compressed exit move. If q ∈ U' satisfies λ_i^downarrow (q)=iota _i(z) , then exiting through q produces the compressed residual configuration Γ_q:=(U' \ {q},F',m') and hence the exit label (q,τ(Γ_q), π ) . Compressed child excursion. Let σ ∈ T_k satisfy m'_σ>0 , and let b ∈ P_σ satisfy λ_σ(b)=iota _i(z) . For each exit label (q,τ',c) ∈ A_b^σ , let z_q ∈ X_i be the unique vertex satisfying iota _i(z_q)=λ_σ(q) . The corresponding compressed successor state is (z_q, U', F', m'-e_σ+e_ τ' , π ∘ c).

label: lem:compressed-transitions
title: Soundness and completeness of compressed transitions
statement_text: Let Γ=(U,F,m) be a compressed residual configuration, let a ∈ U , and let S=(z,U',F',m',π) be a compressed local state relative to a . Let S =(z,U',F',C',π) be any expanded realization of S . Then the following hold. Internal moves. A compressed internal move from S along an edge {z,z'} ∈ F' exists if and only if the corresponding expanded internal move exists from S . The expanded successor state realizes the compressed successor state. Exit moves. A compressed exit move through a port q ∈ U' is legal if and only if the corresponding expanded exit move is legal from S . In that case both produce the same exit label, namely (q,τ(Γ_q), π ), Γ_q:=(U' \ {q},F',m'). Child excursions. Let σ ∈ T_k satisfy m'_σ>0 , and let b ∈ P_σ satisfy λ_σ(b)=iota _i(z) . Then: for every exit label (q,τ',c) ∈ A_b^σ , there exists a legal expanded child excursion from S that enters some residual child subinstance H ∈ C' with τ(H)=σ , returns to the parent bag with that label, and yields an expanded successor state realizing the compressed successor state (z_q, U', F', m'-e_σ+e_ τ' , π ∘ c); conversely, every legal expanded child excursion from S that returns to the parent bag induces one of these compressed successor states.

paper_title: How to Avoid Debate: Scalable AI Safety via Doubly-Efficient Interactive Proofs
title: (Oracle) Boolean circuit
statement_text: For every n ∈ N , an n -input, single-output Boolean circuit is a directed acyclic graph with n sources , i.e., vertices with no incoming edges, and one sink , i.e., a vertex with no outgoing edges. Every non-source vertex is called a gate and is labelled with one of ∨ , ∧ , or ¬ ; ∨ and ∧ gates have two incoming edges and ¬ gates have one incoming edge. For some input string x ∈ {0, 1}^n , the output of the i th source vertex is the i th bit of x , and the value of a gate is defined recursively as the result of applying the logical operation of the gate on the values of its children , i.e., the vertices with an edge going into the gate. The output of the circuit on x is the output of the sink vertex. The size of a circuit is the number of gates it contains, and the depth is the length of the longest path from a source vertex to the sink vertex. An oracle Boolean circuit with respect to oracle O: {0, 1}^* → {0, 1} additionally has oracle gates, which have an arbitrary number of incoming edges. We view the input to an oracle gate as a string given by the values of its children. The value of an oracle gate is the value of the oracle applied to its input string.

paper_title: How to Avoid Debate: Scalable AI Safety via Doubly-Efficient Interactive Proofs
label: defn:closeness
title: Closeness
statement_text: Consider the following `` ε -closeness'' algorithm: given a d -adaptive oracle circuit C^O with ℓ oracle gates, an input x , and the true query-answer string Q = (Q_1, ... , Q_d) , we set T_1 = Q_1 and modify some positions in T_1 , obtaining a string Q_1' . Then for i = 2, ... , d , we set T_ i ^ in = C_ i-1 (x, Q_1', ... , Q_ i-1 ') and T_i = (T_ i ^ in , O(T_i^ in )) , where O(T_ i ^ in ) is obtained by applying O to each query in T_ i ^ in , and modify some positions in T_i , obtaining a string Q_i' . If we can obtain Q' = (Q_1', ... , Q_d') via this algorithm by modifying at most ε ℓ positions (across all of the T_i 's), then we say that Q' is ε -close to Q .

paper_title: How to Avoid Debate: Scalable AI Safety via Doubly-Efficient Interactive Proofs
label: defn:robustness
title: Robustness
statement_text: We say that C^O is ε -robust if, for any length- n binary string x , C_ Q' (x) = C^O(x) for any Q' that is ε -close to the true query-answer string Q .

paper_title: How to Avoid Debate: Scalable AI Safety via Doubly-Efficient Interactive Proofs
label: def:funcdesc
title: Succinct Description of Functions
statement_text: We say that a function f : {0,1}^n → {0,1} of size s has a succinct description if there exists a string lrag f of length polylog (n) and a logspace Turing machine M (of constant size, independent of n ) such that on input 1^n , the machine M outputs a full description of an NC ^1 circuit C such that for every x ∈ {0,1}^n it holds that C(lrag f, x) = f(x) . We refer to lrag f as the succinct description of f .

paper_title: How to Avoid Debate: Scalable AI Safety via Doubly-Efficient Interactive Proofs
label: def:setdesc
title: Succinct Description of Sets
statement_text: We say that a set S ⊆ [k] of size s has a succinct description if there exists a string lrag S of length polylog (k) and a logspace Turing machine M such that on input 1^k , the machine M outputs a full description of a depth polylog (k) and size poly (s, log k) circuit (of constant fan-in) that on input lrag S outputs all the elements of S as a list (of length s · log (k) ).

paper_title: How to Avoid Debate: Scalable AI Safety via Doubly-Efficient Interactive Proofs
label: defn:ip
title: Interactive proof system
statement_text: An interactive proof for a language L is an interactive protocol between a probabilistic polynomial-time verifier algorithm V and a computationally unbounded prover algorithm P . On common input x , V and P back-and-forth exchange messages in a number of rounds. In each round, V sends P a message and then P sends V a message. Both V 's and P 's messages can depend on x and any prior messages, and V 's messages can additionally depend on V 's random bits r . At the end of this interaction, their messages form a transcript t = ( V (r), P )(x) , and based on t , r , and x , V decides to accept or reject. The protocol satisfies completeness and soundness properties, namely, (Completeness.) For every x ∈ L , there exists an honest prover strategy P such that Pr _r[V(x, t, r) = 1] = 1 , where t = ( V (r), P )(x) . ( δ -Soundness.) For every x ∉ L and for every (computationally unbounded) prover algorithm P , Pr _r[V(x, t , r) = 1] ≤ δ , where t = ( V (r), P )(x) .

paper_title: How to Avoid Debate: Scalable AI Safety via Doubly-Efficient Interactive Proofs
label: deIP
statement_text: Let L be a language that has logspace-uniform Boolean circuits of depth D = D(n) and size S = S(n) . For any soundness parameter σ ∈ N , there is a doubly-efficient interactive proof for L with the following parameters: soundness error 2^ -σ ; communication complexity O(σ · D · polylog (S)) ; round complexity O(D · polylog (S)) ; verifier running time O(σ · (n + D · polylog (S))) ; and prover running time poly (S, σ) .

paper_title: How to Avoid Debate: Scalable AI Safety via Doubly-Efficient Interactive Proofs
label: def:ipp
title: Interactive proof of proximity
statement_text: An interactive proof of proximity for a pair language L is an interactive protocol between a probabilistic sublinear-time verifier algorithm V and a polynomial-time prover algorithm P . Both V and P have access to explicit input x and a proximity parameter ε , and V has query access to implicit input Q while P has direct access to Q . The protocol satisfies completeness and a relaxed notion of soundness, namely (Completeness.) For every (x, Q) ∈ L and proximity parameter ε ∈ (0, 1] , there exists an honest prover strategy P such that Pr [lrag P (x), V ^Q(x) = 1] = 1 . ( δ -Soundness.) For every (x, Q) that is ε -Hamming-far from L , and for every (computationally unbounded) prover algorithm P , we have Pr _r[lrag P (x), V ^Q(x) = 1] ≤ δ .

paper_title: How to Avoid Debate: Scalable AI Safety via Doubly-Efficient Interactive Proofs
label: rothblumx2ipp
statement_text: Let ε = ε(m) ∈ (0, 1] be a proximity parameter, let σ ∈ N be a soundness parameter, and let L be a pair language that is computable by logspace-uniform Boolean circuits of depth D = D(m) ≥ log (m) and size S = S(m) ≥ m with fan-in 2 , where we use n for the length of the explicit input and m for the length of the implicit input. Then there is a public-coin IPP with ε proximity for L with the following parameters: soundness error 2^ -σ ; query complexity q = O(σ/ε) ; communication complexity cc = O(σ · ε · m · D · polylog (S)) ; round complexity O(D · polylog (S)) ; verifier running time O(σ · (ε · m · D · polylog (S)+(1/ε) · polylog (S) + n log S)) ; and prover running time poly (S,σ) . Furthermore, the verifier can make all of his queries to the implicit input at the end of the interaction. More formally, at the end of the interaction either the verifier rejects or in time O(σ · ε · m · D · polylog (S)) it outputs a succinct description lrag Q of a set Q ⊆ [m] of size q and a succinct description lrag φ of a predicate φ: {0,1}^q → {0,1} so that its decision predicate given an implicit input x^ imp is equal to φ(x^ imp _Q) . Furthermore, the predicate can be evaluated in time q · polylog (m) .

paper_title: How to Avoid Debate: Scalable AI Safety via Doubly-Efficient Interactive Proofs
label: def:unique-decoding-checksum
title: Unique-Decoding Checksums
statement_text: Let k,ρ, R_ cksum ∈ N and let F be a field. A function cksum _ρ:{0,1}^k → {0,1}^ R_ cksum is a ρ -unique decoding checksum function if for any m ∈ {0,1}^k , and for any m', m'' ∈ {0,1}^k that are both ρ -close to m and m' ≠ m'' , cksum _ρ(m') ≠ cksum _ρ(m'') .

title: Linear-code checksums
statement_text: Let C ⊆ F ^k be a linear code of minimum distance D and codimension R_ cksum , and H ∈ F ^ R_ cksum × k be a parity-check matrix for C . Assume that | F | = 2^ s and Enc : {0,1}^s → F , Dec : F → {0,1}^s are linear maps converting between a binary string and the corresponding field element. For any ρ ∈ N satisfying 2ρ < D , the syndrome map cksum _ρ: {0,1}^ ks → {0,1}^ s R_ cksum , cksum _ρ(m) coloneqq Dec (H Enc (m)), where Enc is applied blockwise and Dec coordinate-wise, is a ρ -unique decoding checksum function. Moreover, with O hiding polylogarithmic factors, cksum _ρ can be evaluated in O (k R_ cksum s) .

title: Interactive argument system
statement_text: Let ℓ ≥ 0 be an integer. A (2 ℓ + 1) -message public-coin argument system Π = ( Setup , P , V ) for a relation R consists of a PPT (probabilistic polynomial time) algorithm Setup and a (2 ℓ + 1) -message protocol between an interactive PPT prover P and an interactive PPT verifier V associated with a tuple (X, W, (Z_ i-1 , C_i)_ i ∈ [ ℓ ] , Z_ ℓ ) , with the following properties: The Setup algorithm takes as input the security parameter 1^λ and outputs some public parameters pp . Both P and V receive as input the public parameters pp and a statement x_0 = x ∈ X . The prover P additionally receives a witness w_0 = w ∈ W . The public parameters pp , the statement x_0 , and the 2 ℓ + 1 messages sent by P and V in the protocol, are collectively called a transcript, labelled as ( pp , x_0, z_0, c_1, ... , z_ ℓ -1 , c_ ℓ , z_ ℓ ), where z_i ∈ Z_i is sent by P and c_i ∈ C_i is sent by V . The challenges c_i are sampled by V uniformly at random from C_i . A transcript ( pp , x_0, z_0, c_1, ... , z_ ℓ -1 , c_ ℓ , z_ ℓ ) is said to be accepting for Π if V ( pp , x_0, z_0, c_1, ... , z_ ℓ -1 , c_ ℓ , z_ ℓ ) = 1 holds.

statement_text: An argument system Π = ( Setup , P , V ) for the relation R has statistical completeness with correctness error ε if for all adversaries A , Pr [ b = 0 ∧ ( pp , x, w) ∈ R middle | c pp arrow Setup (1^λ) (x, w) arrow A ( pp ) ( tr , b) arrow ⟨ P ( pp , x, w), V ( pp , x) ⟩ ] ≤ ε(λ). Furthermore, we say that Π satisfies perfect completeness if ε = 0 .

statement_text: An argument system Π = ( Setup , P , V ) for the relation R has computational soundness if for all stateful PPT adversary P ^* , there exists a function δ negligible in λ , such that: Pr [ b = 1 ∧ ( pp , x) ∉ L middle | c pp arrow Setup (1^λ) (x, st ) arrow P ^*( pp ) ( tr , b) arrow ⟨ P ^*( pp , x, st ), V ( pp , x) ⟩ ] ≤ δ(λ).

Here, the extractor E has a black-box oracle access to the (malicious) prover P ^* and can rewind it to any point in the interaction.

label: def:hash_tree
statement_text: A hash tree consists of a tuple of algorithms ( G _ ht , H _ ht , P _ ht , V _ ht ) with the following syntax: G _ ht (1^λ, S) → hk . This is a randomized algorithm that takes as input a security parameter λ , and a space bound S , and outputs a hash key hk . We implicitly assume that hk includes 1^λ, S . H _ ht ( hk , D) → rt . This is a deterministic algorithm that on input a hash key hk and a database D ∈ {0,1}^S outputs a root rt . P _ ht ( hk , D, i) → ρ . This is a deterministic algorithm that on input a hash key hk , a database D ∈ {0,1}^S , an index i ∈ [S] , outputs an opening proof ρ . When a set I ⊆ [S] is given as input, we interpret this as providing an opening proof for every i ∈ I . V _ ht ( hk , rt , i, v,ρ) → b . This is a deterministic algorithm that on input a hash key hk , a hash tree root rt , an index i ∈ [S] , a bit v ∈ {0,1} , and an opening proof ρ , outputs a bit b ∈ {0,1} indicating whether to accept or reject the opening proof. When a set I ⊆ [S] and values v ∈ {0,1}^ |I| are given as input, we interpret this as verifying, for every j ∈ [|I|] , the proof for the value v[j] at the j th smallest index in I . We require ( G _ ht , H _ ht , P _ ht , V _ ht ) to satisfy the following properties: Opening completeness. For any λ,S ∈ N , i ∈ [S] , database D ∈ {0,1}^S , it holds that Pr [ l V _ ht ( hk , rt , i, D[i], ρ) = 1 : l hk gets G _ ht (1^λ, S) rt = H _ ht ( hk , D) ρ = P _ ht ( hk , D, i) ] = 1. Efficiency. In the opening completeness experiment above for S ≤ 2^λ , G _ ht and V _ ht run in poly (λ) time, and H _ ht and P _ ht run in S · poly (λ) time. Also we require | hk | ≤ poly (λ) and |ρ| ≤ poly (λ) . Binding. For any non-uniform polynomial-time algorithm A = {A_λ}_ λ ∈ N and polynomial S , there exists a negligible function μ such that for all λ ∈ N , it holds that Pr [ l v ≠ v' ∧ 1 = V _ ht ( hk , rt , i, v, ρ) ∧ 1 = V _ ht ( hk , rt , i, v', ρ') : l hk gets G _ ht (1^λ, S(λ)) ( rt , i, v, v', ρ, ρ') gets A_λ( hk ) ] ≤ μ(λ).

After processing the stream, the algorithm outputs either a triple of vertices τ={u,v,w} ⊆ [n] or a failure symbol perp . The output is valid if and only if τ ∈ Tri (G) , equivalently all three edges {u,v},{u,w},{v,w} belong to E . title: Positive Operator-Valued Measure
statement_text: Let H be a d -dimensional Hilbert space representing the state space of k qubits, where d = 2^k . Let Ω be a finite set of measurement outcomes. A Positive Operator-Valued Measure (POVM) on Ω is a collection of positive semidefinite operators {M_ω}_ ω ∈ Ω acting on H that satisfies: M_ω succeq 0 ∀ ω ∈ Ω , and the completeness relation: Σ _ ω ∈ Ω M_ω = I .

paper_title: Quantum Communication Lower Bounds for Search Problems via Matrix Discrepancy
title: Quantum one-way communication complexity
statement_text: Let R ⊆ A × B × Z be a relation, and let ε ∈ [0,1] . We assume that Alice and Bob share no prior entanglement. A quantum one-way protocol Π of message dimension d consists of the following parts: For each input a ∈ A , Alice prepares a density operator ρ_a ∈ D(C^d) and sends it to Bob. For each input b ∈ B , Bob performs a POVM M^ (b) ={M_z^ (b) }_ z ∈ Z on C^d , where M_z^ (b) succeq 0 and Σ _ z ∈ Z M_z^ (b) = I_d . On inputs (a,b) , the protocol outputs z ∈ Z with probability Pr [z | a,b] = Tr (M_z^ (b) ρ_a ). The quantum one-way communication cost of Π is log _2 d .

title: Ex Post Pacing Equilibrium
statement_text: Fix bidders [n] and divisible items [q] . Bidder i has budget B_i , value v_ ij for item j , and paced bid b_ ij (α) := α_i v_ ij under multiplier α_i ∈ [0,1] . Let H_j(α) := arg max _ k ∈ [n] b_ kj (α) be the highest paced bidders for item j . A pacing equilibrium consists of multipliers α ∈ [0,1]^n , allocation x ∈ [0,1]^ n × q , and prices p ∈ R _+^q such that, for all i ∈ [n] and j ∈ [q] : · setlength sep 0pt setlength parsep 3pt setlength topsep 3pt setlength partopsep 0pt setlength margin 1em setlength width 1em setlength sep 0.5em Market clearing. Each item is fully allocated: Σ _ i=1 ^n x_ ij = 1 . Moreover, only highest paced bidders receive positive allocation: x_ ij > 0 ⇒ i ∈ H_j(α) . Auction pricing. If x_ ij > 0 , then the price of item j is determined by the auction format: p_j = b_ ij (α) for first-price auctions, and p_j = max _ k ≠ i b_ kj (α) for second-price auctions. Budget feasibility Each bidder respects their budget: Σ _ j=1 ^q p_j x_ ij ≤ B_i . If bidder i does not exhaust their budget, then they are unpaced: Σ _ j=1 ^q p_j x_ ij < B_i ⇒ α_i = 1 .
